In the year 1606.

# PREFACE: TO THE READER

*Preface to this Book.*

*Hedeon Balaban, by the mercy of God humble Bishop of Halych, Lviv, and Kamianets, Exarch of the Ecumenical Throne of the Great Church of Constantinople: To the reverend priests and deacons, and to the other fellow ministers of the sacred clergy, and to the brethren beloved in the Lord, I pray for salvation.*

Seeing that many zealous lovers of the Divine law take care concerning the sacred books, by which the Church of God is adorned, and the faith is defended, the praise of the Most High is multiplied, the faithful are confirmed, and heretics are confounded; and the people, raised up as if by a certain spur from slothfulness, are moved unto learning and are encouraged; and above all, by which God is entreated. Therefore, being desirous to print this book, I deemed it right to inform you in this preface—even as you were previously informed of this in the Liturgies[^3]—whence I arrived at this work, God prospering me: namely, having been moved by the writings of the blessed Meletios, Pope of Alexandria;[^4] but also, more than ten years ago, a synod having taken place in Brest of Lithuania,[^5] under Mikhail Rahoza, Metropolitan of Kyiv,[^6] and the other bishops then assembled, before his apostasy with his partisans from the One Holy Eastern Catholic Apostolic Church: there was much inquiry and consideration by them concerning the great discrepancy of Church rites, and especially concerning the Euchologion,[^7] that is, the Molitvoslovets or Trebnyk: by which, being instructed as by a certain artistic guidance, those who perform sacred rites accomplish decently all things pertaining to the perfect calling of Christianity, and agree in their prayers unto God. And having considered these matters at the synod, they entrusted to humble me, the Bishop of Lviv, to take all care and diligence concerning the correction of that book of the said Trebnyk. And shortly thereafter, Metropolitan Mikhail, having apostatized with certain bishops from the Holy Eastern Church and cast off the pastorship of the Ecumenical Patriarch, departed along the path of insubordination according to the devise of their own hearts. Yet I, following my own shepherd,[^8] did not apostatize; and keeping in remembrance the task entrusted unto me, I gathered many Trebnyks, both from these local regions and from the lands of Wallachia, Moldavia, and Serbia:[^9] in which, when I saw the great discrepancy, concerning this I grieved exceedingly; but I found a remedy for my sorrow through an epistle sent to the most blessed Meletios, Pope of Alexandria—who had attained to the height of external wisdom and of our noble instruction, as an excellent steersman of the ship of Christ, who was then administering the place of the Throne of Constantinople[^10]—informing him concerning the discordance and lack of correction in our Slavonic books, whether on account of unskilled scribes or because of certain other causes; and at the same time beseeching him that, for the sake of certain and unconflicting knowledge of the Church services, he would send us a Greek Euchologion. And he did not disregard my petition, but sent me a Sluzhebnik, and this book, the Trebnyk, well corrected according to the ancient Trebnyks of the Holy Mountain;[^11] which also he signed with his own hand with his pastoral blessing, commanding that it be printed for the common benefit of the renowned Russian race.[^12] And since I had as my fellow laborer in this work the noble Teodor Yurievych Balaban, the son of my brother, with whom having established a printing house in our ancestral estate of Striatyn,[^13] fittingly, as was most urgent, with typographical instruments, having previously an urge toward this, as I said before, [encouraged] by the most blessed Meletios: we first printed the Sluzhebniks,[^14] and thereafter we resolved to print this Trebnyk; in which, lest anyone reproach us among those who delight in dissension concerning certain matters—especially concerning the Proskomedia,[^15] and concerning the particles of bread placed upon the diskos on account of discordance with ancient manuscript Sluzhebniks: let each know that not from my own opinion or speculation did I thus set this down; but having commanded [the translators] to interpret into Slavonic with all diligence the understanding and exposition concerning this formerly of blessed memory Jeremiah, Ecumenical Patriarch,[^16] who also traveled as a pilgrim here among us, and likewise of the most blessed Meletios, from the Greek books sent unto us by him, we have thus set it down. And having translated also this book, the Trebnyk,[^17] to issue it for the common need of the churches: yet lest there be any differing opinion concerning this also, we commanded that there be a synod of priests experienced in the sacred rites, to inspect and examine it. And I saw it to be necessary that what is found in our old Slavonic Trebnyks—namely, how to receive those coming from various heresies unto the Holy Catholic and Apostolic Church,[^18] the Consecration of the Great Myron,[^19] and the rest—lest the book be deficient in this also, we commanded to append this as well. And if there are any who take offense at this, that the authors of all the sequences are not known, let such know that neither do we know [the authors] for the other sequences of the Church's holy mysteries—namely, Baptism, Holy Unction,[^20] and others; yet we know from the commandments of the Holy Apostles that these were instituted by them. Concerning which also the fiery-tongued Dionysius the Areopagite in the book *On the Ecclesiastical Hierarchy* clearly testifies (that these were handed down by the Apostles),[^21] and the rest by the Holy Fathers; which, having received from both, we firmly maintain. For if, as the Great Basil says, we begin to neglect unwritten customs as having little force, we shall unawares bring harm even unto the written things themselves.[^22] And the Divine Chrysostom said: Hence it is manifest that the Apostles did not hand down all things by writing, but many things also unwritten; and both the one and the other are alike worthy of belief. Therefore we also deem the tradition of the Church worthy of belief: it is a tradition; seek nothing further.[^23] And when I was occupied with other necessary Church needs, and was taking care concerning other books—namely, Psalters and Didactic Gospels—to issue them from my printing house of Krylos,[^24] the aforementioned noble Teodor Yurievych Balaban zealously applied himself unto the work of this book: a man flourishing in many righteous deeds, and exceedingly [a fervent lover] of the pious dogma and the traditions of the fathers, a fervent lover, who not in word only, but also in deed kept blamelessly the piety of the fathers. And especially where many of the multitude who go abroad—I mean to Italy[^25]—being beguiled by the vain philosophy of secular learning, fall into various heresies, and being stripped of piety fall away from the Church. But he, having lived there for a long time in his youth, harmed not piety, and turned aside not even a little from the traditions of the Eastern Church; but even as one in the midst of fire remained unburned, or as one in the midst of the sea's surges suffered no shipwreck. Therefore I praise him; on account of the righteousness of his virtue I praise him; whose zeal and care in this was to issue into the light of day the books necessary for the Church: among which, after the Sluzhebnik, he took diligence to print this Trebnyk from his printing house of Striatyn, with the counsel and blessing of our humility, at his own cost and expense, having gathered for this work men skilled in that craft. Who, before this book had yet reached its completion, passed away, the faithful servant of his Lord, Teodor Yurievych, in the year after the Nativity of Christ one thousand six hundred and six, on the twenty-fourth day of the month of May.[^26]
And the composition of this book is proportioned to the span of man's age,[^27] from when he is born, a man receives the naming of a name, and Holy Baptism, with the anointing of the Great Myron, and the other sacred rites according to the Church tradition even unto his demise. Nor have we omitted the monastic sequences; likewise the prayerful supplication sequences for various necessary needs. And because the canons are not found among all priests, for this reason, having selected the most necessary from the Apostolic and Holy Fathers' commandments, we have appended them at the end of this book.[^28] Which do you, receiving with gratitude and love, honor, performing what has been labored over and corrected sacredly without any gainsaying, in concord; [remembering] those who exerted themselves and [brought] all diligence into this work, having brought it for the sake of your common benefit. And especially remember zealously the departed and ever-memorable servant of God, Teodor, at the accomplishment of the dread, bloodless sacrifice,[^29] and in the other lityas and supplications: that by grateful love and devotion to books you may also sharpen us for the work of other books.
Fare well, praying for us both here and after our departure from this flesh, being bound unto us by love.[^30]

# PART I: ORDER FOR THE NAMING OF A CHILD ON THE EIGHTH DAY

[Fol. 1r. Headpiece: woodcut engraving with a central oval vignette depicting the Crucifixion of Christ with the Holy Virgin Mary and Saint John the Theologian standing by the Cross, framed by Renaissance strapwork, acanthus foliage, winged cherubim, and pelicans.]

THE ORDER OF THE DEDICATION OF A CHILD[^31]

*Be it known that on the eighth day after birth, the newborn infant is brought by the midwife[^32] to the church, to receive a name.*
*And the priest makes prayer over him before the church doors. First he signs his forehead, mouth, and breast. And he says:* **Let us pray to the Lord.**
*Prayer to sign the child, and to name his name:*

*At the Dedication [of a Child]*

O Lord our God, unto Thee do we pray, and of Thee do we make supplication: let the light of Thy countenance be signed upon this Thy servant, [N.], and let the Cross of Thine Only-begotten Son be signed upon his heart and upon his thoughts, that he may flee from the vanity of the world, and follow after Thy commandments.[^33] And grant, O Lord, that Thy holy Name may remain unrenounced upon him, being united in due time unto Thy Holy Church, and perfected by the most pure and dread Mysteries of Thy Christ:[^34] that having lived according to Thy commandments, he may preserve the seal unharmed, and keep the robe undefiled, and obtain the blessedness of the elect in Thy Kingdom: by the grace and compassions and love for mankind of Thine Only-begotten Son, with Whom Thou art blessed, together with Thine All-holy, and good, and life-creating Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages.[^35]

*And so he dismisses them.*

*Prayer for the midwife after receiving the child:*[^36]

O Lord Jesus Christ our God, Who wast born before the ages of the Father without a mother, and in the latter years wast sent to be born on earth without a father, having come forth from an unwedded Mother; Who didst receive gifts from the magi, glorification from the shepherds, singing from the angels; how [Thou didst accept] wrapping in swaddling clothes, and being laid in a manger of brute beasts:

laid in a manger of brute beasts: do Thou now also come by Thy visitation, and sanctify this Thy servant who hath been the midwife that received the infant; and save her who hath come unto Thy holy church, granting purification of soul and body, through the prayers and supplications of our most pure Lady, the Theotokos and Ever-Virgin Mary, and of all the saints. For Thou art He that blesses and sanctifies all things, O Christ our God; and so bless the soul of Thy servant, [N.], [saying the name,] and unto Thee do we send up glory, with the Father, and the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.

*Order on the third day for a woman after giving birth to a child:*[^37]

*The priest says:*
> **Priest:** "Blessed is our God..."
*And we [say] the Trisagion; O Most Holy Trinity; after [which:* Our Father...*]*

> **Priest:** "For Thine is the kingdom..."

*Troparion, Tone 4:*[^38]
Thy Nativity, O Virgin Theotokos, has announced joy unto all the universe; for from Thee has shone forth the Sun of Righteousness, Christ our God; and having loosed the curse, He has given blessing, and having abolished death, He has granted us life eternal.

*Kontakion, Tone 4:*
Joachim and Anna were freed from the reproach of childlessness, and Adam and Eve from the corruption of death, O Most Pure, by Thy holy Nativity. This do Thy people celebrate, being delivered from the guilt of transgressions, crying out unto Thee: The barren woman gives birth to the Theotokos and the nourisher of our Life.

*Then the prayer:*

*Let us pray to the Lord.*

O Lord our God, Who from the dust didst fashion man, and from him didst form woman, and didst honor her with equal dignity; and when they transgressed Thy commandment, Thou didst cast [them] out of Paradise into this laborious life, and didst say unto the man: In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread; and unto the woman: In sorrow shalt thou bring forth children:[^39] Who Thyself didst deign sinlessly to be born of a woman without sin for the salvation of our race: do Thou now also, we pray Thy tender mercy, sanctify this Thy servant, [N.], [saying the name,] who has given birth to an infant; and cleanse her bodily defilement and spiritual passion, and make her worthy to keep her house purely and blamelessly; and cleanse every doubt from her soul.[^40] For Thou art He that blesses and sanctifies all things, O Christ our God, and unto Thee do we send up glory, with the Father, and the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.

*Second Prayer, to the Same [Woman]. Let us pray to the Lord.*

Unto Thee, O God and Creator of all creation, Who didst make the entrances and goings out of man, fleeing for refuge do we make supplication: and upon this Thy servant, [N.], [saying the name,] let Thy holy Name be signed, and that of Thine Only-begotten Son, our Lord Jesus Christ. Deliver her from all uncleanness, and from the cohabitation of the devil, and from every manner of defilement;[^41] and make her a chosen vessel, that she may be unto Thee a pure handmaid; and let her be signed with the power of Thy precious and life-creating Cross from this present day and hour, and be sanctified with the seal of Thy Christ: with Whom Thou art blessed, together with Thine All-holy, and good, and life-creating Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages.

*Third Prayer, to the Same [Woman], and for the Women Who Were Present at That Childbirth.*[^42]
*Let us pray to the Lord.*

O Master, Lord Jesus Christ, Word of God and of the Father, Only-begotten Son: Who for our salvation, by the good pleasure of Thine Unoriginate Father, and the cooperation of Thine consubstantial and co-eternal Spirit, having descended at the end of the ages into the womb of the Holy Virgin, and having become incarnate and been born ineffably and unutterably as Thou Thyself alone knowest, having become perfect man, that Thou mightest deliver us from the enemy's tyranny; and having abolished the first curse, that Thou mightest exalt us to Heaven by the God-given gift of divinity, and seat us upon the Father's throne; Who didst keep Thy Mother, Ever-Virgin both before childbirth and after childbirth, free of pain:[^43] do Thou so deign, O compassionate Master, all-good Lord Jesus Christ, now also that Thy servant who has given birth, [N.], [saying the name,] may be delivered from every snare of the enemy; and being sanctified by Thy grace, cleanse and sanctify her by the gift and visitation of the Holy Spirit: that both the women who ministered unto her when she gave birth, and likewise those who were present in this house, as they come may all receive Thy sanctification without doubt. Grant also that the one who has been born may be preserved above the snare of the enemy, and be counted worthy of the bath of regeneration,[^44] and become an honorable vessel of Thy grace, and by the communion of Thy most pure and divine Mysteries become an heir of Thy Heavenly Kingdom: that for this cause also Thine all-holy Name may be glorified, with the Father, and with the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.

[In the margin: Note well.]

*And after this he sprinkles the whole house with holy water.*

*It is fitting to know:*[^45]

*If the newborn infant is sick and does not nurse, it is not fitting to wait for the fifth or sixth day, and then baptize, as some have evilly said; but in that very hour wherein he is born, wash him and immediately baptize him, lest he die unillumined. For if after five months from conception it happen that by some cause the infant is miscarried, they are guilty under the laws and the canons of the penalty for murder;[^46] how much more ought one to avoid the judgment concerning those already born, lest they pass away unillumined.*

*And on the fortieth day [the child] is again brought to be churched,[^47] that is, to begin to be brought into the church.*

*And he is brought by the mother, being already cleansed and washed; [the godparent] being present who will receive him after baptism;[^48] and she having bowed her head together with the infant before the doors of the church.*

*The priest begins:*
> **Priest:** "Blessed is our God..."
*Then:*
> **Reader:** "Holy God... *(3)*. Most Holy Trinity..."
*After* Our Father:
> **Priest:** "For Thine is the kingdom..."

*Troparion, Tone 1:*[^49]
Rejoice, O Virgin Theotokos, full of grace! For from Thee has shone forth the Sun of Righteousness, Christ our God, illumining those who are in darkness. Rejoice thou also, O righteous elder, who dost receive in thine arms [who dost receive in thine arms] the Liberator of our souls, Who grants us the Resurrection.[^50]

*Kontakion, Tone 1:*[^51]
Thou Who didst sanctify the Virgin's womb by Thy birth, and didst bless the hands of Symeon as was fitting, having anticipated [us], hast now also saved [us], O Christ God; but grant peace in times of war to our commonwealth,[^52] and strengthen the rulers whom Thou hast loved, O only Lover of mankind.

*Then, touching her head, he signs her crosswise, saying:*
> **Priest:** "Let us pray to the Lord."

O Lord our God, unto Thee do we pray, and of Thee do we ask, and we make supplication: for Thou art He that is, the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, Who hast created all rational and irrational nature by Thy word, and hast brought all things from non-existence into being: do Thou also by Thy will save this Thy servant, [N.], [saying the name,] and cleanse her from every defilement and every sin, as she approaches Thy holy church, that she may without condemnation be counted worthy of Thy Holy Mysteries.

*If, therefore, before the fortieth day the infant has died, read the prayer up to this point;[^53] but if he is alive, read this also unto the end:*

And this infant born of her do Thou bless, and sanctify, and cause to grow, and endow with understanding: for Thou hast brought him into the sensory light, that he may be counted worthy of the spiritual light,[^54] at the time which Thou hast pre-ordained; and that he] may be numbered with Thy holy flock, for the sake of Thine Only-begotten Son, with Whom Thou art blessed, together with Thine All-holy, and good, and life-creating Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.

*The priest says:*
> **Priest:** "Peace be unto all."
> **Reader:** "And to thy spirit."
> **Priest:** "Bow your heads unto the Lord."
> **Reader:** "Unto Thee, O Lord."

*Then this prayer secretly:*[^55]

O Lord our God, Who didst come into the world for the salvation of the human race: come Thou also unto this Thy servant, [N.], [saying the name,] and count her worthy through Thy venerable presbyterate of the entrance into the temple of Thy glory; wash away her defilement of soul and body at the completion of the forty days, making her worthy of the communion of Thy precious Body and Blood.

> **Priest:** "For blessed and glorified is Thine all-honorable and majestic Name, with the Father, and with the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen."

*Then the priest himself, having received the child in his hands, carries him into the sanctuary;[^56] and he touches his mouth to both sides of the doors in the likeness of kissing. Likewise, having brought him to the Holy Table, he positions the infant as though bowing, going around three times. And if he be of the male sex, he does thus; but if it be of the female sex, she is not brought into the altar, but only to the holy doors and the icons, as has been said.[^57] And when these things have been done, the priest says to himself:*

> **Priest:** "Now lettest Thou dismiss Thy servant, O Master... unto the end."[^58]

*After this, he places the infant before the doors of the sanctuary, and says the prayer:*
> **Priest:** "Let us pray to the Lord."

O Lord our God, Who on the fortieth day wast brought as an infant unto the temple of the Law by Mary, Thine unwedded Mother, and wast received into the arms of righteous Symeon: do Thou Thyself, O Almighty Master, bless also this infant who has been brought to appear before Thee, the Creator of all, and cause him to grow unto every good work that is well-pleasing unto Thee, driving away from him every contrary power by the signing of the form of Thy Cross: for Thou art He that preserves infants, O Lord; that being counted worthy [that being counted worthy] of Holy Baptism, he may obtain the portion of the elect of Thy Kingdom, being preserved with us by the grace of the Holy, and Consubstantial, and Undivided Trinity. For unto Thee is due all thanksgiving, honor, and worship, with Thine Unoriginate Father, and with Thine All-holy, and good, and life-creating Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.

*After the Amen, he signs the child.*
*And the mother with the child, having stood before the holy icon of the Mother of God, makes forty bows.[^59] The priest makes the dismissal. And so the receiver receives him, and departs.*
*And the receiver is called the sponsor [koum].[^60]*

# PART II: CANONS OF THE HOLY APOSTLES AND OF THE GOD-BEARING HOLY FATHERS CONCERNING HOLY BAPTISM

[Fol. 10r. Headpiece: Renaissance woodcut engraving with strapwork, foliate scrollwork, and mythological figures flanking a central cartouche.]

CANONS OF THE HOLY APOSTLES AND OF THE GOD-BEARING HOLY FATHERS CONCERNING HOLY BAPTISM[^61]

*Canon 47 of the Holy Apostles says:*[^62]
If any bishop or presbyter shall baptize anew one who has true baptism, or shall not baptize one who has been defiled by the ungodly, let him be deposed: as mocking the Cross and the death of the Lord, and not distinguishing priests from false priests. Likewise also Canon 50 of the Council of Carthage ordains.[^63]

*Canon 49 of the Holy Apostles:*[^64]
To baptize into the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit, according to the Lord's com- mand, but not into three unoriginate, nor into three sons, nor into three parakletes: for one is the Unoriginate Father, by reason of having no cause; and one is the Son, by reason of His ineffable generation; and one is the Paraklete, the Holy Spirit, by reason of His procession from the Unbegotten.[^65] And those bishops or presbyters who do not so baptize incur the sentence of final deposition.

*And Canon 50:*[^66]
To accomplish three baptisms of one mystery, that is, three immersions in one baptism; and at each immersion to commemorate one Name of the Holy Trinity; but not a single baptism into the death of the Lord, [a single baptism into the death of the Lord] administered: that is, the one being baptized immersed once, and in that single immersion glorifying the death of the Lord, as the Eunomian heresy, full of folly, ordains (which also Canon 7 of the Second Council mentions). For the Lord said not: "Baptize into My death"; but: *Go, teach all nations, baptizing them in the Name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit* [Matthew 28:19]; and any bishop or presbyter who does not do thus [the canon] destroys by deprivation of the priesthood.[^67]

*Canon 7 of the Second Ecumenical Council:*[^68]
Moreover, Canon 7 of the Second Ecumenical Council also very accurately ordains how it is fitting to receive those turning from heresies:

[accurately ordains: for having divided] all into two classes, it legislates that some should be anointed with myron, while others should be baptized from the beginning: namely, the Arians, Macedonians, Sabbatians, and Novatians (who call themselves the pure and the left), and the Quartodecimans (that is, the Tetradites), and the Apollinarians.[^69] Since, therefore, they perform the divine baptism equally with us, it is not deemed proper to baptize them again; but upon their written renunciation and anathematization of their heresy, [the canon] commands to anoint them with the holy myron: the forehead, the eyes, and the nostrils, the mouth, and the ears; and signing them, to say: "The seal of the gift of the Holy Spirit."[^70]

[The seal of the gift of the Holy Spirit.] But the Eunomians, who baptize into a single immersion, and the Montanists, who are called Phrygians, and the Sabellians, who teach the Son-Fatherhood, and those like unto them: as judging and abiding in truth to be nothing better than unbaptized pagans, [the canon] commands immediately to be baptized when coming unto the Catholic Church.[^71] For if they have either not been baptized at all, or having been baptized were not signed according to the canons of the Orthodox Church, for this cause they are accounted by the divine Fathers as unilluminated.

*And Canon 48 of [the Council] in Laodicea legislates that those being enlightened be anointed with myron:*[^72]

[legislates that those being enlightened be anointed with myron:] for this [myron], being sanctified by prayers and the invocation of the Holy Spirit, sanctifies those who are anointed, and makes them partakers of the heavenly Kingdom of Christ, unless carelessness of life and the malice of deeds alienate us from this.

*And Canon 6 of the Council of Neocaesarea does not forbid pregnant women who desire it to be baptized:*[^73] for the unborn child within her does not partake with her of illumination, not having yet received from nature a disposition for good or for worse, nor is it possible to test what kind of disposition [the child] might have. But infants, through the actions of the anadochoi— [through the actions of the anadochoi—] that is, the sponsors [receivers]—laid upon them, being illuminated themselves, are made partakers of the Divine radiance.[^74]

*And Canon 6 of Timothy of Alexandria says:*[^75]
If a catechumen woman, on that day on which she was to be baptized, should experience her customary female condition, let her illumination be deferred unto a subsequent day.

*Of the same [Timothy], before all [Canon 1] says:*[^76]
If a catechumen child, or an adult man, when the sacred Sacrifice is being celebrated, having approached guilelessly, should partake of the Divine Gifts, the priest not knowing him to be a catechumen: let him immediately be [let him immediately be] baptized, for he has been called by the Lord.

*And Canon 4 of Saint Cyril says:*[^77]
Even if any of the catechumens undergo excommunication, having fallen under severe penance, and they are about to die, let them be baptized, and let them not depart unpartaking of human loving-kindness [grace].

*And Canon 2 of Timothy of Alexandria:*[^78]
Forbids a demon-possessed catechumen to be baptized before he is cleansed from the unclean demon: for it is not right that one who has given himself over to be a dwelling for an evil demon through turning aside unto wicked deeds should receive into himself the light of the Holy Spirit, unless he has been unreservedly freed from the dark and [freed from the dark and] evil spirit. But if it should come to him to die, [the canon] commands him to be baptized, that he may not depart from life empty and unpartaking of Divine grace.

*And the fourth [canon of Timothy] says:*[^79]
If a catechumen is troubled not by a demon, but is stricken by a disease of derangement of mind, so that he is not even able to reply to questions or make his profession; yet inasmuch as he showed of his own free choice that he embraced the faith, and was voluntarily enrolled among the catechumens: let him be baptized without doubt.

*And Canon 121 of the Council in Carthage says:*[^80]
The grace given unto us in baptism not only [grants] remission of sins, but [not only grants remission of sins, but] also brings power that we may no longer sin, unless through slothfulness, being self-willed, we embrace sinful deeds. And those who do not hold thus, [the canon] commits unto anathema.

[Fol. 14v. Tailpiece: Renaissance woodcut cul-de-lampe depicting a grotesque mascaron with scrolled horns, foliate strapwork, crown/crest, and curly beard.][^81]

# PART III: THE ORDER OF THE CATECHUMENATE FOR THOSE WHO WISH TO BE BAPTIZED [^82]

*The catechumen is brought, or is carried if he be an infant, unto the church. And they divest him, and stand him facing toward the east, unloosed of his belt, uncovered, and barefoot, having his hands hanging down.[^83] And the priest breathes upon him thrice, and signs his face and breast thrice, and lays his hands upon his head,[^84] and says this prayer:*

**Deacon [or Priest]:** Let us pray to the Lord.

> **Priest:** ""
[Fol. 15v. Decorative woodcut initial O.]
In Thy Name, O Lord God of truth, and [in the Name] of Thine Only-begotten Son, and of Thy Most Holy Spirit: I lay my hand upon this Thy servant, *[Name]*, who has been accounted worthy to flee unto Thy holy Name, and to be preserved under the shelter of Thy wings.[^85] Remove from him that ancient deception, and fill him with faith, hope, and love in Thee; that he may know that Thou art the only true God, and Thine Only-begotten Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, and Thy Holy Spirit. Grant him to walk in all Thy commandments, and to do and keep the things pleasing unto Thee: for if a man do them, he shall live in them. Inscribe him in the book of life, and unite him unto the flock of Thine inheritance,[^86] that Thy holy Name may be glorified in him, and [the Name] of Thy beloved Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, and of Thy life-creating Spirit. Let Thine eyes look upon him mercifully at all times, and Thine ears give ear unto the voice of his supplication. Gladden him in the works of his hands, and in all his generation, that he may give thanks unto Thee, worshipping and glorifying Thy great and most high Name, and may praise Thee alway in all the days of his life: for all the heavenly powers sing praise unto Thee, and Thine is the glory unto ages of ages. Amen.

*First Exorcism.*[^87]

**Deacon [or Priest]:** Let us pray to the Lord.

> **Priest:** ""
[Fol. 16v. Decorative woodcut initial Z.]
The Lord rebukes thee, O devil: He Who came into the world and dwelt among men, that He might destroy thy tyranny and deliver mankind; Who upon the Tree exposed the adverse powers, when the sun was darkened, and the earth was shaken, and the graves were opened, and the bodies of the saints arose; Who destroyed death by death, and brought to naught him that had the power of death, that is, thee, O devil. I adjure thee by God, [I adjure thee by God,] Who showed forth the tree of life, and appointed the cherubim and the flaming sword turning every way to keep it: be rebuked and depart! For I adjure thee by Him Who walked upon the sea as upon dry land, and rebuked the tempest of winds; at Whose glance the deeps dry up, and at Whose rebuke the mountains melt away.[^88] For He now commands thee through us: Fear, come forth, and depart from this creature; and turn not back, neither hide thyself in him, neither encounter him, nor work in him, neither in night, nor in day, nor in an hour, nor at midday; but depart into thine own abyss [tartarus], until the prepared great day of judgment. Fear God Who sits upon the cherubim and looks down upon the deeps; before Whom tremble angels and archangels, thrones, dominions, principalities, authorities, powers, the many-eyed cherubim, and the six-winged seraphim; before Whom the heaven and the earth tremble, the sea, and all that in them is. Come forth and depart from the signed and newly chosen soldier of Christ our God. For I adjure thee by Him Who walks upon the wings of the wind, Who makes His angels spirits, and His ministers a flame of fire: come forth and depart from this creature with[^89] [with] all thy power and thine angels. For glorified is the Name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto [ages of ages. Amen.]

*Second Exorcism.*[^90]

**Deacon [or Priest]:** Let us pray to the Lord.

> **Priest:** ""
[Fol. 18r. Decorative woodcut initial B.]
O God, holy, fearful, and glorious, Who art incomprehensible and unsearchable in all Thy works and Thy power: Thou Who didst ordain for thee, O devil, the torment of eternal punishment: through us, His unworthy servants, He commands thee and all thy collaborative power to depart from him that has newly been signed in the Name of our Lord Jesus Christ, our true God. I adjure thee therefore, all-evil, unclean, defiled, abominable, and alien spirit, by the power of Jesus Christ, Who has all power in heaven and on earth; Who said unto the deaf and dumb demon: "Come out of the man, and enter no more into him!" Depart, recognize thy vain power, which had no authority even over the swine! Remember Him Who commanded thee at thy request to enter into the herd of swine. Fear God, by Whose command the earth was established upon the waters; Who created heaven, and set the mountains by a plummet, and the valleys by a measure; and placed sand as a boundary for the sea, and a firm path in the mighty waters; Who touches the mountains, and they smoke;[^91]

Who decks Himself with light as with a garment; Who covers His upper chambers with waters; Who founded the earth upon its firmness, and it shall not be shaken unto ages of ages; Who calls forth the water of the sea, and pours it out upon the face of all the earth: come forth and depart from him that is preparing for holy illumination! I adjure thee by the saving Passion of our Lord Jesus Christ, and His precious Body and Blood, and His fearful coming: for He shall come and will not delay, judging all the earth and thee, and He will torment thy collaborative power in fiery Gehenna, where the worm[^92] dies not, and the fire is not quenched: for the dominion is of Christ our God, with the Father and the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages [of ages. Amen.]

*Third Exorcism Prayer.*[^93]

**Deacon [or Priest]:** Let us pray to the Lord.

> **Priest:** ""
[Fol. 19v. Decorative woodcut initial G.]
O Lord of hosts [Sabaoth], God of Israel, Who healest every disease and every infirmity: look down upon Thy servant, *[Name]*, seek out, claim, and drive away from him all workings of the devil. Rebuke the unclean spirits, and drive them away, and cleanse the work of Thy hands; and, putting forth Thy swift operation, crush Satan under his feet shortly; and grant him victory over him and over his unclean spirits: that, having obtained mercy from Thee, he may be accounted worthy of Thine immortal and heavenly Mysteries, and send up glory unto Thee, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.

*Fourth Exorcism Prayer.*[^94]

**Deacon [or Priest]:** Let us pray to the Lord.

> **Priest:** ""
[Fol. 20r. Decorative woodcut initial S.]
O Sovereign Lord, Who hast made man according to Thine own image and likeness, and given him the power of life everlasting; and then, when he had fallen through sin, didst not despise him, but didst provide salvation for the world through the incarnation of Thy Christ: do Thou now, having delivered this Thy creature from the bondage of the enemy, receive him into Thy heavenly kingdom. Open his spiritual eyes, that the illumination of Thy Gospel may shine in him. Yoke with his life an angel of light, delivering him from every snare of the adversary, from encounter with the evil one, from the noonday demon, and from wicked apparitions.[^95]

*And he breathes again thrice, and signs his brow, and his mouth, and his breast, and says this prayer:*

**Deacon [or Priest]:** Let us pray to the Lord.

> **Priest:** ""
[Fol. 20v. Decorative initial I.]
Expel from him every wicked and unclean spirit, hiding and nesting in his heart.

*(And he says thrice:)*
A spirit of deception and wickedness; a spirit of idolatry and all covetousness; a spirit of lying and of all impurity, wrought according to the prompting of the devil. And make him a reason-endowed sheep of the holy flock of Thy Christ, an honorable member of Thy Church, a consecrated vessel, a child of light, and an heir of Thy kingdom: that, having lived according to Thy commandments, and preserved the seal unbroken, and kept the garment undefiled, he may attain the blessedness of Thy chosen ones in Thy kingdom.[^96]

**Exclamation:**
Through the grace and compassions and love for mankind of Thine Only-begotten Son, with Whom Thou art blessed, together with Thy Most Holy, good, and life-creating Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. [Amen.]

*And when he that is to be baptized is divested and ungirded, the priest turns him toward the west, with his hands uplifted. And the priest says:*[^97]

> **Priest:** "Dost thou renounce Satan?"

**Catechumen:** I renounce Satan.

> **Priest:** "And all his works, and all his service, and all his angels, and all his pride?"

*(And it is said thrice. And the catechumen, or his sponsor, answers at each phrase.)*

*If he be an infant and cannot speak, then let the sponsor [kum] say on his behalf:* "He renounces Satan," *and the rest.*

*Likewise, if he be a foreigner [of another tongue] and knows not how to answer, let the sponsor [answer on his behalf]* let him speak on his behalf, or the deacon.[^98]

*Thereafter the priest says again:*
> **Priest:** "Dost thou renounce Satan?"

*He that is being baptized says:*
**Catechumen:** I have renounced Satan.

*And when he has said it the third time, the priest says unto him:*
> **Priest:** "And breathe, and spit upon the demon."

*And when he has done this, the priest turns him again facing toward the east, having his hands down. And he says, thrice:*
> **Priest:** "Dost thou pledge thyself unto Christ?"

*And he that is being baptized, or the sponsor, answers:*
**Catechumen [or Sponsor]:** I pledge myself unto Christ.

> **Priest:** "Dost thou believe in Him?"

**Catechumen [or Sponsor]:** I believe in Him as King and God.

*And he says:*
**Catechumen [or Sponsor]:**
I believe in one God, the Father Almighty... unto the end, thrice.

*And when he has completed* the Holy Creed, *he says again unto him thrice:*
> **Priest:** "Hast thou pledged thyself unto Christ?"

*And he answers:*
**Catechumen [or Sponsor]:** I have pledged myself.

> **Priest:** "Bow down before Him."

*And he bows down, saying:*
**Catechumen [or Sponsor]:**
I bow down before the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit: Trinity consubstantial and undivided.

*Then the priest says:*
> **Priest:** "Blessed is God, Who wills all men to be saved, and to come unto the knowledge of the truth; now and ever, and unto ages of ages."[^99]

*Then he says this prayer:*
**Deacon [or Priest]:** Let us pray to the Lord.

> **Priest:** ""
[Fol. 22v. Decorative initial V.]
O Master, Lord our God, call Thy servant, *[Name]*, unto Thy holy illumination, and count him worthy of this great grace of Thy holy baptism. Wash away from him the oldness [of sin], and regenerate him unto eternal life; and fill him with the power of Thy Holy Spirit, into the union of Thy Christ: that he may no longer be a child of the flesh, but a child of Thy kingdom; through the good pleasure and bounty of Thine Only-begotten Son, with Whom Thou art blessed, together with Thine All-holy, and good, and life-creating Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.[^100]

[Fol. 23r. Tailpiece: Renaissance woodcut vignette ornament with scrolled acanthus leaves and central palmette.]

# PART IV: THE ORDER OF HOLY BAPTISM [^101]

*The priest enters into the church, and having vested in white priestly vesture and cuffs, all the candles being lighted, he takes the censer and goes unto the font, and censes round about. And having given back the censer, he bows.*[^102]

*Then the deacon says:*
> **Deacon:** "Bless, Master."

*And the priest [says] with a loud voice:*

> **Priest:** "Blessed is the kingdom of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. [Choir: Amen.]"

*The Great Litany:*[^103]
> **Deacon:** ""
In peace let us pray to the Lord.
For the peace from above, and for the salvation of our souls, [let us pray to the Lord].
For the peace of the whole world, and the good standing [of the holy churches of God, let us pray to the Lord].
For this holy temple, and those that [enter into it] with faith, [reverence, and the fear of God, let us pray to the Lord].
For our Archbishop, *[Name]*, for his venerable presbyterate, and the diaconate in Christ, [let us pray to the Lord].
That this water may be sanctified by the power, operation, and descent of the Holy Spirit, let us pray to the Lord.
That there may be sent down upon it the grace of redemption, the blessing of Jordan, let us pray to the Lord.
That there may come upon this water the cleans- ing operation of the supersubstantial Trinity, let us pray to the Lord.[^104]
That we may be illuminated with the light of understanding and piety through the coming of the Holy Spirit, let us pray to the Lord.
That it may receive the turning away of every assault of visible and invisible enemies, let us pray to the Lord.
That he who is baptized therein may be made worthy of the incorruptible kingdom, let us pray to the Lord.
For him who now approaches unto holy illumination, and for his salvation, let us pray to the Lord.
That he may be shown forth a child of light, and an heir of eternal blessings, let us pray to the Lord.

That he may be conformed unto the likeness and partake of the death and resurrection of Christ our God, let us pray to the Lord.[^105]
That he may preserve the garment of baptism and the betrothal of Christ undefiled and blameless in the dread day of Christ our God, let us pray to the Lord.
That this water may be unto him a laver of regeneration, unto the remission of sins, and a garment of incorruption, let us pray to the Lord.[^106]
That the Lord God may give ear unto the voice of our supplication, let us pray to the Lord.
That he and we may be delivered from all affliction, wrath, and necessity, let us pray to the Lord.
*Help us, save us, have mercy on us, and keep us Commemorating our Most Holy, pure, most blessed and glorious Lady, the Theotokos and Ever-Virgin Mary, with all the saints...*[^107]

*And while the deacon is saying this litany, the priest reads this prayer within himself secretly:*[^108]

> **Priest:** ""
[Fol. 25v. Decorative initial B.]
O compassionate and merciful God, Who triest the hearts and reins, and Who alone knowest the secrets of men; for there is no thing that is unmanifest before Thee, but all things are naked and exposed before Thine eyes: knowing what concerns me, loathe me not, neither turn away Thy face from me; but take away my transgressions at this hour, Thou that overlookest the sins of men unto repentance. Wash away my bodily uncleanness and my spiritual defilement, and sanctify me wholly by Thine invisible power, and by Thy spiritual right hand: that while promising freedom unto others, through perfect faith in Thine ineffable love for mankind, I myself may not become reprobate as a slave of sin. Yea, O Master, Who alone art good and the Lover of mankind, let me not return humbled and put to shame; but send me power from on high, and strengthen me for the ministry of this Thy present Mystery, great and heavenly; and form the image of Thy Christ in him who is about to be reborn through my unworthiness.[^109] And build him upon the foundation of Thine Apostles and Prophets, and destroy him not; but plant him as a true planting in Thy holy, catholic, and apostolic Church; and pluck him not up: that as he advances in piety, through him also may be glorified Thine all-holy Name, of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages.

*It is proper to know that he does not make exclamation aloud, but says even the "Amen" within himself.*[^110]

*Then he reads this prayer with a loud voice:*[^111]

> **Priest:** ""
Great art Thou, O Lord, and marvelous are Thy works, and no word is sufficient to sing the praise of Thy wonders.
*(And say this thrice.)*

[Fol. 26v. Decorative initial T.]
For by Thy will Thou hast brought all things out of non-existence into being; by Thy power Thou holdest creation together, and by Thy providence Thou directest the world. Thou hast composed creation; with four seasons Thou hast crowned the circle of the year.[^112] All the spiritual powers tremble before Thee; the sun sings Thy praise; the moon glorifies Thee; the stars make supplication unto Thee; the light obeys Thee; the abysses tremble before Thee; the springs serve Thee. Thou hast stretched out the heaven like a curtain; Thou hast established the earth upon the waters; Thou hast hedged the sea with sand; Thou hast poured out the air for breathing. The Archangelic powers minister unto Thee; the Angelic choirs worship Thee; the many-eyed Cherubim and the six-winged Seraphim, standing round about and flying, with fear cover themselves from Thine unapproachable glory.[^113] For Thou, being God uncircumscribed, without beginning, and ineffable, camest down upon the earth, taking the form of a servant, being made in the likeness of men. For Thou couldest not endure, O Master, through the tender compassion of Thy mercy, to behold mankind tormented by the devil; but Thou camest and didst save us. We confess Thy grace, we proclaim Thy mercy, we conceal not Thy benefactions. Thou hast set free the nature of our race; Thou didst sanctify the virginal womb by Thy nativity. All creation sings the praise of Thee Who didst manifest Thyself. For Thou, our God, didst appear upon the earth, and didst dwell among men. Thou the waters of Jordan didst sanctify, sending down from heaven Thy Holy Spirit, and didst break the heads of the dragons that nested there.[^114]

Do Thou Thyself, therefore, O King, Lover of mankind, come even now through the descent of Thy Holy Spirit, and sanctify this water. *(Thrice.)*

And grant unto it the grace of redemption, the blessing of Jordan. And make it a fountain of incorruption, a gift of sanctification, a loosing of sins, a healing of diseases, a destruction of demons, unapproachable to adversary powers, filled with Angelic strength; that they who plot against Thy creature may flee from it. For I have called upon Thy Name, O Lord, marvelous and glorious, and terrible unto adversaries.[^115]

*And he breathes upon the water thrice, and signs it with the sign of the Cross with his hand, and says:*

> **Priest:** ""
Let all adversary powers be crushed beneath the sign of the representation of Thy Cross. *(Thrice.)*

And let all airy and invisible phantoms depart from us; and let no dark demon hide himself in this water; neither let there descend with him that is baptized (we beseech Thee, O Lord) an evil spirit, bringing darkness of thoughts and tumult of mind. But do Thou, O Master of all, manifest this water as water of repose, water of redemption, water of sanctification, cleansing of the defilement of flesh and spirit, loosing of bonds, remission of sins, illumination of souls, the laver of regeneration, renewal of the Spirit, the gift of adoption, the garment of incorruptibility, the renewal of the soul, a fountain of life.[^116] For Thou hast said, O Lord: "Wash you, make you clean, put away evil from your souls." Thou hast bestowed upon us regeneration from on high through water and the Spirit. Manifest Thyself, O Lord, in this water, and grant that he who is baptized therein may be transformed, so that he may put off the old man, corrupt according to the deceits of lust, and put on the new man, renewed according to the image of Him that created him; that having been united unto the likeness of Thy death through baptism, a partaker of the resurrection also shall he be, and having preserved the gift of Thy Holy Spirit,[^117] and increased the deposit of grace, he may receive the prize of the high calling, and be numbered among the firstborn enrolled in heaven.

*Ekphonesis:*
For unto Thee is due all glory, thanksgiving, honor, and worship, to God and our Lord Jesus Christ, together with Thine unoriginate Father, and with Thine all-holy, good, and life-creating Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages.

> **Priest:** ""
Peace be unto all.[^118]

*Bow your heads unto the Lord.*

*And having bowed his head over the vessel of oil, he breathes upon it thrice, and blesses with his hand, thrice. And the deacon, holding the oil in his hand, says:*

> **Deacon:** ""
Let us pray to the Lord.

*And the priest says this prayer:*

> **Priest:** ""
O Master, Lord God of our fathers, Who to them that were in the ark of Noah didst send a dove bearing a twig of olive in its mouth,[^119] the sign of reconciliation and of salvation from the flood, and didst prefigure through these the mystery of grace; and didst provide the fruit of the olive for the fulfillment of Thy holy mysteries; and thereby didst fill them that were under the Law with the Holy Spirit, and perfectest them that are under grace: Do Thou Thyself bless this oil also by the power, and operation, and descent of Thy Holy Spirit, that it may be an anointing of incorruption, an armor of righteousness, a renewal of soul and body, a fountain of life, an averting of every operation of the devil, for the removal of all evils, unto them that are anointed with faith, or that partake of it:[^120]

*And having stood erect, he exclaims aloud:*

> **Priest:** ""
Unto Thy glory, and of Thine Only-begotten Son, and of Thine all-holy, and good, and life-creating Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages.

> **Choir:** ""
Amen.

> **Deacon:** ""
Let us attend.

*And the priest, having taken the oil, makes crosses with drops upon the water thrice, singing Alleluia with the people, thrice. Then he exclaims aloud:*

> **Priest:** ""
Blessed is God, Who enlightens and sanctifies every man that comes into the world, now and ever, and unto ages of ages.[^121]

> **Choir:** ""
Amen.

*And he that is to be baptized is brought unto the priest. And he, having taken of the holy oil with his finger, makes the sign of the Cross upon the infant, on the forehead, and on the breast, and on the face, and on the shoulders, saying:*

> **Priest:** ""
The servant of God, [Name], is anointed with the oil of gladness, in the Name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages.

> **Choir:** ""
Amen.

*And he signs his breast and shoulders. On the breast indeed, saying:*

> **Priest:** ""
Unto the healing of soul and body.

*And on the ears:*[^122]

> **Priest:** ""
Unto the hearing of faith.

*On the feet:*

> **Priest:** ""
That he may walk in Thy steps.

*On the hands:*

> **Priest:** ""
Thy hands have made me and fashioned me.

*When his whole body has been anointed,*

*The priest baptizes him, holding him upright, and facing eastward, saying:*[^123]

> **Priest:** ""
The servant of God, [Name], is baptized in the Name of the Father,

*and he immerses him once, saying:*
Amen.

and of the Son, Amen,

*and he immerses him and brings him up;*

and of the Holy Spirit, Amen, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.

*At each naming immersing him into the water, and bringing him up.*

*And after the baptism, the priest washes himself, singing with the people Psalm 31:*[^124]

Blessed are they whose iniquities are forgiven, and whose sins are covered. Blessed is the man unto whom the Lord does not impute sin, neither is there guile in his mouth. Because I kept silence, my bones waxed old through my crying all the day long. For day and night Thy hand was heavy upon me; I turned into misery when the thorn was pierced into me. I acknowledged my sin, and mine iniquity have I not hidden. I said: I will confess against myself mine iniquity unto the Lord; and Thou forgavest the ungodliness of my heart. For this shall every one that is holy pray unto Thee in a time acceptable;

surely in a flood of many waters they shall not come nigh unto Him. Thou art my refuge from the affliction that surrounds me; my joy, deliver me from them that compass me about. I will give thee understanding, and instruct thee in this way wherein thou shalt go; I will fix Mine eyes upon thee. Be ye not as horse and mule, which have no understanding; whose jaws thou must bind with bit and bridle, lest they come nigh unto thee. Many are the scourges of the sinner; but mercy shall compass him that hopes in the Lord. Be glad in the Lord, and rejoice, ye righteous; and boast, all ye that are upright in heart.[^125]

*And this psalm is said thrice.*

*And if he that is baptized is an infant, he seats him in the font, the water reaching unto his neck, holding him with his left hand; and taking warm water with his right hand, he pours it upon his head, because care must be taken lest the infant drown; and he says the aforesaid words, that is: In the Name of the Father, and the rest. But if he that is baptized has reached understanding, he immerses him in three immersions as we have said above.*[^126]

*Thereafter he clothes him in a garment, saying:*

> **Priest:** ""
The servant of God, *[Name]*, is clothed with the robe of righteousness, in the Name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.

*And he sings this troparion, in Tone 8:*[^127]

*Troparion, Tone 8:*
Grant unto me a robe of light, O Thou that deckest Thyself with light as with a garment, O greatly merciful Christ our God.[^128]

*And after he has been clothed, the priest prays again, saying this prayer:*

> **Deacon:** "Let us pray to the Lord."

> **Priest:** ""
Blessed art Thou, O Lord God Almighty, Fountain of good things, Sun of Righteousness, Who hast caused the light of salvation to shine forth unto them that were in darkness, through the manifestation of Thine Only-begotten Son and our God; and Who hast granted unto us unworthy ones blessed cleansing in holy water, and divine sanctification in the life-creating anointing; Who even now hast been well pleased to regenerate Thy servant newly-illumined, *[Name]*, by water and the Spirit, and granted unto him remission of sins voluntary and involuntary.[^129] Do Thou Thyself, O Master of all, compassionate King, grant unto him also the seal of the gift of Thy Holy, all-powerful, and adorable Spirit, and communion of the holy Body and precious Blood of Thy Christ. Preserve him in Thy sanctification; confirm him in the Orthodox faith; deliver him from the evil one and all his snares; and by Thy saving fear keep his soul in purity and righteousness: that pleasing Thee in every deed and word, he may become a son and heir of Thy Heavenly Kingdom.

*Ekphonesis:*

> **Priest:** ""
For Thou art our God, a God to show mercy and to save us, and unto Thee do we send up glory, to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages.[^130]

> **Choir:** ""
Amen.

*Then he anoints the baptized with the holy Chrism, making the sign of the Cross: on the forehead, on the eyes, on the breast, on the hands, and on the feet, saying:*[^131]

> **Priest:** ""
The seal of the gift of the Holy Spirit. Amen.

*Then the priest with the sponsor and the newly-baptized walk round about the analogion, singing thrice:*[^132]

> **Choir:** ""
As many of you as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ. Alleluia. *(Thrice.)*

*Then the Prokeimenon, Tone 3:*

> **Reader:** ""
The Lord is my illumination and my Savior; whom shall I fear?[^133]

*Verse:*
The Lord is the defender of my life; of whom shall I be afraid?

*Epistle to the Romans:*[^134]

> **Reader:** ""
Brethren, as many of us as were baptized into Christ were baptized into His death. Therefore we were buried with Him through baptism into death; that like as Christ was raised up from the dead by the glory of the Father, even so we also should walk in newness of life. For if we have become united with Him in the likeness of His death, so also shall we be partakers of His resurrection: knowing this, that our old man was crucified with Him, that the body of sin might be done away, that henceforth we should not serve sin. For he that is dead is justified from sin. Now if we died with Christ, we believe that we shall also live with Him: knowing that Christ, having been raised from the dead, dies no more; death has dominion over Him no more. For in that He died, He died unto sin once; but in that He lives, He lives unto God. Likewise reckon ye also yourselves to be dead indeed unto sin, but alive unto God in Christ Jesus our Lord.[^135]

> **Choir:** ""
Alleluia.

> **Deacon:** ""
Wisdom. Stand upright. Let us hear the Holy Gospel.

> **Priest:** ""
The reading from the Holy Gospel according to Matthew.

> **Deacon:** ""
Let us attend.

> **Priest:** ""
At that time, the eleven disciples went into Galilee, into a mountain where Jesus had appointed them. And when they saw Him, they worshipped Him; but some doubted. And Jesus came and spake unto them, saying: All power is given unto Me in heaven and in earth. Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the Name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit: teaching them to observe all things whatsoever I have commanded you. And lo, I am with you always, even unto the end of the age. Amen.[^136]

*Then the deacon says the litany:*[^137]

> **Deacon:** ""
Have mercy on us, O God, according to Thy great mercy...

Again we pray for our pious sovereign.

Again we pray for our Bishop, *[Name]*;

Again we pray for mercy, life, and the remission of sins for the servant of God, *[Name]*, the sponsor;

Again we pray for the newly-illumined servant of God, *[Name]*, that he may be preserved in the faith of a pure confession, all the days of his life.

*Ekphonesis:*

> **Priest:** ""
For Thou art a merciful God and the Lover of mankind, and unto Thee do we send up glory, to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages.

*Then: Glory... both now... Lord, have mercy (thrice). Bless.*

*Priest: The Dismissal:*

> **Priest:** ""
May He Who deigned to be baptized in the Jordan by John for the sake of our salvation, Christ our true God, through the prayers of His most pure Mother, by the power of the precious and life-creating Cross, and of all the saints, have mercy on us and save us[^138] for He is good and the Lover of mankind.[^139]

*It is fitting to know that if there be a Liturgy, they carry the newly-illumined infant with candles at the Great Transfer [Entrance].[^140] But if the one who has been baptized be an adult, let him go himself before the divine Gifts at the Great Entrance, holding a candle in each hand. And he partakes of the Holy Mysteries of Christ our God, whether he be an infant or an adult.*

*And after the dismissal, he goes forth unto his own house holding burning candles, his kin escorting him. And if, therefore, the one baptized be an adult he is brought each day unto the church, likewise holding burning candles: to Vespers, and to Matins, and to the Liturgy, even unto the eighth day.*[^141]

# PART V: THE ORDER FOR THE ABLUTION OF THE BAPTIZED ON THE EIGHTH DAY [^142]

*Again they bring him into the church, and the sponsor with him. And the priest looses the garments which are the papish from baptism, and the belt.[^143] And he says:*

> **Priest:** ""
Blessed is our God alway, now and ever, and unto ages of ages.

> **Reader:** ""
Amen.
Heavenly King... Trisagion... Most Holy Trinity... After: Our Father...

> **Priest:** ""
For Thine is the kingdom...

*Then the troparion of the day, and of the saint that has occurred. Glory... both now... Theotokion.*

**Choir [or Reader]:**
Through the prayers, O Lord, of all the saints and of the Mother of God, give Thy peace unto us, and have mercy on us, as the only compassionate One.

*Then the priest says the prayers.*

> **Deacon:** ""
Let us pray to the Lord.

> **Priest:** ""
[Fol. 38v. Decorative woodcut initial I.]
O Thou Who hast granted remission of sins unto Thy servant through holy baptism, and hast bestowed upon him renewal of life:[^144] do Thou Thyself, O Master and Lord, be well pleased that the illumination of Thy countenance shine alway in his heart. Preserve the strength of his faith free from the snares of enemies; preserve spotless and unstained upon him the garment of incorruptibility wherewith he was clothed; keeping inviolate within him the spiritual seal by Thy grace; showing mercy both unto him and unto us, according to the multitude of Thy tender compassions.

*Ekphonesis:*

> **Priest:** ""
For blessed and glorified is Thy most honorable and majestic Name, of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages.

[Choir: Amen.]

*Second Prayer.*

> **Deacon:** ""
Let us pray to the Lord.

> **Priest:** ""
[Fol. 39r. Decorative woodcut initial V.]
O Master, Lord our God, Who through the font bestowest heavenly illumination upon them that are baptized; Who hast regenerated Thy newly-illumined servant by water and the Spirit,[^145] and hast granted unto him the remission of sins voluntary and involuntary: lay upon him Thy mighty hand, and preserve him by the power of Thy grace; preserve unstolen the pledge of the Spirit; and account him worthy of eternal life, and of pleasing Thee.

*Ekphonesis:*

> **Priest:** ""
For Thou art our sanctification, and unto Thee do we send up glory, to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages.

[Choir: Amen.]

> **Priest:** ""
Peace be unto all.

> **Deacon:** ""
Let us bow our heads unto the Lord.

*The priest says this prayer secretly:*

> **Priest:** ""
[Fol. 39v. Decorative woodcut initial O.]
He that has put on Thee, Christ our God, has bowed his head unto Thee with us; whom do Thou preserve, that he may remain an unconquered champion against them that vainly stir up enmity against him and against us;[^146] and by Thine incorruptible crown, show forth all victors even unto the end.

*Ekphonesis:*

> **Priest:** ""
For Thine it is to show mercy and to save us, O Christ our God, and unto Thee do we send up glory, with Thine unoriginate Father, and Thine All-holy, and good, and life-creating Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages.

[Choir: Amen.]

*And he looses the belt from the child, and the garment which is the papish; and having removed them, he dips their ends into this pure water, and sprinkles the child, saying:*

> **Priest:** ""
Thou hast been justified; thou hast been enlightened; *and the rest.*

*And taking a new sponge saturated with water, he wipes his face and head, and breast, and the rest, saying:*

> **Priest:** ""
Thou hast been baptized; thou hast been enlightened; thou hast been anointed with myron; thou hast been sanctified; thou hast been washed: in the Name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.[^147]

*PRAYER at the Tonsure of the Hair.*

> **Deacon:** ""
Let us pray to the Lord.

> **Priest:** ""
[Fol. 40v. Decorative woodcut initial V.]
O Master, Lord our God, Who didst honor man with Thine image, composing him of a rational soul and a comely body, so that the body might serve the rational soul;[^148] for Thou hast placed the head in the highest position, and in it hast implanted the majority of the senses, not obstructing one another; and with hairs hast Thou covered the head, so that it may not be injured by changes of the winds; and all his members hast Thou planted fittingly, that for all things he might give thanks unto Thee, the excellent Craftsman: do Thou Thyself, O Master, a vessel of Thine election through Paul the Apostle having commanded us to do all things unto Thy glory: bless this Thy servant, *[Name]*, who has come to make a beginning of shearing the hairs of his head, together with his sponsor;[^149] and grant unto them alway to meditate upon Thy commandments, and to do the things well-pleasing unto Thee.

*Ekphonesis:*

> **Priest:** ""
For Thou art a merciful God and the Lover of mankind, and unto Thee do we send up glory, to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages.

[Choir: Amen.]

> **Priest:** ""
Peace be unto all.

> **Deacon:** ""
Let us bow our heads unto the Lord.

*The priest says this prayer secretly:*

> **Priest:** ""
[Fol. 41v. Decorative woodcut initial G.]
O Lord our God, Who through the fullness of the font hast sanctified by Thy grace them that believe in Thee: bless this present infant, and let Thy blessing descend upon his head. And even as Thou didst bless David the king through Samuel Thy prophet, so bless also the head of this Thy servant, *[Name]*, by the hand of me, a sinner, overshadowing him with Thy Holy Spirit; that advancing in stature and unto grey hairs of old age, he may send up glory unto Thee, and see the good things of Jerusalem all the days of his life.[^150]

*Ekphonesis:*

> **Priest:** ""
For unto Thee is due all glory, honor, and worship, to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.

*And he shears him crosswise, saying:*

> **Priest:** ""
The servant of God, *[Name]*, is shorn: in the Name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.[^151]

*After this, he places upon him the koukoulion, that is to say, a small cap [klobuchets], saying:*[^152]

> **Priest:** ""
The servant of God, *[Name]*, is clothed in the koukoulion of innocence: in the Name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.

*Then the litany, in which he commemorates the king, and the sponsor with the newly-illumined one:*[^153]

**Deacon [or Priest]:**
Have mercy on us, O God, according to Thy great mercy, we pray Thee, give ear and have mercy.
Again we pray for our pious king, *[Name]*.
Again we pray for mercy and life of the servant of God, *[Name]*, the sponsor, and of the newly-baptized one.

*Ekphonesis:*

> **Priest:** ""
For Thou art a merciful God and the Lover of mankind, and unto Thee do we send up glory, to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages.

[Choir: Amen.]

*And the dismissal takes place according to custom.*[^154]

# PART VI: THE ORDER OF HOW IT IS BEFITTING TO RECEIVE THOSE WHO COME TO THE HOLY AND CATHOLIC APOSTOLIC CHURCH FROM HERETICS UNTO THE ORTHODOX FAITH [^155]

*For Arians, and Macedonians—that is, adversaries of the Spirit—Sabbatians who call themselves pure, and Quartodecimans, who are called Tetradites, and Apollinarians, we receive when they give a written confession [libellus] and anathematize their own heresy, and every senseless heresy, that they may hold the mind even as the holy Church of God and apostolic [Church].*

*He is brought whensoever he desires [to come unto] the Orthodox faith. And it is befitting for him to fast fourteen days, or [the fast of the] Panagia, and to exercise himself in prayers morning and evening, learning the psalms, as a catechumen. And thus is it befitting that he be accounted worthy of the Orthodox faith.*[^156]

*And the priest places him before the holy font, and says unto him thus: "Say:"*

**Penitent:**
Anathema to *[Name of heresiarch]*, and his teaching, and his accomplices, and those that hold the same mind with him. For I renounce him and every heretical teaching.

And I believe in the Holy and Consubstantial Trinity, according to the exposition of the Holy Fathers, who have rightly set forth the word of truth.

*Then he recites "I believe in one God" unto the end, verse by verse.*

*But if he knows it not, let his sponsor recite it, and let him recite after him.*

*And the priest interrogates him thrice:*

> **Priest:** ""
Believest thou in the Holy and Consubstantial Trinity?

*And he answers:*

**Penitent:**
I believe.

*And the one being baptized [received] bows his head. And the priest prays:*[^157]

> **Priest:** ""
[Fol. 44r. Decorative woodcut initial B.]
O Holy God and our Savior, Who desirest that all men should be saved and come unto the knowledge of the truth: receive this Thy servant, *[Name]*, who has scarcely recovered himself from deception,[^158] and who has loved to come unto the knowledge of the truth. For Thou, O Lord, didst say: "Other sheep I have which are not of this fold; them also I must bring, and they shall hear My voice; and there shall be one fold, and one shepherd."[^159] Shepherd him unto Thy glory, in the true knowledge according to the exposition of Thy holy and glorious Apostles; and account him worthy of the seal of the holy myron, and of communion of the holy Body and Blood. Show forth this Thy servant, *[Name]*, complete, that he also may be numbered among Thy flock, unto the praise and glory of Thy Name.

*Ekphonesis:*

> **Priest:** ""
For Thine is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.

*And he anoints him with myron even as a newly-illumined one, making the same invocation over him.*[^160]

*And again he says a prayer:*

> **Priest:** ""
[Fol. 45r. Decorative woodcut initial G.]
O Lord our God, Who hast accounted worthy to show forth complete this Thy servant, *[Name]*, for the sake of the right-believing faith which is toward Thee, and of the seal of Thy holy myron: do Thou, O Master of all, preserve in him the true faith which is toward Thee; nurture him in righteousness; and adorn him with all Thy gifts. For Thou art our God, and unto Thee do we send up glory, to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. [Amen.]

*And after these things, he communicates him. And he commands him for seven days not to eat meat, and not to wash his face, but even as a newly-baptized one so to abide, and on the eighth day to be washed.*[^161]

[Fol. 45v. Tailpiece: Two mirrored woodcut ornamental floral vignettes.]

*PRAYER TO SIGN A PERSON WHO HAS COME FROM THE HEATHEN TO BE BAPTIZED, AND TO NAME HIM.*[^162]

> **Priest:** ""
[Fol. 45v. Decorative woodcut initial K.]
Unto Thee, O God of all creation visible and invisible, Who didst make all things by the Word: this man is brought, that upon him may be signed the light of Thine Only-begotten Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, and of Thy Holy Spirit. Deliver him, O Lord, from all uncleanness, and from every deception of the adversary, and from every heretical name. Make him a chosen vessel; that this man also may be an equal Christian, known from this day forth, bearing the seal of Christ, Thy true God: with Whom Thou art blessed, together with Thine All-holy, and good, and life-creating Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.[^163]

[Fol. 46r. Tailpiece: Renaissance woodcut floral ornament.]

[Fol. 46v. Headpiece: Woodcut engraving depicting two mythological tritons grasping scrolling acanthus foliage.]

*ARMENIANS TURNING UNTO OUR ORTHODOX FAITH ARE NOT BAPTIZED, BUT ARE ANOINTED WITH MYRON, GIVING A CONFESSION OF THIS MANNER:*[^164]

**Penitent:**
[Fol. 46v. Decorative initial Ya.]
I, *[Name]*, come unto the Orthodox Catholic and Apostolic Church; and I renounce and anathematize every heresy: Armenian, and Chazinzarian, and Jacobite; and their feasts, and their fasts, and food and drink, and all their heresy.[^165]

And I believe in one God...

*And he recites the entire holy symbol, which is: "I believe in one God"*[^166] **Penitent:**
...and one essence indeed of the Holy Trinity do I confess. And in the bodily dispensation of our Lord Jesus Christ, two natures do I confess, of Godhead and of manhood; and the Savior's Passion I declare Him to have suffered in the flesh, and not in the Godhead; for the Godhead is impassible.

I receive also the seven holy Ecumenical Councils; and I anathematize all whom they anathematize:[^167] Simon the first heretic; and Manes; and Marcion, and those with him; and Arius, and Eunomius; Macedonius, and Apollinarius; Paul of Samosata; Sabellius; Theodore; Nestorius; Eutyches; Dioscorus; Theodosius; Timothy;

**Penitent:**
...Julian; Peter the Mongus, and Peter the Fuller, who unite suffering unto the Godhead; Severus the headless, and his disciple Jacob Zanzalus; Cyrus and Marcian; Sergius, and Pyrrhus; and Polychronius the childish elder.[^168] From all these I separate myself purely.

And if I do this with falsehood and deceit, and say in my heart that I will return unto my former heresy: now therefore let all the curses come upon me, and the trembling of Cain, and the leprosy of Gehazi; and in addition may I be liable to the inexorable punishment of the civil law; and in the age to come may I be cast out and accursed. And[^169] **Penitent:**
...may my soul be numbered with Satan and the demons.

Anathema to all heretics! *Thrice.*[^170]

*And the one being renewed bows his head. And the priest says the prayer:*

> **Priest:** ""
[Fol. 48r. Decorative cinnabar initial B.]
O God our Savior, Who willest all men to be saved, and to come unto the knowledge of the truth: receive Thy servant, *[Name]*, who has scarcely recovered himself from deception, and has desired to come unto the knowledge of the truth.[^171] For Thou didst say, O Lord: "Other sheep I have which are not of this fold; them also I must bring, and they shall hear My voice; and there shall be one flock, and one shepherd." Shepherd him in...

> **Priest:** ""
...Thy glory and true understanding, according to the commandment of Thy holy and glorious Apostles. And make him worthy of the seal of the holy myron, and of the communion of the precious Body and Blood; and show forth Thy servant perfect, that he too may be a partaker of Thy flock, unto the praise and glory of Thy majesty.

*Ekphonesis:*

> **Priest:** ""
For Thine is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages.

[Choir: Amen.]

*And after this he anoints him with myron as a newly illumined one, making the same invocation over him.*[^172]

*THEN THE PRAYER.*

> **Priest:** ""
[Fol. 49r. Decorative cinnabar initial G.]
O Lord our God, Who hast deigned to show forth this Thy servant, *[Name]*, perfect, through faith of true belief which is toward Thee, and through the seal of Thy holy myron: do Thou, Master of all, preserve in him the true faith, increase him in righteousness, and adorn him with all Thy gifts. For Thou art our God, and unto Thee do we send up glory, to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages.

[Choir: Amen.]

*And thus he clothes him. And he charges him for seven days not to eat meat, nor to wash his face, but to abide even as a newly baptized person. And on the eighth day he is washed.*[^173]

[Fol. 49v. Headpiece: Monumental Renaissance woodcut engraving with scrolling acanthus strapwork and floral ornamentation.]
