# PART XVI: THE ORDER OF HOLY COMMUNION [^893]

*If a priest, he says:* Blessed is our God...[^894] *If not a priest, the verse:* Through the prayers of our holy fathers, Lord Jesus Christ our God, have mercy on us, amen.[^895] *And after the Amen, we begin:* Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.[^896] *O Heavenly King... Trisagion... After "Our Father...":* For Thine is the kingdom... Lord, have mercy, 12.[^897] *Come, let us worship... 3.*[^898] *Then:* *Psalm 15.*[^899]

Preserve me, O Lord, for in Thee have I hoped.[^900] I said unto the Lord: Thou art my Lord, for of my goods Thou hast no need.[^901] Unto the saints that are in His earth, the Lord hath made marvelous all His desires in them.[^902] Their infirmities were multiplied; after these things they made haste. I will not assemble their assemblies of blood, neither will I make mention of their names with my lips.[^903] The Lord is the portion of mine inheritance and of my cup; Thou art He that restorest mine inheritance unto me.[^904] The lines are fallen unto me among my strongholds; for mine inheritance is strong unto me.[^905] I will bless the Lord Who hath given me understanding; moreover even unto the night my reins have instructed me.[^906]

I beheld the Lord ever before me, for He is at my right hand, that I may not be moved.[^907] Therefore my heart was glad, and my tongue rejoiced; moreover my flesh also shall dwell in hope.[^908] For Thou wilt not leave my soul in Hades, neither wilt Thou suffer Thine Holy One to see corruption.[^909] Thou hast made known to me the ways of life; Thou shalt fill me with joy with Thy countenance; pleasures are in Thy right hand for evermore.[^910]

*Psalm 21:*[^911]

O God, my God, attend unto me; why hast Thou forsaken me?[^912] Far from my salvation are the words of my transgressions.[^913] O my God, I will cry by day, and Thou wilt not hear; and by night, and [it shall] not [be counted] for[^914] folly unto me.[^915] But Thou dwellest in the holy place, O Praise of Israel.[^916] In Thee our fathers hoped; they hoped, and Thou didst deliver them.[^917] Unto Thee they cried, and were saved; in Thee they hoped, and were not put to shame.[^918] But I am a worm, and no man; a reproach of men, and the outcast of the people.[^919] All they that saw me laughed me to scorn; they spoke with their lips, they shook the head:[^920] He hoped in the Lord, let Him deliver him; let Him save him, for He desires him.[^921] For Thou art He that drewest me forth from the womb, my hope from my mother's breasts.[^922] Unto Thee was I cast from the womb; from my mother's belly Thou art my God.[^923]

Depart not from Me, for affliction is near; for there is none to help Me.[^924] Many bullocks have compassed Me; fat bulls have beset Me round. They have opened their mouth against Me, as a ravening and a roaring lion. I am poured out like water, and all My bones are scattered.[^925] My heart is become like wax, melting in the midst of My belly. My strength is dried up like a potsherd, and My tongue cleaves to My throat; and Thou hast brought Me down into the dust of death. For many dogs have compassed Me; the assembly of the wicked hath beset Me round.[^926] They have pierced My hands and My feet; they have numbered all My bones.

My bones; they looked and stared upon Me. They parted My garments among them, and upon My vesture did they cast lots.[^927] But Thou, O Lord, remove not Thy help far from Me; attend unto My defense. Deliver My soul from the sword, and Mine only-begotten from the hand of the dog. Save Me from the mouth of the lion, and My lowliness from the horns of the unicorns.[^928] I will declare Thy name unto My brethren; in the midst of the church will I sing praise unto Thee. Ye that fear the Lord, praise Him; all ye seed of Jacob, glorify Him; let all the seed of Israel fear Him.[^929] For He hath not despised nor abhorred the prayer of the poor; neither hath He turned away His face from Me; but when I cried unto Him, He gave ear unto Me.[^930] From Thee is My praise; in the great church will I confess unto Thee; My vows will I pay before them that fear Him. The poor shall eat and be satisfied, and they that seek the Lord shall praise Him; their heart shall live unto ages of ages.[^931] All the ends of the earth shall remember and turn unto the Lord; and all the kindreds of the nations shall worship before Him. For the kingdom is the Lord's, and He is the ruler over the nations. All the fat ones of the earth have eaten and worshipped; all they that go down into the earth shall fall down before Him.[^932] And My soul unto Him shall live, and My seed shall serve Him.[^933] The generation to come shall be declared unto the Lord; and they shall declare His righteousness unto a people that shall be born, whom the Lord hath made.

*Psalm 22.*[^934]

The Lord is my shepherd, and nothing shall be lacking unto me.[^935] In a place of green pasture, there hath He made me to dwell; by the water of rest hath He nourished me. He hath converted my soul; He hath guided me into the paths of righteousness for His name's sake. For though I should walk through the midst of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for Thou art with me; Thy rod and Thy staff, they have comforted me.[^936] Thou hast prepared a table before me against them that afflict me.[^937] Thou hast anointed my head with oil, and Thy cup which inebriates me, how excellent it is! And Thy mercy shall pursue me all the days of my life, and that I may dwell in the house of the Lord unto length of days.

*Psalm 23.*[^938]

The earth is the Lord's, and the fullness thereof; the world, and all that dwell therein.[^939] He hath founded it upon the seas, and prepared it upon the rivers. Who shall ascend into the mountain of the Lord, or who shall stand in His holy place? He that is innocent in hands and pure in heart; who hath not received his soul in vain, nor sworn deceitfully unto his neighbor. He shall receive a blessing from the Lord, and mercy from God his Savior.[^940] This is the generation of them that seek the Lord, that seek the face of the God of Jacob. Lift up your gates, O ye princes, and be ye lifted up, ye everlasting gates; and the King of glory shall enter in.[^941] Who is this King of glory? The Lord strong and mighty, the Lord mighty in battle. Lift up your gates, O ye princes, and be ye lifted up, ye everlasting gates; and the King of glory shall enter in. Who is this King of glory? The Lord of hosts, He is the King of glory.

*Psalm 115.*[^942]

I believed, therefore have I spoken; but I was humbled exceedingly.[^943] I said in mine ecstasy: Every man is a liar. What shall I render unto the Lord for all that He hath rendered unto me?[^944] I will take the cup of salvation, and will call upon the name of the Lord. My vows will I pay unto the Lord in the presence of all His people. Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of His saints.[^945] O Lord, I am Thy servant; I am Thy servant and the son of Thine handmaid; Thou hast broken my bonds asunder. To Thee will I offer the sacrifice of praise, and will call upon the name of the Lord. My vows will I pay unto the Lord in the presence of all His people, in the courts of the Lord's house, in the midst of thee, O Jerusalem.

*Glory... Both now...*

*Alleluia, thrice. And these Troparia, Tone 8:*[^946]

Overlook mine iniquities, O Lord Who wast born of the Virgin, and cleanse my heart, making it a temple for Thine all-pure[^947] Body and Blood; neither cast Thou me away from Thy presence, O Thou Who without measure hast great mercy.[^948]

*Glory...*[^949]

Into the communion of Thy holy things how shall I, the wretched one, dare to enter?[^950] For if I dare to approach Thee with the worthy, my garment convicts me, for it is not a wedding garment, and condemnation do I procure for my most sinful soul. Cleanse, O Lord, the defilement of my soul, and save me, as Thou art the Lover of mankind.

*Both now...*[^951]

Great is the multitude of my transgressions, O Theotokos;[^952] unto thee have I fled, O all-pure one, requiring salvation. Visit my ailing soul, and pray unto thy Son and our God, that He grant unto me remission of the evils which I have done, O only blessed one.[^953]

*Then Psalm 50.*[^954]

*Have mercy on me, O God. Canon for Holy Communion. Tone 2. Ode 1. Heirmos:*[^955]

*Come, ye peoples.*

*Verse:* Create in me a clean heart, O God; and renew a right spirit within me.[^956]

May Thy holy Body and precious Blood, O compassionate Lord, be unto me the Bread of eternal life, and healing of manifold infirmities.[^957]

*Verse:* Cast me not away from Thy presence, and take not Thy Holy Spirit from me.[^958]

Vouchsafe me, an unworthy one, O Master, to receive and eat with longing Thine all-pure Blood and Thy most holy Body,[^959] and with faith to drink.[^960]

*Glory...*[^961]

Defiled by improper deeds, wretched that I am, and unworthy of the communion of Thine all-pure Body and divine Blood, do Thou, O Christ, make me worthy thereof.[^962]

*Both now...*[^963]

O good and blessed Bride of God, who hast brought forth the unplowed Ear of grain that is salvation to the world: vouchsafe that I, eating thereof, may be saved.[^964]

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*

*Establish me upon the rock of faith.*[^965]

*Verse:* Create in me a clean heart, O God; and renew a right spirit within me.

Grant me drops of tears, O Christ, purifying the defilement of my heart,[^966] that being cleansed with a good conscience, I may come in faith and fear, O Master, unto the communion of Thy Gifts.[^967]

*Verse:* Cast me not away from Thy presence, and [take not Thy Holy Spirit from me].[^968]

May Thy most pure Body and divine Blood be unto me for the remission of sins, O Lover of mankind, and for communion of the Holy Spirit, and unto life eternal, and for estrangement from passions and afflictions.[^969]

*Glory...*[^970]

Vouchsafe us, O Lord, to partake without condemnation of Thy Body and of Thy precious Blood, and to hymn Thy goodness.[^971]

*Both now...*[^972]

O most pure table of the Bread of life that came down from on high for mercy's sake, and gives new life unto the world: vouchsafe even me now, unworthy though I am,[^973] to taste thereof with fear, and to live.[^974]

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 2:*

May the reception of Thine all-pure and life-creating Mysteries be fire and light unto me, O Savior, consuming the tares of sins, and enlightening all of me unto true theology; not betraying the Holy Things to enemies in fierce surrender, nor will I give Thee a deceitful kiss; but like the harlot I fall down before Thee, and like the thief confessing I cry unto Thee: Remember me, O Lord, when Thou comest into Thy kingdom.[^975]

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*

*Having come from the Virgin.*[^976]

*Verse:* Create in me a clean heart, O God; [and renew a right spirit within me].[^977]

Thou wast pleased for our sake, having become incarnate,[^978] O most merciful One, to be slain as a sheep for the sins of men; therefore I pray Thee to wash away also my transgressions.[^979]

*Verse:* Cast me not away from Thy presence, [and take not Thy Holy Spirit from me].[^980]

Heal the wounds of my soul, O Lord, and sanctify all of me; and vouchsafe, O Master, that I, wretched though I am, may be a partaker of Thy mystical and divine Supper.[^981]

*Glory...*[^982]

Let us all stand with fear and trembling, having the eyes of our heart directed on high, and crying unto the Savior: Establish and give understanding unto us in Thy fear, O merciful God.[^983]

*Both now...*[^984]

Make Thy compassionate Son merciful also unto me, O Sovereign Lady, and preserve me, thy servant, without sorrow and without[^985] blemish, that having received within me the spiritual Pearl, I may be sanctified.[^986]

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*

*O Giver of light.*[^987]

*Verse:* Create in me a clean heart, O God; and [renew a right spirit within me].[^988]

As Thou hast foretold, O Christ, so let it be unto Thy humble servant, and abide in me as Thou didst promise; for behold, I eat Thy divine Body and drink Thy Blood.[^989]

*Verse:* Cast me not away from Thy presence, [and take not Thy Holy Spirit from me].[^990]

O Word of God and God, may Thy divine Body be a live coal unto me, for the enlightenment of me who am darkened, and Thy Blood for the cleansing of my defiled soul.[^991]

*Glory...*[^992]

Having an all-defiled soul and unclean lips, I dare not now draw near unto Thee,[^993] O Christ, and receive Thy Body; but do Thou show me worthy.[^994]

*Both now...*[^995]

O Mary, Mother of God, venerable dwelling of sweet fragrance: by thy prayers make me a chosen vessel, that I may partake of the holy Mysteries of thy Son.[^996]

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*

*In the abyss of sins.*[^997]

*Verse:* Create in me a clean heart, O God; and [renew a right spirit within me].[^998]

Sanctify my mind, soul, and heart, O Savior, and my body; and vouchsafe, O Master, that I may approach Thine awesome Mysteries without condemnation.[^999]

*Verse:* Cast me not away from Thy presence, [and take not Thy Holy Spirit from me].[^1000]

May I be estranged from passions, and be vouchsafed an increase of Thy grace, and the confirmation of life, by reason of the communion[^1001] of Thy holy Mysteries, O Christ.[^1002]

*Glory...*[^1003]

With fear and trembling let us all approach, and receive the holy Body of Christ, and His holy and precious Blood.[^1004]

*Both now...*[^1005]

O God, holy Word of God, sanctify all of me now as I come unto Thy divine Mysteries, by the supplications of thy holy Mother.[^1006]

*Kontakion, Tone 2, Podoben: "Seeking the highest" (Вы́шнихъ и҆ща̀):*

Despise me not, O Christ, as I take the Bread, which is Thy Body, and Thy divine Blood, and partake, wretched as I am, of Thine all-pure and dread Mysteries, O Master; let it not be unto me, wretched though I am, for judgment, but let it be unto me for life eternal and immortal.[^1007]

*Ode 7.*[^1008]

*Heirmos: Unto the golden image.*[^1009]

*Verse:* Create in me a clean heart, O God; and [renew a right spirit within me].[^1010]

May the communion of Thine immortal Mysteries now be unto me a fountain of good things, O Christ: light, and life, and impassibility, and leading unto advancement and increase in divine virtue, O Thou only Good One, that I may glorify Thee.[^1011]

*Verse:* Cast me not away from Thy presence, [and take not Thy Holy Spirit from me].[^1012]

Delivered from passions, and enemies, and necessity, and every affliction, as I now draw near with trembling and love, with reverence, O Lover of mankind, unto Thine immortal and divine Mysteries, may I sing unto Thee: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers.[^1013]

*Glory*[^1014] O my wretched soul, O my passionate soul, be dismayed beholding the most glorious Mysteries; sighing, weep, beating thy breast and saying: O God, cleanse me even as the prodigal.[^1015]

*Both now...*[^1016]

O Lady graced of God, who beyond understanding didst bear Christ the Savior: I, thine unclean servant, now entreat thee, who art pure: as I now desire to approach the most pure Mysteries, cleanse all of me from defilement of flesh and spirit.[^1017]

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*

*He who into the fiery furnace.*[^1018]

*Verse:* Create in me a clean heart, O God; and [renew a right spirit within me].[^1019]

Of Thy heavenly, dread, and holy Mysteries, O Christ, and of Thy divine and mystical Supper, a partaker[^1020] vouchsafe me to be, despondent though I am, O God my Savior.[^1021]

*Verse:* Cast me not away from Thy presence, [and take not Thy Holy Spirit from me].[^1022]

Fleeing unto Thy compassion, O Good One, with fear I cry unto Thee: Abide in me, O Savior, and I, even as Thou hast said, in Thee; for behold, trusting in Thy mercy, I eat Thy Body and drink Thy Blood.[^1023]

*Glory...*[^1024]

I tremble as I receive the Fire, lest I be burned up like wax and like grass! O dread Mysteries! O compassion of God! How do I, being clay, partake of the divine Body and Blood, and am made incorruptible![^1025]

*Both now...*[^1026]

The divine Bread of life was truly baked in thy womb, O Mother of God,[^1027] preserving unharmed thine undefiled belly; therefore, as our nourisher, we hymn thee unto all ages.[^1028]

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*

*The Son of the unoriginate Father.*[^1029]

*Verse:* Create in me a clean heart, O God; and [renew a right spirit within me].[^1030]

Christ is here; taste and see the Lord: for having of old become like us for our sake, and having once offered Himself as a sacrifice unto His Father, He is ever slain, sanctifying them that partake.[^1031]

*Verse:* Cast me not away from Thy presence, and take not Thy Holy Spirit from me.[^1032]

May I be sanctified in soul with body, O Master; may I be enlightened, may I be saved; may I become Thy dwelling by the communion of the sacred Mysteries, having Thee dwelling within me with the Father and the Spirit,[^1033] O most merciful Benefactor.[^1034]

*Glory...*

May Thy Body and Thy most precious Blood, O my Savior, be unto me as fire and as light, consuming the substance of sin, and burning up the thorns of passions, and enlightening all of me who worship Thy Divinity.[^1035]

*Both now...*

God was incarnate of thy pure blood; whence every generation hymns thee, O Sovereign Lady, and the bodiless multitudes glorify thee, as having through thee clearly beheld the Sovereign of all, substantialized in humanity.[^1036]

*Then: It is truly meet... Trisagion. And after Our Father... Troparion, Tone 8:*[^1037]

When the glorious disciples at the washing of the supper were illuminated, then was Judas the ungodly, diseased with the love of silver, darkened; and unto lawless judges he betrayed Thee, the righteous Judge.[^1038] Behold, O lover of possessions, him who on account of them acquired insatiability, and gave himself unto hanging![^1039] Flee, O insatiable soul, that dared such things against the Teacher! O Lord Who art good towards all, glory unto Thee!

*Lord, have mercy (40), and twelve prostrations, or unto each according to his strength. After this, all the prayers in order:*[^1040]

*Prayer of Basil the Great unto Holy Communion:*

O Master, Lord Jesus Christ our God, King of them that reign, and Lord of them that rule;[^1041] Fountain of life and immortality; Maker of all creation, visible and invisible; co-eternal and co-unoriginate Son of the unoriginate Father; Who for Thine exceeding goodness in the last days didst clothe Thyself in flesh, and wast crucified, and buried for us ungrateful and perverse ones,[^1042] and by Thine own Blood didst renew our nature corrupted by sin: Thyself, O immortal King, Master, Lover of mankind, accept my sinful repentance; incline Thine ear unto me, and hear my words.[^1043]

For I have sinned, O Lord, I have sinned against heaven and before Thee,[^1044] and I am not worthy to gaze upon the height of Thy glory; for I have provoked Thy goodness, having transgressed Thy commandments, and not having given ear unto Thy precepts. But Thou, O Lord, being forgiving, longsuffering, and plenteous in mercy, hast not given me over to perish with mine iniquities, awaiting my conversion by every means. For Thou, O Lover of mankind, hast said by Thy prophet: *As I live, says the Lord, I desire not the death of the sinner, but rather that he turn and live.*[^1045] For Thou willest not, O Master, to destroy the creation of Thy hands, nor dost Thou take pleasure in the perdition of mankind, but Thou willest that all should be saved, and come unto the knowledge of the truth.[^1046] Therefore I also, though I am unworthy of heaven and of earth, and of this fleeting life, having wholly subjected myself unto sin, and enslaved myself unto pleasures, and defiled Thine image; yet being Thy creature and Thy creation, I, wretched one, despair not of my salvation. But trusting in Thine immeasurable compassion, I draw near. Receive therefore even me, O Lord, Lover of mankind, as the harlot, as the thief, as the publican, and as the prodigal;[^1047] and take away my heavy burden of iniquities, Thou Who takest away the sins of the world,[^1048] and healest the infirmities of men; Who callest unto Thyself the weary and heavy laden, and givest them rest; Who camest not to call the righteous, but sinners unto repentance:[^1049] cleanse Thou me from all defilement of flesh and spirit; and teach me to accomplish holiness in Thy fear;[^1050] that in the pure testimony of my conscience, receiving a portion of Thy Holy Things, I may be united unto Thy holy Body and Blood, and may have Thee living and abiding in me with the Father and with the Holy Spirit. Yea, O Lord Jesus Christ my God, let not the communion of Thine all-pure and life-creating Mysteries be unto me for judgment, nor may I become weak in soul and body from partaking thereof unworthily; but grant me unto my last breath to receive without condemnation the portion of Thy Holy Things, for communion of the Holy Spirit, for provision on the way unto eternal life,[^1051] and for an acceptable defense at Thy dread judgment-seat; that I also, with all Thine elect, may be a partaker of Thine incorruptible and eternal good things, which Thou hast prepared for them that love Thee, O Lord, in which Thou art glorified unto ages of ages. Amen.[^1052]

*Of the same Basil the Great:*[^1053]

*Prayer unto Holy Communion:*

O Master, Lord our God, only-begotten Son and Word of the living and immortal Father, Who didst give Thyself as a sacrifice for us, for whose sake Thou didst become man, that Thou mightest show us conformed unto Thine image, and unite us unto Thyself by communion of Thy life-creating Mysteries:[^1054] I will extol Thee, for Thou hast lifted me up, and hast not made my foes to rejoice over me; but Thou hast brought up my soul from hades, and hast saved me from them that go down into the pit.[^1055] And now incline Thine ear unto me, and hear my words, and make me, unworthy though I am, a partaker, even as of Thine image, so also of Thy most pure Flesh and of Thy very precious Blood: for the remission of sins, for the forgiveness of transgressions, for communion of the Holy Spirit;[^1056] overlooking for me, for the riches of Thy goodness, all sins voluntary and involuntary, both those committed with my knowledge and those in ignorance. For though I am unworthy of heaven and of earth, yet I am Thy creature, and the work of Thine all-pure hands, even if by transgression of Thy commandments I have corrupted Thine image. Overlook my sins, O Thou Who alone takest away the sins of the world, and art the sinless Lord; for against Thee only have I sinned, and before Thee do I fall down, my good God.[^1057]

Even though by my evil deeds I continually provoke Thee to anger, abhor me not who am unclean in heart, defiled in lips, passionate in soul; but trusting in Thy mercy and drawing near, receive me as the harlot, and as the thief, and as the publican; and forgive me the multitude of my many evil deeds, as having authority to remit sins unto them that sin, for the sake of the communion of Thine all-pure Mysteries.[^1058] And as the coal of Thy holy Body burns up the passionate motions of the soul, cleanse my heart, as once the lips of Thy prophet, for the sake of Thine awesome[^1059] seraph:[^1060] enlighten also my thoughts with the light of Thy gladness, and fill me wholly with holiness, for Thou art holy by nature. And by communion of Thy Blood, fill my heart with gladness, and my mind with Thy rejoicing. Mortify all my bodily members through communion of Thy holy Mysteries; and free [me] from every carnal desire by the descent of Thy Holy Spirit.[^1061] Yea, O God, Who comest and makest Thine abode with the Father and with Thy Holy Spirit in all Thy saints;[^1062] Who hast deigned to be received by me, a sinner and unworthy one, in the bloodless sacrifice offered unto Thee, for the sake of Thine immeasurable goodness: do Thou abide in me acceptably[^1063] and inseparably unto the end of my life; and be Thou unto me an addition of life, against the destroyer; a light unto the revelation of Thy hidden mysteries; a guide unto the path of Thy commandments; unto the Heavenly Kingdom, unto eternal gladness; unto the fulfillment of wisdom; unto the completion of the word; unto the contemplation of Thy sayings; a revealer of mysteries of divine and noble things; strength against warring spirits; and the supreme quencher of every desire in me.[^1064] Yea, O God consubstantial with the Father, and Word of God unto us: be Thou all things unto me, Thy servant; and for the sake of the communion of Thy divine Gifts, unite Thyself unto me in one spirit, according to the prayer unto Thy Father and God on behalf of us unworthy ones:[^1065] for I am flesh of Thy flesh, and bearing Thee from divine Baptism,[^1066] even if I have defiled Thy garment.[^1067] For Thou art He that said: *He that eats My Flesh, and drinks My Blood, dwells in Me, and I in him.*[^1068] And Thine is the glory unto ages of ages. Amen.

*Prayer of the same Basil the Great, unto Holy Communion:*[^1069]

O holy, all-pure, undefiled Master, Who through Thy great mercy didst not disdain to receive without sin and without defilement our nature, which had become subject to passions through sin; and having cleansed it with Thy holy Blood, poured out for the sake of our salvation, the creation of Thy holy hands;[^1070] Who didst accomplish Thine ineffable dispensation, not for the sake of them that have not sinned against Thee, nor of them that have been well-pleasing unto Thee, but for the sake of them that provoked Thee to anger and turned away:[^1071] Who art the hope of salvation unto them that for their sins have despaired of all hope;[^1072] for Thou Thyself, O good One, hast said: *They that are whole need not a physician, but they that are sick;*[^1073] and: *Thou camest not to save them that are saved, but the lost.*[^1074] Do Thou therefore, O compassionate One, receive in Thy tender mercy also me, unworthy though I am, who trust in Thy compassions, and have dared to draw near unto Thy most pure Body and Blood; and endure to accept my unworthiness as a partaker of Thy dread Mysteries;[^1075] and abhor me not, neither be wroth, nor set me forth as guilty; seeing that I am sinful and unclean, and draw near unworthily.[^1076] But, O gracious Lord,[^1077] Who hast given unto us sinners Thy Body and Blood for the remission of sins: grant unto me, through the communion thereof, of Thine indwelling in me, Thine unprofitable servant, and of my abiding in Thee, my good Master and Savior. And make the communion of these things to be unto me for the lightening of the unspeakable burdens of mine iniquities, for deliverance from guilt, for the cleansing of soul and body;[^1078] for on behalf of sinners, condemned and without defense, hast Thou poured out Thy divine and life-flowing Blood by Thy great mercy:[^1079] which vouchsafe me to drink without condemnation, and to eat Thy life-creating Body. And let not communion be unto me for judgment, who eat and drink unworthily, O Lover of mankind, nor unto a heavier reckoning, instead of obtaining remission of my evil deeds.[^1080] For Thou knowest, Who knowest all things, that not presumptuously, nor as one uncondemned, or as being worthy, do I draw near with boldness; but with fear and trembling,[^1081] with quaking of heart, and of the bones and very marrow;[^1082] for I know myself self-condemned, and unworthy even to look with mine eyes upon Thy dread table.[^1083] Yet because of that whereby Thou hast shown unto sinners Thine ineffable mercy, through the fraction of Thy holy Body and the pouring out of Thy precious Blood: I desire to be nourished with Thy soul-nourishing food, O Christ our God; and I cast myself daringly into the abyss of Thy mercy.[^1084] Gazing upon Thy worshipful and incorruptible Mysteries, which Thou didst receive in Thy love for mankind for the remission of our sins, I am held by fear and joy: by the one indeed because of mine unworthiness, and by the other because of the hope of forgiveness for my sins.[^1085] Behold therefore, O Lord, my lowliness;[^1086] and grant me without guilt and without condemnation to receive Thy divine and deifying Mysteries: for cleansing, for salvation, for remission of my sins; for fleeing the punishment to come, and for obtaining glory; and for the reception of the things prepared for them that love Thee, and that live and abide in Thee:[^1087] by the intercession of Thine all-glorified and all-pure Mother, and of all the saints. Amen.

*Prayer of our father among the saints, John Chrysostom, unto Holy Communion:*[^1088]

Lord, I know that I am not worthy, nor sufficient, that Thou shouldest enter under the roof of the house of my soul, because it is all deserted and fallen;[^1089] and Thou hast not in me a worthy place where to lay Thy head.[^1090] But even as from the height Thou didst humble Thyself for our sake, so humble Thyself now also unto my lowliness.[^1091] And as Thou didst deign to lie in a cave and in a manger of brute beasts,[^1092] so receive [me], and enter into the manger of my unreasoning soul, and into my defiled body.[^1093] And even as Thou didst not disdain to enter and sup with sinners in the house of Simon the leper,[^1094] so deign to enter also into the temple of my humble soul, leprous and sinful.[^1095] And as Thou didst not thrust away the sinful harlot like unto me, who came and touched Thee,[^1096] so have compassion also upon me, a sinner, who come and touch Thee; and even as Thou didst not abhor her defiled and unclean lips that kissed Thee,[^1097] so also of mine lips, abhor not [lips] even more defiled and more unclean than hers;[^1098] nor my darkened and unclean and polluted lips, and my unclean tongue. But may the coal of Thy most pure Body, and of Thy precious Blood, be unto me for sanctification, and enlightenment, and health unto my humble soul and body;[^1099] for lightening the weight of my many transgressions; for preservation from all diabolical operations; for the overcoming and restraint of my evil and wicked habits; for the mortification of passions; for the keeping of Thy commandments; for the addition of Thy divine[^1100] grace, and adoption into Thy Kingdom. For not as one who despises do I draw near unto Thee, O Christ God, but as trusting in Thine ineffable goodness: that I be not, through being long removed from Thy communion, devoured by the noetic wolf.[^1101] Therefore I entreat Thee, as Thou alone art holy Master: sanctify my soul and body, mind and heart, reins and inward parts; and renew me wholly, and root Thy fear in my members; and make Thy sanctification irremovable from me.[^1102] And be Thou unto me a helper and protector, steering my life in peace, and vouchsafing me to stand at Thy right hand,[^1103] by the prayers and supplication of Thine all-pure Mother, and of Thy bodiless ministers and most pure powers, and of all the saints who from the ages have been well-pleasing unto Thee. Amen.[^1104]

*Prayer of the same Saint John Chrysostom, unto Holy Communion:*[^1105]

O Master, Lover of mankind, Lord Jesus Christ my God: trusting in Thy compassions, I entreat Thee, that Thou place me not on Thy left hand with the goats that have provoked Thee to anger;[^1106] neither say unto me: *Amen, I say unto thee, I know thee not.*[^1107] But grant me according to Thy goodness weeping ever, and compunction, and humility unto my heart; and cleanse it with Thy fear; and[^1108] through communion of Thy most pure and life-creating Mysteries, that it may be a temple of Thy goodness.[^1109] For I am exceedingly sinful and unworthy, yet ever do I knock at Thy doors; even if I am despondent and slothful, and negligent concerning my salvation, yet nevertheless I walk in Thy path.[^1110] Save me for the sake of Thy mercy: for Thou art blessed, O Lord, by all things; Thy compassions are upon all Thy works; and Thine is the dominion unto the ages. Amen.[^1111]

*Prayer of the same most holy John Chrysostom, unto Holy Communion:*[^1112]

O Master, Lord Jesus Christ our God, Who alone hast authority to remit[^1113] sins:[^1114] as Thou art good and the Lover of mankind, overlook my transgressions committed in knowledge and in ignorance; and vouchsafe me without condemnation to partake of Thy divine, all-glorious, most pure, and life-creating Mysteries: not unto heaviness, nor unto punishment, nor unto the addition of sins; but unto cleansing, and sanctification, and for the betrothal of the life and Kingdom to come;[^1115] for a wall and help; for the repelling of adversaries; for the destruction of my many transgressions.[^1116] For Thou art the God of mercies, and the Giver of compassions, and of love for mankind; and unto Thee do we send up glory, with the Father, and the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.[^1117]

*Prayer of the same Saint John Chrysostom, unto Holy Communion:*[^1118]

I know, O Lord, that unworthily do I partake of Thy most pure Body and of Thy precious Blood, and am guilty; and eat and drink judgment unto myself, not discerning the Body and Blood of Christ and my God.[^1119] But trusting in Thy compassions, I draw near unto Thee, Who hast said: *He that eats My Flesh, and drinks My Blood, dwells in Me, and I in him.*[^1120] Have compassion therefore upon me, O Lord, and reprove me not, a sinner, but deal with me according to Thy mercy;[^1121] and may these holy things be unto me for enlightenment, and unto salvation, and unto healing, and preservation, and cleansing, and sanctification of soul and body;[^1122] for the driving away of every fantasy, and wicked deed, and diabolical operation working mentally in my members;[^1123] unto boldness and love toward Thee; for the amendment of life and steadfastness; unto the increase of virtue and perfection; for the fulfillment of the commandments; for communion of the Holy Spirit; for the viaticum of eternal life; for an acceptable defense at Thy dread judgment-seat; not unto judgment or unto condemnation.[^1124]

*Prayer of the same Hierarch John Chrysostom, unto Holy Communion:*[^1125]

O God, remit, pardon, have compassion, forgive me my transgressions, whereinsoever I have sinned against Thee: whether by word, or deed, or thought; willingly, or unwillingly; in knowledge, or in ignorance: forgive me all things, as Thou art good and the Lover of mankind;[^1126] by the prayers of Thine all-pure Mother, of Thy noetic ministers and holy powers, and of all the saints who from the ages have been well-pleasing unto Thee.[^1127] Vouchsafe me without condemnation to receive Thy holy and most pure Body and precious Blood, unto the healing of both soul and body, and unto the cleansing of my wicked thoughts.[^1128] For Thine is the Kingdom, and the power, and the glory, of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.[^1129]

*Prayer of the same Saint John Chrysostom, unto Holy Communion:*[^1130]

I believe, O Lord, and I confess, that Thou art truly the Christ, the Son of the living God, Who camest into the world to save sinners, of whom I am first.[^1131] I believe also that this is truly Thine own most pure Body, and this is truly Thine own precious Blood.[^1132] Therefore I pray Thee: have mercy upon me and forgive me, and pardon my transgressions, voluntary and involuntary, whether in word or deed, whether in knowledge or ignorance, whether in mind or thought; and vouchsafe me without condemnation to partake of Thy most pure Mysteries,[^1133] unto the remission of sins, and unto life everlasting. For blessed art Thou unto the ages. Amen.[^1134]

*Prayer of the same Saint John Chrysostom, unto Holy Communion:*[^1135]

O Master, Lord, Lover of mankind: let not the communion of Thy holy Mysteries be unto me for condemnation, but unto the cleansing and sanctification of both soul and body, and for the attainment of the life to come and of the Kingdom. For blessed art Thou unto the ages. Amen.[^1136]

*Prayer of our holy and God-bearing father John of Damascus, as after the manner of them that confess, unto Holy Communion:*[^1137]

As sitting upon Thy dread and unbribable throne, O Christ God, guilty of condemnation and subject to examination, and giving an account of the evils wrought by me:[^1138] even so today, before the day of my condemnation is come, I stand before Thee, and before Thy dread and holy angels, bowed down by my conscience, bringing forward my evil, polluted, and lawless deeds;[^1139] exposing and reproving them, I humble myself. Look therefore, O Lord, upon my humility, and remit all my transgressions; look, for my iniquities are multiplied more than the hairs of my head.[^1140]

What evil therefore have I not committed? What transgression have I not wrought? What evil have I not imagined in my soul? Nay, already in deeds also have I committed them:[^1141] fornication, adultery, sodomy, presumption, pride, reproach, debauchery,[^1142] insolence, disobedience, slander, falsehood, evil-speaking, belittling, perjury, calumny, swearing of oaths, blasphemy, idle talking, inflamed passion, mockery, drunkenness, gluttony, belly-madness, hatred, envy, love of money, avarice, usury, vainglory, covetousness of possessions, self-love, extortion, unrighteousness, filthy lucre,[^1143] greed of gain, jealousy, defaming, lawlessness, disobedience, polluted thoughts, and unclean and enervated imaginings, blasphemous also and unspeakable; all my senses and every member have I defiled, corrupted, mired in filth, and made unprofitable;[^1144] I have become in every way a worker for the devil. I know, O Lord, that mine iniquities are gone over my head;[^1145] but measureless is the multitude of Thy compassions, and ineffable the mercy of Thine ungrudging goodness, and there is no sin that can overcome Thy love for mankind.[^1146] Therefore, O most marvelous King, unresentful Lord: make marvelous Thy mercies upon me also, a sinner;[^1147]

show forth the power of Thy goodness, and manifest the strength of the tender-hearted compassion of Thy mercy, and receive me, a sinner returning to Thee. Receive me, even as Thou didst receive the prodigal, the publican, the thief, Manasseh, and the harlot;[^1148] receive me who have transgressed beyond measure, in word, and in deed, and in thought, and by improper lust, and by unreasoning desire; and even as Thou didst receive those that came at the eleventh hour, who had wrought nothing worthy:[^1149] so receive me also, a sinner. For greatly have I sinned, and greatly have I committed iniquity, and become defiled;[^1150] greatly have I provoked Thy Holy Spirit to wrath, and have bitterly grieved the compassionate bowels of Thy love for mankind, both by word, and deed, and thought, by night and by day, willingly and unwillingly, manifestly and secretly.[^1151] And I know that openly Thou wilt set all my sins before me, even such as they were wrought by me; and Thou wilt require an account of me, concerning those things wherein knowingly and in ignorance I have boundlessly transgressed.[^1152] But O Lord, Lord, do not by Thy righteous judgment, nor in Thine indignation rebuke me, neither in Thy wrath chasten me! Have mercy upon me, O Lord, for not only am I weak, but also I am Thine own creation.[^1153]

Thou hast set Thy hand heavily upon me; yet I have done evil before Thee, and against Thee only have I sinned. Enter not into judgment with Thy servant;[^1154] for if Thou shalt enter into judgment with Thy servant, and if Thou shalt mark iniquities, O Lord; O Lord, who shall stand?[^1155] For I am an abyss of transgressions, and I am not worthy, neither able to look up and behold the height of heaven, by reason of the multitude of my sins, whereof there is no number.[^1156] For every evil deed, and device, and subtlety of Satan, and craftiness; corruptions, and divers emissions, effeminacies, masturbations, defilements of youth,[^1157] incests, scorns, remembrance of wrongs, evil counsel unto sin, perjuries, wanton assaults, titillations;[^1158] and other boundless passions have I committed, and they have not departed from me. By what evils was I not held fast? By what transgressions was I not corrupted? Every sin have I committed, every sin have I cast into my soul; unprofitable have I become unto God and unto men.[^1159] And who shall raise me up, that am fallen into so many wicked transgressions? O Lord my God, in Thee have I put my trust: if there be any hope of salvation for me; if Thy love for mankind shall prevail over the multitude of mine iniquities:[^1160]

be Thou unto me a savior and protector; and according to the multitude of Thy compassions, and Thy mercy: remit, pardon, and forgive me whatsoever I have sinned against Thee.[^1161] For with many evils is my soul filled, and there is in me no hope of salvation. Have mercy upon me, O God, have mercy upon me according to Thy great mercy;[^1162] and render not unto me according to my works, neither put me to shame according to my deeds; but turning again, save and deliver my soul from the evils growing together with her, and from grievous assaults.[^1163] Save me, O Lord, for Thy mercy's sake: that where sin hath abounded, Thy grace may much more abound.[^1164] And I will praise and glorify Thee always, all the days of my life; for Thou, O God, art the God of them that repent, and unto Thee do we send up glory: to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.[^1165]

*Prayer of the same Saint John of Damascus, unto Holy Communion:*[^1166]

Wounded in heart am I, and Thy zeal hath melted me away, and Thy love hath transformed me, O Master; bound am I with desire for Thee:[^1167] that I may be filled with Thy Flesh, that I may be satisfied with Thy life-creating and deifying Blood, that I may receive of Thy good things, that I may be nourished with Thy Godhead,[^1168] that I may be worthy when Thou comest to meet Thee with glory in the airy catching up in the clouds, with all Thine elect:[^1169] that I may sing and worship, and glorify Thee thankfully in confession, with Thine unoriginate Father, and Thy most holy, and good, and life-creating Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.[^1170]

*Prayer of the same Saint John of Damascus, unto Holy Communion:*[^1171]

Looking upon the multitude of Thy compassions, and the abyss of Thy love for mankind, O Christ God: lo, now have I dared to draw near, having desire to partake of Thy holy and[^1172] life-creating Mysteries; held fast by fear and dread, I fear to touch them because of the multitude of my sins, lest instead of enlightenment I be burned up.[^1173] Therefore I pray Thee and fall down before Thee, O all-good and marvelous King: forgive my transgressions, voluntary and involuntary; and vouchsafe me without condemnation to receive Thine all-pure Body and Thy precious Blood, unto enlightenment, unto delight, unto joy, and unto gladness of my soul and body,[^1174] now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.

*Prayer of the same Saint John of Damascus, unto Holy Communion:*[^1175]

And grant mercy unto them that hate me, and that make war against me, and that reproach me; likewise also unto them that slander me; that none of them in any wise on account of me, an unclean man, may suffer any evil, neither in this present nor in the world to come; but cleanse them by Thy mercy, and cover them by Thy grace, O Good One; illumine and enlighten them unto ages of ages. Amen.[^1176]

*Prayer of Saint Symeon the Metaphrast, unto Holy Communion:*[^1177]

O only pure and incorrupt Lord, Who through the compassionate mercy of Thine ineffable love for mankind didst take upon Thyself our nature[^1178] from the pure and virginal blood of her that bore Thee beyond nature,[^1179] by the descent of the Divine Spirit and the good pleasure of the co-eternal Father; O Christ Jesus, Wisdom of God, and Peace, and Power;[^1180] Who in Thy flesh didst deign to accept life-creating and saving passions: the Crucifixion, the Cross, the nails, the spear, and death;[^1181] mortify in me the soul-corrupting passions of the body; Who by Thy burial didst despoil the kingdoms of hades: bury my evil counsels by good thoughts, and scatter the spirits of wickedness;[^1182] Who by Thy third-day and God-bearing Resurrection didst raise up the fallen forefather:[^1183]

raise up me that am slipped by sin, setting before me the ways of repentance; Who by Thy glorious Ascension didst deify the assumed flesh and honor it with a session at the right hand:[^1184] vouchsafe me through communion of Thy Holy Mysteries to obtain the right-hand portion of them that are saved;[^1185] Who by the descent of Thy Comforter Spirit didst make Thy consecrated disciples precious vessels: show forth me also to be a dwelling-place of His coming;[^1186] Who shalt come again to judge the world in righteousness: be pleased that I also may meet Thee in the clouds, my Judge and Creator, with all Thy saints,[^1187] so that I may endlessly hymn and praise Thee, with Thine unoriginate Father, and Thy most holy, and good, and life-creating, and consubstantial Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.[^1188]

*Prayer of the same Saint Symeon the Metaphrast, unto Holy Communion:*[^1189]

O Father, Son, and Spirit, Holy Trinity, inexhaustible goodness flowing unto eternity, beauty greatly beloved that hath no satiety:[^1190] save me by faith alone, and through hope;[^1191] O Thrice-radiant Light, O Most Holy Trinity: Trinity in Persons, and Unity in Essence;[^1192] Fount of wisdom, and Giver of sanctification;

By faith alone save me, and through hope;[^1193] O Fire cleansing sins:[^1194] cleanse my soul of transgressions; wash my soul of ignorances; snatch my soul away from defilements; bridle the thoughts of my soul; and make the mind king over the intelligible faculties; show it forth as an all-powerful king over the passions;[^1195] cause an intellectual candle to shine unto my heart; deliver me from the darkness of sin; enlighten and adorn him that is darkened;[^1196] look upon me with a merciful eye; cleanse and whiten him that is blackened;[^1197] O Father, Son, and Spirit, Holy Trinity: do Thou grant me a radiant angel, a helper to my mind,[^1198] a tutor and protector, a guardian of my soul and body, a guide directing me unto salvation.[^1199] Do Thou make me that am earthly to be sanctified; do Thou separate me from earthly mindsets; do Thou dry up for me the torrents of wickedness; do Thou pour forth for me showers of tears;[^1200] for Thou art a merciful God and Benefactor, bearing no malice toward all that have worked lawlessness; all-accessible unto all that have sinned, longsuffering toward all that have fallen away;[^1201] not established for the righteous alone, nor revealed only to the blameless; Thou hast ordained salvation through confession, and hast granted patterns of repentance:[^1202] and unto me that am loathsome, and polluted; unto me that am deceitful and wretched; unto me that am dark and defiled;[^1203] for I have wrought lawlessness far more than the ancients; I have provoked Thee to anger, and have embittered Thee exceedingly; more than the number of the innumerable stars, more than the number of the sand of the sea have I sinned against Thee;[^1204] there is no form of evil more wicked, there is no shame of evil more deceitful, which I have not committed at every time and place, in soul, and in thought, and in words, and in deeds;[^1205] the abominations of my wickedness are multiplied; by myriads are my evil deeds multiplied; multiplied are the burdens of my transgressions; as by iron bands embittered through conceit[^1206] is my neck; with inescapable bonds am I constricted in heart; neither can I lift up my head, nor have I any relief in conscience;[^1207] unworthily therefore do I look upon the heavenly height; unworthily do I look upon the sight of men; unworthily do I give counsel unto my neighbor; unworthily do I tread upon the earthly dust;[^1208] for I have kindled Thine indignation utterly, and have excessively inflamed Thy dreadful wrath;[^1209] I have provoked Thee to anger, and have embittered Thee exceedingly; before Thee have I committed every abomination; neither have I desired any one of Thy pure volitions;[^1210] nor have I longed for any one of Thy desirable judgments;[^1211] neither have I kept any one of Thy most wise commandments; nor have I held fast any one of Thy sovereign words. And now I bend unto Thee the knees of my heart;[^1212] I bow down my darkened head; I bow down my defiled neck; unto Thy goodness do I bow down my neck; unto Thy goodness do I offer supplication.[^1213] I have sinned, I have wrought lawlessness, and I have committed offence; I have sinned, I have dealt unrighteously, and have transgressed Thy commandments; I have sinned, I have dealt unrighteously, and have condemned others; I have sinned, I have turned away, and was not ashamed;[^1214] yet I make supplication unto Thy goodness, yet I offer a prayer[^1215] unto Thy malice-free loving-kindness; but I beseech Thine extreme tender-heartedness; yea, I beseech and cry aloud: Save and cleanse me![^1216] Remit the multitude of my transgressions; remit the grievous burden of my debts; remit my many defilements; remit all my abominations.[^1217] And crush me not together with my sins; put me not to death together with mine iniquities; snatch me not away together with evil thoughts; burn me not up together with abominations.[^1218] Deprive me not of eternal good things; cast me not out from the immortal banquet; alienate me not from the joy of the saints; deprive me not of my salvation.[^1219]

Grant me again the gift of baptism, the divine Great Monastic Schema;[^1220] for the first I have mired in sins, the first I have defiled with abominations. Vouchsafe me sacred Communion, life, the chalice of God-streaming blood,[^1221] unto the cleansing of my sins, unto deliverance, and unto salvation. And in the final hour, the bitter hour of death; the hour grievous and painful; the hour dark and obscured:[^1222] save, have compassion, and cleanse me! Gently separate my soul from my defiled flesh; make my darkened soul to be illumined; deliver it from the wicked demons; and all the handwritten bonds of my sins,[^1223] tear up the writings of my debts; scatter them into the abyss of hades; rend them, turn them to ashes, burn them utterly to the end![^1224] Send then gentle and radiant angels, repelling the demonic hosts, snatching the soul away from torment, showing mercy to the wretched soul, bearing it on high apart from sins;[^1225] bearing it on high to bow down before the fiery-formed and radiant throne,[^1226] where all the saved offer praise, vouchsafing it the joy of the saints. Accept Thy goodness as an intercessor; grant me Thy grace as a pre-eminent intercessor:[^1227] Thy loving-kindness, Thy malice-free mercy, Thy compassion, Thine extreme tender-heartedness;

...tender-heartedness. Accept as a second intercessor Her Who is higher than the cosmos, the Adornment, the Mother, Virgin, and Maiden, the Divine Ladder and the Rod, the Animate Throne;[^1228] accept as intercessors the lightning-rayed ranks: Thrones, Cherubim, fiery Seraphim, Dominions, Powers, Authorities, Principalities, Archangels, and Angels;[^1229] accept as intercessor Thy radiant and light-bearing Forerunner, sanctified before swaddling-clothes, the God-proclaiming preacher who shone forth before the Master unto those that were in darkness;[^1230] accept as intercessors the choirs of the saints: the choirs of prophets, patriarchs, fathers, apostles, and crown-bearing martyrs,[^1231] and the assembly of all the holy and light-bearing ones. Accept as intercessor Mary of Egypt: a mortal from the earth, yet one who ascended into heaven;[^1232] accept as intercessor Onuphrius the Great, who, having stripped his body naked, was marvelously robed in divine raiment through good deeds.[^1233] For Thou art a merciful and beneficent God, a God meek unto transgressors, a God Who hast granted deliverance unto sins, a God bestowing salvation upon all; unto me also show all Thy goodness, and pour out upon me the streams of Thy tender-heartedness; for I have transgressed the law more than all men, from my very mother's womb even unto my present time.[^1234] Save me beyond merit,[^1235] and through hope, by Thy grace and Thy loving-kindness alone; that I may bless Thee and magnify Thee with love; that I may give thanks unto Thee and chant unto Thee with piety, being saved in the age to come; that I may bless the blessed Master, Whom the heavenly hosts bless, unto all unnumbered ages. Amen.[^1236]

*Prayer before Holy Communion, of Saint Symeon the New Theologian, from the Hymns of Divine Love:*[^1237]

From defiled lips, from an abominable heart, from an unclean tongue, from a polluted soul, receive supplication, O my Christ;[^1238] and despise not my words, nor my manners, nor my shameless boldness;[^1239]

give me leave to speak boldly what I desire, O my Christ; and rather teach me what is fitting for me to do and to speak.[^1240] I have sinned more than the harlot, who, having learned where Thou didst abide, bought myrrh and came boldly to anoint Thy feet, my Master Christ and my God.[^1241] Even as Thou didst not cast her out when she approached from the heart, neither reject me, O Word;[^1242] but grant me to hold and kiss Thy feet, and with streams of tears, as with precious myrrh, dare to anoint them.[^1243] Wash me with my tears, cleanse me with them, O Word; remit my transgressions, and grant me mercy. Thou knowest the multitude of mine evils,[^1244] multitude; Thou knowest also my sores, and seest my wounds; yet Thou knowest also my faith, and seest my goodwill, and hearest my sighing.[^1245] For there is not hidden from Thee, O my God, my Creator, and my Redeemer, even a tear-drop, nor any part of a drop, nor any movement of the heart.[^1246] Thine eyes did see mine unformed substance, and in Thy book all things are written before Thee.[^1247] Look upon my lowliness, look upon all my toil, and forgive me all my sins, O God of all;[^1248] that with a pure heart, with fearful contemplation, and with a contrite soul, I may partake of Thy most pure and undefiled Mysteries,[^1249] whereby whosoever drinks and eats with a pure heart is vivified and deified.[^1250] For Thou hast said, O Master: *Whosoever eats My flesh and drinks My blood, he abides in Me, and I in him.*[^1251] True indeed is every word of my Master and God; and he who partakes of the divine and deifying graces is no longer alone, but with Thee, O my Christ, the Light of the Three-Sunned Radiance.[^1252] That I may not be alone apart from Thee, the Giver of Life, my breath, my life, my rejoicing, the salvation of the world:[^1253] therefore have I drawn near unto Thee, as Thou seest, with tears and a contrite heart,[^1254] asking to receive deliverance from my transgressions, and to partake uncondemned of Thy life-giving and undefiled Mysteries, that Thou mayest abide, even as Thou hast said, with me, a wretched man; lest the Deceiver, finding me bereft of Thy grace, seize me craftily, and having deceived me, lead me away from Thy deifying words.[^1255] Therefore do I fall down before Thee, and fervently cry unto Thee: Even as Thou didst receive the Prodigal, and the harlot that drew near, so receive me, prodigal and defiled, O Compassionate One, who now come unto Thee with a contrite soul.[^1256] I know, O Saviour, that no other man hath sinned against Thee as I,[^1257] nor did deeds such as I did. But this again I know, that neither the magnitude of transgressions, nor the multitude of sins, surpass the abundant love of my God for mankind;[^1258] but with the mercy of compassion Thou cleansest and makest radiant them that fervently repent, and makest them partakers of the Light; and, marvelous to angelic and human minds, Thou conversest with them many times, even as with Thine own near friends.[^1259] These things make me bold, these things give me wings, O my Christ; and trusting in Thy rich benefits toward us, I rejoice and tremble at once, partaking of fire, being but grass. A marvelous wonder:[^1260]

now dewed without being consumed, even as of old the bush burned without being consumed.[^1261] Now with a grateful word, and with a grateful heart, and with the grateful members of my soul and body, I worship and magnify and glorify Thee, O my Christ, Who art blessed now, and unto ages of ages. Amen.[^1262]

*After this, the Confession of the Orthodox Faith:*
**"I believe in one God..."**[^1263]

*Then:*
Of Thy Mystical Supper, O Son of God, receive me today as a communicant; for I will not speak of the Mystery to Thine enemies, neither will I give Thee a kiss as did Judas, but as the thief do I confess Thee: Remember me, O Lord, in Thy kingdom.[^1264]

*The Apostle to the Corinthians:*[^1265]

Brethren, I received of the Lord that which also I delivered unto you, that the Lord Jesus, in the night in which He was betrayed, took bread, and having given thanks, He brake it and said: Take, eat; this is My Body which is broken for you; this do in remembrance of Me. In like manner also the cup, after supper, saying: This cup is the New Testament in My Blood; this do, as often as ye drink it, in remembrance of Me. For as often as ye eat this bread and drink this cup, ye proclaim the Lord’s death, till He come. Therefore, whosoever shall eat this bread,[^1266] or drink the cup of the Lord unworthily, shall be guilty of the Body and Blood of the Lord. But let a man examine himself, and so let him eat of the bread, and drink of the cup. For he that eats and drinks unworthily, eats and drinks judgment unto himself, not discerning the Lord’s Body. For this cause many are weak and sickly among you, and not a few sleep. For if we would judge ourselves, we should not be judged. But when we are judged, we are chastened by the Lord, that we should not be condemned with the world.[^1267]

*The Gospel according to John:*

The Lord said unto the Jews who came unto Him: I am the bread of life. Your fathers did eat[^1268] manna in the wilderness, and died. This is the bread which comes down from heaven, that if anyone eat thereof, he may not die. I am the living bread which came down from heaven. If anyone eat of this bread, he shall live unto ages; and the bread that I will give is My flesh, which I gave for the life of the world.[^1269] The Jews therefore strove among themselves, saying: How can this man give us His flesh to eat? Then Jesus said unto them: Truly, truly, I say unto you: Except ye eat the flesh of the Son of Man and drink His blood, ye have no life in you. Whosoever eats My flesh and drinks My blood hath eternal life,[^1270] and I will raise him up at the last day.[^1271]

*Say these things also from the soul as thou drawest near to the Divine Mysteries, reproving thy conscience in thy mind:*[^1272]

Behold, I draw near unto Divine Communion; O Master, burn me not by partaking, but cleanse me from every defilement; for Thou hast spoken of fire consuming the unworthy. Behold, this is set forth, O Christ, for food unto all; but for me, it is good to cleave unto God, and to put the hope of my salvation in the Lord. Amen.[^1273]

*After this, say this also if thou wilt, even thrice, as thou drawest near:*[^1274]

O man, seeing the deifying Blood, shudder!

For It is a coal consuming the unworthy.[^1275] The Flesh of God deifies me and nourishes me: It deifies the spirit, and marvelously and wonderfully nourishes the mind.[^1276] O man, shudder when thou eatest unworthily, for It is fire burning up sins. And cleanse me, O Lord, from every defilement.

*After this, having placed thy hands crosswise upon thy breast, partake with fear of the Body and Blood of the Crucified One.*[^1277]

*[Woodcut headpiece: Renaissance floral ornament with acanthus scrollwork, floral garlands, and two symmetric winged putti.]*
