# PART XX: CANONICAL CHAPTERS OF PATRIARCH THEODORE CONCERNING BURIAL IN CHURCHES [^1406]

*The Funeral Order. From the Answers of the Most Holy Patriarch, the Lord Theodore. Question:*

According to the ancient custom of that place, the remains of Orthodox [Christians] are buried in city churches. I seek therefore to be taught whether this is sinless.

*Answer:*

There is a great difference between churches: those that are consecrated, receiving dedication and the erection of an altar table, by anointing with holy chrism and the deposition of holy relics of martyrs; and those that are not thus consecrated, but hold the rank of a house of prayer.[^1407] Therefore in the former in which the holy relics of martyrs are visibly treasured up, and which have received in their midst anointing with holy chrism: let human remains of whatever kind by no means be buried, according to the second chapter of the first title of the fifth book of ecclesiastical [laws], which says: "Let no one bury a dead body in church." And according to the civil ancient law, which says: "It is unlawful to bury anyone in church, unless visibly a martyr's body is to lie there." But in those that are not so consecrated, being designated holy houses of prayer, remains may be buried without harm.[^1408]

---

# PART XXI: THE ORDER OF BURIAL [^1409]

*When one of the Orthodox has reposed, his kinsmen immediately summon the priest; and having arrived at the house wherein the remains lie, and having put on the epitrachelion and put incense into the censer, he begins in the usual manner:*

> **Priest:** **"Blessed is our God..."**

*And those with him say:*

> **People:** **"Holy God..."** **"All-Holy Trinity..."** after **"Our Father..."**[^1410]

> **Priest:** **"For Thine is the kingdom..."**

*And these troparia, Tone 4:*

*Troparion, Tone 4:*
With the spirits of the righteous made perfect, give rest to the soul of Thy servant, O Savior, preserving it in the blessed life which is with Thee, O Lover of mankind.[^1411]

*Troparion:*
In Thy resting place, O Lord, where all Thy saints repose, give rest also to the soul of Thy servant, for Thou alone art the Lover of mankind.

*Glory...*

*Troparion:*
Thou art the God Who descended into hades and loosed the bonds of the bound: do Thou Thyself give rest also to the soul of Thy servant.[^1412]

*Both now...*

*Theotokion:*
O only pure and spotless Virgin, who without seed didst bear God: intercede that our souls may be saved.

*The priest [says] the litany:*

> **Priest:** ""
Have mercy on us, O God, according to Thy great mercy, we pray Thee, give ear and have mercy.[^1413]
Furthermore we pray for the repose of the soul of the servant of God [Name], departed this life.
That every transgression committed by him, voluntary and involuntary, may be forgiven him.
That the Lord God may establish his spirit where the righteous repose.
The mercies of God, the kingdom of heaven, and the remission of his sins, let us ask of Christ, the immortal King and our God.

*Let us pray to the Lord:*

O God of spirits and of all flesh, Who hast trampled down death, and abolished the devil, and given life unto Thy world:[^1414] do Thou Thyself, O Lord give rest to the soul of Thy departed servant [Name], in a place of light, in a place of green pasture, in a place of refreshment, whence sickness, sorrow, and sighing have fled away.[^1415] Every sin committed by him, in word, or in deed, or in thought, do Thou as the good One and Lover of mankind forgive. For there is no man that shall live and not sin; for Thou alone art without sin; Thy righteousness is an everlasting righteousness, and Thy word is truth.[^1416]

*Exclamation:*
For Thou art the resurrection and the life and the repose of Thy departed servant [Name], O Christ our God, and unto Thee do we send up glory together with Thine unoriginate Father, and Thy most holy and good and life-creating Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages.

*Glory... Both now... and the dismissal:*

*And if, then, all things for the departure are ready, the priest immediately makes the beginning again. And we begin to chant: **"Holy God..."** with fear and all contrition. And having taken up the body of the deceased, we go forth to the church, the priests going before with candles and the deacons with censers. And when they come into the church, the remains are placed in the narthex opposite the great doors; then*[^1417] *we begin:* **"Come, let us worship..."** *(Thrice).*

*Psalm 90:*[^1418]
He that dwells in the help of the Most High shall abide in the shelter of the God of heaven.
He shall say unto the Lord: Thou art my protector and my refuge; my God, in Him will I hope.
For He shall deliver thee from the snare of the hunters, and from troubling speech.
With His pinions shall He overshadow thee, and under His wings shalt thou hope; His truth shall encircle thee with a shield.
Thou shalt not be afraid of the terror of the night, nor of the arrow that flies by day;
Nor of the thing that walks in darkness, nor of mishap and the noonday demon.[^1419]
A thousand shall fall at thy side and ten thousand at thy right hand, but it shall not come near thee.
Only with thine eyes shalt thou behold, and see the reward of sinners.
For Thou, O Lord, art my hope; Thou hast made the Most High thy refuge.
No evil shall come upon thee, and no scourge shall draw near unto thy body.[^1420]
For He shall give His angels charge concerning thee, to keep thee in all thy ways.
Upon their hands shall they bear thee up, lest at any time thou dash thy foot against a stone.
Upon the asp and basilisk shalt thou tread, and trample down the lion and dragon.
Because he has set his hope on Me, I will deliver him; I will protect him, because he has known My name.
He shall call upon Me, and I will answer him; I am with him in affliction; I will deliver him and glorify him.
With length of days will I satisfy him, and show him My salvation.

*After this, with a most elevated voice they chant the Blameless [Verses].[^1421] And at the end of each verse we sing the refrain: "Blessed art Thou, O Lord, teach us Thy statutes."*

*Psalm 118:*[^1422]
Blessed are the blameless in the way, who walk in the law of the Lord.
Blessed are they that search out His testimonies; with their whole heart shall they seek Him.
For they that work iniquity have not walked in His ways.
Thou hast commanded Thy precepts to be kept diligently.
O that my ways were directed to keep Thy statutes!
Then shall I not be put to shame, when I look upon all Thy commandments.
I will confess Thee in uprightness of heart, when I have learned the judgments of Thy righteousness.
I will keep Thy statutes; do not utterly forsake me.
By what means shall a young man direct his way? By keeping Thy words.[^1423]
With my whole heart have I sought Thee; cast me not away from Thy commandments.
In my heart have I hidden Thy words, that I might not sin against Thee.
Blessed art Thou, O Lord; teach me Thy statutes.
With my lips have I declared all the judgments of Thy mouth.

In the way of Thy testimonies have I found delight, as in all manner of riches.
In Thy commandments will I meditate, and I will understand Thy ways.
In Thy statutes will I meditate; I will not forget Thy words.
Reward Thy servant; give me life, and I will keep Thy words.
Open Thou mine eyes, and I will understand the wonders of Thy law.
A sojourner am I upon the earth; hide not Thy commandments from me.
My soul has longed to desire Thy judgments at all times.
Thou hast rebuked the proud; cursed are they that turn aside from Thy commandments.[^1424]
Take away from me reproach and contempt, for I have sought after Thy testimonies.
For princes sat and slandered me; but Thy servant meditated on Thy statutes.
For Thy testimonies are my meditation, and Thy statutes are my counselors.
My soul has cleaved unto the earth; quicken Thou me according to Thy word.
I have declared my ways, and Thou didst hear me; teach me Thy statutes.
Make me to understand the way of Thy statutes, and I will meditate on Thy marvels.
My soul slumbered from grief; strengthen Thou me in Thy words.[^1425]
Remove from me the way of iniquity, and by Thy law have mercy on me.

I have chosen the way of truth, and Thy judgments have I not forgotten.
I have cleaved unto Thy testimonies; O Lord, put me not to shame.
I ran the way of Thy commandments, when Thou didst enlarge my heart.
Set before me for a law, O Lord, the way of Thy statutes, and I will seek it out continually.
Give me understanding, and I will search out Thy law; and I will keep it with my whole heart.
Guide me in the path of Thy commandments, for I have desired it.
Incline my heart unto Thy testimonies, and not to covetousness.
Turn away mine eyes from beholding vanity; quicken Thou me in Thy way.
Establish unto Thy servant Thy word, for Thy fear.[^1426]

Take away my reproach which I have dreaded; for Thy judgments are good.
Behold, I have longed after Thy commandments; quicken Thou me in Thy righteousness.
And let Thy mercy come upon me, O Lord, even Thy salvation according to Thy word.
So shall I give answer to them that reproach me with a word; for I have hoped in Thy words.
And take not the word of truth utterly out of my mouth; for I have hoped in Thy judgments.
So shall I keep Thy law continually, forever and unto ages of ages.[^1427]
And I walked at large; for I sought out Thy commandments.
And I spoke of Thy testimonies before kings, and was not ashamed.
And I meditated on Thy commandments which I loved exceedingly.
And I lifted up my hands unto Thy commandments, which I loved; and I meditated continually on Thy statutes.
Remember Thy words unto Thy servant, wherein Thou hast caused me to hope.
This has comforted me in my lowliness, that Thy word has quickened me.
The proud have transgressed exceedingly, yet have I not declined from Thy law.
I remembered Thy judgments from of old, O Lord, and was comforted.
Grief has taken hold of me because of the sinners that forsake Thy law.
Thy statutes were my songs in the place of my sojourning.[^1428]
I remembered in the night Thy name, O Lord, and kept Thy law.
This has happened unto me, because I sought after Thy statutes.
Thou art my portion, O Lord; I said that I would keep Thy law.
I entreated Thy face with my whole heart; have mercy on me according to Thy word.
I thought on Thy ways, and turned my feet unto Thy testimonies.
I made ready and was not disquieted, that I might keep Thy commandments.
The cords of sinners have entangled me, and Thy law have I not forgotten.[^1429]
At midnight I arose to give thanks unto Thee for the judgments of Thy righteousness.
I am a companion of all them that fear Thee and of them that keep Thy commandments.
The earth, O Lord, is full of Thy mercy; teach me Thy statutes.
Thou hast dealt kindly with Thy servant, O Lord, according to Thy word.
Teach me goodness and instruction and understanding, for I have believed Thy commandments.
Before I was humbled I transgressed; for this cause have I kept Thy word.
Good art Thou, O Lord, and in Thy goodness teach me Thy statutes.
The iniquity of the proud has been multiplied against me; but with my whole heart will I search out Thy commandments.
Their heart is curdled like milk; but as for me, in Thy law[^1430] have I meditated.
It is good for me that Thou hast humbled me, that I might learn Thy statutes.
The law of Thy mouth is good to me, above thousands of gold and silver.
Thy hands have made me and fashioned me; give me understanding, and I shall learn Thy commandments.
*Have mercy on Thy servant.*[^1431]
They that fear Thee shall see me and be glad, because I have hoped in Thy words.
I know, O Lord, that Thy commandments are righteousness,[^1432] and that in truth Thou hast humbled me.
Let Thy mercy be for my comfort, according to Thy word unto Thy servant.
Let come unto me Thy compassions, that I may live; for Thy law is my meditation.
Let the proud be put to shame, for they have transgressed against me unjustly; but as for me, I will meditate on Thy commandments.
Let those that fear Thee turn unto me, and those that know Thy testimonies.
Let my heart be blameless in Thy statutes, that I may not be put to shame.
My soul faints for Thy salvation; I have hoped in Thy words.
Mine eyes fail for Thy word, saying: When wilt Thou comfort me?
For I am become like a wineskin in the frost;[^1433] yet have I not forgotten Thy statutes.
How many are the days of Thy servant? When wilt Thou execute judgment on them that persecute me?
Transgressors have told me idle tales,[^1434] but not as Thy law, O Lord.
All Thy commandments are truth; they persecuted me unjustly: help Thou me.
They had almost consumed me upon the earth; but I forsook not Thy commandments.
*Quicken Thou me according to Thy mercy,*[^1435] and I shall keep the testimonies of Thy mouth.
Forever, O Lord, Thy word abides in heaven.
Thy truth is from generation to generation; Thou hast founded the earth, and it abides.
By Thine ordinance the day abides, for all things are Thy servants.

Unless Thy law had been my meditation, I should then have perished in my humiliation.
Forever will I not forget Thy statutes, for in them Thou hast quickened me.
*Save me; unless Thy law [had been my meditation]...*[^1436]
*Say thrice. Then the deaconal petitions:*
> **Deacon:** "Again and again in peace let us pray to the Lord."
Again let us pray for the repose of the soul of the servant of God, [Name], and that every transgression, voluntary and involuntary, may be forgiven him.
That the Lord God may establish his soul where the righteous repose.
The mercies of God, the kingdom of heaven, and the remission of his sins, let us ask of Christ the immortal King and our God.
Let us pray to the Lord.
*The priest [recites] the prayer: O God of spirits...*[^1437] *And the exclamation:*
> **Priest:** "For Thou art the resurrection and the life and the repose of Thy departed servant, [Name], O Christ our God; and unto Thee do we send up glory, together with Thine unoriginate Father, and Thine all-holy, good, and life-creating Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages."
*And after this we begin to chant the second stasis. Refrain:*
*O Savior, save Thy servant.*
*Second Stasis:*[^1438]
I am Thine, save Thou me; for I have sought after Thy statutes.
Sinners waited for me to destroy me, but I understood Thy testimonies.
I have seen an end of all perfection; but Thy commandment is exceedingly broad.[^1439]
How have I loved Thy law, O Lord! It is my meditation all the day.
Thou hast made me wiser than mine enemies by Thy commandment, for it is mine forever.
I have understood more than all my teachers, for Thy testimonies are my meditation.
I have understood more than the elders, because I sought after Thy commandments.
I have restrained my feet from every evil way, that I might keep Thy words.
I have not departed from Thy judgments, for Thou hast laid down a law for me.
How sweet are unto my throat Thy words, yea, sweeter than honey to my mouth!
Through Thy commandments I got understanding; therefore have I hated every way of unrighteousness.
Thy law is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my paths.
I have sworn and determined to keep the judgments of Thy righteousness.
I have been humbled exceedingly, O Lord; quicken Thou me according to Thy word.
Accept the freewill offerings of my mouth, O Lord,[^1440] and teach me Thy judgments.
My soul is continually in Thy hands, and I have not forgotten Thy law.
Sinners have laid a snare for me, yet have I not strayed from Thy commandments.
I have inherited Thy testimonies forever for they are the rejoicing of my heart.
I have inclined my heart to perform Thy statutes forever, for a recompense.[^1441]
Transgressors have I hated, but Thy law have I loved.
Thou art my helper and my protector; I have hoped in Thy words.
Depart from me, ye evildoers, and I will search out the commandments of my God.
Uphold me according to Thy word, and I shall live; and put me not to shame from mine expectation.
Help Thou me, and I shall be saved, and I will meditate on Thy statutes continually.
Thou hast brought to naught all them that depart from Thy statutes, for their inward thought is unrighteous.

I have reckoned all the sinners of the earth as transgressors; therefore have I loved Thy testimonies.
Nail down my flesh with the fear of Thee,[^1442] for I am afraid of Thy judgments.
I have done judgment and righteousness; give me not over unto them that wrong me.
Receive Thy servant unto good, that the proud may not slander me.
Mine eyes have failed for Thy salvation, and for the word of Thy righteousness.
Deal with Thy servant according to Thy mercy, and teach me Thy statutes.
I am Thy servant; give me understanding, and I shall know Thy testimonies.
It is time for the Lord to act;[^1443] they have made void Thy law. Therefore have I loved Thy commandments above gold and topaz.
Therefore I directed myself unto all Thy commandments; every way of unrighteousness have I hated.
Thy testimonies are wonderful; therefore has my soul searched them out.
The unfolding of Thy words gives light and gives understanding unto infants.[^1444]
I opened my mouth and drew in breath, for I longed for Thy commandments.
Look upon me and have mercy on me, according to the judgment of them that love Thy name.
Direct my steps according to Thy word, and let no iniquity gain dominion over me.
Deliver me from the slander of men, and I shall keep Thy commandments Thy commandments.[^1445]
Make Thy face to shine upon Thy servant, and teach me Thy statutes.
Streams of waters have mine eyes poured down, because they kept not Thy law.
Righteous art Thou, O Lord, and upright are Thy judgments.
Thou hast commanded righteousness in Thy testimonies, and truth exceedingly.
Thy zeal has consumed me,[^1446] because mine enemies have forgotten Thy words.
Thy word is tried exceedingly in the fire,[^1447] and Thy servant has loved it.
I am young and despised, yet have I not forgotten Thy statutes.
Thy righteousness is righteousness forever, and Thy law is truth.
Afflictions and distresses have found me; Thy commandments are my meditation.
Thy testimonies are righteousness forever; give me understanding, and I shall live.
I cried with my whole heart: Hear me, O Lord; I will search out Thy statutes.
I cried unto Thee: Save me, and I shall keep Thy testimonies.
I anticipated the dawn and cried;[^1448] I hoped in Thy words.
Mine eyes anticipated the morning watch, that I might meditate on Thy words.
Hear my voice, O Lord, according to Thy mercy; quicken Thou me according to Thy judgment.
They that persecute me have drawn near unto iniquity,[^1449] but they have removed far from Thy law.
Thou art near, O Lord, and all Thy paths are truth.

From the beginning have I known from Thy testimonies that Thou hast founded them forever.[^1450]
Behold my humiliation and deliver me, for I have not forgotten Thy law.
Judge my cause and deliver me; quicken Thou me for Thy word's sake.
Salvation is far from sinners, for they have not searched out Thy statutes.
Many are Thy compassions, O Lord; quicken Thou me according to Thy judgment.
Many are they that persecute me and afflict me; yet have I not declined from Thy testimonies.
I saw them that deal faithlessly, and I was grieved,[^1451] because they kept not Thy words.
Behold how I have loved Thy commandments, O Lord; quicken Thou me in Thy mercy.

The beginning of Thy words is truth,[^1452] and all the judgments of Thy righteousness endure forever.
Princes persecuted me without a cause, and my heart was afraid because of Thy words.
I will rejoice over Thy words, as one that finds great spoil.
Unrighteousness have I hated and abhorred, but Thy law have I loved.
Seven times a day have I praised Thee for the judgments of Thy righteousness.
Great peace have they that love Thy law, and there is no stumbling block unto them.
I looked for Thy salvation, O Lord, and I have loved Thy commandments.
My soul has kept Thy testimonies, and loved them exceedingly.
I have kept Thy commandments and Thy testimonies, for all my ways are before Thee, O Lord.
Let my supplication come near before Thee, O Lord; give me understanding according to Thy word.
Let my petition come before Thee, O Lord; deliver Thou me according to Thy word.
My lips shall pour forth praise,[^1453] when Thou hast taught me Thy statutes.
My tongue shall speak of Thy words, for all Thy commandments are righteousness.
Let Thy hand be near to save me, for I have chosen Thy commandments.
I have longed for Thy salvation, O Lord, and Thy law is my meditation.
My soul shall live and shall praise Thee, and Thy judgments shall help me.

I have gone astray like a lost sheep; seek Thy servant, for I have not forgotten Thy commandments.[^1454]
*This verse thrice. Then again the troparia:*[^1455]
*Tone 5. Verse: Blessed art Thou, O Lord, teach me Thy statutes.*
*Troparion:*
The choir of the Saints has found the fountain of life and the door of paradise;[^1456] may I also find the way through repentance. I am the lost sheep: call me back, O Savior, and save me.
*Blessed art Thou, O Lord.*
*Troparion:*
Thou Who of old fashioned me from nonexistence with Thy hand,[^1457] and honored me with Thy divine image, but because of the transgression of the commandment didst return me again unto the earth whence I was taken: lead me back unto the likeness, and adorn me once more with the ancient beauty.[^1458]
*Blessed art Thou, O Lord.*
*Troparion:*
I am an image of Thine ineffable glory, even though I bear the wounds of transgressions. Have compassion on Thine own creature, O Master, and cleanse me by Thy lovingkindness; and grant me the longed-for homeland, making me once more a citizen of paradise.
*Blessed art Thou, O Lord, teach us.*
*Troparion:*
Ye who proclaimed the Lamb of God,[^1459] and were slain as lambs, and have been translated unto life unaging and ever-existing, O holy ones: fervently entreat Him, O Martyrs, that He may grant us remission of our debts.
*Blessed art Thou, O Lord, teach us.*

*Troparion:*
Ye who have walked the narrow and sorrowful way,[^1460] all ye who in life have taken up the cross as a yoke, and followed Me by faith: come and receive the honors and heavenly crowns which I have prepared for you.
*Blessed art Thou, O Lord.*
*Troparion:*
Give rest, O God, unto Thy servant,[^1461] and establish him in paradise, where the choirs of the Saints, O Lord, and the righteous shine as the stars; unto him who is fallen asleep, O Master, we pray, overlooking all his transgressions.
*Glory to the Father and to the Son and to the Holy Spirit.*
*Triadikon:*
Let us piously hymn the threefold radiance of the one Godhead,[^1462] crying aloud: Holy art Thou, O unoriginate Father, and co-unoriginate Son, and Divine Spirit; enlighten us who by faith serve Thee, and snatch us from the eternal fire.
*Now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.*
*Theotokion:*
Rejoice, O pure one, who didst bear God in the flesh without seed unto the salvation of all,[^1463] for through thee the human race has found salvation; and through thee may we find paradise, O pure and blessed Theotokos.
*Alleluia, alleluia, glory to Thee, O God. (Thrice)*
*Then the deacon:*
> **Deacon:** "Again and again in peace let us pray to the Lord."
Again let us pray for the repose... *and the rest as before.*[^1464]
*And after the exclamation we sing these troparia:*
*Tone 4:*
Give rest, O our Savior, with the righteous unto Thy servant,[^1465] and settle him in Thy courts, as it is written, overlooking, as Thou art good, his transgressions, voluntary and involuntary, and all those done in knowledge and in ignorance, O Lover of mankind.
*Glory to the Father and to the Son and to the Holy Spirit.*
*Ending:*
And all those done in knowledge and in ignorance, O Lover of mankind.
*Now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.*
*Theotokion:*
O Christ God, Who from the Virgin didst shine forth upon the world,[^1466] and through her didst make us sons of light: have mercy on us.
*Then Psalm 50: Have mercy on me, O God.*
*And the Canon, whose acrostic is: Unto the departed I sing the sixth song. By Theophanes.*[^1467]
*Ode 1, Tone 6. Heirmos:*
*Traversing the deep on foot as if on dry land, Israel...*[^1468]
*Troparion:*
In the heavenly bridal chambers the noble-souled Martyrs ever beseech Thee, O Christ: vouchsafe the faithful one whom Thou hast translated from the earth to attain eternal good things.

*Troparion:*
Thou Who didst adorn all things, and didst fashion me, man, as a composite living creature, midway between lowliness and majesty: therefore give rest, O Savior, unto the soul of Thy servant.[^1469]

*Troparion:*
In the beginning Thou didst appoint me a citizen of paradise and a tiller of the ground; but when I transgressed Thy commandment, Thou didst banish me: therefore give rest, O Savior, unto the soul of Thy servant.[^1470]

*Theotokion:*
He Who of old fashioned Eve from the rib, our first mother,[^1471] is clothed in flesh from thy most pure womb, whereby, O pure one, He has destroyed the power of death.

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*
*There is none holy as Thou...*[^1472]

*Troparion:*
Having lawfully contested, Thy Martyrs, O Giver of life, and having been adorned with the crown of victory intercede for the departed faithful one,[^1473] that he may obtain eternal redemption.

*Troparion:*
Having of old instructed me who had gone astray with many miracles and signs,[^1474] in the latter times Thou didst empty Thyself as Thou art compassionate; and seeking me out, Thou didst find and save me.

*Troparion:*
Vouchsafe him who has fled the unstable corruption of fleeting things and come unto Thee,[^1475] O Good One, to dwell with rejoicing in the eternal habitations, justified by faith and by grace.

*Theotokion:*
There is none blameless as thou, O most pure Mother of God; for thou alone from of old didst conceive in thy womb the true God, Who destroyed the power of death.[^1476]

*The deacon:*
> **Deacon:** "Again and again in peace let us pray to the Lord."
*And the rest. And after the exclamation, Sessional Hymn, Tone 6:*[^1477]
*Sessional Hymn, Tone 6:*
Truly all things are vanity, and this life is a shadow and a dream; for in vain every earthborn man disquiets himself, as the Scripture says: when we have gained the world, then we shall dwell in the grave, where kings and beggars are together.[^1478] Therefore, O Christ God, give rest unto Thy servant who is translated, as Thou art the Lover of mankind.

*Glory to the Father and to the Son and to the Holy Spirit.*
*Ending:*
Therefore, O Christ God, give rest unto Thy servant who is translated, as Thou art the Lover of mankind.

*Now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.*
*Theotokion:*
With unceasing hymns we glorify the most pure Theotokos, Mother of the Light, as the mighty hope of our souls, and who shelters us from every adversity.[^1479]

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*
*Christ is my power, God and Lord...*[^1480]

*Troparion:*
Manifesting a proof of greater wisdom, and of Thy bountiful goodness in Thy gifts, O Master, Thou didst unite the choirs of the Martyrs with the Angels.[^1481]

*Troparion:*
Vouchsafe him who has been translated unto Thee to attain Thy most pure glory, where, O Christ, is the dwelling of those who rejoice, and the voice of pure gladness.[^1482]

*Troparion:*
Receive him who hymns Thy divine dominion, whom Thou hast taken from the earth, making him a child of light, cleansing away the mist of sin, O Plenteous in mercy.[^1483]

*Theotokion:*
A most pure receptacle, a temple all-blameless, an all-holy ark, a virginal place of sanctification: thee, the beauty of Jacob,[^1484] has the Master chosen.

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*
*With Thy divine light, O Good One...*[^1485]

*Troparion:*
As a sacred whole-burnt offering and as the firstfruits of human nature, the Martyrs, having offered themselves to God Who is glorified above all, ever bestow salvation upon us.[^1486]

*Troparion:*
Vouchsafe heavenly life and the distribution of gifts, O Lord, unto Thy faithful servant who has fallen asleep before us, granting him deliverance from transgressions.[^1487]

*Troparion:*
O Thou Who alone art by nature the Giver of life, truly an unsearchable abyss of goodness: unto him who has departed this life vouchsafe Thy Kingdom, O Compassionate One, O only Immortal One.[^1488]

*Theotokion:*
He Who was born of thee unto the world, O Sovereign Lady, became strength and song and salvation unto the perishing,[^1489] delivering from the gates of hades those who in faith call thee blessed.

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*
*Beholding the sea of life surging...*[^1490]

*Troparion:*
Nailed to the Cross, Thou didst gather unto Thyself the choirs of the Martyrs, who imitated Thy Passion, O Good One; therefore we beseech Thee: give rest now unto him who has been translated unto Thee.[^1491]

*Troparion:*
In Thine ineffable glory, when Thou shalt come in dread to judge all the world, be well pleased, O Redeemer, that he whom Thou hast taken from the earth, Thy faithful servant, may meet Thee in radiance upon the clouds.[^1492]

*Troparion:*
Being the Fountain of life, in Thy divine might leading forth the bound one, O Master, settle Thy servant, who has departed unto Thee in faith, in the delight of paradise.[^1493]

*Theotokion:*
We returned unto the earth when we transgressed God's holy commandment; but through thee, O Virgin, we have been lifted up from the earth unto heaven, having shaken off the corruption of death.[^1494]

*The deacon:*
> **Deacon:** "Again and again in peace... *and the rest. And after the exclamation, Kontakion, Tone 8:*"[^1495]
*Kontakion, Tone 8:*
With the saints give rest, O Christ, unto the soul of Thy servant, where there is neither sickness, nor sorrow, nor sighing, but life everlasting.[^1496]

*Ikos:*
Thou Thyself alone art immortal, Who didst make and fashion man; for we mortals were fashioned from the earth, and unto the very same earth shall we return, as Thou didst command Who didst fashion me, saying unto me: Dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return; whither all we mortals shall go, making as our funeral lamentation the song: Alleluia.[^1497]

*And again:*
With the saints give rest, O Christ...[^1498]

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*
*The furnace shed dew...*[^1499]

*Troparion:*
Redeemed by Thy blood from the former transgression, and sprinkled with their own blood, the Martyrs clearly foreshadow Thy slaughter: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers![^1500]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst put to death fierce death, O Word most source of life; receive him who has fallen asleep in Thy faith, hymning and saying, O Christ: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers![^1501]

*Troparion:*
Having animated me, man, by a divine breathing, O Thou Most Origin of Godhead:[^1502] vouchsafe him who has been translated Thy Kingdom, O Master, and to sing unto Thee, O Savior: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Theotokion:*
Thou hast become higher than all creation, O all-blameless one, having conceived God Who shattered the gates of death and broke the bars asunder: therefore, O pure one, we the faithful hymn thee in song as Mother of God.[^1503]

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*
*Out of the flame didst Thou pour forth dew for the godly, and the righteous*[^1504] *Troparion:*
Having striven steadfastly, ye were adorned with the crown of victory, O trophy-bearing Martyrs of Christ, crying aloud: Thee do we exalt above all, O Christ, unto the ages![^1505]

*Troparion:*
Receive gently him who has holily left this life in faith and migrated unto Thee, the Master, giving him rest as Thou art tenderhearted, who exalts Thee unto the ages.[^1506]

*Troparion:*
Be well pleased now, O Savior, that Thy servant may be lodged in the land of the meek with all who have fallen asleep before,[^1507] justified by faith in Thee and by grace, who exalts Thee unto the ages.

*Theotokion:*
We all call thee blessed, O all-blessed one, who didst bear the Word, Who is truly blessed, Who became flesh for our sake[^1508] Whom we exalt above all unto all ages.[^1509]

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*
*God it is impossible for men to see...*[^1510]

*Troparion:*
Hope strengthened the choirs of the Martyrs, and with winged ardor inflamed them toward Thy love, prefiguring unto them the future, truly unshakable rest: whereof vouchsafe Thy faithful one, O Good One, who has been translated.[^1511]

*Troparion:*
Be well pleased, O Christ, that he who has been translated in faith may obtain the radiant and divine illumination of Thy countenance, granting him rest in the bosom of Abraham, as Thou alone art merciful, and vouchsafing him eternal blessedness.[^1512]

*Troparion:*
O Thou Who art by nature good and merciful, and desirous of mercy, an abyss of compassion Whom Thou, O Savior, hast translated from this place of affliction and the shadow of death: establish him where Thy light shines forth.[^1513]

*Theotokion:*
We know thee, O pure one, to be the holy Tabernacle, and the Ark, and the Table of the law of grace; for through thee remission was granted unto those justified by the blood of Him Who was incarnate of thy womb, O all-immaculate one.[^1514]

*The deacon:*
> **Deacon:** "Again and again in peace let us pray to the Lord."
*And the rest. And after the exclamation, we begin the Idiomela of John Damascene the monk. Tone 1:*[^1515]

*Tone 1:*
What earthly pleasure abides unmixed with sorrow? Or what glory stands upon the earth immutable? All things are fainter than a shadow, and all things are more deceptive than a dream; in a single hour, death takes all these things away. But in the light of Thy countenance, O Christ, and in the delight of Thy beauty, give rest unto him whom Thou hast chosen, as Thou art the Lover of mankind.[^1516]

*If thou wilt sing also the other stanzas, look in the Monastic Funeral (see fol. 334);[^1517] but we have set down here as it is in the Euchologion of the Most Holy Patriarch Meletios, without alteration.[^1518] Tone 2:*

*Tone 2:*
Woe is me! What a struggle the soul undergoes as it is parted from the body! Woe is me! How many tears it sheds then and there is none to have mercy upon it! Lifting its eyes unto the Angels, it prays in vain; stretching out its hands unto men, it has none to help. Therefore, my beloved brethren, having reflected upon our brief life, let us ask of Christ rest for him who is translated, and for our souls great mercy.[^1519]

*Tone 3:*
All human things are vanity, whatsoever abides not after death; riches abide not, nor does glory go down with us; for when death comes upon us, it destroys all these things. Therefore let us cry aloud unto the immortal Christ: Give rest unto him who has been translated from us, where the abode of all who rejoice is found.[^1520]

*Tone 4:*
Where is worldly attachment? Where is the fantasy of transient things? Where is gold and silver? Where is the multitude of servants and the tumult? All are dust, all are ashes, all are a shadow! But come, let us cry aloud unto the immortal King: O Lord, vouchsafe Thy eternal good things unto him who has been translated from us, and give him rest in the ageless blessedness.[^1521]

*Tone 5:*
I called to mind the Prophet crying aloud: "I am earth and ashes"; and again I looked into the graves and beheld the bare bones, and I said: Who then is this? A king, or a beggar? Or a righteous man, or a sinner? But give rest, O Lord, unto Thy servant with the righteous.[^1522]

*Tone 6:*
My beginning and my substance was Thy creative command; for wishing to fashion me as a living creature from both the invisible and the visible natures, Thou didst form my body from the earth, and gavest me a soul by Thy divine and life-creating breathing. Therefore, O Savior, give rest unto Thy servant in the land of the living and in the tabernacles of the righteous.[^1523]

*Tone 7:*
Having created man in the beginning according to Thine image and likeness, Thou didst place him in paradise to have dominion over Thy creatures. But deceived by the envy of the devil, having partaken of the food, he became a transgressor of Thy commandments; therefore Thou didst sentence him, O Lord, to return again unto the earth whence he was taken, and to ask for rest.[^1524]

*Tone 8:*
I weep and I lament when I contemplate death, and behold our beauty, fashioned according to the image of God, lying in the graves, formless, inglorious, having no shape. O wonder! What is this mystery that has befallen us? How have we been surrendered unto corruption, and how have we been yoked unto death? Truly by God's command, as it is written, Who grants rest unto the departed.[^1525]

*Then the Beatitudes, Tone 6:*[^1526]
*Remember us when Thou comest in Thy Kingdom.*
*Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.*
*Blessed are they that mourn, for they shall be comforted.*
*Blessed are the meek, for they shall inherit the earth.*
*Blessed are they that hunger and thirst after righteousness, for they shall be filled.*
*Blessed are the merciful, for they shall obtain mercy.*

*Troparion:*
Thou didst make the thief a citizen of paradise, O Christ, when he cried aloud to Thee upon the cross, "Remember me!", by reason of his repentance beforehand; vouchsafe also me, the unworthy one.[^1527]

*Blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall see God.*
*Troparion:*
O Thou Who rulest over souls and bodies, in Whose hands is our breath the consolation of the sorrowful: give rest in the land of the living unto Thy servant whom Thou hast translated.[^1528]

*Blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called sons of God.*
*Troparion:*
May Christ give thee rest in the land of the living, and open unto thee the gates of paradise, and reveal thee as a citizen of the Kingdom, and grant thee remission of the sins which thou hast committed in life, O lover of Christ.[^1529]

*Blessed are they that are persecuted for righteousness' sake, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.*
*Troparion:*
Let us go forth and behold in the graves how man has become bare bones, food for worms and a stench; and let us learn what riches were, and beauty, might, and comeliness.[^1530]

*Blessed are ye when they shall revile you, and persecute you, and say all manner of evil against you falsely for My sake.*

*Troparion:*
When Thou shalt come upon the clouds in Thy glory, O Christ, to judge the living and the dead, vouchsafe also him then to meet Thee with joy.[^1531]

*Rejoice and be exceedingly glad, for great is your reward in heaven.*
*Troparion:*
Establish with all the saints and righteous ones, O Word, him whom Thou hast translated in faith from temporal things, that we may glorify Thee.[^1532]

*Glory to the Father and to the Son and to the Holy Spirit.*
*Troparion:*
By reason of unoriginate begetting and proceeding, I worship the Father Who begat, I glorify the Son Who was begotten, and I hymn the Holy Spirit Who shone forth with the Father and the Son.[^1533]

*Now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.*
*Theotokion:*
How dost thou pour forth milk from thy breasts, O Virgin? How dost thou nourish the Nourisher of creation? Even as He Himself knows[^1534] He Who brought forth water from the rock, streams of water for the thirsty people, as it is written.[^1535]

*Prokeimenon, Tone 6:* Blessed is the way wherein thou walkest today, for a place of rest has been prepared for thee.[^1536]
*Verse:* Unto Thee, O Lord, will I call.[^1537]

*Epistle: The Reading is from the Epistle of Paul to the Thessalonians:*[^1538]
Brethren, I would not have you to be ignorant concerning them that are asleep, that ye sorrow not, even as others who have no hope. For if we believe that Jesus died and rose again, even so them also that sleep in Jesus will God bring with Him. For this we say unto you by the word of the Lord, that we who are alive and remain unto the coming of the Lord shall not precede them that are asleep. For the Lord Himself shall descend from heaven with a shout, with the voice of the archangel, and with the trumpet of God; and the dead in Christ shall rise first; then we who are alive and remain shall be caught up together with them in the clouds, to meet the Lord in the air; and so shall we ever be with the Lord.[^1539]

*Alleluia. Blessed is he whom Thou hast chosen and taken, O Lord.*[^1540]

*Gospel according to John:*[^1541]
The Lord said unto the Jews who came unto Him: Truly, truly, I say unto you, he that hears My word, and believes on Him that sent Me, has everlasting life, and shall not come into judgment, but is passed from death unto life. Truly, truly, I say unto you, the hour is coming, and now is, when the dead shall hear the voice of the Son of God; and they that hear shall live. For as the Father has life in Himself, so has He given to the Son to have life in Himself; and has given Him authority to execute judgment also, because He is the Son of Man. Marvel not at this; for the hour is coming in which all that are in the graves shall hear the voice of the Son of God, and shall come forth: they that have done good, unto the resurrection of life; and they that have done evil, unto the resurrection of judgment.[^1542] I can of Mine own self do nothing; as I hear, I judge and My judgment is just; because I seek not Mine own will, but the will of the Father Who sent Me.[^1543]

> **Deacon:** ""
Have mercy on us, O God, according to Thy great mercy:
Again we pray for the repose of the soul of the departed servant of God, [Name], and that he may be forgiven every transgression, both voluntary and involuntary;
That the Lord God may establish his soul where the righteous rest;
The mercies of God, the heavenly kingdom, and the remission of his sins, let us ask of Christ, the Immortal King and our God.[^1544]

*And upon the conclusion thereof, the first among the fathers, or the presiding hierarch, says the prayer:* O God of spirits and of all flesh *with a loud voice, having approached near to the relics; likewise also all the priests who are with him.*

*And it is to be known that while each litany is said by the deacon, for as long as the supplication is said by him, each of the priests who is present says the written prayer secretly according to his rank near the relics, and makes the exclamation:*

> **Priest:** "For Thou art the resurrection and the life..."

*In this manner it is said with a loud voice by the first priest, or the hierarch, as was stated above.*

*And the spiritual father reads this prayer over the deceased:*[^1545]

In the Name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, and of our Most Holy Lady the Theotokos and Ever-Virgin Mary, and of the holy heavenly Hosts, of the honorable Prophet, Forerunner, and Baptist John, and of the holy all-laudable Apostles, and of the holy three hundred and eighteen Fathers who were in Nicaea.[^1546] For the Lord, having commanded His Apostles, said: "If men sin against you seventy times seven, forgive them, that they may be forgiven in heaven; whatsoever ye shall loose on earth shall be loosed in heaven."[^1547] Therefore, according to the commandment of the Lord and God and our Savior Jesus Christ, I also, the priest, [Name], forgive thee, my spiritual child, [Name], that thou mayest be forgiven in this world and in that which is to come, when the righteous Judge shall come to judge the living and the dead. For unto Him is due all glory, honor, and worship, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.[^1548]

*After this takes place the Last Kiss:*[^1549]

*And we sing the following Stichera. Tone 2, Podoben: "When from the Tree" (Е҆гда̀ ѿ дрѣ́ва тѧ̀):*[^1550]

*Sticheron 1:* Come, brethren, let us give the last kiss unto the deceased, praising God; for behold, he has departed from his kindred and hastens unto the grave, no longer caring for vain things and the much-toiling flesh. Where are now kinsfolk and friends? Behold, we are parted! For him who has departed, let us pray unto the Lord that He may give him rest.[^1551]

*Sticheron 2:* What parting is this, O brethren! What weeping, what lamentation in the present hour! Come therefore, kiss him who a little while ago was with us. For he is delivered unto the grave; he is covered with stones; he dwells in darkness; he is buried with the dead. But all we who are kinsfolk and friends are now parted! For him who has departed, let us pray unto the Lord that He may give him rest.[^1552]

*Sticheron 3:* Now is all the deceitful triumph of vain life dissolved; for the spirit has departed from its tabernacle; the clay has blackened; the vessel is shattered: speechless, senseless, dead, motionless! Escorting the departed unto the grave, let us pray unto the Lord to give him rest unto ages.[^1553]

*Sticheron 4:* What is our life? Truly a flower, and a vapor, and morning dew! Come therefore, let us look clearly into the graves: where is bodily beauty? Where is youth? Where are the eyes and the form of the flesh? All have withered like grass, all have vanished! Come, let us fall down before Christ with tears.[^1554]

*Sticheron 5:* Great is the weeping and lamentation, great is the groaning and distress, the parting of the soul! Hades and destruction is the life of temporal things; an unsubstantial shadow, a deceitful dream, unseasonably imagining, labor unto earthly life! Far off let us flee from the world and from every sin, that we may inherit the heavens.[^1555]

*Sticheron 6:* Beholding him lying dead before us, let us take the image of the final hour; for behold, he departs like smoke from the earth, he has withered like a flower, he has been mown down like grass, wrapped in grave-cloths, covered with earth. Leaving the departed unseen, let us pray unto Christ to give him rest unto ages.[^1556]

*Sticheron 7:* Come, ye that are of the race of Adam, let us behold him who is laid in the earth, who is according to our likeness: he has put off all comeliness, dissolved in the grave, wasted away by the stench of worms in darkness, covered with earth! Leaving the departed unseen, let us pray unto Christ to give him rest unto ages.[^1557]

*Sticheron 8:* When the soul is about to be violently snatched from the body by fearsome angels, it forgets all kinsfolk and acquaintances, and takes thought for appearing before the judgment seat that is to come. O the vanity and the much-toiling flesh! Then, entreating the Judge, let us all pray for the departed, that the Lord may forgive him the deeds he has done.[^1558]

*Sticheron 9:* Come unto the grave, O brethren, let us see the ashes and dust from which we were created! Whither go we now? What indeed have we become? Who is the poor man, or who the rich? Or who is the master, and who the free? Are not all dust? The beauty of the countenance has rotted, and death has withered all the flower of youth.[^1559]

*Sticheron 10:* Truly vanity and corruption are all the sweet and glorious things of life! For all of us vanish, all of us die: kings and princes, judges and the mighty, rich and poor, and all human nature. For now those who once were in life are laid in the tombs: whom let us pray unto the Lord to give rest.[^1560]

*Sticheron 11:* All the bodily instruments are now seen to be idle, which a little while before were active; all are inactive, dead, insensate. For the eyes have closed, the feet are bound, the hands have fallen still, and hearing with them; and the tongue is locked in silence, delivered unto the grave. Truly[^1561] all human things are vanity!

*Theotokion:* Save those that hope in thee, O Mother of the unwaning Sun, O Birthgiver of God! By thy prayers ask of the all-good God, we pray, to give rest unto him who has now been translated, where the souls of the righteous repose. Show him forth as an heir of divine good things in the courts of the righteous, in everlasting memory, O all-immaculate one.[^1562]

*Glory... Tone 6:*[^1563]

*Doxastikon:* Beholding me lying before you speechless and breathless, weep for me, all ye brethren and friends, and kinsfolk and acquaintances! For yesterday I conversed with you, and suddenly the fearsome hour of death came upon me.

But come, all ye that love me, and kiss me with the last kiss; for no longer shall I walk with you or converse henceforth. For I depart unto the Judge, where there is no respect of persons: for slave and master stand together, king and soldier, rich and poor, in equal dignity; for each from his own deeds shall either be glorified or put to shame. But I ask and beseech all, unceasingly to pray for me unto Christ God, that I may not be appointed according to my sins unto the place of torment, but that He may appoint me where is the light of life.[^1564]

*Both now... Theotokion:*[^1565]

*Theotokion:* By the prayers of Her that bare Thee, O Christ, and of Thy Forerunner, of the Apostles, Prophets, and Hierarchs, of the Venerable and Righteous, and of all the Saints, give rest unto Thy reposed servant.[^1566]

*Then the Trisagion. All-Holy Trinity. Our Father. For Thine is the kingdom. And the Troparia: "With the spirits of the righteous..." and the rest. The litany by the deacon. The general prayer. And after the exclamation: Glory... Both now... The Dismissal:*[^1567]

May He Who rose from the dead, Christ our true God, through the prayers of His all-pure Mother, of the holy, glorious, and all-praised Apostles, of our venerable and God-bearing Fathers, and of all the Saints: [appoint] the soul of His servant who has been translated from us[^1568] in the tabernacles of the righteous; give him rest in the bosom of Abraham, number him among the righteous, and have mercy upon us, as He is good and the Lover of mankind. Amen.[^1569]

Eternal memory unto thee, O our brother worthy of blessedness and everlasting memory! *(Thrice)*

*And having thus taken the remains, we depart unto the grave, singing: "Holy God..." and the rest. And the remains are laid in the grave. And the priest, having taken earth upon a shovel in the form of a cross, casts it upon the remains, saying:*

The earth is the Lord's, and the fullness thereof; the world, and all that dwell therein.

*And then he pours oil upon the remains from a lamp, or ashes from the censer. And thus according to*[^1570] custom they close the grave, while these Troparia are being said: "With the spirits of the righteous..." and all the rest, and the Dismissal.[^1571]

Glory to God Who has thus been well pleased.

*End of the Funeral Sequence for Laymen.*[^1572]

*[Fol. 264v — Vacat]*[^1573] [Woodcut headpiece: Christ in the Tomb (The Man of Sorrows / Akra Tapeinosis), surrounded by Renaissance foliage and cherubs]

# PART XXII: PRAYERS OF ABSOLUTION FOR EVERY CURSE AND EXCOMMUNICATION OVER THE DEPARTED [^1574]

*Read by a hierarch, or out of necessity by a spiritual father, if there be no hierarch.*

*It is befitting to know that the present prayers are read in this manner:*

*At the Proskomedia, all the priests who intend to celebrate the Liturgy read these prayers with compunction. And at the Great Entrance, when the priests have gone outside the altar with the Holy Gifts and are standing there*[^1575] the hierarch, having bent his knees, proclaims these prayers aloud with compunction and tears. And after having completed these, rising up, he receives the Holy Gifts.[^1576]

> **Deacon:** "Let us pray to the Lord."

> **Hierarch:** "O Lord our God, Who by Thine ineffable wisdom hast fashioned man from the dust, and hast formed him in beauty and fair appearance, and hast adorned him as a precious and heavenly possession, unto the doxology and majesty of Thy glory and kingdom, bringing him into being according to Thine image and likeness; and when he transgressed the commandment of Thy bidding, having partaken of the image and not preserved it, and on this account, that evil might not be immortal[^1577] in Thy love for mankind Thou hast commanded this composition and mingling, and this Thine ineffable bond, as God, by divine spiritual will to be severed and dissolved: for the soul indeed to depart thither whence it received its being, even unto the general resurrection;[^1578] and for the body to be dissolved into those things from which it was composed. On this account do we pray unto Thee, the unoriginate Father, and unto Thine Only-begotten Son, and unto Thy Most-holy and consubstantial and life-creating Spirit: that Thou despise not Thine own creation, that it be swallowed up by perdition, but for the body to be dissolved into those things from which it was composed[^1579] and for the soul to be numbered in the assembly of the righteous.[^1580] Yea, O Lord our God, let Thine immeasurable mercy and ineffable love for mankind overcome [all]: and if under the curse of a father or mother, or fallen under his own curse, this Thy servant has fallen; or having embittered someone of the consecrated [clergy], and from him received an indissoluble bond; or having fallen into heavy excommunication from a hierarch, concerning which he was neglectful, and abiding in slothfulness, did not obtain forgiveness: do Thou forgive him through me, Thy sinful and unworthy servant; and the body indeed of this man, do Thou dissolve into those things from which it was composed, and the soul[^1581] do Thou order in the tabernacles of the saints. Yea, O Lord our God, Who didst give unto supreme Peter this authority, to grant remission of sins, and didst say: "Whatsoever ye shall bind and loose, let them be bound and loosed," and through them hast bestowed this authority also upon us sinners: do Thou loose Thy departed servant, [Name], from soul and bodily sin;[^1582] and let him be forgiven in the present age, and in the future: by the prayers of Thy Most-pure and Ever-Virgin Mother, and of all Thy saints. Amen."[^1583]

*Second Prayer, for the same:*[^1584]

> **Deacon:** "Let us pray to the Lord."

**Hierarch [or Priest]:** O Master, plenteous in mercy, Lord Jesus Christ our God, Who didst build Thy Church upon the chief of Thy disciples and apostles, Peter, and didst give unto him the keys of the Kingdom of Heaven, and by Thy grace wast pleased that all authority should be given him, so that whatsoever things are bound by him should be bound also in heaven, and whatsoever things are loosed by him upon earth should likewise be loosed in heaven; and Who by Thine ineffable love for mankind hast deemed us, Thy humble and unworthy servants, worthy to be successors of the authority given unto him, so that we also likewise might bind[^1585] and loose the things that befall among Thy people: do Thou Thyself, O all-good King, also through me, Thy humble and unprofitable servant, forgive Thy servant [Name], if in the present life he has sinned anything as a man; and remit unto him whatsoever he has sinned in word, or in deed, or in thought;[^1586] having loosed also the bond lying upon him in whatsoever manner, wherewith he bound himself through haughtiness or through any other cause; whether from a hierarch, or from anyone else, through the envy and cooperation of the evil one, he suffered such a slip[^1587] do Thou be well pleased, as the only good and plenteous in mercy, for his soul indeed to be numbered with the saints who from the age have been well-pleasing unto Thee, and for the body to be given unto nature created by Thee: for blessed and glorified art Thou unto the ages. Amen.[^1588]

[Woodcut tailpiece: stylized foliate vignette][^1589] [Woodcut headpiece: Renaissance foliate strapwork with tritons holding clubs and serpents, flanked by birds]

# PART XXIII: THE ORDER FOR BURIAL ON HOLY PASCHA AND THROUGHOUT BRIGHT WEEK [^1590]

*IT IS BEFITTING TO KNOW:*

*If anyone departs unto the Lord on Holy Pascha, or on any day of Bright Week until Thomas Sunday, nothing customary for the departed is sung over him, but only [the priest] begins:*[^1591]

> **Priest:** **Blessed is our God.**

*And we sing: "Christ is risen," in Tone 5, both choirs with its verses. And the priest censes according to the rule. And immediately he begins the Canon of Pascha:* **"The Day of Resurrection,"** *in order, as many as he wishes, to 4. [After each] ode, the little litanies of the deacon, and the exclamation:*

> **Priest:** **For Thou art the Resurrection and the Life** *Then:* **"Preventing the morning..."** *And again the Canon in order. After the 6th Ode, the little litanies of the deacon, [and] the exclamation:* **"For Thou art the Resurrection and the Life..."** *Then the Kontakion:* **"With the saints give rest..."** *The Oikos:* **"Thou Thyself alone art immortal..."**[^1592] *And instead of the Trisagion:* **"As many of you as were baptized into Christ..."** *The Epistle: In the Acts, the one appointed for that day. Alleluia in the [appointed] tone. The Gospel: The Resurrection Gospel, the first. And after this:* **"Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ..."** *and the remaining odes of the Canon, and the kissing of the departed, while saying: "Christ is risen."*[^1593] *And after the completion of the Canon and the kissing, we say the Exapostilarion:* **"Having fallen asleep in the flesh..."** *twice. Afterward we sing:* **"Blessed art Thou[^1594] O Lord, teach me Thy statutes: The assembly of the Angels..."** *Then the Stichera of Pascha with their verses:* **"Glory... Both now... The Day of Resurrection,"** *and:* **"Christ is risen,"** *thrice.*[^1595] *Afterward the litanies of the deacon, and the exclamation:*

> **Priest:** **For Thou art the Resurrection and the Life...**

*Then the Prayer of Absolution, and the Dismissal. And they bury the departed with thanksgiving and with joy.*[^1596]

# PART XXIV: THE ORDER FOR THE BURIAL OF AN INFANT [^1598]

> **Priest:** **Blessed is our God.**

*Then the Trisagion. All-Holy Trinity. After "Our Father...":*[^1599]

> **Priest:** **For Thine is the Kingdom...**

*Lord, have mercy (12 times). "Come, let us worship..." (thrice). Then:*

*Psalm 19:*[^1600]

The Lord hear thee in the day of affliction; the Name of the God of Jacob defend thee. May He send thee help from the sanctuary, and protect thee out of Zion. May He remember all thy sacrifice, and may thy whole burnt offering be made fat. May the Lord grant thee according to thine heart, and fulfill all thy counsel. We will rejoice in Thy salvation, and in the Name of the Lord our God will we be magnified. The Lord fulfill all thy petitions. Now have I known that the Lord has saved His Anointed: He will hear Him from His holy heaven; in mighty deeds is the salvation of His right hand. Some [glory] in chariots, and some in horses: but we will call upon the Name of the Lord our God. They were tripped up and fell, but we have risen and are set upright. O Lord, save the king, and hear us in the day whensoever we call upon Thee.[^1601]

*Psalm 141:*[^1602]

With my voice unto the Lord have I cried, with my voice unto the Lord have I made supplication. I will pour out before Him my prayer, and my affliction before Him will I declare. When my spirit was fainting within me, then Thou knewest my paths. In this way wherein I walked have they hidden a snare for me. I looked upon the right hand and beheld, and there was none that knew me. Flight perished from me, and there is none that seeks after my soul. I cried unto Thee, O Lord; I said: Thou art my hope, my portion art Thou in the land of the living. Attend unto my prayer, for I am brought very low. Deliver me from them that persecute me, for they are stronger than I.[^1603]

Bring my soul out of prison, that I may give thanks unto Thy Name. The righteous wait for me, until Thou shalt recompense me.[^1604]

*Psalm 27:*[^1605]

Unto Thee, O Lord, will I cry; O my God, be not silent from me: lest at any time Thou be silent from me, and I become like them that go down into the pit. Hear, O Lord, the voice of my supplication, when I pray unto Thee, when I lift up my hands toward Thy holy temple. Draw me not away with sinners, and destroy me not with the workers of iniquity: who speak peace with their neighbors, but evils are in their hearts. Give them, O Lord, according to their deeds and according to the wickedness of their endeavors. According to the works of their hands give Thou unto them; render their recompense unto them. Because they regarded not the works of the Lord, nor the works of His hands: Thou shalt destroy them, and not build them up. Blessed is the Lord, because He has heard the voice of my supplication. The Lord is my helper and my protector; in Him my heart hoped, and I was helped: and my flesh flourished again, and willingly will I give thanks unto Him. The Lord is the strength of His people, and He is the saving protector of His Anointed. Save Thy people, and bless Thine inheritance: and shepherd them, and lift them up unto the age.[^1606]

*We sing: "Glory... Both now"*[^1607] *Trisagion. All-Holy Trinity. After "Our Father...":*

> **Priest:** **For Thine is the Kingdom...**

*And the Troparion, Tone 2:*[^1608]

Remember, O Lord, as Thou art good, Thy servant, and whatsoever he has sinned in life, forgive: for none is without sin, save only Thou Who art able to grant rest unto the departed.

*Theotokion:*[^1609]

Holy Mother of the ineffable Light, honoring thee with angelic hymns, we sing unto thee and magnify thee.

*Then the Kontakion:* **With the saints give rest...**[^1610]

*The priest's exclamation:*

> **Priest:** **For holy art Thou, O our God...**

*And we sing:* **Holy God...**

*Prokeimenon, Tone 6:*

> **Reader:** **Blessed is the way wherein thou walkest [today], O soul.**

*Verse:* **Return, O my soul, unto thy rest.**

*Epistle: The reading from the Epistle of Paul to the Corinthians:*

> **Reader:** "Brethren, not all flesh is the same flesh: but there is one indeed of men, another flesh of beasts, another of fish, and another of birds. There are also celestial bodies, and bodies terrestrial: but the glory of the celestial is one, and the glory of the terrestrial is another. There is one glory of the sun, and another glory of the moon, and another glory of the stars: for star differs from star in glory. So also is the resurrection of the dead: it is sown in corruption, it is raised in incorruption. It is sown in dishonor, it is raised in glory. It is sown in weakness, it is raised in power. It is sown a natural body, it is raised a spiritual body."[^1611]

There is a natural body, and there is a spiritual body. And so it is written: The first man Adam was made a living soul; the last Adam was made a life-giving spirit.[^1612]

*Alleluia.*[^1613]

*Verse:* **Blessed is he whom Thou hast chosen and taken, O Lord.**

*Verse:* **His soul shall dwell among good things.**

*The Gospel according to John:*

> **Priest:** "The Lord said unto the Jews who came unto Him: I am the bread of life: he who comes to Me shall not hunger, and he who believes in Me shall never thirst. But I said unto you, that ye also have seen Me, and believe not. All that the Father gives Me shall come to Me and him that comes to Me I will in no wise cast out. For I came down from heaven, not to do Mine own will, but the will of the Father Who sent Me. And this is the will of the Father Who sent Me, that of all which He has given Me I should lose nothing, but should raise it up at the last day."[^1614]

*Then the litany:*

> **Deacon:** **Have mercy on us, O God...** *and the rest. And the prayer:* **O God of spirits...** *The exclamation:* **For Thou art the Resurrection and the Life...** *(see fol. 230)*[^1615]

*After this the priest says this prayer:*[^1616]

> **Deacon:** "Let us pray to the Lord."

> **Priest:** "O Lord Who guardest infants in the present life, and in the age to come hast prepared for them the spacious bosom of Abraham, and according to their purity the angelic radiant places wherein the souls of the righteous dwell: do Thou Thyself, O Master Christ, receive in peace the soul of Thy servant, the infant, [Name]. For Thou Thyself hast said: "Of such is the Kingdom of Heaven." For unto Thee is due all glory, honor, and worship, with the Father and the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen."[^1617]

*Then also the Dismissal.*[^1618]

# PART XXV: THE ORDER OF THE FUNERAL SINGING FOR ALL DEPARTED FATHERS AND OUR BRETHREN, AND OTHER DECEASED CHRISTIANS (THE PARASTAS) [^1619]

*The ranking priest, or the hegumen himself, with all the priests who are found there, go into the altar; and all the priests vest themselves in phelonia, and the deacons in sticharia. And having taken the censer with incense, the hegumen himself begins:*[^1620]

> **Priest:** **Blessed is our God.**[^1621]

*And we say the Trisagion. All-Holy Trinity. "Our Father...":*

> **Priest:** **For Thine is the Kingdom...**

*Lord, have mercy (12 times). "Come, let us worship..." (thrice). Then Psalm 90: "He that dwells in the help of the Highest..." (see fol. 231).*[^1622]

*Glory... Both now... Alleluia (thrice) in Tone 8. And we sing the Troparion in the same tone:*[^1623]

*Troparion, Tone 8:*

O Thou Who by the depth of wisdom in love for mankind dost order all things, and dost dispense unto all that which is profitable, O only Creator: give rest, O Lord, unto the soul of Thy servant; for on Thee have they set their hope, on our Creator and Fashioner and God.

*Glory...*

For on Thee have they set their hope, on our Creator and Fashioner and God.

*Both now Theotokion, Tone 8:*[^1624]

Thee we have as a city and a haven, and an acceptable intercessor before God Who was born of thee, O unwedded Mother of God, the salvation of the faithful.

*Then the usual diaconal petitions, and the prayer:* **O God of spirits...** *together, all the priests.*[^1625]

*Then we sing the Blameless according to their order, until we arrive at the verse which is:*

**Unto the ages I will not forget Thy statutes, for in them Thou hast given me life.**

*We say it, singing it thrice. Then again the priest says the usual diaconal petitions, and the prayer, together all [the priests]. Then we complete the Blameless unto the end according to their order, and with their troparia, even as thou hast in the layman's burial, all in order.*[^1626]

*(See fol. 232).* *Then again the diaconal petitions and the prayer. Afterwards Psalm 50:* **Have mercy on me, O God...**[^1627]

*Canon for the Departed, Tone 8. Ode 1.*[^1628]

*Heirmos:* **Having traversed the water as upon dry land...**

*Troparion [Martyrikon]:*

Through the death of Christ, and emulating His holy passions, all the venerable martyrs attained unto the divine and blessed life.

*Troparion:*

Overlooking the sins of youth and passing by transgressions, O Christ Savior, number Thy servant who has fallen asleep before with Thine elect.

*Glory...*

*Troparion:*

Unto him that has obtained glory and joy, having acquired a blessed life, grant richly unto Thy servant whom Thou hast taken, O Plenteous in mercy.[^1629]

*Both now...*

*Theotokion:*

Thou didst conceive the Father's Word, hypostatically united unto the flesh, Who came forth from thee, O all-spotless Maiden, and by divine power abolished Hades.

*Ode 3. Heirmos:* **Of the heavenly vault...**[^1630]

*Troparion [Martyrikon]:*

Cleansed from the ancient ancestral fall by baptism and rebirth, and sprinkled with the streams of their own blood, the blessed [martyrs] reign with Christ.

*Troparion:*

O Savior, Who of Thine own will wast laid dead in a tomb, and dost raise up them that dwell in the tombs: be well pleased that he whom Thou hast taken from us should dwell in the tabernacles of Thy saints.

*Glory Troparion:*[^1631]

Implored by Thy divine compassion, O Master, and by Thy consubstantial innate goodness: grant remission of sins unto Thy servant, and give him rest with Thyself.

*Both now...*

*Theotokion:*

Incarnate from thy womb and having become man, He that is pre-eminently the Lover of mankind saves man from the gates of death, O all-pure Mother of God, who alone art lauded.

*Katavasia [Heirmos]:*[^1632]

**Celestial vault's supreme Creator, O Lord, and Builder of the Church: do Thou confirm me in Thy love, Thou pinnacle of desires and confirmation of the faithful, O only Lover of mankind.**

*Then the diaconal petitions, and the prayer:* **O God of spirits...** *After this, the Sessional Hymn, Tone 5:*

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 5:*[^1633]

Give rest, O our Savior, with the righteous unto Thy servant, and settle him in Thy courts, even as it is written: overlooking, as Thou art good, his sins, both voluntary and involuntary, and all things known and unknown, O Lover of mankind.

*Glory...*

And all things known and unknown, O Lover of mankind.

*Both now... Theotokion:*

Thou Who didst shine forth from the Virgin unto the world, O Christ God, and through her didst reveal [us as] sons of light: have mercy on us.

*Ode 4. Heirmos:* **Thou art my Lord, O Christ, Thou art also my strength...**[^1634]

*Troparion [Martyrikon]:*

That they might behold Thy glory, O Master, and brightly obtain in heaven the rays of Thy light-giving [splendor], the divine martyrs endured every manner of torment singing unto Thee, O Christ: "Glory to Thy power, O Lover of mankind!"[^1635]

*Troparion:*

Many mansions are with Thee, O Savior, apportioned unto all according to dignity, according to the measure of virtues: be well pleased, therefore, O Compassionate One, that he who has faithfully departed, piously crying unto Thee: "Glory to Thy power, O Lover of mankind!", should fill these.

*Glory...*

*Troparion:*[^1636]

Having appeared as a man like unto us, O Immortal One, Thou didst manifestly endure death for all, and showedst the path unto life. As the Lover of mankind, vouchsafe unto him that has departed, granting remission of sins as Master, and bestowing communion in [Thy] light.

*Both now Theotokion:*[^1637]

Thou art the boast of the faithful, O unwedded Bride; thou art the protectress, thou art also the refuge of Christians, a wall and a haven. Thou bearest supplications unto Thine own Son, O all-spotless one, and savest from perils those who with faith and love know thee as pure Mother of God.

*Ode 5. Heirmos:* **Why hast Thou cast me away...**[^1638]

*Troparion:*

Having had compassion, vouchsafe him that has departed unto immortal life to partake of Thine ineffable glory, and of Thy beatitudes which are beyond word, in the tabernacles of the righteous, where the voice of them that feast is beautiful, O only Lover of mankind.

*Troparion:*

Where the angelic ranks and the assemblies of the righteous rejoice, in the bosom of Abraham settle Thy servant, O Savior; and be well pleased that he stand with boldness before the dread and divine throne, O Compassionate One.[^1639]

*Glory...*

*Troparion:*

Thou didst appear unto us as purification, righteousness, and redemption; and by Thy stripe Thou hast healed our weakness. Do Thou Thyself, therefore, O Compassionate One, as Thou art good, establish him that has departed in the delight of paradise.

*Both now...*

*Theotokion:*[^1640]

Mercifully, O Merciful One, Thou didst assume the measure of humanity, Who art adorned with the exceeding heights of divine glory: taking unto Thyself from virginal loins an animate flesh, whereby Thou didst destroy death.

*Ode 6. Heirmos:* **Cleanse me, O Savior, for many** *Troparion [Martyrikon]:*

Thy martyrs, O Savior, endured many torments, their souls having been wounded with Thy love, O Holy One,[^1641] desiring Thine everlasting glory and the sweet communion of Thyself.

*Troparion:*

Thou didst rend asunder the hostile womb of death, O Savior, and didst raise up all the prisoners therein, bestowing life; vouchsafe the same, O Benefactor,[^1642] unto him that has been translated.

*Glory...*

*Troparion:*

Deliver Thy servant from the tears and sighing in Hades, O Savior; for as Thou alone art compassionate, Thou hast taken away every tear from every face of them that faithfully bless Thee.[^1643]

*Both now...*

*Theotokion:*

He Who by nature is the Creator is fashioned in thy womb; as God, being emptied, O all-spotless one, the only Immortal One dies by death for the salvation of all.[^1644]

*Katavasia [Heirmos]:*[^1645]

**Cleanse me, O Savior, for many are my iniquities, and lead me up from the depth of evils, I pray Thee; for unto Thee have I cried, and give ear unto me, O God of my salvation.**

*The Little Litany:*[^1646]

*Again and again in peace [let us pray to the Lord].*

*Kontakion, Tone 8:*[^1647]

**With the saints give rest, O Lord, unto the soul of Thy servant, where there is neither sickness, nor sorrow, nor sighing, but life everlasting.**

*Ikos:*[^1648]

Thou alone art immortal from the beginning, Who didst make and fashion man but we mortals were fashioned from the earth, and unto the same earth shall we go, even as Thou didst command, Who didst fashion me, and saidst unto me: "Earth thou art, and unto earth shalt thou return"; whither all we mortals depart, making over the tomb the weeping song: Alleluia.[^1649]

*Ode 7. Heirmos:* **The Hebrew children in the furnace...**[^1650]

*Troparion [Martyrikon]:*

All the desire of the martyrs was extended unto the only Master; united unto Him in love, and singing: "Blessed is the God of our fathers!"[^1651]

*Troparion:*

Fill with joy and gladness him whom Thou hast translated, Thy servant, O Compassionate One, having vouchsafed him to cry unto Thee, and to sing: "Blessed is the God of our fathers!"[^1652]

*Glory Troparion:*

Thou grantest unto them that have departed in faith the brightness of the divine Kingdom, bestowing the garment of incorruption on them that cry: "Blessed is the God of our fathers!"[^1653]

*Both now...*

*Theotokion:*

Dissolving the curse of Eve, Thou didst take up Thine abode in the all-spotless Virgin, pouring forth the fountain of blessing unto them that cry: "Blessed is the God of our fathers!"[^1654]

*Ode 8. Heirmos:* **The harmony of musical instruments...**[^1655]

*Troparion [Martyrikon]:*

Having passed through earthly sufferings, the true martyrs received heavenly crowns, crying unto the Savior: "Praise the Lord, all His works, and exalt Him above all unto the ages!"[^1656]

*Troparion:*

Descending into the lowest pit, Thou didst raise up with life-originating hand them that dwell in the tombs; and grantest rest, O Compassionate One, unto Thy servant who in faith has fallen asleep before.[^1657]

*Glory...*

*Troparion:*

As the ever-existing fountain of life, as the torrent of delight,[^1658] Thou waterest Thy servant who in piety has been translated unto Thee, who sings and exalts Thee, O Christ, unto the ages.

*Both now...*

*Theotokion:*

O Virgin Mary, Mother of God, who didst bear in the flesh God, the Savior of men: save them that in faith hymn thy childbearing, and exalt thee unto the ages.[^1659]

*Ode 9. Heirmos:* **Every hearing was affrighted...**[^1660]

*Troparion [Martyrikon]:*

Having unsubdued and unconquerable strength, O martyrs of Christ, ye brought to naught the godless command of the tyrants, and manifestly were vouchsafed the heavenly Kingdom, being illuminated by the rays of the Trinity, O richly blessed ones.[^1661]

*Troparion:*

Bitter Hades was destroyed when Thou didst overthrow it, O Lover of mankind, and didst raise up them that slept there from of old; but even now, as Thou art good, vouchsafe him that has passed over unto Thee, the Merciful One, unto Thy never-setting light.[^1662]

*Glory...*

*Troparion:*

Wholly art Thou sweetness, O Savior, wholly desire and insatiable love in truth; wholly art Thou ineffable beauty.[^1663] Therefore, be well pleased that he who has departed unto Thee should delight in Thy comeliness, and vouchsafe him Thy divine goodness.

*Both now...*

*Theotokion:*

Save me, O Mother of God, who didst bear Christ my Savior, dual in nature but not in hypostasis,[^1664] only-begotten indeed of the Father, and from thee the firstborn of all creation, with Whom we all magnify thee.

*Katavasia [Heirmos]:*[^1665]

**Every hearing was affrighted at the ineffable condescension of God: how the Most High of His own will came down even unto flesh, having become man from the virginal womb; therefore, we the faithful magnify the all-pure Mother of God.**

*Then the Trisagion. All-Holy Trinity. After "Our Father...": Troparia, Tone 4:*[^1666]

**With the spirits of the righteous who have been perfected, give rest to the soul of Thy servant, O Savior, keeping it in the blessed life which is from Thee, O Lover of mankind.**

*Troparion, Tone 4:*

In Thy resting place, O Lord, where all Thy saints repose, give rest unto the soul of Thy servant.[^1667]

*Glory...*

*Troparion, Tone 4:*

Thou art God Who descended into Hades and loosed the bonds of the chained: do Thou give rest to the soul of Thy servant.[^1668]

*Both now...*

*Theotokion, Tone 4:*

O only pure and spotless Virgin, who didst bear God without seed: entreat Him that our souls may be saved.[^1669]

*Then the diaconal petitions:*[^1670]

> **Deacon:** "Have mercy on us, O God, according to Thy great mercy, we pray Thee: give ear and have mercy."

> **Deacon:** "Again we pray for the repose and blessed memory and the remission of sins of the departed servant of God, [Name]..."

> **Deacon:** "...that every transgression, voluntary and involuntary, may be pardoned him;"[^1671]

> **Deacon:** "That the Lord God may establish his spirit where all the righteous repose;"

> **Deacon:** "The mercy of God, and the Kingdom of heaven, and the remission of his sins having asked for him, let us commend ourselves and one another, and all our life unto Christ God."

> **Choir:** "Unto Thee, O Lord."

> **Deacon:** "Let us pray to the Lord."

*Then the priest says the prayer secretly:*[^1672]

> **Priest:** **[O God] of spirits and of all flesh, Who hast trampled down death, and abolished the devil, and given life unto Thy world: do Thou Thyself, O Lord, give rest to the soul of Thy departed servant, [Name], in a place of light...**[^1673]

> **Priest:** **...in a place of verdure, in a place of repose, whence sickness, sorrow, and sighing have fled away; and every transgression committed by him, in word, or deed, or thought, do Thou, as the good God and Lover of mankind, forgive. For there is no man that shall live and not sin against Thee; for Thou alone art without any sin, Thy righteousness is righteousness forever, and Thy word is truth.**[^1674]

*Exclamation:*[^1675]

> **Priest:** **For Thou art the resurrection, and the life, and the repose of Thy departed servant ever to be remembered, [Name], O Christ our God; and unto Thee we send up glory, with Thine unoriginate Father**[^1676] and Thine all-holy and good and life-creating Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.

*Then also the Dismissal:*[^1677]

> **Priest:** **May Christ our true God, Who rose from the dead, through the prayers of His all-pure Mother, by the power of the precious and life-creating Cross, and of all the saints: give rest to the soul of His servant who has been translated from us, [Name], in the abodes of the righteous where the righteous repose; and number him in the bosom of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob; and have mercy on us and save us, for He is good and loves mankind.**[^1678]

*Then all say:*

*How to sing the Memory:*[^1679]

**All:** **Memory eternal unto thee, O ever-to-be-remembered servant of God, our brother, [Name]!**

*We say thus thrice. Then also we depart.*

[Woodcut tailpiece: Renaissance grotesque strapwork cartouche featuring a horned satyr mascaron with foliate flourishes] [Woodcut headpiece: Renaissance foliate strapwork ornament with acanthus foliage and blossoms]
