# PART XXXII: THE ORDER UNTO OUR LORD JESUS CHRIST, CHANTED IN GENERAL DROUGHT AND RAINLESSNESS, AND FOR THE TEMPERAMENT OF THE SEASONS, AND FOR THE DRIVING AWAY OF ADVERSE WINDS, AND AT THE INCURSION OF BARBARIANS [^2300]

[Woodcut decorative typographic tailpiece ornament] (*Woodcut headpiece ornament: Christ as the Man of Sorrows in the Tomb with inscription (*ІС҃ ХС҃*)*)

*The priest says:* Blessed is our God...[^2301]

*Then the Trisagion; Most Holy Trinity; and after Our Father: For Thine is the kingdom...*[^2302]

*Lord, have mercy (12).*[^2303]

*O come, let us worship... thrice.*[^2304]

*Then Psalm 142:* O Lord, hear[^2305] my prayer...

*After this:* God is the Lord...[^2306]

*And these troparia, Tone 6:*

Have mercy on us, O Lord, have mercy on us; for, at a loss for any defense, we sinners offer this supplication unto Thee as Master: have mercy on us, O Lord, have mercy on us.[^2307]

*Glory...*

O Lord, have mercy on us, for in Thee have we hoped; be not exceedingly wroth with us, nor remember our iniquities; but look down even now as Thou art compassionate, and deliver us from our enemies; for Thou art our God, and we are Thy people, and all of us are the work of Thy hands, and we call upon Thy Name.[^2308]

*Both now...*

Open unto us the doors of compassion, O blessed Theotokos; hoping in thee, may we not stumble, but may we be delivered through thee from afflictions; for thou art the salvation of the Christian race.[^2309]

*Then Psalm 50:* Have mercy on me, O God...[^2310]

*Supplication Canon unto our Lord Jesus Christ, whose acrostic is: Receive, O Christ, the common prayers of Thy servants. And in the Theotokia, by Lord Philotheos. Tone 6.*[^2311]

*Ode 1. Tone 6. Heirmos:*
Traversing the deep on foot as on dry land, and beholding the persecutor Pharaoh engulfed, Israel cried: Let us sing a song of victory unto God, for He has been glorified.[^2312]

*Troparion:*
Let us make a common lamentation now, O brethren, every age and order, race and clan, and bitterly sigh together, and make the Creator of all merciful.[^2313]

*Troparion:*
Thou Who out of tender compassion didst of old bring human nature forth from non-being, O Master, redeeming, Thou hast saved them who were imperiled from corruption; even now have mercy on us.[^2314]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst sacredly offer Thine own blood, O Word of God, and dost die as man, being God for our sake; yet we, having forsaken Thy fearful grace, have now been sorely wounded.[^2315]

*Troparion:*
Having cast aside Thy laws and ordinances, outraging Thee, O Christ, with shameless nature, we suffer righteous stripes, since the elements have departed from their natural order.[^2316]

*Theotokion:*
All things are full of terror and trembling and shame, seeing now the righteous wrath of the Master; but make Him merciful unto us, as Thy Son and God, O Lady.[^2317]

*Ode 3. Tone 6. Heirmos:*
There is none holy as Thou, O Lord my God, Who hast exalted the horn of Thy faithful, O Good One, and established them upon the rock of Thy confession.[^2318]

*Troparion:*
Adam, having disobeyed the first commandment, was driven out from Paradise, and from life, and from God; while we, having departed from all things together, are now put to death.[^2319]

*Troparion:*
Wicked Cain appeared of old as an exemplar, having murdered his brother out of evil envy; emulating whom now we all have been condemned to groan and tremble grievously, even as he.[^2320]

*Troparion:*
Fiercely does creation grow stubborn against us, and exceedingly rages, moving the natural impulses, proclaiming unto all the righteous wrath of the Master.[^2321]

*Troparion:*
The brightness of the sun is hidden, O Master Christ, and the flow of accustomed rains is withheld; drought and darkness hold sway; for Thou, the Sun of glory, hast turned away.[^2322]

*Theotokion:*
There is no strength in us, and we all have been stripped of all boldness because of shameful deeds; but do thou, as a pure Mother, appease the Master of all.[^2323]

*Ode 4. Tone 6. Heirmos:*

"Christ is my power, God and Lord," the venerable Church sings in a manner befitting God, crying out from a pure mind, keeping festival in the Lord.[^2324]

*Troparion:*
Today, O Master, is a day of wrath and affliction; and this day is neither day nor night, which now according to the prophets has overtaken all, and there is none who delivers.[^2325]

*Troparion:*
Of old the multiplying cry grievously opened heaven unto the Sodomites; but now, O Master, the multitude of sins righteously shuts it against us.[^2326]

*Troparion:*
The sun is extinguished; contrary to nature, O Master, the clouds have withheld rain; while the earth, groaning, is menacing, foreseeing the wound of its nakedness.[^2327]

*Troparion:*
Having seen, O Lover of mankind, behold the affli- -ction of Thy people; and give heed unto our groaning, send down rain by Thy nod, and rebuke the contrary winds.[^2328]

*Theotokion:*
Without having known travail, before all travails thou didst bear the Master of all, O Lady; therefore, do thou now loose the sorrows of thy people, calming the tempest.[^2329]

*Ode 5. Tone 6. Heirmos:*
With Thy divine light, O Good One, lovingly illumine the souls of them that rise early unto Thee, O Lord, that they may see Thee, the only God, Who deliverest all from the gloom of sins.[^2330]

*Troparion:*
"We are hard-pressed on every side," David cried out, having seen the coming wrath of God; but what shall we do, passion-plagued ones, seeing this and repenting not?[^2331]

*Troparion:*
Even as Thou didst save Thy people of old from Pharaoh, O Good One, suddenly parting the deep, snatch us also from barbarian hands, and having calmed the sea, quiet the winds.[^2332]

*Troparion:*
Stay the distress of floods and the fierce rising of waves and contrary blast of winds; and let rains be stayed by Thy command, and let every slaughter cease, O Lover of mankind.[^2333]

*Troparion:*
A wave of mire and stench of pleasures and sins of every kind has covered us; therefore waves of divine wrath breathe forth, and now vex all.[^2334]

*Theotokion:*
They who of old were delivered through thee, O Lady from death and barbarian corruption, distress and sorrow; now also, we pray, loose these afflictions, for we are thy people and thine exceptional portion.[^2335]

*Ode 6. Tone 6. Heirmos:*
Beholding the sea of life surging with the tempest of temptations, and fleeing to Thy calm haven, I cry unto Thee: Lead up my life from corruption, O Greatly Merciful One.[^2336]

*Troparion:*
Having formerly enslaved themselves to the flesh, the foolish were shamefully delivered unto the flood; imitating whom now, having evilly become carnal, we suffer corruption like unto them.[^2337]

*Troparion:*
Having turned aside from the right path, we ran in crooked ways, having departed from Thy commandments; therefore into the pit of manifold temptations do we fall.[^2338]

*Troparion:*
Look down from on high as a compassionate God; hear the sighings, and give ear unto the tears of Thy people; and despise not the voice of the infants singing unto Thee, O Greatly Merciful One.[^2339]

*Troparion:*
From the mouths of babes of old, O Master, Thou didst marvelously perfect praise; give ear also unto these; therefore receive their supplication, granting recompense unto these praises.[^2340]

*Theotokion:*
Having become the Mother of God, O Lady, thou upholdest all creation radiantly, and especially us, thine own handiwork; therefore make haste and deliver Thy flock from famine and barbarians.[^2341]

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*

The Angel made the furnace dew-yielding unto the holy children, but the command of God consumed the Chaldeans, persuading the tyrant to cry: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers.[^2342]

*Troparion:*
Even as Thou didst loose the famine of the widow, sending Elijah Thy prophet, O Master, so also loose by Thy word the drought and famine for us, as Good One feeding Thy people as is Thy custom: O God of our fathers, blessed art Thou.[^2343]

*Troparion:*
Thy prophet of old raised up the dead son of the Sareptan woman, having bestowed rain upon the scorched earth, O Master; therefore by his prayers give rain now also unto the grievously dried-up earth.[^2344]

*Troparion:*
In the multitude of Thy goodness, O Long-suffering One, having overlooked the sins of all, nourish now Thy city and people; through the prayers of Thine immaculate Mother, swiftly loose for us the grievous evils that hold us fast.[^2345]

*Troparion:*
The angelic choirs entreat Thee, O Lover of mankind: deliver Thy people and city from every sorrow, and cast down the fierce multitude of barbarians, and grant strength against them unto our faithful kings.[^2346]

*Theotokion:*
Show thyself in tribulations, we pray, both deliverer and champion unto those who honor thee, snatching them from trials and evil sorrows and the godless slaughter of the impious by thy mighty hand, O Lady.[^2347]

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*
Out of the flame Thou didst pour forth dew for the holy youths, and didst consume the sacrifice of the righteous one with water; for Thou, O Christ, doest all things whatsoever Thou willest, Whom we exalt supremely unto the ages.[^2348]

*Troparion:*
Let us now humble our haughty disposition, and let us all flee plunder and deceit; let us put away from our soul false oaths, and hate them, that we all may find the Master merciful.[^2349]

*Troparion:*
Having been created rational, we have shown ourselves irrational, having unseemly dishonored the divine image and dignity with shameful deeds; save us, as Thou art compassionate, through the prayers of Thy saints.[^2350]

*Troparion:*
Even as Thou didst formerly save the harlot, O my Christ, and the prodigal, as Thou didst save the thief and many publicans, and as Thou didst save Manasseh when he prayed, O Savior: save all of us also through the prayers of Thy saints.[^2351]

*Troparion:*
The tongues of infants, the young and the old, monks and seculars, we all pray Thee: loose Thy wrath, and rebuke the winds, and grant rain unto the thirsting earth.[^2352]

*Theotokion:*
Wounded all in soul and body because of shameful deeds by plagues from on high, let us run together and fall down before the Lady, that she may appease toward us the Creator of all.[^2353]

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*

More honorable than the Cherubim, and beyond compare more glorious than the Seraphim, who without corruption didst bear God the Word: thee, truly the Mother of God, do we magnify.[^2354]

*Troparion:*
Receive the supplications of those who flee unto thee, as thou art good, and be thou an intercessor for us; stand forth, O Sovereign Lady, and loose our afflictions; for as a Mother thou art able to do all things, O Lady.[^2355]

*The Lady:*
O compassionate Son of Mine, with Thine hands Thou didst raise up these who were dead, and Thou didst feed them with Thine own flesh; Thou didst marvelously make Me a Mother unto these just ones; therefore receive My supplication, O My Word.[^2356]

*The Master:*
What debt, O Mother, dost Thou ask now?

What mercy dost Thou hasten to obtain from Me? These are unworthy of any love of mankind; they have proved false to the divine kinship.[^2357]

*The Lady:*
I know this, O Master and Son; but having repented, they now fall down, as Thou seest; they weep and lament, all lacerating themselves; My womb cannot endure to behold their wounds.[^2358]

*The Master:*
I hear Thee, O Mother, and let the wounds now cease; though they fall down grievously, yet for Thy sake do I now, as is My custom, mercifully bestow this grace upon Thee as My Mother.[^2359]

*The Lady:*
Beyond all speech, O Word, are all Thy deeds: Thine Incarnation, Passion, and awesome deification the great wealth of common repentance, for the sake of which we bow down before Thy glory, O Son.[^2360]

*We chant:* **"It is truly meet..."** *Then:* **"Holy God..."** **"All-holy Trinity..."** *after* **"Our Father..."** *the troparia:* **"Have mercy on us, O Lord, have mercy on us..."** *(see at the beginning of this rule, fol. 398)[^2361]. Then the deacon's litanies:*

> **Deacon:** "Have mercy on us, O God, according to Thy great mercy, we pray Thee: hear and have mercy."[^2362]

> **People:** "Lord, have mercy *(thrice)*."

> **Deacon:** "Again we pray unto the Lord our God: that this place and this holy monastery, and every city and countryside, may be preserved from famine, pestilence, earthquake, flood, from fire and the sword the incursion of aliens, civil strife, and every deadly wound; and that the good and mankind-loving God may be merciful and gracious regarding our sins, and turn away all His righteous wrath moving against us; and that He may rain down upon the earth beneficial rain through His goodness, let us all say: Lord, hear and have mercy."[^2363]

> **People:** "Lord, have mercy *(thrice)*."

*Ecphonesis:*

> **Priest:** "Hear us, O God our Savior, the hope of all the ends of the earth, and of those who are far off upon the sea; O Merciful One, be merciful unto our sins, and have mercy on us: for a merciful and mankind-loving God art Thou, and unto Thee do we send up glory, to the Father and to the Son and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen."[^2364]

*Prayer of the same Lord Philotheos, said in drought, and for the temperament of the seasons, and against contrary winds, and at the incursion of barbarians:*[^2365]

> **Deacon:** *Let us pray to the Lord.*

> **Priest:** ""
O Master, Lord our God, Who by Thy co-essential and unoriginate Word, and Thy life-creating and equally honored Spirit, didst bring all things out of non-existence into being; Who hast placed the sand as a bound for the sea, and hast set the mountains and abysses with a plumb-line; Who hast measured the heaven with a span, and holdest all in Thy fist[^2366] earth; Who hast given measures, and rules, bounds, and compositions, and orders to this sensible creation;[^2367] and the changes of seasons, and solar circuits, and the constitution of the mixture of the elements, holding them unspeakably by Thy nod, governing them unto impassibility and immutability:[^2368] do Thou Thyself, all-good King, receiving again Thy natural and customary love for mankind and goodness toward us, visit the work of Thy hands, and take not away from us Thy mercies and Thy compassions, neither break Thy covenant; Who in an incomprehensible manner didst fashion us according to Thine own image;[^2369] Who didst give Thine only-begotten Son as redemption for us, and through the unspeakable communion of His Godhead didst impart the Spirit unto us: forgive the multitude of our transgressions by the surpassing multitude of Thy compassions; Who by the Cross and Blood of Thy Son didst wash away the sin of our race:[^2370] restore Thine own creation to its natural likeness and order, from our unnatural and evil way of life; show unto us the customary brightness of this great luminary, having dispersed the mist and the darkness oppressing the sun's rays; command the clouds to give rain to the earth in season,[^2371] natural sustenance and suitable [nourishment] unto all the seeds and plantings in it. Rebuke the surging of the sea, and the unnatural movements of the winds; let the stormy blast cease, and let turbulent things turn unto stillness, that those who go down to the sea in ships, and do business in great waters, may again see Thy works and Thy wonders.[^2372] Yea, Master Who lovest mankind, imitating Thine own love for mankind, grant also creation to be reconciled toward us, which rages and surges up against us on account of our disorder and our disregard of Thy commandments, repaying us;[^2373] so that many people may indeed be nourished in this day, knowing Thine only Name, not knowing any other God besides Thee, looking ever unto Thine only hand, Who openest it and fillest every living thing with good pleasure.[^2374] Save, O Lord, Thy servants, our faithful rulers,[^2375] and subdue under them every assault of impending warfare, visible and invisible. Preserve, O Lord, this Thy city, and every city and country, from famine, plague, earthquake, and fire and sword, and from every foreign and soul-corrupting heresy and deception, and every evil:[^2376] by the prayers and supplications of our most blessed Lady the Theotokos, and the God-beholding angels, and all the saints.

Through the good pleasure and goodness of Thine only-begotten Son, with Whom Thou art blessed, together with Thine all-holy and good and life-creating Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.

*Another prayer of the same, said in sudden and terrible death:*[^2377]

> **Deacon:** *Let us pray to the Lord.*

> **Priest:** ""
O Master, Lord our God, Who art the inexhaustible fountain of compassions, the unfathomable depth of love for mankind, the impassable abyss of longsuffering and goodness; Who also, according to generations, bringest down wounds and plagues that befall the human race, for the benefit of well-measured love for mankind;[^2378]

...so that our unrestrained and swift propensity toward sin, being curbed as with a bridle by Thy divine fear, may not move disorderly against the divine image, nor wickedly encroach upon the nobility of the soul:[^2379] stay, we pray Thee, this sharp and untimely weapon of death brought upon our nature; lest Thou make us diminished more than all nations,[^2380] nor let us become a reproach to our intelligible and sensible enemies;[^2381] and lest cities become desolate, and marketplaces be consumed, and sacred assemblies, and feasts, and compositions of divine songs be silenced for the most part and good and great houses, according to the Scripture, are made desolate, and there is no one living in them;[^2382] fear and trembling are come upon us, and the thick and dark gloom of this terrible death has covered all. We have not time, O Master, to weep as is customary for kinsmen who have passed away, and the end overtakes us; we seek others who would weep, and together are we given over to the grave; nor do we who are seen living think that we yet live; by reason of this terrible plague, we scarcely believe even ourselves; each one of us thinks that he has in himself the mark of death and the plagues, and before death we die grievously of fear.[^2383]

This is the appointed reward of our malice; behold, the fitting conclusion of our wicked and unclean deeds; these are the severe corrections for defilement, injustice, and perjury; this three-headed serpent, having plunged bitter teeth into us, has violently brought upon us corruption and death.[^2384] For because of these things, it is said, the wrath of God comes upon the sons of disobedience.[^2385] Therefore we are able neither to lift up the eyes of our mind, nor to pray purely, nor to draw down mercy; weighed down by the burden of conscience, as by certain iron fetters, each of us is distressed.[^2386] But deliver us not over unto the end, for Thy Name's sake, neither break Thy covenant; nor let us, who are subject to passions, be deprived of time for repentance and conversion, for the sake of which Thou hast in Thy love for mankind brought upon us this deadly plague. We know that having many times promised repentance, and many times proved false, we have been condemned to be cut down like the barren fig tree;[^2387] but yet again have patience, O mankind-loving Husbandman; Who willest not the death of a sinner, but rather that he turn and live;[^2388] Who hast commanded that a brother's transgressions be forgiven seventy times seven; Who art able from the hard and barren stone to raise up children unto Abraham;[^2389]

...for unto Thee alone all things are possible which are impossible with men, O Master Who lovest mankind;[^2390] that in us also Thine all-holy Name may be glorified, of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.

*Third prayer of the same Lord Philotheos, in common necessity, concerning repentance:*[^2391]

> **Deacon:** *Let us pray to the Lord.*

> **Priest:** ""
We have sinned, we have committed iniquity, we have done unrighteously before Thee, O all-good Master; we have transgressed Thy saving commandments, and our sacred vows which we made in holy baptism before Thy great altar, before angels and men, we have disregarded[^2392] [counting as common] the fearful blood of the covenant, wherewith we were sanctified, and having insulted the Spirit of grace,[^2393] and having neglected the fearful and venerable adoption of sons. Every Scripture and divine law, and God-inspired teaching, has been accounted among us as a vain beating [of the air], and as mere utterances empty of deeds.[^2394] In name only and in words do we, wretched ones, hold the precious Gospel of true Christianity. Our hands have been diligent unto every rapine and extortion; and our feet swift and insolent, evilly running unto every unrighteousness;[^2395] ready to snatch away the portions of our brethren and to trample upon, and to devour the poor.[^2396] Our mouth, which was an instrument of sacred prayers and of the word, through every uncleanness, and vain talking, and perjury, have we made an instrument of demons. Our eyes and all our senses have we filled with the multitude of fornication and of every defilement, having trodden under foot that divine seed of the mind reigning within us; and having made Thy members, O Christ, members of an harlot,[^2397] instead of a temple of God we have become storehouses of corruption and of every uncleanness.[^2398] Therefore, O all-good Master, have we wretched ones turned Thy great love for mankind into provocation; and the many gifts of Thy goodness have we foolishly converted unto punishments. Whence, having become better neither by the good things done unto us, nor by the afflictions of our neighbors, we have righteously stirred up against ourselves the wounds of Thy righteous chastisement. But rebuke us not in Thine anger, neither chasten us in Thy wrath, O Lord.[^2399] Against Thee only do we sin, yet Thee only also do we worship;[^2400] and with a contrite heart, as a pure sacrifice, do we offer confession unto Thee.[^2401] Relent, O Master Who lovest mankind, stay the wound righteously inflicted; let the multitude of Thy compassions overcome that wicked gathering of our sins; and let the deep of Thy countless goodness cover the bitter sea of our tears. We hold in our hands the image and greatness of Thy love for mankind: the thieves, and the publicans, and the harlots, and the prodigal son, who, surpassing us wretched ones, have gone before us into the heavenly kingdom.[^2402] Along with these accept also us, O Master, who confess Thee and fall down before Thee. And if we fall far short of their complete conversion and the fullness of their repentance, may Thine immeasurable goodness supply what is lacking—or rather, even the whole; since indeed we fall completely short of everything.[^2403]

We offer unto Thee the wailings of the poor, and the voices of infants, the wretched and most simple portion of every age, worthy of Thy compassions and of Thy forgiveness. In addition to this, Thou hast interceding with Thee unto tender-heartedness and mercy: the Cross and the voluntary death which Thou didst endure for us ungrateful ones;[^2404] the apostolic labors, and the venerable, and the ascetics, and the martyrs' blood; and above all, the common hope and salvation of all, who beyond word and without seed gave birth unto Thee.[^2405] Receive their supplications in Thy love for mankind, and deliver us from present evils, and from future eternal torments. By the grace and love for mankind of Thine all-pure Father, with Whom Thou art blessed, together with Thine all-holy and good and life-creating Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.

*Another prayer of the same, in drought:*[^2406]

> **Deacon:** *Let us pray to the Lord.*

> **Priest:** ""
O Master, Lord God, Who didst hear Elijah the Tishbite, zealous for Thee,[^2407] and didst command the rain sent in season upon the earth to be withheld, and then again through his supplication didst grant a fruit-bearing rain unto it:[^2408] do Thou Thyself, O Master of all, entreated by Thine own compassion, grant a willing rain unto Thine inheritance;[^2409] and our transgressions overlook, and send Thy rains upon the places that need them and pray for them, gladdening the face of the earth, for the sake of the poor of Thy people, the infants, and the cattle, and all others; for they wait upon Thee to give them food in due season.[^2410] For Thou art our God, a God to show mercy and to save; and unto Thee do we send up glory, to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.

*Another prayer of the same, in drought:*[^2411]

> **Priest:** ""
O Lord God Almighty, Who bringest up clouds from the ends of the earth, and didst make lightnings for the rain; Who bringest forth the winds out of His treasuries; Who callest the water of the sea, and pourest it out upon the face of all the earth:[^2412] unto Thee do we pray, and Thee do we entreat, confessing our sins, asking of Thee rich mercy. Open the floodgates of heaven;[^2413] command the clouds to rain down rain, having compassion upon all Thy land. Have mercy upon the old, and the young, and the infants sucking the breasts; and upon Thy manservants and maidservants, sons and daughters; and upon all the beasts of the earth:[^2414] Who bringest forth bread for us for food, and green herb for the cattle.[^2415] Receive the supplication of all Thy people, and the sighing of the poor; and rebuke us not in Thine anger, neither chasten us in Thy wrath.[^2416] And destroy not Thy people with famine and thirst; for the eyes of all look unto Thee, to receive food from Thee in due season.[^2417] For in Thee do we hope; besides Thee we know no other; and from Thee do we await rich mercy.

*Exclamation:*
For Thou art a good God Who lovest mankind, and unto Thee do we send up glory, to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.

*By the same Lord Philotheos, prayer 1 in time of earthquake:*[^2418]

> **Deacon:** *Let us pray to the Lord.*

> **Priest:** ""
O holy King, Lord Who lovest mankind, O longsuffering King, O Lord; Who art the Creator of every sensible and intelligible creation;[^2419]

...Who upholdest all things by the word of Thine unspeakable power;[^2420] Who alone hast authority over life and death;[^2421] chastening righteously, and in love for mankind rather showing mercy; Who by Thine all-wise providence pilotest this our temporal life, and on every side fitly orderest our salvation: we know that on account of the multitude of our evil sins Thou hast shaken the earth, and made it to tremble;[^2422] and fear and dread are come upon us from the face of Thy wrath, O Long-suffering One. Our heart is troubled, being wounded by it, and the pain of death is fallen upon us as it is shaken;[^2423] lest at any time it seize [our soul] like a lion our soul, and there be none to deliver;[^2424] lest at any time [the earth] swallow us up, and darkness cover us, while there is none to deliver nor to save. Therefore we make ourselves suppliants unto Thee, and Thee do we entreat, the only God Who art without malice: remember not our former iniquities, nor those that have now occurred;[^2425] neither weigh the heaviness of our sins with an equal recompense.[^2426] For if Thou shouldest enter into judgment with this our race, no one shall be justified before Thee;[^2427] but the remembrance of us all would utterly perish from the earth.[^2428] Remember, O Longsuffering One, Thy compassions and Thy mercies which are from of old;[^2429]

...and of Thy true covenant made with our fathers.[^2430] And let not the depth of the earth swallow us up, neither let her mouth devour us;[^2431] but have compassion upon us who are contrite, and have mercy upon us who are humble; and visit [us who are] held fast by great fear and trembling from the fearful threatening of the earthquake, [and from] confusion. And if there be anywhere even some among us that fear Thy Name and keep Thy commandments,[^2432] a certain small chosen portion, a blessed seed, a hidden treasure, known and preserved unto Thee alone: hear them, as Thou art good, on behalf of us unworthy ones, for the sake of the beneficence of Thy mercy. Receive their supplications offered unto Thee for the people that have sinned, O Master Who lovest mankind; as [Thou didst receive] Abraham on behalf of the Sodomites,[^2433] as [Thou didst receive] Daniel and Jeremiah, Thy divine prophets, who entreated Thy goodness for Israel in captivity:[^2434] that from generation to generation the unfathomable deep of Thy love for mankind may be glorified; that we also may bring unto Thee a thank-offering of our conversion and repentance, being strengthened by Thy mighty hand;[^2435] through the prayers and supplication of Thine all-pure Mother, and of all the saints who from the ages have been well-pleasing unto Thee. Amen.

*By the same holy Lord Philotheos, a prayer to the Most Holy Theotokos, concerning the incursion of enemies,[^2436] and the deliverance of captives:*[^2437]

> **Priest:** ""
As [Thou art] Lady Theotokos,[^2438] who beyond nature and word didst give birth unto the only-begotten God the Word,[^2439] the Creator and Master of every visible and intelligible creation, one Lord of the Trinity, both God and Man;[^2440] the divine receptacle of every holiness and receiver of grace, in Whom dwells the fullness of the Godhead bodily,[^2441] by the good pleasure of God the Father and the cooperation of the Holy Spirit;[^2442] who wast chosen out of all creation, and by Godlike dignity ineffably surpassest and transcendest [all things]: the glory and food and unspeakable gladness of the angels, [the joy] of the Church, the crown of the apostles and prophets, the marvelous and all-lauded courage of the martyrs, who art the cause of their contest and victories, and the all-pure mediatress of their everlasting crowns of suffering and of their Godlike recompense; the honor and glory of the venerable ascetics; who art the unerring teacher of the way of stillness;[^2443] the door of revelations of spiritual mysteries; O fountain of light; the inexhaustible river of mercy; the unfathomable sea of miracles of all Godlike gifts:[^2444] thee do we entreat, and unto thee do we make supplication [thee,] the merciful Mother of the Master Who loves mankind, that mercy may be shown unto us, thy humble and unworthy servants. Look down mercifully upon our captivity; heal the crushing of our souls and bodies; destroy visible and invisible hosts; a strong tower, a weapon in battle, and a firm bulwark, and a general, an invincible ally, be thou unto us unworthy ones against the face of our enemies;[^2445] show forth in us thy ancient mercies, and show wonders this day unto our lawless enemies: that Thy Son and God is the only King and Master, and that thou art truly the Theotokos, who didst bear the true God according to the flesh. And thou canst do all things, and art powerful to accomplish whatsoever thou willest in heaven and on earth;[^2446] grant every petition that is profitable unto each, O Sovereign Lady:[^2447] healing unto the ailing; stillness and piloting unto those at sea; traveling with those that travel, do thou preserve them; delivering the captives from bitter bondage; comforting the sorrowful; lightening poverty and every bodily affliction; above all delivering [us] from spiritual infirmities and passions by thy invisible intercessions and guidance: so that the course of this temporal life we may finish well and without stumbling, and for thy sake obtain those eternal good things in the heavenly kingdom. And invisibly strengthen our faithful rulers,[^2448] who are honored with the awesome Name of Thine only-begotten Son, and who put their trust in thy protection and grace, and who set thee forth everywhere as mediatress and helper, against the enemies that encompass them; disperse the cloud of despondency hanging over their souls;[^2449] take away sicknesses from their souls and hearts, and bring in radiant good cheer and peaceful joy, establishing their dominion and realm unshaken; deliver, O Sovereign Lady by these prayers [of thine], this city which is especially dedicated unto thee, and every city and country: from famine, pestilence, earthquake, flood, fire, sword, the incursion of foreign nations, and civil war; and turn away all wrath righteously stirred up against us:[^2450] through the good pleasure and goodness of Thine only-begotten Son, to Whom is due all glory, honor, and worship, with His unoriginate Father, and His co-eternal and life-creating Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.

*After this, the dismissal.*

---

# PART XXXIII: THE ORDER THAT TAKES PLACE IN TIME OF DROUGHT [^2451]

[Woodcut headpiece ornament: foliate scrollwork with twin flower-bearing vases]

*The priest says:* Blessed is our God...[^2452]

*Then the Trisagion; Most Holy Trinity; and after Our Father: For Thine is the kingdom...*[^2453]

*Lord, have mercy (12).*[^2454]

*Glory... Both now...*

*O come, let us worship... thrice.*[^2455]

*Then Psalm 142:* O Lord, hear my prayer...[^2456]

*After this:* God is the Lord... *in Tone 6.*[^2457]

*Then the troparia:*

Have mercy on us, O Lord, have mercy on us...[^2458]

*Glory...*

O Lord, have mercy on us...[^2459]

*Both now...*

[The door of] compassion[^2460] open unto us;[^2461]

*For all this, (see fol. 398).[^2462]*

*Then Psalm 50:* Have mercy on me, O God...[^2463]

*Supplicatory Canon for drought unto our Lord Jesus Christ.[^2464] Ode 1, Tone 2. Heirmos:*

Come, ye peoples, let us sing a song unto Christ God, Who divided the sea and guided the people whom He brought forth from the bondage of Egypt, for He hath been glorified.[^2465]

*Troparion:*
Receive, O Savior, the supplication from our unworthy lips, and send down from heaven upon the earth a fruitful dew; for Thou art the Lover of mankind and a God of manifold mercy, overlooking our transgressions.[^2466]

*Troparion:*
Overlook now, O Lord, our transgressions, and turn away Thy wrath which Thou hast now justly brought upon us, O our Savior, and grant dew from heaven unto the earth and unto Thy people.

*Troparion:*
Come, O men, let us weep before God and our Creator, crying out with compunction:[^2467] Overlook our transgressions, O Lover of mankind, and send down rain from heaven upon the parched earth.

*Theotokion:*
Through thee have we known the Light, O Theotokos;[^2468] therefore do we pray thee: cease not interceding with thy Creator and Son to overlook our sins, and to send down dew upon His earth.

*Another Supplicatory Canon unto the Most Holy Theotokos. Tone 4. Ode 1. Heirmos:*[^2469]

I shall open my mouth, and it will be filled...[^2470]

*Troparion:*
Open, O Sovereign Lady, the heavens that are shut up because of our evil sins and because of our innumerable stumbling-blocks; pouring out the floodgates of heaven[^2471] for the nourishment of earthly dwellers, entreat the Meek One.

*Troparion:*
Having conceived without seed the heavenly Cloud[^2472] Who nourishes earthly dwellers with spiritual dew: pour out upon us a heavenly shower, appeasing the wrath of the Most Merciful God.

*Glory...*
O Master of all creation, thrice-unoriginate in properties, divided in Persons yet in one will:[^2473] not in wrath nor in anger punish us, Thou Who hast Thine innumerable love for mankind.

*Both now...*
O Thou Who didst shut up the heavens by the prayer of Thy prophet:[^2474] now open, O Master, the floodgates of heaven,[^2475] accepting the prayer of the Mother of God and Virgin who bore Thee without seed and without mingling, who entreats Thee for us in time of drought.

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*
Establish us in Thyself, O Lord, Who by the Tree didst put to death sins; and plant Thy fear in our hearts, for Thou art the Lover of mankind.[^2476]

*Troparion:*
O Lord Who holdest all creation in Thy palm:[^2477] as Thou art compassionate, hear the supplications of Thy servants, and send down dew upon the face of all the earth.

*Troparion:*
Good art Thou and merciful, O Lord, as Thou hast an abyss of compassions; overlook not our supplication, but send us a peaceful cloud with good rain, O Merciful One.

*Troparion:*
The wealth which Thou gavest us we have foully squandered;[^2478] yet as Thou hast an abyss of mercy, O Christ—for Thou art a good Father—be moved with pity, granting fruitful rains unto the earth, overlooking our transgressions.

*Theotokion:*
As thou hast acceptable boldness toward the Lover of mankind and thy Son, O pure one: entreat Him to grant unto the earth well-tempered rain,[^2479] by thy prayers.

*Another Heirmos:* Thy hymnographers[^2480] *Troparion:*
Receiving our entreaties chanted unworthily from our lips: grant us cleansing from our innumerable offenses; for thee alone have we as helper before our God.

*Troparion:*
Turn back Thy wrath, O Lord, and give us not over to reproach;[^2481] but while chastening us,[^2482] show forth also Thy mercy upon us, through the prayers of Thine all-pure Mother who entreats Thee for us, O Christ.

*Glory...*
All-holy and Divine Trinity, glorified in three Persons: overcome the hardness of our hearts,[^2483] and hear the supplication of Thy sinful servants who pray with fervor.

*Both now...*
Thou art the cloud bearing Christ, and the door[^2484] heavenly, O all-pure Virgin: pour out upon thy people thine innumerable mercy; for thee alone have we as protection and mediatress and speedy help.

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*
I sing to Thee: for having heard the report of Thee, O Lord, I was afraid;[^2485] for Thou didst come unto me, seeking me who was gone astray;[^2486] therefore do I glorify Thy great dispensation toward us, and our renewal.

*Troparion:*
Look down from on high upon us who have sinned against Thee, O Lord;[^2487] and do Thou Who art good grant Thy mercy unto all the earth; and send down, we pray, Thy most rich mercies unto Thy servants, O Master.

*Troparion:*
There hath come upon us who sin against Thee Thy wrath, O Merciful One; Thou hast shut up the heavens so as not to give rain unto the earth;[^2488] therefore do we Thy servants entreat Thee: punish us not in Thine anger, O Word, compassionate Master.

*Troparion:*
Altering the temperaments of the air by Thy command, O Lord: grant us abundant rain,[^2489] sending bountiful fruits unto the earth, that every living thing may be satisfied[^2490] through the good pleasure of Thy mercy.

*Theotokion:*
Thou hast appeared as Mother unto our God, O Virgin Theotokos; therefore we all entreat thee, O Sovereign Lady, as thou hast boldness: pray Him on behalf of us all to overlook our transgressions, and to send down rain upon the earth through thy prayers, O Lady.

*Another Heirmos. To the Archangels:*

He Who sits in glory upon the throne of the Godhead...[^2491]

*Troparion:*
Holy Archistrategoi Michael and Gabriel,[^2492] standing before the throne: fervently entreat Christ for the people, to deliver them from afflictions and tribulations, and to enrich the face of the earth for fruit-bearing.[^2493]

*Troparion:*
O Most Merciful God, not in wrath nor in anger punish us, but prevail over our manifold sins, according to Thy great mercy.

*Glory...*
As of old Thou didst receive the prodigal and the publican who repented:[^2494] receive us also, O Master, who pray unto Thee, enriching the face of the earth and giving rain in due season,[^2495] through the prayers of Thine all-pure Mother, O Christ.

*Both now* Cast down the assaults of enemies and assuage our afflictions, subduing them beneath the feet of our Christ-loving sovereign;[^2496] and through the prayers of the Most Holy Theotokos, loose the malice of our sins.

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*
O Lord, Giver of light and Creator of the ages:[^2497] guide us all in the light of Thy commandments, for beside Thee we know no other God.[^2498]

*Troparion:*
Through the prayers of Thy bodiless hosts, O Savior: graciously hear us who ever pray unto Thy dominion, and send down abundant and good water unto the thirsty earth,[^2499] for Thou alone art the Lover of mankind.

*Troparion:*
Be merciful unto us, O Lord, in the time[^2500] of our afflictions, and from the impending wrath save us; send rain unto Thy land, O Master, of Thy good pleasure, O Lover of mankind.[^2501]

*Troparion:*
The Twelve Apostles,[^2502] with all the choirs of martyrs, make prayer for us, to deliver [us] from every affliction and wrath, and not to deprive us Thy servants of Thy mercy.

*Theotokion:*
We earthly ones have thee as Mediatress of all unto God,[^2503] O Virgin Theotokos; therefore we pray thee, O holy one: save thy people from every affliction, and deliver [us] from the present wrath, by thy prayers, O Theotokos.

*Another Heirmos:*
All things were amazed at Thy divine [glory][^2504] *Troparion:*
Marvelous art Thou, O Christ God, in Thy holy powers,[^2505] chastening, and again by mercy protecting us; through the prayers of Thine all-pure Mother, being entreated by her, grant unto us remission of sins.

*Troparion:*
O Pure and undefiled Virgin, who without seed hast borne God, Whom an earthly father sowed not, nor did a mother bring forth in the heavens:[^2506] Him fervently entreat to grant unto us remission of sins, bringing to fullness in abundance the fruits of the earth.

*Glory...*
I glorify the Thrice-unoriginate Trinity,[^2507] uncreated in essential properties, yet divided in Persons, existing in one will and purpose, Whom the bodiless hosts glorify; and we earthly ones glorifying, ask mercy and the watering of the earth.

*Both now...*
Being compassionate, O Lady, having borne the most compassionate Lord: therefore consume my stumbling blocks, and cast down enemies, granting us victory, and subduing every foe and adversary beneath the feet of our faithful sovereign.[^2508]

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*
Held fast in the abyss of sins, I call upon the unfathomable abyss of Thy compassion: from corruption, O my God, raise me up.[^2509]

*Troparion:*
O multitude of all martyrs, as having great boldness toward God:[^2510] pray Him now to grant good rain unto the parched earth and to bestow fruits of abundance, and grace unto His people.

*Troparion:*
We pray Thee, O Master, through the prayers of Thy disciples: overlook, O Lord, and forgive our transgressions, and turn away Thy wrath from us, O Compassionate One;[^2511] and grant dew unto Thy land, through the prayers of Thy disciples.

*Troparion:*
O Master, our Creator, Thee as good God and Lover of mankind we entreat with all our soul: spare us, O Lord, spare [us], and grant unto the parched earth temperate rain,[^2512] bringing forth good fruits for all flesh.

*Theotokion:*
Praying unceasingly unto thy Son for us, we entreat thee, O all-pure Mother of God: overlook not thy unworthy servants; for thou hast boldness as Mother: entreat Him, O Virgin, that He may deliver us from the impending wrath.

*Another Heirmos:*
Prefiguring, he cried out...[^2513]

*Troparion:*
Graciously hear us who cry unto Thee faithfully, O Merciful Lord; pour forth the floodgates of heaven,[^2514] and remit our sinful stumbling blocks; grant victory over our invisible and visible enemies, O Most Merciful One.

*Troparion:*
Lifting up thine all-pure hands and eyes, O Lady: shelter us from enemies visible and invisible, subduing [their] malice beneath our feet, granting us rain from heaven from God.

*Glory...*
Held fast by hardness of sin,[^2515] we have not in our soul tearful lamentation: O all-pure Lady, ask for us rain from heaven from the Lord, for the fruitfulness of the earth.

*Both now...*
Overcome my darkening, and pour out upon my heart showers of tears, that through thee the fruit of repentance may grow in me, O all-pure Virgin.

*Kontakion, Tone 6:*
O Champion of Christians that cannot be put to shame, unchanging Mediatress unto the Creator:[^2516] overlook not the suppliant voice of sinners, but anticipate, as thou art good, to our help who faithfully cry unto thee; hasten to prayer and speed to supplication, ever protecting, O Theotokos, them that honor thee.

*Ikos:*
Stretch forth thy palms, wherewith thou didst embrace the Master of all as an Infant;[^2517] according to the multitude of mercy, forsake not us who ever hope in thee; by watchful protection and boundless compassion have mercy upon us, and spare our souls, being the fountain of compassion;[^2518] for thee have we gained as Protectress, O all-pure one, delivered from grievous afflictions; but as having a heart of compassions: hasten to prayer and speed to supplication, ever protecting, O Theotokos them that honor thee.

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*
The most wise youths bowed not down to the golden image, but into the flame went they of themselves; standing in the midst of the fire they sang; and an angel bedewed them, saying: Heard now is the prayer of your lips.[^2519]

*Troparion:*
We know Thee as Lord and Creator of every creature: therefore we pray, spare [us], O Compassionate One, and overlook our iniquities as Thou art good and the Lover of mankind; and from the present righteous wrath deliver Thy servants, and grant as Thou art good dew unto the thirsty earth.

*Troparion:*
As of old, O Master, Thou didst deliver Manasses repenting,[^2520] and from deadly afflictions didst rescue and save [him]: so also for us now, O Compassionate and Bountiful One, overlook all transgressions, and grant rain unto the earth, and mercy unto Thy servants, and preserve us from famine and affliction.

*Troparion:*
Have compassion upon us now as Thou art good and merciful; for we have sinned and committed iniquity exceedingly,[^2521] and that which is unrighteous before Thee have we all done; therefore we pray Thee with fear: punish not Thy people in Thine anger, but bestow rain unto the earth, O Compassionate One.

*Theotokion:*
Thee all we faithful have as an awe-inspiring refuge and unconquerable weapon, O Theotokos;[^2522] we Thy servants pray thee deliver us from every affliction, from famine and pestilence, and every distress; and send fruitful dew unto the earth, and unto thy servants, O Sovereign Lady.

*Another Heirmos:*
He Who saved in the fire the Abrahamic children...[^2523]

*Troparion:*
Thou art He Who saved in the sea and in perils, O Lover of mankind, and them that are held fast in sicknesses, a Helper in battles: therefore receive us also, and protect us by the prayer of Thy holy Mother.

*Troparion:*
Turn not away Thy face from us, O Merciful One, for we have provoked Thee to anger, not doing Thy commandment; therefore we pray Thee for the sake of the Theotokos: deliver Thy servants from every affliction and sorrow.

*Glory*[^2524] Let not the wrath of Thy rebuke consume us, O Christ, but show others instructed through us unworthy ones; water all the fruits with dew, gladdening our hearts.[^2525]

*Both now...*[^2526]

*Theotokion:*
Receive our contrite supplication, O Theotokos, seeing us sinking in passions; overcome our coarseness,[^2527] and be moved unto thy compassions, entreating the Savior and God for us.[^2528]

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*
Him Who descended into the fiery furnace unto the Hebrew children, and turned the flame into coolness, as God: praise, all ye works of the Lord, and exalt Him above all unto the ages![^2529]

*Troparion:*
Elijah once by a word restrained rain from being upon the earth, and again by a word brought rain from heaven upon the earth; therefore we pray Thee, O Master: by his prayers send us rain from heaven upon Thy land.[^2530]

*Troparion:*
Angelic choirs, assemblies of apostles and prophets, of martyrs and hierarchs, and multitudes of the venerable: as the Creator of all and God, pray Him to save them that faithfully hymn Him.[^2531]

*Troparion:*
As Thou didst deliver Jonah from the beast and the sea, and Daniel from the pit and the lions, O Savior, by Thy mercy: likewise now give ear unto Thy servants, and deliver Thy people from every evil.[^2532]

*Theotokion:*
The Theotokos who bare Thee, O Savior, do we now summon unto supplication, that Thou mayest have compassion upon us, and save the people and the city that have sinned against Thee, and that exalt Thee above all unto the ages.[^2533]

*Another Heirmos:*
The godly youths in the furnace the childbearing...[^2534]

*Troparion:*
Make us not likened, O Master, unto the wrath of Elijah for our transgressions, but as Thou art compassionate, send gentle lightnings, watering the face of the earth, and granting the perfection of fruits; for Thou art the Giver of good things: beside Thee we know no other God, Whom as Lord praise, ye works, and exalt Him above all unto the ages.[^2535]

*Troparion:*
Thou Who didst receive the weeping of Manasseh, and didst turn Thy wrath into love for mankind therefore even now, O Master, not with wrath, but with Thy compassions, raise up the chastened people, by the prayers of Thy most pure Mother, of them that unceasingly cry aloud: "Hymn the Lord, ye works, and exalt Him above all unto the ages!"[^2536]

*Glory...*[^2537]

*Troparion:*
O Forerunner and Baptist John, despise us not that lie prostrate in passions, but raise us up by thy prayers; and stir up also the prophets to pray earnestly for all the people that call upon the Name of the Lord, that He may turn His rebuke unto meekness, according to His love for mankind, through your prayers.[^2538]

*Both now...*[^2539]

*Theotokion:*
By thy compassions, O Mother of God, cover thy people who by passions are held fast; pray earnestly unto thy Son, for our transgressions cannot overcome thee; for thou loosest the bonds of sins, and healest infirmities, and deliverest from distresses them that faithfully cry aloud: "Praise the Lord and exalt Him above all unto the ages!"[^2540]

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*
Him Who is God the Word of God, Who by ineffable wisdom came down to renew Adam, who had evilly fallen through corrupt food, and Who for our sake was ineffably incarnate of the Holy Virgin: with one accord[^2541] in songs, we faithful magnify Him.[^2542]

*Troparion:*
Unto the thirsty earth, O Compassionate One, and unto us who ask Thy mercy, O Lover of mankind show Thyself merciful, O Lord, as God all-compassionate, and grant us good, fruit-bearing rain, and save our souls, O Tenderhearted One.[^2543]

*Troparion:*
Have mercy, O Merciful One, upon the work of Thy hands; O Creator, forgive our transgressions, as Thou art good; chasten us not in Thy wrath, but incline Thine ear, and attend unto our prayers, and grant unto Thy land streams of rain, O Lover of mankind.[^2544]

*Troparion:*
Deliver from afflictions, O Lord, all Thy people, and Thy city and all villages; and bestow upon us fruit-bearing rains, O Master, unto the abundance of every fruit, and unto us salvation, O Tenderhearted One.[^2545]

*Theotokion:*
Prefiguring thee, O Theotokos, the Chaldean furnace refreshed the Children with dew as they danced in the midst of the flame; likewise now, refresh with rain us also who are burning with drought as in a furnace of fire, O Sovereign Lady, and save thy servants.[^2546]

*Another Heirmos:*
Eve indeed by the disease of disobedience...[^2547]

*To the Apostle Peter:*

*Troparion:*
O Peter, supreme apostle, who didst receive the keys of the Heavenly Kingdom: loose, we pray thee, our offenses, and ask rain for us from God, that He may open the cataracts of heaven; as thou didst have authority to bind and to loose, be thou a speedy helper unto us, to entreat from the Lord great mercy.[^2548]

*To the Apostle Paul:*

*Troparion:*
O Paul, who didst ascend unto the third heaven, and didst behold the ineffable glory of the Lord: having boldness toward God, with all the apostles pray that the Master and Lord may grant us early and latter rain; for the Lord accepts your supplications.[^2549]

*Glory...*[^2550]

*Troparion:*
Holy Stephen, who didst behold the glory of God, the heavens opened, and Christ standing at the right hand of the Father, and giving thee a crown from heaven, and authority to bind and to loose: entreat abundance from heaven from Christ, and with all the martyrs pray for us.[^2551]

*Both now...*[^2552]

*Theotokion:*
Thou art our help, and protectress unto the human race; defend against them that wage war with us, and stop the blasphemous mouths of the heretics, and grant victory to our king over adversary enemies; for thou art the glory and praise of all Christians; therefore do we all worthily glorify thee.[^2553]

*Then: "It is truly meet," the Trisagion, "All-holy Trinity," and after "Our Father," "For Thine is the kingdom," and the troparia, Tone 6: "Have mercy on us, O Lord, have mercy on us," and the remaining verses in order (see fol. 398).[^2554]*

*We sing the psalm: "Holy God." Then the Prokeimenon, Tone 4:*[^2555]
Turn us back, O God of our salvations, and turn away Thine anger from us.[^2556]
*Verse:*

Wilt Thou be angry with us unto ages? Or wilt Thou stretch out Thy wrath from generation to generation?[^2557]

*The Epistle: The Reading is from the Catholic Epistle of James:*[^2558]
Brethren: Submit yourselves therefore to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you. Draw nigh to God, and He will draw nigh to you. Cleanse your hands, ye sinners, and purify your hearts, ye double-minded. Be afflicted, and mourn, and weep: let your laughter be turned into mourning, and your joy into sorrow. Humble yourselves before God, and He will exalt you. Speak not evil one of another, brethren; for he that speaks evil of a brother, or[^2559] judges his brother, speaks evil of the law, and judges the law; but if thou judge the law, thou art not a doer of the law, but a judge. One is the Lawgiver and Judge, Who is able to save and to destroy; but who art thou that judgest another?[^2560]

Hear now, ye that say: "Today and tomorrow we will go into this city, and spend a year there, and trade and make a profit"; whereas ye know not what shall happen tomorrow. For what is our life? For it is a vapor that appears for a little time, and then vanishes away; instead of your saying: "If the Lord wills,[^2561] and we shall live, and do this or that." But now ye boast in your proud boastings; all such boasting is evil. Therefore to him that knows to do good, and does it not, to him it is sin.[^2562]

Elijah was a man of like passions with us, and he prayed earnestly in prayer that it might not rain; and it rained not upon the earth for three years and six months. And he prayed again, and heaven gave rain, and the earth brought forth her fruit.[^2563]

Brethren, if any of you wander from the way of truth, and one turn him back, let him know that he who turns a sinner from the error of his way[^2564] shall save a soul from death, and shall cover a multitude of sins.[^2565]

*Alleluia, Tone 8:*
Look upon us and have mercy on us.[^2566]
*Verse:*
Direct our steps according to Thy word.[^2567]

*The Gospel according to Luke:*[^2568]
At that time, the multitudes marveled at the words of grace that proceeded out of the mouth of Jesus, and they said: "Is not this the son of Joseph?" And He said unto them: "Ye will surely say unto Me this proverb: 'Physician, heal Thyself! Whatsoever we have heard done in Capernaum, do also here in Thine own country.'" And He said: "Amen I say unto you: No prophet is accepted in his own country;[^2569]

...but of a truth I say unto you: Many widows were in Israel in the days of Elijah, when the heaven was shut up three years and six months, so that there was a great famine throughout all the land; and unto none of them was Elijah sent, save unto Sarepta of Sidon, unto a woman that was a widow. And many lepers were in Israel in the time of Elisha the prophet; and none of them was cleansed, save Naaman the Syrian." And all in the synagogue, when they heard these things, were filled with wrath, and rose up, and thrust Him out of the city, and led Him unto the brow of the hill whereon their city was built, that[^2570] they might cast Him down headlong. But He, passing through the midst of them, went His way.[^2571]

*Another Gospel from Mark:*[^2572]
The Lord said unto His disciples: "Have faith in God. For amen I say unto you, that whosoever shall say unto this mountain: 'Be thou taken up and cast into the sea,' and shall not doubt in his heart, but shall believe that those things which He says come to pass, he shall have whatsoever he says. Therefore I say unto you: All things whatsoever ye ask when ye pray, believe that ye receive them, and ye shall have them. And when ye stand praying, forgive, if ye have ought against any, that your Father also Who is in heaven[^2573] may forgive you your trespasses. But if ye do not forgive, neither will your Father Who is in heaven forgive your trespasses.[^2574]

*Then the deacon, or the priest, says the litanies discreetly:*[^2575]

> **Deacon:** "Have mercy on us, O God, according to Thy great mercy, we pray Thee: give ear and have mercy."[^2576]

*People: "Lord, have mercy," thrice.*[^2577]

> **Deacon:** "Thou Who desirest not the death of sinners, but awaitest their return and repentance: give ear unto us and have mercy."[^2578]

> **Deacon:** "Thou Who bringest up clouds from the ends of the earth by Thy command: O Master, King, send down rain upon us; we pray Thee: give ear and have mercy."[^2579]

> **Deacon:** "Thou Who callest for the water of the sea, and pourest it out upon the face of all the earth: show compassions upon us, O Master, and gladden us with Thy blessing; we pray Thee: give ear and have mercy."[^2580]

> **Deacon:** "Grant a bountiful rain unto the earth, O Savior; water all things, O Lover of mankind, and multiply the grain in the fields; we pray Thee: give ear and have mercy."[^2581]

> **Deacon:** "Thou Who clothest the heaven with clouds, Who preparest rain for the earth, Who makest grass to spring up for cattle, and green herb for the service of men: save men and cattle, O holy Lord; we pray Thee: give ear and have mercy."[^2582]

> **Deacon:** "Water the furrows of the earth, and multiply her grain; we pray Thee, O Lord: give ear and have mercy."[^2583]

> **Deacon:** "As the eyes of servants look unto the hands of their masters, so do our eyes look unto Thee, O God, until Thou have mercy upon us; we pray Thee: give ear and have mercy."[^2584]

> **Deacon:** "Thou Who makest the sun to rise on the good and on the evil, and sendest rain on the just and on the unjust, and multipliest seed by Thy mercy: we pray Thee: give ear and have mercy."[^2585]

> **Deacon:** "Thou Who coverest Thyself with light as with a garment: look upon us, O Master, and send down rain upon us by Thy mercy; we pray Thee: give ear and have mercy."[^2586]

> **Deacon:** "Thou Who dwellest in the highest: look upon Thy people, O Holy One, Lover of mankind;"

...we pray Thee: give ear and have mercy.[^2587]

> **Deacon:** "Remember not our iniquities, O Master; for if Thou shouldest mark iniquities, O Lord, O Lord, who shall stand? We pray Thee: give ear and have mercy."[^2588]

> **Deacon:** "Give ear unto us, O Lord, for sweet is Thy mercy; sustain the earth with Thy blessing; we pray Thee: give ear and have mercy."[^2589]

> **Deacon:** "Give ear unto us, O God, for good is Thy mercy, and water the earth with Thy blessing; we pray Thee: give ear and have mercy."[^2590]

> **Deacon:** "Let Thy tender mercies speedily prevent us, O Lord, and look upon the earth with rain; we pray Thee: give ear and have mercy."[^2591]

> **Deacon:** "That this monastery, and every city and countryside may be delivered from famine, plague earthquake, flood, fire, the sword, the invasion of foreign nations, and from civil warfare and strife; we pray Thee, O Lord: give ear and have mercy."[^2592]

> **Deacon:** "That we may be delivered from all affliction, and that rich mercy may be granted unto all of us in need and who wait upon Thee; we pray Thee, O Lord: give ear and have mercy."[^2593]

> **Deacon:** "Furthermore we pray, that the Lord our God may give ear unto the voice of our prayer and have mercy on us, and that Thy love for mankind may be upon our sins, so as to deliver us from all these afflictions that lie before us from the face of Thy wrath; and who shall stand[^2594] against the face of Thy wrath? Now we cry unto Thee with tears: give ear unto the voice of our prayer, we pray Thee, O Lord, and have mercy."[^2595]

> **Deacon:** "Furthermore we pray the Lord our God, that He may give ear unto the voice of our prayer, and have mercy on us, and send down rain bountifully upon the face of all the earth, and gladden it, and have mercy on us; we pray Thee: give ear and have mercy."[^2596]

> **Deacon:** "Furthermore we pray, that the Lord our God may give ear unto the voice of our prayer, and have mercy on us, and turn away all His wrath moved against us, and deliver us from His impending righteous threat, and have mercy on us, and rain upon the earth a good rain by His goodness; let us all say: O Lord, give ear and have mercy."[^2597]

*People:* Lord, have mercy *(fifty times).*[^2598]

*Then the priest says the exclamatory prayer with a loud voice:*[^2599]

> **Priest:** "Give ear unto us, O God our Savior, the hope of all the ends of the earth, and of them that be far off upon the sea; and be merciful, be merciful, O Master, unto us concerning our sins, and have mercy on us.[^2600] For a merciful God and Lover of mankind Thou art, and unto Thee do we send up glory: to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages."[^2601]

> **Priest:** "Peace be unto all."

> **Deacon:** "Bow your heads unto the Lord."[^2602]

*While we all bow our heads and knees, the priest says the prayers in order with all attentiveness and compunction of heart:*[^2603]

> **Deacon:** "Let us pray to the Lord."

> **Priest:** "Master, Lord our God, Who didst give ear unto Elijah the Prophet, Thy zealous servant, so as to send rain upon the earth in its season; Who likewise in the days of Elijah didst command that it should not rain, and again through his prayer didst bestow a fruitful shower:[^2604] do Thou Thyself, O Master of all, being entreated through Thine own tender compassion, send down bountiful rain upon Thine inheritance; and overlook our transgressions through Thy compassions; send Thy mercy upon those who have need and ask for mercy. Gladden the face of the earth for the sake of the poor among Thy people, for the sake of the infants and cattle, and of all who stand in need of mercy from Thee; for they trust in Thee, Who givest them food in due season.[^2605] For Thou art our God, a God of mercy and of salvation, O Lord our God; and unto Thee do we send up glory: to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen."[^2606]

*Second Prayer for the Same:*[^2607]

> **Deacon:** "Let us pray to the Lord."

> **Priest:** "O Lord Almighty, Who bringest up clouds from the ends of the earth, Who hast made lightnings for the rain, Who bringest forth the winds out of His treasuries; Who callest the waters of the sea[^2608] and pourest them out upon the face of all the earth: unto Thee do we pray, and Thee do we implore, and rich mercy do we ask of Thee.[^2609] Open the cataracts of heaven; command the clouds to rain down rain, and show compassion upon all Thy land, which Thou didst make with Thine all-pure hands, O Christ, the true Light. Have tender compassion upon the elders, and the youths, and the suckling infants at the breast; upon the male and female servants, and upon the beasts of the earth; that the fields may bring forth grass for the cattle, and green herb for the service of men, that the earth may yield her fruit.[^2610] We pray Thee, O King of hosts: receive the supplication of all Thy people; and rebuke us not in Thine indignation; slay not Thy people through famine and thirst. For the eyes of all look with hope unto Thee, and Thou givest them their food in due season; for in Thee do we put our trust, and beside Thee we know no other God; of Thee do we ask rich mercy.[^2611] For a good God and Lover of mankind Thou art, and unto Thee do we send up glory: to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen."[^2612]

*Third Prayer:*[^2613]

> **Deacon:** "Let us pray to the Lord."

> **Priest:** "Master, Lord our God, high and glorious Lover of mankind, Who renderest unto each man honor and glory according to his labors: make us partakers of Thine own Kingdom. Remember, O good Master, Thy servants who pray unto Thee, and receive our supplication, for Thy name is Lord, the Lover of mankind.[^2614] Even though we possess no good works, yet for the sake of Thy manifold tender compassion save us, O Lord, Lover of mankind; for Thou art our God, and we are Thy people, and the sheep of Thy pasture: the flock which in the beginning, when Thou didst become incarnate, Thou didst gather together, tearing us away from idolatry.[^2615] O Good Shepherd, Who didst lay down Thy life for the sheep, forsake us not; though we still wander until eventide, though we sin against Thee as newly bought servants in their first year unto a master of their own, abhor us not. Even though we are a little flock, cast us not away; but say unto us: "Fear not, My little flock, for it is your heavenly Father's good pleasure to give you the Kingdom."[^2616] O merciful Lord, good Lover of mankind, rich in mercy and compassions, Who hast promised to receive those who repent unto Thee, and Who awaitest the turning of sinners: remember not our manifold sins, but receive those who turn unto Thee, and blot out the handwriting of our stumbling blocks; appease the wrath whereby we have provoked Thee to anger, O Lover of mankind.[^2617] For Thou art the Lord and Master, and all things are Thine, and in Thee is the power either for us to live or to die. Appease Thy wrath, O Merciful One, of which we are worthy according to our deeds; turn aside the trial, for we are dust and ashes before Thee, O Lord.[^2618] Enter not into judgment with Thy servants, for we are Thy people; Thee do we seek, and before Thee do we fall down; unto Thee do we pray.[^2619] We have sinned before Thee, and have done evil; we have not kept nor observed as Thou didst command us; for being earthly, we have inclined unto earthly things, and have done wickedly before Thy face; turning away from Thy glory and love, we have rushed headlong into carnal lust, and we have enslaved ourselves to sin and to the cares of this life; and we have become runaways from our own Master, and, wretches that we are, destitute of good works by reason of our evil life. But we repent, and ask, and pray Thee, O merciful Lord, Lover of mankind, Who callest sinners to repentance, that Thou send Thy fear into our hearts.[^2620] We pray Thee, O Heavenly King, that at the dread judgment Thou wilt have mercy on us. Save and show compassion; look down and visit; have tender compassion and have mercy; for we are Thy servants, and the work of Thy hands.[^2621] If Thou shouldest mark our iniquities, O Lord, O Lord, who shall stand?[^2622] Or if Thou shouldest render unto each man according to his works, who then shall be saved? For with Thee is propitiation and mercy, and plenteous redemption.[^2623] Our soul is in Thy two hands, our breath is in Thy will; for as long as Thy gracious regard is upon us, we prosper; but if Thou lookest upon us with wrath, we perish like the morning dew.[^2624] For as dust stands not against the wind, so neither can we stand against Thy wrath; but as the creation, we ask mercy from Him Who created us.[^2625] Have mercy on us, O Lord, sinners that we are; have mercy on us according to Thy great mercy, and according to the multitude of Thy compassions blot out our iniquities; for all good comes from Thee upon us, whereas all that is unrighteous is from us toward Thee.[^2626] We have all turned aside together, and are become unprofitable; there is none among us that is diligent concerning heavenly things, but all look unto earthly things; and all of us are intent upon the cares of this life, having no care for the Kingdom of God, as though permanent upon the earth.[^2627] Not that Thou, O Lord, forsakest us, but rather that we seek Thee not, cleaving unto these visible things; therefore do we fear lest at some time Thou do unto us as Thou didst unto Jerusalem, when they had forsaken Thee and walked not in Thy ways; yet do not Thou unto us as unto them according to their deeds nor reward us according to our sins; but have patience with us yet, O long-suffering Lord; stay Thy wrathful flame that stretches forth against Thy servants.[^2628] Do Thou Thyself guide us into Thy truth, and teach us to do Thy will; for Thou art our God, and we are Thy people, Thy portion, Thine inheritance, and Thy creation.[^2629] We have not lifted up our hands unto a strange god, nor followed false prophets, nor do we hold heretical teaching; but Thee do we call upon, the true God; and unto Thee Who dwellest in heaven do we lift up our eyes[^2630] and unto Thee do we lift up our hands, and we pray Thee: forgive us, for Thou art good and the Lover of mankind; have mercy on us, Who callest sinners to repentance.[^2631] And at the dread judgment, separate us not from standing at Thy right hand, but make us worthy of the blessedness of the righteous.[^2632] As long as this world stands, bring not upon us tribulations and temptations, and deliver us not into the hands of aliens, lest Thy city be called a captive city, and Thy people be in a land not their own, lest the nations say: "Where is their God?"[^2633] Send not upon us tribulation, nor famine, nor civil strife, nor sudden death, nor from fire, nor deluge, lest they fall away from the faith, for they are not steadfast in the faith.[^2634] Chastise a little, but have mercy abundantly; wound a little, but heal mercifully; grieve a little, but gladden speedily; for our nature cannot endure to bear Thy prolonged wrath, even as stubble before the fire; but be Thou speedily moved to compassion, for Thine it is to show mercy and to save.[^2635] Therefore, O Master, extend Thy mercy upon Thy people: drive away enemies; establish peace; subdue barbarians; enrich the city with abundance; make our faithful sovereigns and princes formidable unto the nations; endow the boyars with wisdom; make the city mighty; make Thy Churches to grow; preserve Thine inheritance; save men, and women, and infants; deliver those that are in servitude, captivity, and exile; and have mercy on all those in prisons, in hunger, in thirst, and in nakedness; comfort them all, make them all glad; grant unto them joy both of soul and body; through the prayers of the all-pure Theotokos, and of the holy heavenly hosts; and of Thy Forerunner and Baptist John; and of the holy Apostles; and of the holy Prophets; and of the holy Martyrs; and of the holy venerable and God-bearing Fathers; and through the prayers of all the saints, be Thou moved to compassion upon us, that by Thy mercy being pastured in the unity of the faith, we may cheerfully and joyfully glorify Thee unto ages of ages. Amen."[^2636]

*And if thou wilt read the other prayers for rainlessness, look back (see fol. 97 and 98);[^2637] then, the dismissal.*[^2638]

[Woodcut tailpiece: Large diamond-shaped floral strapwork ornament framed by Renaissance arabesque foliage] [Fol. 451v. Blank leaf (*vacat*) concluding the Order in Time of Drought; faint show-through visible from the woodcut tailpiece on Fol. 451r.][^2639]
