# PART XLVII: THE ORDER CONCERNING THE COMMUNION OF THE HOLY WATER OF THE THEOPHANY OF THE GREAT SANCTIFICATION [^3817]

*When it is not permitted to partake of the life-creating, most pure mysteries of Christ, of His Body and Blood: by the counsel of one's spiritual father, when the time directs, one partakes of the consecrated water, according to the customary preparation for sanctification; and the priest having made the beginning, he says these prayers:*[^3818]

> **Priest:** "Blessed is our God, always, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen."[^3819]

*Heavenly King; Trisagion; after Our Father; Lord, have mercy (12 times); Come, let us worship (3 times); Psalm 50: Have mercy on me, O God; after these, these troparia:*[^3820]

*Troparion:* O Thou Who hast the cup of inexhaustible treasures, grant me to draw water unto the remission of sins, for I am constrained with thirst, O Compassionate Lord![^3821]

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:*

*Theotokion:* O pure Virgin, palace of the Word, show my soul to be a temple of the Spirit; with water from the life-originating spring give me to drink, who am consumed by the burning of sin, that according to my duty I may glorify thee.[^3822]

*After these, the prayer of our father among the saints, John Chrysostom:*[^3823]

> **Priest:** "O Lord our God, Who art understood together with Thine immortal and unoriginate Father, and Who co-abidest with Thy co-eternal Spirit;[^3824] Who art the Giver of all sanctification; Who of old didst sanctify the waters by Thine own baptism,[^3825] and Who now ever sanctifiest them through Thine invocation: do Thou Thyself, through the descent and operation of Thy Holy Spirit, make also this holy water consecrated, that it may be unto me, Thy servant partaking thereof, for the enlightenment of the soul, for the sanctification of the body, for the mortification of passions, for the rejection of wicked thoughts, for a bulwark and putting away of the evil[^3826] assaults, and unto every profitable benefit; that being covered by its grace, I may remain unharmed by every snare, unto the glory of Thy most good and holy name; through the prayers of our most pure Lady, the Theotokos, and of all the saints. Amen."[^3827]

*Then the assembly makes three bows [metanias], chanting the troparion of the Baptism:*[^3828]

*Troparion of the Theophany, Tone 1:* When Thou, O Lord, wast baptized in the Jordan, the worship of the Trinity was made manifest; for the voice of the Parent bare witness unto Thee, calling Thee His beloved Son; and the Spirit, in the form of a dove, confirmed the steadfastness of the word. O Christ God, Who hast appeared and enlightened the world, glory be to Thee![^3829]

*Glory... Both now... Kontakion:*[^3830]

*Kontakion of the Theophany, Tone 4:* Today Thou hast appeared unto all the universe, and Thy light, O Lord, hath been signed upon us, who with understanding sing praise unto Thee: Thou hast come and hast appeared, the Light unapproachable![^3831]

*Then he partakes of the consecrated water with fear and reverence; and after this, say the prayer of our father among the saints, John Chrysostom:*[^3832]

**Officiant / Communicant:** Glory to Thine ineffable and unsearchable goodness! Glory to Thy most good and forbearing long-suffering! Glory to Thy compassions, that even now Thou hast made me, a sinner and Thine unworthy servant, worthy of sanctification through the partaking of this consecrated water[^3833] strengthen my life on account thereof, keeping me wholly unharmed; make me uncaught by the adversaries; show me unenslaved to unclean thoughts; renew me wholly, vivify me wholly unto good works, wing me wholly unto desire for Thee.[^3834]

*Ecphonesis:*

> **Priest:** "For Thou art the sweetness of our souls, and unto Thee do we send up glory, with Thine unoriginate Father, and Thine all-holy, good, and life-creating Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. [Amen.]"[^3835]

*After this: It is truly meet; Glory... Both now...; Lord, have mercy (3 times); and the dismissal.*[^3836]

# PART XLVIII: THE ORDER OVER THE COMPOUNDING OF THE HOLY GREAT MYRON, CELEBRATED ON HOLY AND GREAT THURSDAY [^3837]

*When the Holy Gifts have been carried into the holy sanctuary and placed upon the holy table, the foremost of the priests brings in the glass phial with the myron, and places it near the diskos on the upper side. And after the ecphonesis: "May the mercies of [our great] God [and Savior Jesus Christ be with you all]"; the doors not being opened, and the deacon upon the ambo remaining silent, while the archdeacon in the altar says:*[^3838]

**Archdeacon:** Let us attend![^3839]

*The hierarch steps up onto the step; and having signed the myron with the cross three times, he steps down; and having inclined his head, he says this prayer:*[^3840]

**Bishop / Hierarch:** O Lord of mercy, Father of lights, from Whom every good giving and every perfect gift is given:[^3841] grant unto us, Thine unworthy servants, the grace and enjoyment of this great and life-creating mystery; even as Thou didst give unto Thy faithful pleasure-pleaser Moses,[^3842] and unto Thy servant Samuel,[^3843] and unto Thine holy Apostles:[^3844] and send down Thine all-holy Spirit upon this myron, and make it a royal anointing, a spiritual anointing, a guardian of life[^3845] succoring souls and bodies; the oil of gladness,[^3846] which came indeed under the Law, and hath shone forth also in the New Covenant; wherewith were anointed priests, high priests, prophets, and kings;[^3847] wherewith also Thou Thyself didst anoint Thine holy Apostles, and all those who through the laver of regeneration have been made bishops and presbyters from them in succession until this present day.[^3848] Yea, O Master Almighty, through the descent of Thine Holy and Adored Spirit show [it to be] a garment of incorruption,[^3849] a perfecting seal,[^3850] delineating Thy divine name, and of Thine Only-begotten Son, and of Thine Holy Spirit, upon those who receive Thy divine laver[^3851] that having been understood before Thee, they may be Thy citizens, Thy menservants and maidservants, sanctified in soul and body, changed from all malice, and delivered from every sin by the vesture of Thy most pure glory;[^3852] recognized on account of Thy holy sign by the holy Angels and Archangels and all the heavenly powers,[^3853] and fearful unto all unclean spirits;[^3854] that they may be unto Thee a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, a holy nation,[^3855] marked by this most pure myron; and having Thy Christ in their hearts for an habitation of Thee, the God and Father[^3856] with the Holy Spirit.[^3857]

*Ecphonesis:*

**Bishop / Hierarch:** For holy art Thou, our God, Who restest upon the saints, and unto Thee do we send up glory, to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages.[^3858]

**People / Choir:** Amen.[^3859]

**Bishop / Hierarch:** Peace be unto all.[^3860]

> **Deacon:** "Let us bow our heads unto the Lord."[^3861]

*The hierarch says this prayer secretly:*[^3862]

**Bishop / Hierarch (secretly):** Unto Thee, O God, King of all, giving thanks, have we bowed the neck of our heart; for although we are unworthy, Thou hast accounted us worthy to be ministers of Thy divine mysteries; and we proclaim Thy mercy which Thou hast richly poured out upon us. To receive[^3863] **Bishop / Hierarch (secretly, continued):** ...consecration from Thee do we pray, as the myron descending upon the head;[^3864] for myron poured forth is the name of Thine Only-begotten Son, Christ our God,[^3865] through Whom the whole world is made fragrant, as much as is visible and as much as is invisible.[^3866]

*Ecphonesis:*

**Bishop / Hierarch:** For Thou art worshiped and glorified, and unto Thee do we send up glory, to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. [Amen.][^3867]

*After this is chanted in order what is upon the ambo; and the opening of the doors takes place; and the hierarch accomplishes the subsequent rites of the divine offering.*[^3868]

# PART XLIX: PRAYERS AT THE BLESSING AND BREAKING OF THE ARTOS [^3869]

*Prayer at the Blessing of the Artos:*[^3870]

> **Priest:** "With joy and gladness let us glorify our risen God, and let us run unto the feast to meet the Resurrection![^3871] Even as the Cherubim and Seraphim glorify [Thee] today, O holy Apostles, today the heavenly hosts having come, worshiped the risen God;[^3872] and earthly men having beheld Thy glory, sang praises unto Thee and glorified Thee, the God of all things.[^3873] Do Thou Thyself, O Lord, come and bless this table, even as Thou didst bless the six apostolic pairs:[^3874] two blessed, two glorified, two calling out and saying: "Glory to God in the highest, and on[^3875]" earth peace, good will toward men!"[^3876] We worship Thee, Who wast tried without sin for our sake.[^3877] Do Thou, O Lord, bless this artos, even as Thou didst bless the five loaves and the two fishes;[^3878] and even as Thou didst bless the granaries of Joseph in drought and waterlessness;[^3879] for Thou art the life and resurrection, O Christ our God,[^3880] and unto Thee do we send up glory, with Thine unoriginate Father, and with Thine all-holy, good, and life-creating Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. [Amen.]"[^3881]

*Prayer at the Breaking of the Artos:*[^3882]

Amen."[^3888]

# PART L: EPISTLE OF JOHN, MOST HOLY BISHOP OF KITROS, UNTO THE MOST SACRED BISHOP OF DYRRACHIUM, CABASILAS: ON THE DISPENSATION OF FOODS IN THE HANDED-DOWN WEEKS, AND WHICH THESE ARE [^3889]

We dispense therefore Wednesday and Friday of the New Week, reckoning this entire week as one single day, and rendering it nothing less than Sunday in radiance; therefore also on every day, at Matins, the reading of the Resurrection Gospels takes place.[^3890] We dispense also the Twelve Days, for the repulse[^3891] of the Armenian fast;[^3892] for these men, fasting the twelve days before Theophany, celebrate thus three feasts combined on the fifth of the month of January: the Annunciation, I say, the Nativity of Christ, and the Baptism; and even more so, not openly in some manner, but in shadowy guise, holding forth the ruinous and defiled glory of their heresiarch, and the name blasphemous unto Him, asserting therefrom that the dispensation of the Word of God was in appearance and not in truth.[^3893]

We dispense also the entire week before Meatfare, deeming another crafty custom of those same Armenians overthrown thereby; for[^3894] they fast throughout this [week] also on account of the loss of a dog, whose namesake was Artzivourion, badly going before and proclaiming in cities or villages the coming of their teacher Sergius; for Artzivourion in the Armenian tongue means "messenger"; which [dog], when Sergius wept for him having been devoured by wild beasts, he commanded all the Armenians to fast during all those days with total abstinence unto the end, and to lament fittingly and mourn;[^3895] even though, craftily concealing the abomination, they strive to accomplish it in remembrance of the Ninevite fast.[^3896]

Throughout the entire week before Cheesefare, the so-called[^3897] Middle-Fasters have a great fast; and for the refutation of them all, we dispense the fasting days equally with the non-fasting days.

From Renewal [Week] even unto Pentecost, on Wednesdays and Fridays, we do not praise fasting until the ninth [hour]; but even if we reject the eating of cheese and meat out of reverence for the Apostolic Canon, yet we receive oil and fish;[^3898] for on these days, even though making remembrance of the Lord's Crucifixion, we sing troparia suitable to the Crucifixion, yet we also join the Resurrectional [hymns] unto them, as also on others we intermingle penitential [hymns].[^3899]

The same do we also at the feast of the Transfiguration, in the midst of the fasting days[^3900] it being in the midst of the fasting days; and at all the universal festivals of the Mother of God, if they fall on a Wednesday or on a Friday; and also of the honorable Forerunner and Baptist, and of the foremost Apostles Peter and Paul, and of any other saint who is celebrated and radiant.[^3901]

If, however, Mid-Pentecost fall on Wednesday, we are accustomed indeed to sing the Resurrectional troparia, and not those of the Cross; yet we do not make a dispensation of meat or cheese; nor do we read the Resurrection Gospel at Matins, as [we do] on the Wednesday and Friday of the New Week, and for this reason neither do we eat meat thereon.[^3902]

Nor yet on the Wednesday before the Ascension; for although we sing the Resurrection Canon thereon, yet with it we also combine the Forefeast hymns of the Ascension, and neither do we read the Resurrection Gospel at Matins.[^3903]

Whenever therefore on Wednesday or Friday honorable feasts occur, it is meet to observe both the joyful character thereof and the reverence of the fast in the single dispensation of oil and fish; for in this manner wilt thou find all our Fathers to have walked.[^3904]

We dispense also the entire week after Pentecost in honor of the Holy Spirit, even as [we dispense] the other in honor of our Savior[^3905] Jesus Christ; for the Holy Spirit is equally honorable, even as unto the Father, so also unto the Son; for by Them, through the Father's good pleasure, the mystery of our edification was ordered, and the illumination of the knowledge of God shone forth unto us.[^3906]

If the Eve of any Master's feast happen to fall on Wednesday or on Friday, it is not fitting to dispense the fast in the evening for the sake of the morrow's feast.[^3907]

He who dispenses the fast of Wednesday and Friday on account of bodily weakness shall be judged according to what the sixty-ninth Apostolic Canon prescribes; but he who is constrained by weakness may comfort the body with oil and[^3908] fish; but as for meat and cheese, neither in the Great Forty Days shall he be forgiven to touch them, even if he be drawing his last breath; nor on any Wednesday or Friday. For when we dispense these, lest we be thought to share the mindset of the heterodox, eating both meat and cheese as an armor of intention—and especially if we happen to dwell among such—it is not unto these appetites that we indulge the belly![^3909]

On fasting days, from the ninth hour, after the customary prayers, with bread only and water, and vegetables[^3910] or figs, or dates, do we satisfy bodily necessity; unless some illness distress him. For since even on the day before the Holy Theophany, it is commanded to fast until after the evening psalmody and the divine hierarchical service joined thereto, when we are accustomed to come unto bodily food: let it be without partaking of oil and fish.[^3911] For if this day—I say, the Eve of the Holy Theophany—happen to fall on a Sunday, Theophilus of Alexandria commands to partake of figs only, or dates, so much as to preserve ourselves from appearing[^3912] to fast on Sunday: how then, if it fall upon another day, shall we touch richer food?

If, however, the day of the Holy Theophany itself fall on a Wednesday or on a Friday: it is sufficient for us to dispense the fast prescribed on such days, according to the sixty-ninth Canon of the Holy Apostles, partaking of oil and fish; but to eat meat or cheese is the invention of those who manifest belly-madness, and not the command of Apostolic legislation. For the Kingdom of God is not food and drink, and the rest.[^3913]
