# PART LI: AGAIN: DIVERSE INJUNCTIONS OF THE HOLY APOSTLES AND OF THE GOD-BEARING HOLY FATHERS [^3914]

I, Peter, and Paul, Apostles of Christ, enjoin upon the servants of Christ concerning human labors, that they shall work six days: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, and Saturday until midday,[^3915] or until the third hour; or again, the entire day on Saturday to rest from heavy labors, and to attend unto the household, and to accomplish the memorials for the deceased, and hospitality unto strangers, and the love of hospitality;[^3916] for Saturday has the grace of creation and is called rest; while Sunday is the first day of God, possessing the grace of the Resurrection.[^3917] Therefore do we enjoin to honor these days: on Saturday to cease from every labor, both small and great, from the eighth hour, and to hasten unto church, all men with their wives and with their children; and to abide therein with the fear of God, praying even until the morning of Sunday; and when the holy[^3918] Liturgy is dismissed, thus to depart unto their homes, and to rest until the morrow on Monday; and thus from the second hour to begin every manual work.[^3919]

*Concerning the Nativity of Christ:*

The feast day of the Nativity is likewise to be kept even as Sunday; for on this day our Lord Jesus Christ granted salvation unto the world.[^3920]

*Concerning the Theophany:*

The feast of the Holy Theophany it behooves every Christian to honor and keep likewise; for on this day the Creator granted renewal unto all by water and the Spirit.[^3921]

*Concerning the Annunciation:*

Render ye honor unto the feast of the Annunciation, as being most honorable among all[^3922] the Master's feasts.[^3923]

[Honor ye also] the Saturday of righteous Lazarus, bearing the beginning and prefiguration of the Resurrection, and the most honorable feast of the miracles of Christ.[^3924]

And again: the Ascension of Christ, and the Descent of the Holy Spirit, when enlightenment and understanding came down into the world unto all; likewise also honor ye and keep all the holy feasts of Christ even as we have said: both the Transfiguration of the Savior, and the Exaltation of the Honorable Cross, being Master's feasts. All these feasts of Christ are thus to be kept and honored even as we have said concerning holy Sunday, the first divine day.[^3925]

*Feasts of the Mother of God:*

The feasts of our most holy Lady, the Mother of God[^3926] it behooves to honor and glorify likewise, even as the feasts of Christ, which we have indicated; thus also these feasts of the Mother of God: the Conception,[^3927] and Her Nativity, the Entry into the Holy of Holies, and Her Dormition; and to accomplish and celebrate the memory of Her holy parents.[^3928]

The feast of the holy and all-praised Apostles Peter and Paul is likewise to be honored and celebrated, as we have said concerning them. Likewise also the feasts of the other twelve Apostles: whenever each one's day shall be, it behooves to celebrate that very day from morning until evening.[^3929]

The feasts of the honorable Prophet, Forerunner, and Baptist John: the Nativity, and the Beheading of his honorable[^3930] head, it behooves to celebrate from the ninth hour and from morning the entire day.[^3931]

The memory of the Protomartyr Stephen the Archdeacon is to be celebrated from morning until evening.[^3932]

In like manner also the memories of the holy and venerable universal teachers, fathers, and hierarchs, pastors unto the rational sheep: these are to be celebrated, whensoever each one's [feast] shall be, from morning until evening.[^3933]

Of the holy Great Martyrs of Christ: George, Demetrius, Theodore, Panteleimon, Procopius, and the holy Unmercenaries; and of the holy Great Martyr women, as many as are called great: unto all these is to be celebrated each one's day, from morning until midday.[^3934]

On all these days wherein we have commanded every Christian to celebrate:[^3935]

And again we say, that we do not command any Christian man to celebrate with timbrels, and pipes, and goat-like bellowing, and drunkenness; but to celebrate and honor with prayers, and hymns, and doxologies; and that every Christian is to call priests unto his house, and to perform blessings in his dwellings. For wheresoever the priest comes not and performs no blessing, thence God also departs; and wheresoever the priest censes not nor makes prayer, in despondency and laxity all things are defiled.[^3936]

These things do we enjoin upon the priests and church clerics: that they themselves[^3937] walk in these commandments, and thereafter also teach the people always: not for the sake of any reward, or of gold, or for the sake of silver, but for the sake of the salvation of their own soul.[^3938]

Unto the people, both small and great, do we thus enjoin you: to give ear and submit unto the hierarchs and priests, and to honor and revere them, each of you according to his ability as he possesses, and to provide for them; for they pray on your behalf.[^3939]

Unto priests we enjoin: not with enmity and hatred to enter into the sanctuary, nor to dare to touch the holy things; nor to be a drunkard, nor to steal; neither to revile one another; nor to be contentious, nor foul-mouthed, nor insolent; as our Lord Jesus Christ, being beaten and[^3940] mocked, suffered for our sake; but let them be gentle, quiet, humble, patient in all things, and walk in the fear of God, and be diligent concerning that ministry of theirs.[^3941]

We counsel them according to the tradition of the holy Apostles to be the husband of only one wife, that he may not approach unlawfully unto the holy altar; and that he be not a fornicator, nor an adulterer, or an abuser of himself with mankind, or an abuser of beasts; for let such a one not draw near, nor ever think upon the priesthood; neither let him be a murderer, nor an extortioner, nor a robber; but let him be pure from all things: the husband of only one wife, as we have said, and free from every sin[^3942] and pure, and undefiled; and thus to approach unto this great and fearful ministry.[^3943]

*Concerning the Church Offering:*

The blessings brought unto the church, we command these to be not only for the priests, but also for all the church servers in the holy work of God; and it is meet to divide them into three parts: two parts unto the priest, and the third part unto the laborers who serve.[^3944]

*Concerning Holy Communion:*

As for those who are under penances: for what sins soever one may be excommunicated, whether for one year, or two, or three, or four, or five, or six, or seven, or eight; and after eight years he is forgiven, according to the strength[^3945] of each one, and according to his labor: how he has compelled himself, or how he has been moved to compunction.[^3946]

And concerning eating and drinking: as each one is able. And when anyone is yet in penance, let him not enter into the church; but let him enter and stand wheresoever he wills at Matins, and at the Hours, and at Vespers, and at the Liturgy. But when the priest arrives at the [Liturgy of the] Catechumens, then let him go out into the church narthex, and let him stand until the dismissal of the Liturgy.[^3947]

And at the Nativity of Christ, and at the Theophany, and on Great Thursday, and on Great Saturday, and at Pascha, let him partake of the agiasma, that is, of the sanctified water; and on Peter's day, and at the Dormition of the Most Holy Theotokos. Such a one on these days is to eat a whole[^3948] week, meat; but if he is a monk, let him eat cheese and fish. And again let him enter into his penance.[^3949]

And every dispensation unto such a one is: one week after Pascha, two weeks after the Nativity of Christ, and Meatfare Week, and Cheesefare Week. And in those four weeks let him eat meat and cheese; and monks likewise cheese and fish. But as for those who are in penance for such [grave offenses], not even then is it fitting to slacken them, on account of the grave sins which they have committed.[^3950]

It is befitting also to examine men and women, and monks, and nuns, and whoever it may be: whether they know the number [and] in how many manners they have committed fornication. But if from the multitude [thereof] they do not know[^3951] nor even the number, such a one is a fornicator.[^3952]

And unto all who are in such sins, the canons of the holy fathers command them to eat once a day throughout all days. Unto monks, exceedingly dry food; and unto laymen, to eat dry food, and injunctions unto each of them as it shall be commanded. And on Wednesday, and Friday, and Monday, xerophagy [dry-eating] until the very evening, except only on account of infirmity and a feast of the Lord. And wine as the spiritual father shall command him according to his strength.[^3953]

---

# PART LII: AGAIN: OTHER INJUNCTIONS FROM THE BOOKS OF THE LAW: CONCERNING DEGREES OF KINSHIP [^3954]

*Concerning Forbidden Marriages and concerning the Diverse Degrees of Lineage Which It Is Befitting to Guard, from Holy Baptism, and concerning That Which Is by[^3955]* flesh and blood.[^3956] Together with this, there is also kinship with marital in-laws, and it is spoken of among men. And it is divided into three orders: into the ascending, and into the descending, and into the collateral.[^3957]

The ascending are those who have begotten and do beget: that is, father, grandfathers, and grandmothers. And the descending are those begotten of us: that is, sons, and daughters, and grandsons, and granddaughters. And the collateral are, as is manifestly said, those holding lineage together with us: that is, brothers, and sisters, and those [descended] from them.[^3958]

And three are the orders of boundaries forbidding related persons in marriage: One order and first boundary: that which is from holy and salvific baptism. The second order and boundary:[^3959]

...that of those manifestly recognized in person according to the kinship of the blood of the flesh.[^3960]

The third order and boundary: that of those recognized from marital affinity; that is, of two-fold in-laws: first, and second, and third.[^3961]

And their degrees, and boundaries, and rules have many distinctions, and rigorous examinations, which it is befitting for us true Christians very diligently to examine concerning marriages; and by no means unto the end should there be found even a lower degree of lineage [than permitted]; and only then may a Christian marriage be accomplished, as is fitting for the servants of God to be, and for such a marriage to be blessed by God: whether with a written contract or without a written contract, only according to the testimony[^3962] of many witnesses, there being testimony of men and women.[^3963]

And when a man is fifteen years of age, so let him enter into marriage; and when a woman is twelve years of age, so let her also enter into marriage; by the consent and desire of their parents, so that the union may be according to much testimony and with blessing.[^3964]

*Concerning Forbidden Marriages:*

That which is forbidden from holy baptism is this: A godfather from his baptized daughter [goddaughter]; and from the sister of that baptized daughter. But the other relatives of the father and mother of such a daughter are not forbidden to marry the relatives of the godfather.[^3965]

If anyone baptizes a maiden, and thereafter takes her as a bride for his son, let such be separated; and the parents who consented are to be excommunicated to do penance.[^3966]

Let it be known concerning relatives according to the flesh: parents, children unto parents; brothers unto brothers; and their children, called first cousins; likewise also their children, called second cousins; likewise also the children unto second cousins, which are third cousins; and unto all these it is not fitting to be joined in marriage.[^3967] But the children of third cousins may assemble and be joined in lawful marriage.[^3968]

*Concerning Degrees:*

Give ear and understand the first degree: as father unto son, and son unto father, are of the first degree, even as it was the first degree of begetting.[^3969]

And grandfather unto grandson are of the second degree, even as it was a degree of begetting. In like manner also a brother unto his own brother is of the second degree, even as there are two degrees; for it calls the begettings degrees.[^3970]

If anyone asks thee, saying: "Of what degree is thy father?" Say thou: "Of the first; for my father begot me, and this was the first begetting, and this is the first degree." And if he says unto thee: "Of what degree is thy grandfather?" Say thou unto him: "Of the second; for my grandfather begot my father, and that is one degree;[^3971]

...and my father begot me, and this is the first degree, but the second begetting; therefore of the second degree is my grandfather unto me."[^3972]

That we may speak manifestly: begin therefore to ascend upon a ladder, and thou desirest to step upon the first step; and this is that which we call the first, of the father. And thereafter from the first step thou shalt step ascending up higher upon the second step; and concerning this we say: my grandfather is the second step.[^3973]

And if he says unto thee: "And of what degree unto thee are thy brethren?" Say thou unto him: "That these also are of the second degree unto me; for my father begot me, and this was the first degree, one begetting; and thus he begot my brethren; and behold, two degrees."[^3974]

In like manner also first cousins [first brother's children], according to the law of kinship, are of the fourth degree; neither is it befitting, nor is it right to join them in marriage.[^3975]

Likewise also the children of first cousins, being second cousins [second brother's children], are of the sixth degree; neither is it befitting for these to marry one another. And if it shall happen that this marriage has taken place, the law commands that they be separated, and rather that they do penance.[^3976]

Likewise also the children of second cousins are third cousins [third brother's children], and are of the eighth degree; neither is it right for these to enter into marriage. But if it has happened from ignorance that such a marriage has taken place, or[^3977] *Concerning Forbidden Marriages:*

...or for the sake of some unknown matter, then let them not be separated now, but let them remain; nevertheless, it is fitting for them concerning such a sin to be diligent with almsgiving and fasting.[^3978] In knowledge, however, let heed be taken unto this, that it by no means take place. Leaving aside therefore the generation and kinship of third cousins from that point unto the eighth degree, and what follows: without any prohibition let them be taken into marriage; within the eighth degree, however, let there be no marriage, that is, for example: the eighth degree is called [the boundary] of the entire generation of third cousins; and if it should happen to take place through some ignorance, let them be separated.[^3979] These things, therefore, are concerning kinship, and[^3980] of natural blood; and concerning these we have written and established for certain knowledge.

*18. Concerning Relatives by Marriage:*[^3981]

That which pertains unto known relatives from marital kinship is this: If anyone takes a widow as wife, and that woman has a daughter by another husband: she is a daughter unto him also, even as unto that woman; and it is fitting for him to keep himself exceedingly from her, as from his very own daughter. In like manner also a father-in-law from the wife of his son; and a son from his stepmother; and a brother-in-law from the wife of his brother, and of a brother-in-law.[^3982]

Let a son look upon the face of his mother with great fear, and let him render honor unto her always. Let a father take heed unto himself concerning the gaze upon his daughter, and let him keep himself.[^3983] In like manner also *Concerning Forbidden Marriages:*

...let brethren take heed unto themselves from their sisters.

Concerning relatives by marriage of whom we spoke above: when they shall assemble at weddings so that marriage may be sought, let it be carefully investigated, lest marital kinship should happen to exist, that is to say, in-laws. It is fitting to search with certainty and with much examination, even as the Divine law commands.[^3984] For there are in-laws of the first, second, and third degree; it is fitting to take heed concerning these. It is fitting also to know concerning this: that unto each spouse, husband and wife, the parents indeed of the husband—the father, and the mother, and the brethren—and the parents of his wife and her brethren, are called the first in-laws.[^3985]

And the first cousins of the husband and of his wife: these are called second in-laws. And the second cousins of the wife and of the husband are again third in-laws.[^3986] And so the first in-laws are not taken in marriage unto the first in-laws, nor unto the second. In like manner also a son or a brother unto a husband does not mix with the first cousins of his wife; but the second cousins of the husband are taken and mixed without hindrance with the second and third cousins of his wife.[^3987]

Since therefore we have spoken concerning the degrees of lineage, and of natural blood, and of kinship, we say again: that until eight degrees of kinsmen and kinship are concluded, let heed be taken that there be no taking in marriage among them;[^3988] *Concerning the Degrees of Kinship:*

...and concerning kinship by marriage, that is, concerning in-laws: and these until the seventh degree is concluded, that is, of husband and wife.[^3989] If that woman has a first cousin, she is with the husband of that woman of the fourth degree. And the son of my first cousin is unto me a nephew, from my first cousin; and it is not fitting to take the first cousin of my wife.[^3990] Even as also my brother [cannot take] the sister of my wife, [nor] can he take my first cousin, nor my nephew, nor the nephew of my son, nor the first cousin of my son, nor the second cousins who are according to the lineage of my wife.[^3991] For a wife with her brethren are of the second degree; and her husband with[^3992] his own first cousin, are of the fourth degree; and the four degrees do not assemble together, nor can marital union exist within them, unless it reaches unto the measure and number of the seventh degree. Neither can the nephew of my wife take the daughter of my sister. For he is called the great maternal uncle who is the sister's brother, that is, brother and sister. And indeed the brother of my mother is unto me a great maternal uncle, and this is of the third degree by measure.[^3993] In like manner also the sister of my mother is unto me a great maternal aunt. And the first cousin of my mother or of my father is unto me a lesser maternal uncle and a lesser aunt.[^3994] And if there be my third cousins, or a son, *Of the Holy Fathers:*

...or a daughter, without hindrance let them be taken [in marriage] with the children, the third cousins of my wife.[^3995]

If anyone baptizes a child, and being godfather shall take him again as son-in-law unto his daughter: let them be separated; and the priest who blessed them, let him be deposed; for he is a godson according to the Holy Spirit.[^3996]

If anyone takes a wife, and lies with her, and thereafter defiles himself with his mother-in-law: then let that mother-in-law go and be tonsured in a monastery, and let her serve God concerning her soul; and let that husband live with his wife; let them labor concerning that sin for fifteen years, having received penance from their spiritual father.[^3997]

If anyone shall be the adoptive son of anyone, that is, an adopted son: such a one cannot defile himself with the wife of his named father, nor with his concubine, whom I call a paramour; therefore he is not to marry any woman whatsoever from the lineage of his named father.[^3998]

It is not fitting during the Holy Great Forty Days to perform dedications of martyrs, or baptisms, or crownings; except on Saturday and on Sunday to perform without hindrance the memory of saints, and for the departed, and baptisms. But if it should occur on account of mortal sickness, then on whatever day it may be, let the infant or anyone whatsoever be baptized.[^3999]

If anyone has a daughter by another wife, and thereafter comes and takes my sister as wife: then I no longer have [the right][^4000] *Of the Holy Fathers:*

...how to take and marry that daughter of his. And if she leaves her husband, and goes and takes another husband, and bears a daughter with him: then I have no way to marry that daughter, nor my son whom I have by another wife; for they are brethren. And if any woman whatsoever be betrothed unto my father, and thereafter, even if he has not lain with her: I have no way to marry her, for she is a mother unto me. In like manner also if she be the betrothed of my brother, even if he has not lain with her: yet she is a sister-in-law unto me, and I dare not touch her.[^4001]

The holy councils, of the holy Apostles, and of the venerable Fathers, commanded that a third marriage shall not exist. But if any priest, knowing this, blesses one who marries thrice: let him be deposed from the priesthood.[^4002]

If anyone does not bear children with his first wife, nor with his second: then let him now desist from marriage; if his second wife dies unto him, let him thus remain in purity in the Lord. But if being yet thirty-five or forty years of age, he marries again a third time: let such a one be forbidden unto repentance for five years, and thereafter let him receive communion. But if being young, he is thirty years of age: then let him do penance for three years. But if he is forty-five or fifty years old, and does this: the Holy Church of God does not receive such a one, as defiled by deceit.[^4003]

*Of the Holy Fathers:*

...and it forbids him for seven years to repent with great repentance; and then let him receive communion on holy Pascha. But if any priest dares to give him communion before he finishes seven years in repentance: then let him again begin to repent, that he may complete seven years. And that priest, if he did this with knowledge: let him be forbidden to serve for a certain time; for it is not befitting for a priest to be a mocker of God. As for those who say that it was commanded and that the Holy Church of God receives one who has married thrice, and one who has married four times: Anathema.[^4004]

*Concerning the Spiritual Father:*[^4005]

Take heed, therefore, O spiritual father: examine well concerning sins, how each one *Injunctions:*

...has zeal to repent. And unto the strong who have zeal, entrust two parts of the rule commanded unto them by the Scripture, and leave the third part upon thyself; but unto the weak and those who have not zeal, entrust half of what is commanded unto them, and half upon thyself.[^4006] And it is befitting for thee day and night to cast [thy care] upon God, and to pray unto Him for those who confess unto thee.[^4007] It is befitting also for thee to make for them twelve prostrations by day and by night:[^4008] and at the Midnight Office, three prostrations; and at Compline, three; and at Matins, three; and at the Hours [three]; so that from the snares of the enemy thou mayest be free, and mayest deliver others from demonic bonds[^4009] *Of the Holy Fathers:*

...deliver. But if thou art not worthy thus to do and to pray for them, and much more not even for thyself: then neither attempt the path of the spiritual fatherhood, nor be called [spiritual father], lest there be woe unto thee: ❧[^4010]

---

# PART LIII: DEGREES OF KINSHIP: AND CONCERNING LAWFUL MARRIAGE, AND THOSE WHO MARRY UNLAWFULLY, AND CONCERNING THE DISTINCTION OF KINSHIP WHICH IS OF FLESH AND BLOOD [^4011]

*Where it is befitting to contract marriage, and where it is not befitting; and where it is fitting to bring any person unto marriage, and whom not to bring; and whom the law forbids, and whom it does not forbid, and whom it discerns:*[^4012]

Three boundaries there are concerning forbidden marriages:[^4013] One which is from salvific *Injunctions:*

...baptism; and the second, which is kinship according to the flesh; and the third, which is the union from marriage, that is, marital affinity [in-laws].[^4014] Moreover, marital in-laws also have many diverse rules according to conjunction, which it is fitting for true Christians very diligently to examine with investigation. And thus, when the man is fifteen years of age, and the woman twelve years of age, with the consent, desire, and blessing of parents, and of the priest.[^4015]

Be it known that what the law of holy baptism forbids:[^4016] it forbids only the baptizer from his baptized daughter [goddaughter], and forbids his son from her; and from the mother of the baptized daughter it forbids them; likewise also their other children born[^4017] *Of the Holy Fathers:*

...it forbids, that is, those of the baptizer, and of that woman whose children he baptizes; but their other relatives, lesser and greater, near and distant, it does not forbid from marriage.[^4018]

Relatives according to the flesh let them be examined well and diligently, and let them be corrected; for kinship, having a generative and lawful origin, is divided into the orders of superior and inferior degrees, and that which is from the right and left sides [collateral], and that which is from distant lineages.[^4019] And the superior of the lineage are: father, and mother, grandfather, and grandmother. And the inferior degrees are: son, and daughter, grandson, and granddaughter. And that which is from the right and left sides are: brother and sister, maternal uncle (*uika*) and paternal uncle/aunt (*lelya*), male first cousin (*anepsios*) and female first cousin (*anepsia*)[^4020] *Injunctions:*

...and indeed the paternal uncle (*stryika*) with the nephew (*anepsios*), a brother's son, are of the first degree;[^4021] and full brothers (*prisnii, yezhe samobratni*) are of the second degree; and first cousins (*pervii bratuchada*) are of the fourth degree; and second cousins (*vtorii bratuchada*) are of the sixth degree; and third cousins (*tretii bratuchada*) are of the eighth degree.[^4022] In all these degrees there is by no means any marital union. But the children and offspring of third cousins are unforbidden unto marriage; for lineage ascends unto the seventh degree, and the eighth is loosed [permitted].[^4023]

Likewise also let marital in-laws be examined well, lest in any way without discretion the union be unlawful, and the wrath of God overtake such persons: and especially bishops and[^4024] *Of the Holy Fathers:*

...spiritual fathers who do not direct rightly concerning these things.[^4025]

Be it known that my own brother by birth, and the brother of my wife, and her mother, are first in-laws; and their first cousins are second in-laws; likewise also their second cousins are third in-laws. And first in-laws are not to unite with first in-laws; nor first with second; but with third in-laws let first in-laws unite without hindrance.[^4026] But my sister with the brother of my wife by no means; nor is my brother's son or daughter to unite with the nephews/nieces (*anepsioi*) of my wife; nor unto my stepmother may I ever even contemplate [marriage], nor unto her daughter whom she has[^4027] *Injunctions:*

...by another husband and not by my father; nor my son unto my sister; nor my daughter with my brother; let them not dare even in mind to contemplate [marriage] unto the daughter of my wife whom she has by another husband, for she is my daughter; nor does my son whom I have by another wife dare anything toward her; nor unto the wife of my son do I dare to contemplate [marriage].[^4028]

Unto all this kinship, therefore, it was forbidden to unite in marriage. But my first cousins do not unite with the first female cousin of my wife; nor with her second female cousin; but my first cousin unites in marriage with the third female cousin of my wife without hindrance; likewise also[^4029] *Of the Holy Fathers:*

...my second cousins unto the third cousins of my wife. The nephews and nieces (*anepsioi*) of my wife do not unite with the children of my brother or of my sister. But the children of the second cousins of my wife unite without hindrance with the children of my second cousins; while the children of the second cousins of my wife do not touch the children of my second cousins.[^4030]

Likewise it is befitting to investigate and search out with certainty also concerning the other lineages that are analogous unto these lineages; and thus to establish marriage, and unite, and accomplish [it] without any doubt, even as is befitting for true Christians: ❧[^4031] *Injunctions:*

---

# PART LIV: CONCERNING CARRION [ABOMINATIONS] WHICH IT IS NOT BEFITTING TO EAT [^4032]

We command therefore, also concerning that which is strangled, and concerning carrion [abominations]: that no one among Christians should taste such things; nor having slaughtered [an animal], to drain the blood and bake it, which certain senseless persons do; for the Law of God commands that meat in the blood—the soul—shall not be eaten (cf. Gen. 9:4; Lev. 17:11–14); for the blood of every beast is its life [soul].[^4033]

Likewise also those who set nets for the sake of hunting, and beasts or creeping things are strangled therein, and they taking them eat [them], or [an animal] hunted and strangled by dogs: unto such persons the Law of God forbids to do these things; except only that which is slain, either with an arrow, or with a spear, or with a sword by human hands[^4034] *Of the Holy Fathers:*

...so that its blood be poured out: this let everyone eat. But if anyone, besides this, eats anything else of the forbidden things: let such a one be separated for one hundred and fifty days, [performing] twelve prostrations each day.[^4035] But as for that which is seized by a hawk, any kind of reptile [or creature]: if anyone takes it quickly and suddenly, while it is still warm in its blood: then let him slaughter it, and let everyone eat [it]; but if he delays, not to eat such a thing.[^4036] But apart from such things as were commanded for every Christian to eat: all other strangled and unslaughtered things let them be cast out unto dogs and creeping things [scavengers].[^4037]

*Those who eat a raven, or a crow, a jackdaw, a cuckoo, a hawk, or whatever kind of*[^4038] *Injunctions:*

...eagle, or gull: let such persons repent under penance for one year, [performing] one hundred prostrations.[^4039]

*Those who eat a wolf, a fox, a bear, a dog, a cat, a hedgehog, a dormouse, a marten, a squirrel, and all other things whatsoever are unclean: a grass-snake, a turtle, and every beast, both small and great; or a horse, or a donkey; whether of wild beasts or of pastured herds, whatsoever the Law of God designates [as unclean]:*[^4040]

If anyone be found eating this of his own will and desire: let him repent for four years; but if he ate through constraint and necessity: let him repent for one year, [performing] fifteen prostrations.[^4041]

*If into a well from which water does not flow out, there fall any reptile [or animal], and be drowned*[^4042] *Concerning Forbidden Foods:*

...any [creature], and be drowned; or an animal: if it be found quickly and taken out, let three buckets of that water be poured out; and so let everyone drink from that well—that is, if that which was drowned in it, whether an animal or a reptile, is found quickly on the first day.[^4043] But if it remains until the second day or until the third, and thereafter is taken out: let nine buckets of that water be poured out, and so let them pour in holy water (*hagiasma*), and let them drink again from that well.[^4044] Thus let them pour in holy water if, being [found] quickly, they suddenly cleanse it. But if, having remained for many days, it rots in it: let them pour out from it forty buckets of water, and so let[^4045] *Injunctions:*

...the priest come with a server [cleric], and kindle three candles around it, and cense, and say the prayer, and sanctify it; and then let them drink from it.[^4046] But if its water flows and goes forth outside: such a thing harms us in no way.[^4047] But if [an unclean creature] falls into wine, or into oil: if it be found quickly, let it be taken out, and let the priest come and sanctify it.[^4048] But if it delays until it begins to rot in it unto the second day: let it be decanted into another clean vessel, and let it be sanctified by the priest. But if it remains until it rots [completely]: it is not befitting to taste it, but let it all be poured out onto the ground.[^4049]

*If it happens that any reptile [or vermin] whatsoever breeds [in wheat]*[^4050] *Concerning Forbidden Foods:*

...or of unclean animals in wheat, and defiles it: then let him wash the wheat well with water, and let it be sanctified by the priest, and then let them grind it and eat [it]; but let them not make prosphora from that wheat.[^4051]

*If a Jew defiles anything whatsoever with his hand, having taken hold of it, whether in wine, or in oil, or anything else of such things:*[^4052]

It is not befitting for a Christian to taste it; but let the priest come and sanctify it, and thereafter let it be tasted.

*Whosoever eats with an Armenian, or with a Paulician, or with any other heretic whatsoever, and especially if anyone has affection [close fellowship] with such a one: unto him we say that he shall desist from this, and come pure unto the church*[^4053] *Injunctions:*

...and if he has done this through ignorance, let the priest cleanse him.[^4054] But if he knows and has heard the admonition, let him again sanctify him, having given him a small penance from the sanctions. But if he does not obey the admonition, but desires to eat and drink with them: let such a one not eat with a Christian, and let him not be received into church, but let every Christian turn away from him as from an idolater.[^4055] And if ever he comes again unto confession: let him be separated for repentance for three years; and during two years let there not be received from his house either prosphora or any offering whatsoever; and in the third year let his prosphora be received in church, and so[^4056] *Of the Holy Fathers:*

...let him complete the third year in repentance.

*If anyone communicates [has fellowship] with a Hebrew, and is like-minded with him in their faith:*[^4057]

And if ever he returns unto Christianity: let him be separated for repentance for nine years: three years in the place of the catechumens; and thereafter let his prosphora be received in church, and let him perform the remainder in repentance; and in the ninth year let him receive communion of the Holy Mysteries.[^4058]

*Those who marry off their sons or daughters unto heterodox persons:*[^4059]

Let such persons be separated for five years; likewise also the priests who crowned [married] them, let them also be separated for three years, outside the church.[^4060]

*A grain-caster [sorcerer], or anyone else of such persons, who knows this diabolical work, or*[^4061] *Injunctions:*

...concerning wine, or by any other bewitchment [*ochybom*]: if they desist from this, let them be separated for four years, [performing] one hundred prostrations each day.[^4062]

*If anyone betroths a maiden, and thereafter someone else seduces her and defiles her, wishing to take her [to wife]:*[^4063]

This is not befitting; but if her first betrothed desires [her] again, let him take her.[^4064]

*Concerning the Memorial of the Departed:*[^4065]

Unto the departed, therefore, it is befitting to make memorials and oblations: on the third day (*tretyny*), and the ninth day (*devyatyny*), and the twentieth day (*dvadesyatyny*), and the fortieth day (*chetyrydesyatyny*), and at six months, and at the completed year; likewise also on Meatfare Saturday, and Cheesefare Saturday, and on the seventh Saturday after Pascha [Ancestral Saturday before Pentecost]: of these[^4066] *Of the Holy Fathers:*

...for on account of these things we believe that they find absolution of their sins.[^4067]

*Those who estrange themselves from prayers and chanting of their own will, and walk like beasts:*[^4068]

Let them be separated for repentance for one year, [performing] one hundred metanias [prostrations].

*Whosoever of his own will casts himself down and kills himself: let them neither chant over him, nor ever make memorial for him. But if not of his own will he falls, but is killed and dies: let them chant over him, and let them make memorial.*[^4069]

*If anyone goes out unto adultery, or unto fornication, or unto theft, or unto brigandage; and if in any way from these things he is killed and dies:*[^4070]

Let no one chant over him, and let them make no memorial whatsoever for him.

*Injunctions:*

*Unto every parent it is befitting to marry his son when the years of his age are completed, fifteen years; and the daughter, twelve years; for this is the true law:*[^4071]

But if, through neglect of the parents, the years lawfully appointed pass by for the son or daughter, and it happens that one of them falls into fornication: this sin is upon the parents.[^4072] But if the daughter before twelve years, or the son before fifteen, one of them commits fornication: this sin is upon the one who commits it, and they shall receive wrath from the Lord.

*If anyone sets fire to someone's courtyard, or threshing floor, or house: let him receive a penance of twenty years, when he confesses*[^4073] *Of the Holy Fathers:*

...unto his spiritual father. But if they exact satisfaction against him, or kill [anyone], or seize him and beat him, and plunder his possessions: then let him receive a penance of ten years, [performing] two hundred prostrations each day.[^4074] But if he receives twenty years of penance, then every day let him perform four hundred prostrations.[^4075] But if he sinned unintentionally, let him repent for ten years.[^4076]

He that contracts a second marriage, being advanced in years: let him repent for two years.[^4077] But if he be young, and his wife dies: then if he is able, let him endure thus according to the word of the Apostle; but if he cannot, let him take a second wife.[^4078] But if he is old and contracts a second marriage[^4079] *Injunctions:*

...such a one angers God: let Him repent and be separated for three years, [performing] twenty-four prostrations.[^4080]

And if he contracts a third [marriage]: let him repent for four years, [performing] sixty-six prostrations each day; for it is called fornication.[^4081]

Having contracted a fourth [marriage]: let him repent for eight years, [performing] one hundred prostrations; for such a one commits fornication and angers God.[^4082]

A fornicator: twelve years.[^4083]

He that commits self-pollution: three years; thirty prostrations.[^4084]

A practitioner of unnatural vice with men: five years; thirty-six prostrations.[^4085]

He that commits fornication with women contrary to nature, into the seat: let him repent for four years; one hundred and fifty prostrations.[^4086]

*Of the Holy Fathers:*

And if he has been doing this with many women: let his spiritual father give him a greater penance.[^4087]

Likewise also is every sin to be calculated and observed, how much and of what manner it is; for it is one thing [with] one woman, and another [with] two; and another [with] a third woman, and another [with] many; likewise also for a woman: it is one thing [with] one man, and another [with] two men, and another [with] a third man, and another [with] many men.[^4088]

If anyone commits carnal sin with a beast which is not eaten: let him repent for three years. But if he has done this for many years: ten or twelve years; three hundred prostrations.[^4089] And if with an animal which is for food: let him repent for fifteen years; [performing][^4090] *Injunctions:*

...five hundred prostrations; and let that beast defiled by him be cut in pieces for the dogs to eat.[^4091]

He that commits bestial sin with a dog: nine years; one hundred and sixty prostrations.[^4092]

And if with a married woman: six years; five hundred prostrations.[^4093]

And if with a maiden, and he does not take her to wife: nine years; three hundred prostrations; and let his property be taken from him and given unto her.[^4094] And if she be betrothed to another man, and that one defiles her: then let him give twenty-four gold pieces unto the Great Church.[^4095]

And if anyone secretly defiled a maiden, and nothing is known concerning him: let him repent for twelve years; [performing][^4096] *Of the Holy Fathers:*

...three hundred [prostrations]; and this [shall be] according to the discretion of the spiritual father.[^4097]

If a married woman, or a maiden, or a nun, is defiled by violence from any man: then if she was far from people, she has cause to say that the man violated her by force, and there was no man anywhere there that she might cry out unto him: let a small penance be given her by the [spiritual] father according to the person, as she may be: if a married woman, then lesser; and if a nun, then greater, with discernment.[^4098] But if in the midst of people, or in the midst of men's houses, he entered and violated such a one: why then did the woman not cry out with a great voice unto the hearing of some? Therefore[^4099] *Injunctions:*

...let her perform half of the prescribed canon in penance: that is to say, [whereas] it is befitting for one who did such a deed of her own will to repent, let this woman who suffered not of her own will likewise perform half of that penance.[^4100] And such a rule is written in this book, and let the spiritual father examine it.[^4101]

If anyone defiles himself with a nun: nine years; one hundred and fifty prostrations.[^4102] But if by the consent of that nun that man did such a deed: then let him repent for five years, and that nun for nine years.[^4103]

And if that man seduced any nun, and moreover took away[^4104] *Of the Holy Fathers:*

...from her the monastic habit, and takes her [to wife] again in worldly fashion: let such a one not receive communion until death.[^4105] But if he brings that nun back again, and restores her unto the monastic life: then let him repent for nine years.[^4106]

If any secular man defiles a nun of the Great Schema: then if it be with the will of that nun, let such a nun repent for twelve years, [performing] one thousand prostrations; and that man for nine years, [performing] three hundred prostrations.[^4107]

If anyone sins with his child's godmother: let him repent for nine years, [performing] one hundred and fifty prostrations.[^4108]

If anyone [sins] with the sister of his child's godfather:[^4109]

*Injunctions:*

...four [years]; seventy prostrations.[^4110]

If anyone [sins] with his goddaughter whom he baptized: twelve years; three hundred prostrations.[^4111]

If anyone [sins] with the mother of his spiritual brother: nine years; one hundred and fifty prostrations.[^4112]

And if with his daughter: five years; one hundred prostrations.[^4113]

And if with his wife: six years; one hundred prostrations.[^4114]

And if with his sister: four years; thirty-six prostrations.[^4115]

And if with his mother-in-law, or with his sister-in-law: five years; sixty-six prostrations.[^4116]

If anyone falls [into sin] with two sisters; or two brothers with one woman: five years; one hundred and fifty prostrations.[^4117]

*Of the Holy Fathers:*

And if children of godparents unite carnally, let them not enter into marriage, nor be crowned; but if they will [if they nevertheless took each other]: let them be separated; let them repent for five years, [performing] thirty-six prostrations.[^4118]

Likewise also if the children of spiritual brothers defile themselves: let them also be treated in the same manner.[^4119]

If two spiritual brothers quarrel or strike one another: let them be separated for sixty days, [performing] twelve prostrations each day.[^4120] And if they forgive one another again and love each other: well and good; but if not, let them be separated from the church continually, since they have proved liars unto Christ and have grieved the Spirit of love.[^4121]

A spiritual brother is he who makes brotherhood upon the Holy Gospel.[^4122]

*Injunctions:*

If any persons whatsoever quarrel: and one of them, taking the initiative, seeks forgiveness with a prostration from the other: he receives a twofold reward from God beyond the other, if his repentance is with love.[^4123]

And he who does not desire to seek forgiveness from his friend makes himself an enemy to his own soul; let such a one be separated from the church, and let the priest receive no prosphora whatsoever from him.[^4124]

And if both do not desire to seek forgiveness with love from the whole heart: then let both be separated from the church.[^4125]

Likewise also those who, concerning any great or small matter, are agitated and hate one another; or if without cause they quarrel, and keeping silence hate one another: let such persons amend themselves[^4126] *Of the Holy Fathers:*

...amend themselves. But if one of them is unwilling, or both are unwilling: let them be separated from the church. For it behooves such persons to be examined before the church, in the presence of two or three witnesses; likewise also if they be brothers according to the flesh.[^4127]

A bearer of malice: let him repent for one year, [performing] twelve prostrations [each day].[^4128]

A slanderer: two years; eighteen prostrations.[^4129]

A false witness: three years; twenty-four prostrations.[^4130]

A scoffer: one year; twelve prostrations.[^4131]

An eavesdropper: one year; fifteen prostrations.[^4132]

A perjurer: three years; one hundred and fifty prostrations.[^4133] A perjurer[^4134] *Injunctions:*

...is like unto a heretic.[^4135]

He that ploughs over a field with a plough, alienating land from fields or from anything else: let him repent for four years; sixteen prostrations.[^4136]

He that robs houses: three years; one hundred prostrations.[^4137]

A liar: six months; twelve prostrations.[^4138]

He that steals cattle: five years; three hundred prostrations.[^4139]

He that steals hens or eggs: one year; thirty-six prostrations.[^4140]

He that steals fruits: six months; fifteen prostrations.[^4141]

He that seizes and takes away another's goods with injustice: five years; one hundred prostrations.[^4142]

A denouncer and a thief receive one and the same judgment.[^4143]

He that receives thieves and that which is stolen from them[^4144] *Of the Holy Fathers:*

...let him likewise repent as a thief.[^4145]

He that robs graves: five years; five hundred prostrations.[^4146]

An extortioner and a lover of money: three years; four hundred prostrations.[^4147]

He that pours water into wine and sells it: five years; sixty-six prostrations.[^4148]

Let a drunkard not receive communion until he desists from becoming intoxicated.[^4149]

A secular man, if he vomits having become intoxicated: let him be separated for sixty days.[^4150]

And if he had received the Holy Mysteries, and thereafter vomits: let him not receive communion on the Nativity of Christ, nor on the Day of Peter; and throughout those fasts let him repent. But if he did this in the Great Fast: let him not[^4151] *Injunctions:*

...receive communion throughout the whole year until two hundred days; [performing] twelve prostrations each day.[^4152]

If anyone eats anything whatsoever, and thereafter receives communion: one year.[^4153]

And if he eats cheese and eggs, and thereafter receives communion: two years.[^4154]

And if he eats meat, and thereafter receives communion: three years; sixty-six prostrations.[^4155]

If anyone receives a penance from his spiritual father not to receive communion, and receives communion without his bidding: let him be separated from the church as a scoffer of God for three years; neither let the priest receive prosphora from him.[^4156]

*Concerning Women:*

A woman who practices sorcery, or a man: let them cease and repent; but if not, let them[^4157] *Of the Holy Fathers:*

...be separated from Christianity.[^4158]

A woman, if she drinks herbs to destroy the fruit of her womb so as not to bear children: let her be separated, and let her repent for five years; three hundred prostrations.[^4159]

And if she moreover has a husband, and does this: it is far worse; neither let the church receive her oblation, nor her prosphora, unless she repents. And if her husband also took counsel with her concerning this, and both do this: let him likewise be separated.[^4160]

A woman, if she lusts after another man, and destroys her husband by sorceries: then if she was seduced by a certain man, and he took her not to wife: let her be separated for five years. But if he takes her to wife, and she takes that man[^4161] *Injunctions:*

...having accomplished an unlawful deed: let both be separated for fifteen years; and let them receive penance concerning murder, to perform the same as an intentional murderer.[^4162]

And if she betrays her husband unto murder, even as Delilah did Samson: then let her be under penance all the days of her life.[^4163]

A woman, if through some craft of the enemy she of her own will slays her infants at birth: let her be separated and repent all the days of her life.[^4164]

A fornicating woman, if she drinks herbs so as not to bear; or having given birth, suffocates her infant: let her repent for nine years; one hundred and seven prostrations.[^4165]

A woman who is a procuress, or a man: let them repent[^4166] *Of the Holy Fathers:*

...for three years.[^4167] But if it be a monk or a nun: five years.[^4168]

We command women to confess in the church narthex, and to have the outer doors open for the sake of avoiding scandal.[^4169]

We have commanded also fully professed monks and those preserving virginity that they shall not receive women unto themselves for confession; only those who have attained unto chaste and orderly old age. Let such a one be assigned unto these, lest he be scandalized in his thoughts; for through women the devil wages warfare against monks and the saints.[^4170]

And whenever any one of them desires to hear a woman's confession, let him first strengthen himself with prayers and supplications, singing the Psalms: [Psalm 50] "Have mercy on me, O God,"[^4171] *Injunctions:*

...and [Psalm 95 / 99 / 65] "Sing unto the Lord, all the earth." And after this let him receive any woman whatsoever unto confession.[^4172]

He that commits these acts of self-pollution and fornication: let him receive a penance of three years; twenty-four prostrations.[^4173]

Now self-pollution has two varieties: one with the hands, the other between one's thighs; and that with the hands is worse than that between the thighs; yet both are evil and corrupt.[^4174]

There is also female self-pollution, which women commit one upon another. Therefore it is fitting for the spiritual father to examine all these things, and to give them a penance of one year.[^4175]

Therefore on account of these things, [to avoid] every stumbling, we command devout women[^4176] *Of the Holy Fathers:*

...[to perform] one hundred prostrations.[^4177]

If any woman enters into church, and while she is there perceives her customary flow: having discovered it, let her depart at that very hour, having no sin.[^4178]

But if, having noticed it, she remains for the sake of human shame, or receives the oblation: let her be separated from the church and from communion for six months; fifty prostrations.[^4179]

Before a woman is cleansed from that which happens according to her custom, let her not bake prosphora, neither let her touch it in any manner whatsoever.[^4180]

She that has her customary flow, if she arrives at the extremity of death: let her be vouchsafed communion without hindrance.[^4181]

A woman having given birth, and having arrived at the extremity of death[^4182] *Injunctions:*

...having received a prayer, let her be vouchsafed communion.[^4183]

And if, having recovered her health, she continues again in life: let her fast for forty days, and on the fiftieth day let her receive communion, performing each day forty prostrations.[^4184]

*Injunctions Concerning Priests:*

That it behooves a bishop to instruct small and great with meekness and humility, and not with malice.[^4185]

If a priest, whether with justice or with injustice, goes unto the striking of strife: let him be deposed.[^4186]

A priest that contracts a second marriage: let him be excluded from celebrating the Liturgy, and let him receive communion without penance.[^4187]

A priest shall not celebrate the Liturgy in coarse peasant slippers [*opintsi*].[^4188]

If a priest engages in trade for usurers[^4189]\n *Of the Holy Fathers:*[fol. 668r][^4190]

Midwives serving at births: we command them to approach Holy Communion by the seventh day, since they perform a truly necessary service.[^4191] But other women who are without work and without service, coming unto this at that hour of birth: let such not be received into church until the twelfth day, and others until the fifteenth day, and others until the twentieth day, according to the work they have served; for if they do not call any woman unto this for the sake of some service, let her not go.

And if a woman gives birth on Holy Pascha: then until the seventh day let her wash herself with water, and let her drink holy water [*agiasma*].[^4192]

*Injunctions:*[fol. 668v]

If a woman runs away from her husband, despising marital cohabitation, but wishing to live thus [alone]: anathema.[^4193]

If a woman does not submit to her husband, and abides not in his will, even as the Apostle says: "The head of the husband is Christ, and the head of the woman is her husband;" and again the Apostle says: "Even as Christ is the head of the church, so the husband is the head of the wife;" and she that does not obey this shall be a partaker with Delilah and Jezebel.[^4194] But if the husband be foolish and corrupt of mind, and his counsel defective, while his wife is sensible and wise: let her not obey him always in every word, but sometimes let her obey[^4195] *Of the Holy Fathers:*[fol. 669r]

...that woman, her husband; and sometimes let the husband also obey his wife.[^4196]

If a woman cuts her hair, supposing that it is good for the sake of God, except only for the monastic life: if she presumes to do this, anathema.[^4197] For it has not been commanded by God for a woman to cut her hair, save only when she enters into the monastic life. But if through some instigation of the enemy she cuts her hair: let her be separated from the church and from communion for one year, and let her repent.[^4198]

If a woman abandons her husband, and takes another in a foreign land, and lives with him: let her be separated from the church for nine years, performing each day[^4199] *Injunctions:*[fol. 669v]

...thirty-six prostrations; eating her bread dry on Monday, Wednesday, and Friday.[^4200] Likewise also her husband, unto whom she was joined second: let him receive the same penance.[^4201] But if that husband was unaware concerning that woman what she had done, and took her in ignorance: then let [the spiritual father] give him a small rule.

If a woman by sorcery puts her husband to death, wishing to take another; likewise also a husband, if he does this: then woe unto such! For concerning such we have nothing to say; for great and terrible is the penance for such, being separated from the church even unto death.[^4202] Likewise also a woman, if [she betrays] her[^4203] *Concerning Priests:*[fol. 670r][^4204]

...let him serve, neither let him put her away; even as our Lord Jesus Christ says: "Whosoever shall put away his wife, except for the cause of fornication, and shall marry another, commits adultery;" for this He spoke concerning every man.

If a priest is tonsured [as a monk], and his wife goes after another husband: let him not be a priest.[^4205]

If anyone castrates himself: let him not be a priest, for he is a murderer of himself.[^4206] And if this happens unto a deacon: henceforth let him not advance unto higher [orders]; but even as we have spoken concerning priests, so likewise do we speak concerning deacons.

If a priest commits fornication: let him be deposed.[^4207] And if his wife wishes to leave him for the sake of her chastity, that she be not defiled with him, let it be her will; but if *Injunctions of the Holy Fathers:*[fol. 670v]

...she does not seek another husband.[^4208] But if that priest desists from fornication, then let him abide with his wife. Likewise also if it happens unto a deacon and a reader.

For we have written that the wife has not power over her own body; likewise also the wife has power over the body of her husband.[^4209] For this cause the Lord said: "And the two shall become one flesh." "What therefore God has joined together, let not man put asunder." Therefore let there be no separation between a wife and a husband, except only of great necessity, and by council and judgment.

For "Every sin is without the body; but he that commits fornication sins against his own body."[^4210]

*Of the Holy Fathers:*[fol. 671r]

And it is fitting for a wife and a husband to have two beds in their house, and to lie apart on Sundays, and on holy feasts of the Lord, and during the Great Week.[^4211] So that if at times someone is unable to abstain for God's sake, at least on these days it is fitting to abstain, and not always to wallow like a swine in the mire. For from such incontinent passions is born an evil and wicked seed; and from such passions comes fearlessness [of God], neither does the remembrance of death ever enter into the mind of a man.[^4212]

If a harlot desists from her wicked way, and now confesses, and promises henceforth not to go into that defiled path, but humbles herself[^4213] *Injunctions:*[fol. 671v]

...and enters into chastity, and now cleanses herself: then after a short repentance, the spiritual father committing this unto loving-kindness, let her receive communion with true Christians, and let her be accepted even as Christ accepted that fornicating woman.[^4214]

If any woman whatsoever is accused by some persons that she has destroyed her husband with poison, or anyone else: then let it be investigated whether it is true, and let her be delivered unto torments, and let there be confiscation of her estate; but before the truth concerning her is known, let no one harm her.[^4215]

Neither is it fitting, nor is it right, to condemn any man whatsoever, unless there rise up against him[^4216] *Of the Holy Fathers:*[fol. 672r]

...many witnesses, and testify the truth clearly concerning that man's offense; then let him be judged according to the church canon.[^4217] But let no one dare of his own will to judge anyone, or to condemn, or to rob, or to plunder; for he that rejoices in such a deed, let him be anathema.

Whosoever, whether slave or free, is found desiring by involuntary violence or by flattery and by some counsel of the enemy to turn another away from Christianity into some heresy: let such a one be condemned unto death, as an enemy of God and of Christians.[^4218]

If anyone steals someone's man [servant] or someone's child, and[^4219] *Injunctions:*[fol. 672v]

...sells him: let his hands be cut off.[^4220]

If anyone finds his wife committing adultery with another man, and slays her unto death: then let him be banished into exile as an unmerciful enemy; and let the Great Church take half of his estate.[^4221]

If a woman through her neglect harms her child, that is to say, if it falls into some evil disease: let her repent for one year; fifty prostrations each day.[^4222]

If through the neglect of a woman her child falls from some height and dies: one year; one hundred and fifty prostrations.[^4223]

If a woman beats her child rashly, and it dies: six years; one hundred and fifty prostrations.[^4224]

*Of the Holy Fathers:*[fol. 673r][^4225]

If a woman giving birth smothers her child: let her repent until death, eating dry food on Monday, Wednesday, and Friday; a thousand prostrations.[^4226]

If any woman drinks a potion that she may not conceive a child: seven years; two hundred prostrations.[^4227]

If a woman, having conceived, drinks any potion for corruption, so that she may cast out that which is conceived in her: eight years; three hundred and sixty-seven prostrations. But if it happens that she dies, let her not be buried.[^4228]

A woman who casts spells upon strangers and her own [family]: nine years; five hundred prostrations.[^4229]

A woman who is a poisoner: let her repent until the end of her life; ten thousand prostrations.[^4230]

*Injunctions:*[fol. 673v][^4231]

If a sorceress repents: nine years; five hundred prostrations.

A *mora* [nightmare-weaver]: five years; three hundred prostrations.[^4232]

A *mavlistra* [enchantress]: seven years; four hundred prostrations.[^4233]

If a woman speaks an evil word unto a priest: let her be cast out from the church for three years.[^4234]

If a woman takes up wood against a priest or a levite, and strikes him: let her repent for six years; three hundred prostrations.[^4235]

If a woman commands a priest concerning his Liturgy, or concerning the hours appointed for him, even if he is very young and that woman is wise; but if by authority she commands the priest: either let her cease, or let her be excommunicated; and if she repents, then let her repent for six months; a thousand prostrations.[^4236]

*Of the Holy Fathers:*[fol. 674r][^4237]

Likewise also a man, both a ruler and one who is in authority: in the same manner let him be forbidden.

Forasmuch, therefore, as from the beginning God created man and woman, that He might raise up the world and His own possession; He gives unto us also to behold a certain custom: so that from that which is seen each month by them, making manifest conception unto that which comes to be; lest, as some say, that a woman experiences childbirth from the man, but from the woman there is nothing. It is made manifest by the things that come to be, that blood is taken from the woman, which is called consanguinity; and flesh from the man, whereby we are called carnal.[^4238]

In the Old Law it was said: for twelve days men are to preserve themselves from[^4239] *Injunctions:*[fol. 674v]

...women, that they might be cleansed and not be defiled. But we, having examined more accurately, command them to wait until the sixth or until the eighth day for the sake of complete cleansing; not making it out to be defilement—far be it!—forasmuch as every creature of God is good, and nothing is to be rejected;[^4240] but for the sake of greater cleansing unto us, for the sake of the assembly of the holy church, and the Liturgy, and Communion.[^4241]

And we command women who have their customary course to stand outside the church for eight days: outside the church porch three days, and inside five; so that the divine [service] be not hindered.[^4242] And whosoever, being in such a state, desire to enter into the church: let them be separated for three years from receiving communion[^4243] *Of the Holy Fathers:*[fol. 675r]

...[and only those women] who have one lawful husband: let such perform every church requirement, and [make] the prosphora, and the offerings. But let not all women be trusted who are not in honor and confession, even if they be virgins; and whosoever transgresses this command, let him be anathema.[^4244]

If a woman gives birth during the Great Fast: let her fast forty days, and let her receive communion.[^4245]

If a woman lies with two brothers, or a man with two sisters: let such a person be excommunicated even until death in repentance; and at death let him receive communion for the sake of [divine] love of mankind. But if he completely abandons both women, that is to say, both sisters, so as not[^4246] *Injunctions:*[fol. 675v]

...to have either of them; or again, if a woman departs from both brothers, so as to have neither of them as husband: and thus shall their repentance be accepted if they repent; but if not, vain is their repentance.[^4247]

When a woman gives birth, let her fulfill forty days, and afterwards let her receive communion. But if she be near death, soon, or before the eighth day, or on the first day of her childbirth, even then let her receive communion; and let the newborn child receive communion, even if death come upon him before the twelfth day, or after many days. But let the woman first be cleansed after her giving birth, and thus let her receive communion; likewise also the child.[^4248]

*Concerning Priests:*[fol. 676r][^4249]

He that greatly multiplies his silver: let him be barred from the Liturgy; forasmuch as he is mixed with falsehood and extortion; and better is he that trades and fornicates. But if he desists from such, let him again minister as priest; and if not, then let him be deposed from the priesthood.

A priest, or deacon, or hegumen who collects tolls: either let him cease from such, or let him be deposed.[^4250]

A priest who sings like a goat and plays: either let him cease from such things, or let him be deposed.[^4251]

If a priest falls into fornication, or masturbation, or with a beast: let such a one be barred from the Liturgy.[^4252] And if anyone be found in these [sins] while not yet[^4253] *Injunctions:*[fol. 676v][^4254]

...being a priest: let such a one not come unto the priesthood.

A priest who lies, or tells fables, or slanders: either let him desist from such things, or let him be deposed.[^4255]

A priest who seeks to perform any worldly services whatsoever, whether civic or princely, and to walk in them, and to attend the assembly of common people or of princes, except only if some necessity be upon him: let such a one either desist from such things, or let him be deposed.[^4256]

If a priest in his priesthood either becomes blind, or becomes lame, or a demonic disease comes upon him: let him desist from the Divine Liturgy, but let him perform the other prayers.[^4257]

*Concerning Priests:*[fol. 677r][^4258]

Likewise also if anyone has any of these blemishes: either blind, scarcely seeing; or lame; or having a withered hand; or leprous; or deaf; or the son of a thrice-married man; or the offspring of incest: of all such, let none dare to approach unto the priesthood. And if a bishop for the sake of reward ordains such a priest, let both be deposed, both that bishop and the priest.

A priest celebrating the sacred mysteries: let him guard himself from conversations with women, that he may preserve the treasure of the soul unstolen; and let him not boast in his virginity, lest he lose that which he has.[^4259]

If the wife of a priest commits adultery, and he knows it not: then let that priest serve.[^4260]

*Injunctions:*[fol. 677v][^4261]

But if someone tells him concerning her: let him cease serving, and let him investigate whether it is true concerning her. And if he sees with his own eyes, then let him put her away; and let him abide in patient endurance, serving again.

But if, having put her away, he falls again with another woman: let him desist from the Liturgy, and let him receive communion unhindered.[^4262]

But if he retains that [first adulterous] woman, he has the same prohibition; and at his death let him be ministered unto as other priests in sacred dignity.[^4263]

But if it happens that his wife dies before that, and if he touches not another, then let him minister as a priest without prohibition.[^4264]

But if she be alive, and cannot be caught openly with that man[^4265] *Of the Holy Fathers:*[fol. 678r][^4266]

...[or if a wife] slays her husband in order to marry another.

If a woman slays her own children by sinful fault, so as to love another man with a devilish love, being seduced by excessive fornication—which we have found to happen frequently among some—the holy Council commands concerning such a woman: that she shall not enter into the church even unto death,[^4267] but let her stand in the place of the catechumens,[^4268] being cast out from every Christian rank.[^4269] And when people enter and depart, let her fall prostrate upon the earth, and let her call out with a loud voice: "Forgive me, a sinner who has committed sins!" And then let her openly declare her sins in the hearing of all, so that *Injunctions:*[fol. 678v][^4270]

...those entering and departing into the holy church may pray for her, that perchance by their prayers she may receive forgiveness from God. And let her fast every day on dry food,[^4271] making prostrations day and night; and on Saturday and on Sunday let her [spiritual] father release her [from dry fasting].[^4272]

If a woman wishes to abstain from her husband upon the bed, or a husband from his wife: it is fitting that both take counsel together, and establish an agreement concerning this; lest one of them wish to abstain, while the other cannot, or will not, and begins to commit fornication, consorting with others; and the greater sin is upon both of them.[^4273]

It is also fitting for every Christian... [breaks off; continues with independent title on leaf p1373][^4274]

# PART LV: CONCERNING THOSE WHO ABDUCT WOMEN FOR MARRIAGE [^4275]

*The eleventh canon of the Council of Ancyra:* Maidens who have been betrothed to someone, and then abducted by others: even if they have unlawfully forced them, it commands that they be restored again to those who betrothed them; for if they openly choose to take them, they are not to be rejected on account of that which was done without their will.[^4276]

*The twenty-seventh of the Fourth Council, and the ninety-second of the Sixth Council command thus:* Those who abduct women under pretext of cohabitation, or who assist them, or who consent and help: if they be clerics, let them be deposed; but if laymen[^4277] *Concerning Abductors:*[fol. 679v][^4278]

...let them be delivered over to anathema: for upon the same charges they condemn also those who consent to help and assist them; and all the more fittingly. For he who desires abduction, even if he offers an exceedingly rotten defense, driving toward an unseemly deed, having been constrained in his mind—that is to say, overcome [by passion]; but to an accomplice, who among those possessing understanding will grant pardon? [To him] nothing else [can be attributed] except that he has his own malice defiling him alongside that loathsome deed, which leads unto other improprieties and throws the orderly governance of civil society into disorder.[^4279] And an accomplice is he who actively carries out the abduction; while an abettor is he who devises plots and provides counsel.[^4280]

*Imperial Laws Concerning Those Taking for Marriage:*[fol. 680r][^4281]

If anyone abducts a woman, whether betrothed or unbetrothed, or a widow, whether noble, or a slave, or a freedwoman; and especially if she is consecrated [a nun]; and even if anyone abducts his own betrothed maiden:[^4282]

If, then, he commits the abduction with weapons, either with swords or with clubs: such a one shall be punished by the sword.[^4283] And those who assisted them, or were privy to it, or willingly escorted [her], or contributed any effort whatsoever: being severely beaten and shorn, let their noses be cut off; since those seeking to abduct are ready also to murder those who resist them.[^4284] But if he committed the abduction without any weapons whatsoever *Concerning Abductors:*[fol. 680v][^4285]

...committed [the abduction without any weapons]: let the hand of the abductor be cut off. And those who cooperated in any manner whatsoever, being beaten and shorn, let them be banished; whether the woman was willing or the abduction was done unwillingly; and especially if they attempted to abduct any women who were living with husbands. Moreover, if the parents of the woman attempt to accept [the match], they are worthy to be shut up in prison; and if a slave is caught having assisted in the deed, let him be burned [at the stake].[^4286]

*Statute:* He who abducts a virgin or a widow cannot have her as a wife, even if her father consents to it and forgives the offense.[^4287]

*Statute:* Let not the abducted woman be married to him who abducted her; but even if her parents consent to such[^4288] *Concerning Marriage of a Woman:*[fol. 681r][^4289]

...cohabitation, her parents shall be cast into prison.

*Statute:* In one way is he punished who has abducted a maiden, and in another way he who has deflowered a virgin by force. For abduction, being shamelessness on the part of the abductor, has no pardon; whereas corruption committed by force, if pardon be accepted from the violated maiden, receives forgiveness, and they are permitted to live together.[^4290]

*Statute:* An abducted woman obtains the property of him who abducted her, if she does not wish to be lawfully joined with him. For if she does not wish to do this, both her property and that of the abductor are confiscated, as well as [the property of] those who consented unto the wickedness, whether they be their parents or strangers.[^4291]

*Statute:* Abduction is greater than adultery; and he who abducts a married woman[^4292] *Concerning Those Abducting for Marriage:*[fol. 681v][^4293]

...or a virgin, is punished to the uttermost, and a third party may accuse him, even if he has been forgiven by the maiden. If a slave discloses the abduction of a virgin, he shall be granted freedom, or if he exposes an abduction that had already been forgiven.[^4294]

*Statute:* A slave who abducts or conceals another's [female slave who is a] harlot is guilty neither as a thief nor as guilty of corruption; for he did this not for the sake of theft, but for the sake of pleasure. Nevertheless, he is fined in his property by the prince, and is brought to chastity.[^4295]

Moreover, the seventeenth Novel of Justinian forbids granting boundaries of immunity [sanctuary] from arrest unto abductors of maidens; but even during the days of Holy Pascha, abductors of maidens are apprehended and bound.[^4296]

# PART LVI: COLOPHON & IMPRINT OF THE STRIATYN TREBNYK [^4297]

By the good pleasure and goodness of God, glorified in Trinity as of one power: this book called the *Trebnik* [Euchologion] began to be printed by the personal expense and outlay of the noble Pan Teodor Yuriiovych Balaban;[^4298] and it was completed after his repose. And it was researched and corrected by the diligence of the greatly-sinful Teodor K.[^4299]

I beseech all who read or transcribe this book: correcting any errors that have occurred in a spirit of meekness, bless and curse not; so that you yourselves may be counted worthy of mercy from God and forgiveness from men.[^4300]

It began to be printed in the year from the creation of the world 7113, and from the saving Incarnation of the Son of God 1605, in the month of[^4301] *Imprint & Location:*[fol. 682v][^4302]

...July 22. And it was completed in the year 7114, and from the Inhumanation of Christ 1606, on the 14th of the month of September.

AT STRIATYN.[^4303]

[Rear (lower) exterior binding cover of the monument: authentic contemporary early seventeenth-century binding (circa 1606) from the Balaban printing house in Striatyn. Dark brown calfskin over bevelled wooden boards with elaborate blind tooling. On the left fore-edge are preserved two wide leather clasp straps secured to the wooden board with four dark iron rivets, displaying surface craquelure from age. On the right edge is the spine joint showing the ridges of five raised cords and traces of leather reinforcement at the head of the spine. The blind-tooled decorative scheme comprises a wide outer ornamental border of roll-stamped foliate vines, leaves, and palmettes enclosed by double concentric linear fillet rules, and an inner rectangular field. The central panel is partitioned by a diagonal saltire cross of double linear fillets into four triangular compartments, each containing an embossed circular medallion bearing the zoomorphic symbols of the Four Evangelists (the Tetramorph): eagle, lion, ox, and angel. In the upper and lower horizontal compartments of the inner field are placed additional circular medallions with profile busts and stylized foliate palmettes. The leather surface displays authentic abrasions, rubbing, craquelure, and patina from centuries of liturgical use, exposing the wooden board at the corner edges.][^4364]

# FOOTNOTES AND SCHOLARLY COMMENTARY



[^1]: Hedeon Balaban (c. 1530–1607), Orthodox Bishop of Lviv, Halych, and Kamianets-Podilskyi from 1569 until his death, prominent defender of Orthodoxy who opposed the Union of Brest.

[^2]: The title of Exarch of the Ecumenical Throne was conferred upon Bishop Hedeon Balaban by Patriarch Jeremiah II Tranos of Constantinople during his patriarchal visitation of the Ruthenian lands in 1589.

[^3]: Refers to the preface of the Striatyn *Sluzhebnik* (Liturgicon) printed in 1604, in which Bishop Hedeon first detailed the background and patriarchal mandate for this liturgical translation and printing undertaking.

[^4]: Blessed Meletios Pegas (1549–1601), Pope and Patriarch of Alexandria (1590–1601), who also served as locum tenens and administrator of the Ecumenical Patriarchate of Constantinople from 1597 to 1598.

[^5]: Refers to the Orthodox conciliar synods held in Brest-Litovsk between 1590 and 1594, which addressed ecclesiastical order and liturgical discrepancy prior to the formal Union of Brest in 1595–1596.

[^6]: Mikhail Rahoza, Metropolitan of Kyiv, Halych, and all Rus' (1589–1599), who signed the Union of Brest in 1595–1596, submitting the Ruthenian Church to the Roman See.

[^7]: Greek: Εὐχολόγιον (*Euchologion*), the comprehensive Byzantine book of rites and sacraments, corresponding in the Slavonic tradition to the *Sluzhebnik* (hieratikon/liturgicon) and *Trebnyk* (ritual/book of needs).

[^8]: That is, remaining in canonical obedience to the Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople as the lawful ecclesiastical head of the Kyivan Metropolia, refusing to follow Metropolitan Rahoza into union with Rome.

[^9]: Refers to the South Slavic (Serbian) and Danubian (Wallachian and Moldavian) Church Slavonic printed and manuscript euchologia collated by Bishop Hedeon to identify copyist variants and recensional corruptions.

[^10]: Patriarch Meletios Pegas administered the vacant Ecumenical Patriarchate of Constantinople from autumn 1597 until spring 1598, actively supporting the Orthodox opposition to the Union of Brest.

[^11]: Mount Athos (the Holy Mountain), whose monastic libraries preserved ancient Byzantine Greek euchologia that served as the primary critical witness for the corrected Greek text sent by Meletios Pegas.

[^12]: Early Modern Ruthenian/Slavonic *роду россійскому* denotes the Orthodox East Slavic people (Ruthenians: Ukrainians and Belarusians) of the Kyivan Metropolia within the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth.

[^13]: Teodor Yurievych Balaban (nephew of Bishop Hedeon, son of his brother Yurii) and the ancestral Balaban estate of Striatyn (now in Rohatyn Raion, Ivano-Frankivsk Oblast), where Bishop Hedeon and Teodor established their private scholarly printing shop (active 1604–1606).

[^14]: The celebrated Striatyn *Sluzhebnik* published in 1604, representing the first fruit of the Balaban-Pegas liturgical reform.
