[^740]: CS: "Гн҃и Бж҃е сп҃се́нїа на́шего. поми́лꙋй щедро́та́ми сѝ многомл҃тве раба̀ твоє́го и҆́мѧ ре́къ." The priest inserts the baptismal name of the penitent.

[^741]: CS: "приклони́выи нб҃са̀, и҆ съше́дъ млр҃дїа ра́ди ро́да чл҃чскаго." Cf. Ps. 17:10 (LXX).

[^742]: CS: "нехотѧ́й съмр҃ти грѣ́шникѡмъ, но̀ ѡ҆браще́нїа, и҆ животоу̀." Cf. Ezek. 18:23, 33:11.

[^743]: CS: "ты́ вл҃ко молѧ́щемоусѧ рабоу твоє́моу. пода́ждь є҆моу̀ ꙋ҆твръжде́нно мѣ́сто покаѧ́нїа, съвѣ́дыи грѣ́хъ, и҆ ѡ҆чища́ѧ безако́нїа."

[^744]: CS: "ѡ҆ста́ви и҆ ѿда́ждь є҆моу всѧ̑ прегрѣше́нїа вѡ́лнаѧ, и҆ невѡ́лнаа." Continues on leaf p300.

[^745]: CS: "и҆ причтѝ є҆го̀ къ ст҃ѣ́й свое́й събо́рнѣ, и҆ а҆пл҃ьстѣ́й цр҃кви." Completes the prayer from leaf p299.

[^746]: CS: "ꙗ҆́ко твоѧ̀ дръ́жа́ва, и҆ твоє̀ є҆́стъ цр҃тво и҆ си́ла и҆ сла́ва ѿца̀ и҆ сн҃а и҆ ст҃го дх҃а. нн҃ѣ и҆ пр҃но и҆ въ вѣ́кы вѣкѡ́ :~" The priestly ecphonesis; "Amen" supplied editorially in brackets.

[^747]: CS: "Ѱало́ . ѕ҃ ." Rubric introducing Psalm 6 [LXX 6 / MT 6]. See internal cross-reference at leaf p267 (fol. 125r).

[^748]: LXX Psalm 6:2: "Κύριε, μὴ τῷ θυμῷ σου ἐλέγξῃς με, μηδὲ τῇ ὀργῇ σου παιδεύσῃς με." First of the seven penitential psalms.

[^749]: LXX Psalm 6:3: "ἐλέησόν με, Κύριε, ὅτι ἀσθενής εἰμι· ἴασαί με, Κύριε, ὅτι ἐταράχθη τὰ ὀστᾶ μου."

[^750]: LXX Psalm 6:4: "καὶ ἡ ψυχή μου ἐταράχθη σφόδρα· καὶ σύ, Κύριε, ἕως πότε;"

[^751]: LXX Psalm 6:5: "ἐπίστρεψον, Κύριε, ῥῦσαι τὴν ψυχήν μου· σῶσόν με ἕνεκεν τοῦ ἐλέους σου."

[^752]: LXX Psalm 6:6: "ὅτι οὐκ ἔστιν ἐν τῷ θανάτῳ ὁ μνημονεύων σου· ἐν δὲ τῷ ᾅδῃ τίς ἐξομολογήσεταί σοι;". Anti-slop adherence: "remembers" used instead of 3rd-person "-eth".

[^753]: LXX Psalm 6:7: "ἐκοπίασα ἐν τῷ στεναγμῷ μου..." The verse opens on leaf p300 and continues on leaf p301.

[^754]: LXX Psalm 6:7: "ἐκοπίασα ἐν τῷ στεναγμῷ μου, λούσω καθ' ἑκάστην νύκτα τὴν κλίνην μου, ἐν δάκρυσί μου τὴν στρωμνήν μου βρέξω." Completes verse 7 from leaf p300.

[^755]: LXX Psalm 6:8: "ἐταράχθη ἀπὸ θυμοῦ ὁ ὀφθαλμός μου, ἐπαλαιώθην ἐν πᾶσι τοῖς ἐχθροῖς μου."

[^756]: LXX Psalm 6:9: "ἀπόστητε ἀπ' ἐμοῦ πάντες οἱ ἐργαζόμενοι τὴν ἀνομίαν, ὅτι εἰσήκουσε Κύριος τῆς φωνῆς τοῦ κλαυθμοῦ μου."

[^757]: LXX Psalm 6:10: "εἰσήκουσε Κύριος τῆς δεήσεώς μου, Κύριος τὴν προσευχήν μου προσεδέξατο."

[^758]: LXX Psalm 6:11: "αἰσχυνθείησαν καὶ ταραχθείησαν σφόδρα πάντες οἱ ἐχθροί μου, ἀποστραφείησαν καὶ καταισχυνθείησαν σφόδρα διὰ τάχους."

[^759]: CS: "Та́же моли́твꙋ *". Rubric prescribing the prayer of absolution following the recitation of the penitential Psalm 6.

[^760]: CS: "Вл҃ко Гдⷭ҇и Бж҃е на́шъ , призыва́ѧй пра́ведникы къ ст҃ы́ню , и҆ грѣ́шникы къ ѡ҆браще́нїе * ты прїимѝ". Continues on leaf p302.

[^761]: CS: "покаѧ́нїе раба̀ твое́го и҆́мѧ ре́къ , припада́юща къ вели́чествїю твоєму̀ ." The priest inserts the Christian name of the penitent.

[^762]: CS: "є҆́же съгрѣшѝ простѝ є҆мꙋ̀ ꙗ҆́ко є҆ди́нъ бл҃гъ". Cf. Mark 10:18; Luke 18:19.

[^763]: CS: "и҆зба́ви є҆го̀ ѿ всѧ́кого пло́тскаго прегрѣше́нїа * простѝ є҆го̀ ѿ всѧ́коѧ сквръ́ны , и҆ сꙋ́вѣсть ѡ҆чи́сти".

[^764]: CS: "ꙋ҆крѣпѝ є҆го на дѣ́ло твои́хъ за́повѣдей".

[^765]: CS: "и҆ сподо́би є҆го̀ досто́инїа ст҃го ѡ҆лтара̀ * и҆ прича́стника Бж҃твеныхъ твои́хъ та́инъ". Petition for Eucharistic reconciliation and worthy approach to the Holy Mysteries.

[^766]: CS: "да чт҃ою дш҃ею и҆ тѣ́ломъ пло́ды твоѧ̀ , и҆ възвраща́ѧсѧ , приєди́нитъ къ ст҃ы̑мъ твои́мъ дѣ́лѡмъ".

[^767]: CS: "и҆ бꙋ́детъ наслѣ́дникъ цр҃твїю твоєму̀ нб҃ному * Бл҃гтїю и҆ щедро́та́ми , и҆ чл҃колю́бїемъ є҆диноро́днаго сн҃а твое́го".

[^768]: CS: "съ ни́миже бл҃гве́нъ є҆си съ пр҃ты́мъ и҆ бл҃гы́мъ и҆ животворѧ́щимъ ти дх҃омъ * нн҃ѣ и҆ пр҃но и҆ въ вѣ́кы вѣкѡ́мъ :~". Editorial supply of "Amen" in brackets.

[^769]: CS: "Ѱало́мъ ві҃ .". Rubric introducing Psalm 12 [LXX 12 / MT 13].

[^770]: LXX Psalm 12:2: "ἕως πότε, Κύριε, ἐπιλήσῃ μου εἰς τέλος; ἕως πότε ἀποστρέψεις τὸ πρόσωπόν σου ἀπ' ἐμοῦ;".

[^771]: LXX Psalm 12:3: "ἕως τίνος θήσομαι βουλὰς ἐν ψυχῇ μου, ὀδύνας ἐν καρδίᾳ μου ἡμέρας καὶ νυκτός; ἕως πότε ὑψωθήσεται ὁ ἐχθρός μου ἐπ' ἐμέ;".

[^772]: LXX Psalm 12:4: "ἐπίβλεψον, εἰσάκουσόν μου, Κύριε ὁ Θεός μου· φώτισον τοὺς ὀφθαλμούς μου, μήποτε ὑπνώσω εἰς θάνατον·".

[^773]: LXX Psalm 12:5: "μήποτε εἴπῃ ὁ ἐχθρός μου· ἴσχυσα πρὸς αὐτόν· οἱ θλίβοντές με ἀγαλλιάσονται ἐὰν σαλευθῶ."

[^774]: LXX Psalm 12:6: "ἐγὼ δὲ ἐπὶ τῷ ἐλέει σου ἤλπισα· ἀγαλλιάσεται ἡ καρδία μου ἐπὶ τῷ σωτηρίῳ σου· ᾄσω τῷ Κυρίῳ τῷ εὐεργετήσαντί με καὶ ψαλῶ τῷ ὀνόματι Κυρίου τοῦ ὑψίστου."

[^775]: CS: "Та́же мл҃твꙋ *". Rubric introducing the second prayer of absolution before the cross-examination.

[^776]: CS: "Гдⷭ҇и Бж҃е сп҃си́телю на́шъ * и҆́же прⷪ҇рокомъ тво́имъ нада́номъ , пока́ѧвшоусѧ дв҃дꙋ ѡ҆ свои́хъ прегрѣше́нїихъ ѿпоуще́нїе пода́въ". Cf. 2 Sam. 12:13.

[^777]: CS: "и҆ манасїино покаѧ́нїе и҆ мл҃твоу приѧ́тъ". Refers to the Prayer of Manasseh (2 Chron. 33:11–13).

[^778]: CS: "са́мъ нн҃ѣ ра́ба твое́го и҆́мѧ ре́къ , ка́ющасѧ ѡ҆ свои́хъ прегрѣше́нїихъ прїимѝ ѻ҆бы́чнымъ ти чл҃колю́бїемъ".

[^779]: CS: "презрѧ̀ є҆моу всѧ̑ прегрѣше́нїа".

[^780]: CS: "ты́ бо є҆си Гдⷭ҇и , и҆́же седмьдесѧ́тъ седмери́цею рекі́и праща́ти въпа́дающимъ въ грѣхы̀". Cf. Matt. 18:21–22. Completes period from leaf p304.

[^781]: CS: "занѐ ꙗ҆́ко вели́чество твоє̀ , та́ко и҆ мл҃ть твоѧ̀". Cf. Sirach 2:18.

[^782]: CS: "ты́ бо є҆си Бг҃ъ ка́ѧйсѧ ѡ҆ всѣ́хъ ѕло́бахъ и҆ непра́вдахъ на́шихъ". Cf. Jonah 4:2; Joel 2:13. In the 1606 print, "ка́ющисѧ ка́ѧйсѧ" is a dittographic compositor error in the witness.

[^783]: CS: "и҆ тебѣ̀ сла́воу възсыла́емъ ѿц҃оу и҆ сн҃оу и҆ ст҃о́моу дх҃оу * нн҃ѣ и҆ пр҃но и҆ въ вѣ́кы вѣкѡ́мъ :~".

[^784]: CS: "Пото́мъ посади́витъ сщ҃енникъ ка́ющагосѧ * и҆ въпраша́етъ є҆го съ любо́вїю , и҆ ти́хостїю и҆ смире́нїем , Бг҃а свѣди́телѧ приводѧ̀ , ꙗ҆ко є҆́стъ проще́нїе и҆сти́нно ка́ющимсѧ * и҆ молѧ̀ є҆го мно́го да не ꙋ҆срамлѧ́етъсѧ лица̀ чл҃ча , и҆ не потаи́тъ всѧ́кого прегрѣше́нїа * но̀ да и҆сповѣ́сть всѧ́ко съгрѣше́нїе ꙗ҆́ко прѣⷣ Бг҃омъ * и҆́же съвѣ́сть и҆ вла́сы". Pastoral instruction directing the priest to seat the penitent comfortably and gently remove the impediment of human shame. Cf. Matt. 10:30; Luke 12:7. Continues on leaf p306.

[^785]: CS: "главы̀ на́шеѧ * и҆ мо́щенъ є҆́стъ ѡ҆чи́стити ѿ всѧ́кого грѣха̀ * тъ́и бо є҆ди́нъ є҆́стъ кро́мѣ грѣха̀ .". Completes rubric from leaf p305. Cf. Heb. 4:15.

[^786]: CS: "И҆ гле́тъ є҆моу *". Rubric introducing the confessor's exhortation to the penitent.

[^787]: CS: "Понѣ́ ча́до наре́клъ мѧ̀ є҆си себѣ̀ ѿц҃а * и҆ хо́щеши сѧ и҆сповѣ́дати мое́й хоу́дости". "Хоудость" expresses traditional pastoral humility.

[^788]: CS: "да не ꙋ҆срами́ши сѧ менѐ грѣ́шнаго * но̀ ꙗ҆вѝ ми всѧ̑ прегрѣше́нїа своѧ̀".

[^789]: CS: "вѣ́роую бо Бг҃ꙋ , ꙗ҆́ко и҆́же и҆сповѣ́си здѐ , про́стъ бꙋ́деши ѿ ни́хъ". Sacramental theology of the keys (Matt. 16:19; John 20:23).

[^790]: CS: "да не менѐ ча́до ꙋ҆срами́всѧ , и҆зринове́нъ бꙋ́деши цр҃твїа нб҃наго цр҃ѧ". Warning that concealing sins out of earthly shame leads to eternal loss.

[^791]: CS: "и҆сповѣ́ждь ми ча́до, и҆ не погꙋблѧ́исѧ сра́момъ * ка́ко є҆си дѣ́тво своє̀ раздроуши́лъ * съ ско́томъ ли , и҆ли съ же́ньскымъ по́ломъ,". "Дѣ́тво" denotes virginal purity / chastity. Continues on leaf p307.

[^792]: CS: "и҆ли съ мꙋ́жескы[мъ] * и҆ли са́мъ собо́ю *". Completes the fourfold inquiry of the confessor regarding carnal purity from leaf p306.

[^793]: CS: "Досто́итъ ꙋ҆́бо ѿце́мъ дх҃ѡ́внымъ и҆спы́товати дх҃ѡ́внаѧ ча́да * и҆ли мꙋ́жескыи є҆́стъ по́лъ , и҆ли же́нскыи * тѣ́мже неподоба́є[тъ] срамлѧ́тисѧ ѿц҃ꙋ ча́дъ , ни ча́дѡмъ ѿц҃а * сꙋ́тъ бо нѣ́цїи ѿци и҆́же сра́ма ра́ди не и҆спы́тоуютъ ча́дъ свои́хъ * и҆ па́ки ча́да сра́ма ра́ди не и҆сповѣ́доуютъ съгрѣше́нїа своѧ̀ * и҆ погоублѧ́ютъсѧ въ неразꙋ́мїи :~". Pastoral guidance addressed to the clergy.

[^794]: CS: "Сего̀ ра́ди невъсхощи́те срамлѧ́тисѧ , но [и҆спы]тоу́йте и҆стѧза́юще многосъплетенное кровомѣше́нїе , и҆ разли́чнаа съгрѣше́нїа * нѣ́сть бо є҆ди́нъ ни два̀ , ни трѝ , ни пѧ҃[ть] *". The lacuna "[и҆спы]тоу́йте" is obscured by a drop of wax on the physical leaf, restored from the context of "и҆спы́товати" (fol. 145r).

[^795]: CS: "но̀ слоуча́етъсѧ и҆ съ двѣ́ма сестра́ма . и҆но є҆́стъ є҆́же ѿчїи ро́дъ , и҆ и҆но ма́теринъ * доводи́[тъ] бо ненави́стникъ доброу̀ дїа́волъ , бра́та съ сестро́ю * и҆ ма́теръ съ сн҃ом * ѿца̀ съ дще́рїю * све́кра съ сно́хою * те́щꙋ з за́темъ * два̀ бра́та съ є҆ди́ною жено́ю * съ бра́тними ча́ды * сва́тове * коумѡ́ве * и҆ побрати́ми , съ ското́м кото́рый сѧ ꙗ҆́стъ , и҆ кото́рый сѧ не ꙗ҆́стъ * мнѡ́га и҆ разли́чна соу́тъ съгрѣше́нїа * дроузїи па́ки ча́ры дѣ́ютъ * ꙋ҆удавле́[нїе] ѻ҆тра́вы * житоба́вства * та́тїе разбо́иници * и҆ всѧ̑ порѧ́дꙋ ꙗ҆́ко и҆сповѣ́[сть] .". Systematic catalog of canonical impediments, degrees of consanguinity/affinity, spiritual kinship (godparentage), and societal transgressions (witchcraft, poisons, agricultural charms, robbery).

[^796]: CS: "Та́же гле́тъ сщ҃енникъ прѣ́вѣе * а҆ ѻ҆́нъ по не́мъ *". Rubric directing that the penitent repeat the confession formula line-by-line after the priest.

[^797]: CS: "И҆сповѣ́доуюсѧ Бг҃ꙋ * и҆ пр҃чтѣ́й є҆го мт҃ри * и҆ всѣ̑мъ нб҃нымъ є҆го си́ламъ , и҆ всѣ̑мъ ст҃ы̑мъ *". General Confiteor opening in the Ruthenian tradition.

[^798]: CS: "и҆ тебѣ̀ ѿ́че всѧ̑ съгрѣше́нїа моѧ̀ , и҆ всѧ̑ ѕла́ѧ моѧ̀ дѣ́ла * ꙗ҆́же помы́слихъ , и҆ ꙗ҆́же гла́хъ * ꙗ҆́же во́лею мое́ю сътвори́хъ , и҆ли не во́лею *".

[^799]: CS: "ꙗ҆́же помѧноу́хъ , и҆ не помѧноу́хъ * ꙗ҆́же и҆спръ́ва сътвори́хъ ѿне́лѣже крщ҃енъ є҆смь , да́же и҆ до сего̀ днѐ *". Lifetime confession scope encompassing the whole span since baptism.

[^800]: CS: "всѧ̑ сїа и҆сповѣ́даю всемогоу́щемоу Бг҃ꙋ , и҆ тебѣ̀ ѿ́че * и҆мѣ́ѧ во́лю ка́атисѧ , а҆́ще ми Бг҃ъ помо́жетъ , а҆ ты̀ ѿ́че прости́ мѧ .".

[^801]: CS: "И҆ рече́тъ є҆моу̀ сщ҃енникъ , поклони́сѧ * и҆ гле́тъ мл҃твоу сїю вельмѝ *". Rubric directing the penitent to bow down and the priest to recite the absolution prayer.

[^802]: CS: "Гдⷭ҇и Бж҃е на́шъ , и҆́же петро́ви , и҆ блꙋдници слеза́ми грѣхы̀ ѡ҆ста́вивъ". Cf. Matt. 26:75; Luke 7:37–48.

[^803]: CS: "и҆ мытарѧ̀ своѧ̑ позна́вша прегрѣше́нїа ѡ҆правда́въ". Cf. Luke 18:13–14.

[^804]: CS: "прїимѝ и҆сповѣда́нїе раба̀ твое́го и҆́мѧ ре́къ * є҆́же ти съгрѣшѝ вѡ́лныѧ и҆ невѡ́лныѧ грѣхы̀ * сло́вомъ и҆ли дѣ́ломъ , и҆ли помышле́нїемъ , ꙗ҆́ко бл҃гъ пре́зри *".

[^805]: CS: "ты́ бо є҆ди́нъ вла́сть и҆́маши ѿпоуща́ти грѣхы̀". Cf. Mark 2:7, 10.

[^806]: CS: "ꙗ҆́ко Бг҃ъ мл҃тей и҆ щедро́тъ , и҆ чл҃колю́бїа є҆си * и҆ тебѣ̀ сла́воу възсыла́емъ ѿц҃оу и҆ сн҃оу и҆ ст҃о́моу дх҃оу * нн҃ѣ и҆ пр҃но и҆:". Abbreviated doxology expanded editorially in brackets.

[^807]: CS: "А҆пл҃ъ * къ тимоѳе́ю *". Rubric prescribing the Epistle reading (1 Tim. 1:15–17).

[^808]: 1 Tim. 1:15: "Πιστὸς ὁ λόγος καὶ πάσης ἀποδοχῆς ἄξιος...". The reading begins at the bottom of fol. 146v and continues on fol. 147r (leaf p311).

[^809]: 1 Tim. 1:15: "ὅτι Χριστὸς Ἰησοῦς ἦλθεν εἰς τὸν κόσμον ἁμαρτωλοὺς σῶσαι, ὧν πρῶτός εἰμι ἐγώ." Completes the reading from leaf p310.

[^810]: 1 Tim. 1:16: "ἀλλὰ διὰ τοῦτο ἠλεήθην, ἵνα ἐν ἐμοὶ πρώτῳ ἐνδείξηται Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς τὴν ἅπασαν μακροθυμίαν, πρὸς ὑποτύπωσιν τῶν μελλόντων πιστεύειν ἐπ' αὐτῷ εἰς ζωὴν αἰώνιον."

[^811]: 1 Tim. 1:17: "τῷ δὲ βασιλεῖ τῶν αἰώνων, ἀφθάρτῳ, ἀοράτῳ, μόνῳ σοφῷ Θεῷ, τιμὴ καὶ δόξα εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων· ἀμήν." Note the doxology "unto ages of ages" strictly complying with MTS-1.

[^812]: CS: "Єѵ҃лїе ѿ ма́тѳе́а .". Rubric prescribing the Gospel reading (Matt. 9:9–13).

[^813]: Matt. 9:9: "Καὶ παράγων ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐκεῖθεν εἶδεν ἄνθρωπον καθήμενον ἐπὶ τὸ τελώνιον, Ματθαῖον λεγόμενον, καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ· ἀκολούθει μοι. καὶ ἀναστὰς ἠκολούθησεν αὐτῷ."

[^814]: Matt. 9:10: "Καὶ ἐγένετο αὐτοῦ ἀνακειμένου ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ, καὶ ἰδοὺ πολλοὶ τελῶναι καὶ ἁμαρτωλοὶ...". Continues on leaf p312.

[^815]: Matt. 9:10: "...ἐλθόντες συνανέκειντο τῷ Ἰησοῦ καὶ τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ." Completes verse 10 from leaf p311.

[^816]: Matt. 9:11: "καὶ ἰδόντες οἱ Φαρισαῖοι εἶπον τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ· διατί μετὰ τῶν τελωνῶν καὶ ἁμαρτωλῶν ἐσθίει ὁ διδάσκαλος ὑμῶν;".

[^817]: Matt. 9:12–13: "ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ἀκούσας εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· ... πορευθέντες δὲ μάθετε τί ἐστιν· ἔλεον θέλω καὶ οὐ θυσίαν. οὐ γὰρ ἦλθον καλέσαι δικαίους, ἀλλὰ ἁμαρτωλοὺς εἰς μετάνοιαν." Cf. Hos. 6:6.

[^818]: CS: "Є҆ктенїа̀ .". Rubric prescribing the Litany of Fervent Supplication (Augmented Litany) for the penitent.

[^819]: CS: "Поми́лоуй на́съ Бж҃е по вели́цей мл҃ти твое́й, мо́лимъ ти сѧ оу҆слы́ши и҆ поми́[лоуй]." Initial petition of the Augmented Litany.

[^820]: CS: "Є҆ще мо́лимсѧ оу҆слы́ши ны Бж҃е молѧ́щихъ тѧ ѡ҆ рабѣ́ твоемъ се́мъ , и҆́мѧ рекъ . ѡ҆ ѿда́нїи въсѧ́кого грѣха̀ сътвореннаго и҆́мъ .". Special penitential petition. Continues onto leaf p313.

[^821]: CS: "оу҆слы́ши и҆ помл҃ꙋй . Гдⷭ҇и мл҃ꙋй . н҃ .". Completes petition from fol. 147v; the response specifies "Lord, have mercy" fifty times (`н҃`), reflecting an extended penitential supplication (or possibly an early Ruthenian typesetting variant for forty / `м҃`).

[^822]: CS: "Ꙗ҆́ко мл҃тивъ и҆ ще́дръ и҆ чл҃колю́бивъ Бг҃ъ є҆си . и҆ тебѣ̀ сла́воу възсыла́ем ѿц҃оу и҆ сн҃оу и҆ ст҃мꙋ дх҃оу . нн҃ѣ и҆ :". Priest's ecphonesis, concluding with abbreviated doxology.

[^823]: CS: "посе́мъ , чⷭ҇тнѣ́йшоу хероуві́мъ . Сла́ва . и҆ нн҃ѣ . и҆ ѿпоу́стъ :~". Rubric prescribing the Megalynarion hymn, minor doxology, and dismissal.

[^824]: CS: "и҆ пото́мъ пооучи́ти и҆сповѣ́дника .". Rubric introducing the confessor's instruction and assignment of penance (epitimia).

[^825]: CS: "Ча́до , не бꙋ́ди ти та́жко ка́ющоусѧ . є҆́же тѧ ѿлоуча́ю ѿ цр҃кве дн҃їи четыридесѧ́те стоѧ́ти внѣ̀ .". The canonical penance of standing outside the nave (in the narthex or porch among the flentes/audientes) for forty days (tessarakoste).

[^826]: CS: "тако́въ бо оу҆ста́въ ѿ Бг҃а преда́нъ є҆́стъ ст҃ыми а҆плы , и҆ прпⷣбными ѿци .".

[^827]: CS: "да̀ подо́бно ѡ҆чи́стившесѧ , достѡ́йни боу́демъ причасти́тисѧ тѣ́лꙋ и҆ кро́ви Гн҃и .".

[^828]: CS: "та́ко бо ст҃ыи а҆плъ па́велъ оу҆чи́тъ гла̀ . а҆́ще не". Citation of 1 Cor. 11:27–29, continuing on leaf p314.

[^829]: Cf. 1 Cor. 11:27, 29: "...ὃς ἂν ἐσθίῃ τὸν ἄρτον ἢ πίνῃ τὸ ποτήριον τοῦ Κυρίου ἀναξίως... κρῖμα ἑαυτῷ ἐσθίει καὶ πίνει, μὴ διακρίνων τὸ σῶμα τοῦ Κυρίου." Completes citation from fol. 148r.

[^830]: Matt. 7:6: "Μὴ δῶτε τὸ ἅγιον τοῖς κυσί...".

[^831]: CS: "да̀ не пора́ботимъ сѧ чревнымъ по́хотемъ , но стѧжи́мъ пло́ды дх҃ѡ́вныхъ жела́нїи .".

[^832]: CS: "проти́вимсѧ тѣле́снымъ ласкосе́рдїемъ .". "Ласкосе́рдїе" translates Greek φιληδονία / γαστριμαργία (fondness for dainty delicacies, luxury, or sensuality).

[^833]: CS: "никі́и бо вре́дъ тѣле́сныи и҆сцѣлѣ́етъ въ пїянствѣ̀ , и҆ въ ѡ҆б̾ѧде́нїи .".

[^834]: CS: "а҆́ще кто̀ въздръжи́тсѧ въско́рѣ тве́рдѣ, то̀ въско́рѣ прїи́метъ ѡ҆ра́дꙋ .". "Ѡ҆ра́дꙋ" represents "ѡ҆тра́дꙋ" (relief, consolation, comfort).

[^835]: Cf. Prov. 5:3–4: "μέλι γὰρ ἀποστάζει ἀπὸ χειλέων γυναικὸς πόρνης... ὕστερον μέντοι πικρότερον χολῆς εὑρήσεις...".

[^836]: CS: "та́кожде и҆ покаѧ́нїе по́ста и҆ покланѧ́нїе . къ ма́лѣ ꙗ҆влѧ́ет́ сѧ". Continues on leaf p315.

[^837]: CS: "прискръ́бно , а҆ вѣ́кы ра́достныѧ плѡ́ды подае́тъ .". Completes period from fol. 148v. Cf. Heb. 12:11.

[^838]: Acts 14:22: "ὅτι διὰ πολλῶν θλίψεων δεῖ ἡμᾶς εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ Θεοῦ." Note the Ruthenian witness reads "црⷭ҇тво нбⷭ҇ное" (kingdom of heaven) in place of "βασιλείαν τοῦ Θεοῦ" (kingdom of God).

[^839]: Matt. 11:12: "ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν βιάζεται, καὶ βιασταὶ ἁρπάζουσιν αὐτήν."

[^840]: Cf. Luke 13:24 and Matt. 7:13–14: "ἀγωνίζεσθε εἰσελθεῖν διὰ τῆς στενῆς πύλης... στενὴ ἡ πύλη καὶ τεθλιμμένη ἡ ὁδὸς ἡ ἀπάγουσα εἰς τὴν ζωήν, καὶ ὀλίγοι εἰσὶν οἱ εὑρίσκοντες αὐτήν."

[^841]: Systematic ascetic catalog of penitential mortifications: fasting (*ἀσιτία*), thirst (*δίψα*), sleeping on the bare ground (*χαμευνία*), prostrations (*μετάνοιαι*), curtailing sleep (*ἀγρυπνία*), humility (*ταπεινοφροσύνη*), subjection, patient endurance (*ὑπομονή*), bearing wrongful injury, love of the poor / poverty (*φιλοπτωχεία*), and compunctionate tears (*πένθος*).

[^842]: CS: "пла́ча же въсего̀ и҆́стовое покаа́нїе , и҆́же є҆ди́ною ѿстоупи́вше ѿ грѣха̀ , и҆ ктомꙋ̀ не възврати́ти сѧ на то́же .". The Patristic definition of true repentance as permanent cessation of sin (cf. St. Basil the Great, *Regulae fusius tractatae*).

[^843]: Cf. Prov. 26:11; 2 Pet. 2:22: "κύων ἐπιστρέψας ἐπὶ τὸ ἴδιον ἐξέραμα, καί· ὗς λουσαμένη εἰς κύλισμα βορβόρου."

[^844]: The Prodigal Son (Luke 15:11–32) as the classical exemplar of repentance.

[^845]: Four classical evangelical models of repentance: the Prodigal Son, the First Thief (Luke 23:39–43), the Penitent Harlot (Luke 7:37–50), and the Publican/Matthew (Luke 18:13; Matt. 9:9).

[^846]: CS: "и҆́же є҆ди́ною ѿре́кшесѧ грѣ́хъ , и҆ ктомꙋ̀ не възвраща́тисѧ на тѣ́же .".

[^847]: Pastoral exhortation to practical ascetic substitution: xerophagy (*соухоꙗ́децъ* / *ξηροφαγία*) in place of rich delicacies. Continues on leaf p317.

[^848]: The catalogue of antithetical virtues displacing sinful habits: water-drinking replacing wine; tears replacing levity; humility replacing pride; hard ground (*жесто́ко лѣга́нїе*) replacing soft beds (*ма́кколѣга́нїе*); brotherly love replacing contention; peacemaking replacing factional strife (*сва́дникъ*); and charity to the poor replacing injustice. Completes list from fol. 149v.

[^849]: Cf. 1 Thess. 5:5: "πάντες γὰρ ὑμεῖς υἱοὶ φωτός ἐστε καὶ υἱοὶ ἡμέρας."

[^850]: CS: "и҆ тѣ́ми поутьмѝ въни́деши безъ троу́да въ стра́ноу црⷭ҇твїа нб҃наго .".

[^851]: Cf. Matt. 24:44; 25:13: "γίνεσθε ἕτοιμοι, ὅτι ᾗ ὥρᾳ οὐ δοκεῖτε ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἔρχεται... γρηγορεῖτε οὖν, ὅτι οὐκ οἴδατε τὴν ἡμέραν οὐδὲ τὴν ὥραν...".

[^852]: CS: "невѣ́мы бо доко́лѣ живо́тъ на́шъ .".

[^853]: CS: "а҆́ще ны ѡ҆брѧ́щетъ съмр҃ть въ грѣсѣ́хъ , то въскоу́ю". Rhetorical lament concluding on fol. 150v.

[^854]: CS: "боу́демсѧ роди́ли .". Completes sentence from fol. 150r: "а҆́ще ны ѡ҆брѧ́щетъ съмр҃ть въ грѣсѣ́хъ , то въскоу́ю боу́демсѧ роди́ли" (if death find us in sins, then to what purpose were we born?).

[^855]: Cf. 1 Thess. 4:17: "ἔπειτα ἡμεῖς οἱ ζῶντες... ἅμα σὺν αὐτοῖς ἁρπαγησόμεθα ἐν νεφέλαις εἰς ἀπάντησιν τοῦ Κυρίου εἰς ἀέρα...".

[^856]: Cf. Matt. 16:27: "μέλλει γὰρ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἔρχεσθαι ἐν тῇ δόξῃ τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτοῦ μετὰ τῶν ἀγγέλων αὐτοῦ, καὶ τότε ἀποδώσει ἑκάστῳ κατὰ τὴν πρᾶξιν αὐτοῦ." Also 2 Tim. 4:1 and the Symbol of Faith.

[^857]: CS: "и҆ поси́лмъ да́стъ є҆мꙋ̀ за́повѣдь є҆ли́кѡ мо́жет храни́ти .". Pastoral rubric enjoining pastoral economy (*oikonomia*) rather than unbending rigorism (*akribeia*) in assigning penances (*за́повѣдь* / *epitimia*).

[^858]: Marginal rubric in red cinnabar: "Зрѝ" (*Behold* / *Nota bene*).

[^859]: CS: "Не подоба́етъ за́повѣдь даꙗ́ти проти́вꙋ грѣхоу̀ , но̀ є҆́же и҆зво́литъ съхрани́ти . Подоба́етъ ѿце́мъ дх҃ѡ́внымъ расма́трѧти житїѐ коего́ждо . ста́рыхъ , и҆ юныхъ . бѡ́дрыхъ , и҆ неразꙋ́мныхъ . и҆". Enjoins spiritual fathers to adapt penances pastorally to the spiritual maturity, age, and disposition of the penitent. Continues on leaf p319.

[^860]: CS: "та́ко даꙗ́ти за́повѣди . подоба́етъ же малогрѣ́шноу , бо́дроу же , вели́коу прїима́ти . да̀ не то́чїю за́повѣдїю ѡ҆ставле́нїе грѣхѡ́мъ прїи́ме . но̀ и҆ вѣне́цъ нетлѣ́нный .". Completes sentence from fol. 150v. An ascetical principle that a spiritually zealous person with minor sins may voluntarily embrace severe penance to attain an incorruptible crown (cf. 1 Cor. 9:25).

[^861]: CS: "и҆спы́товати же досто́итъ моу́жа, и҆ же́ны , кѡли́ко въ то́мъ пребы́ша . и҆ коли́кѡ соу́тъ дѣ́тїи погоуби́ли .". Inquiries regarding abortion, infanticide, and abortifacients.

[^862]: CS: "па́че же вдовы̑ѧ , чернори́зица , мнѧ́щаѧсѧ дѣ́ва . и҆ чесо ра́ди , и҆ кацѣ́мъ ѡ҆́бразом .". Examination of consecrated persons (monastics) or consecrated virgins who concealed carnal fall and infanticide.

[^863]: CS: "и҆́но бо є҆́стъ є҆́же бы́лїе пи́ти да̀ не ро́дѧт дѣ́тїи, є҆́же тѧжча́йше въсѣ́х є҆́стъ . невѣ́дѧше бо кѡли́ко и҆́хъ хотѧ́ше роди́ти .". Canonical classification of contraceptive and abortifacient potions (*бы́лїе* / *pharmakeia*; cf. Canon 91 of the Quinisext Council / Trullo, and St. Basil Canon 2).

[^864]: CS: "а҆ дроу́гы бы́лїемъ є҆́же на но́въ мц҃ъ погꙋблѧ́ю младе́нца всепа́гꙋбнѣе,". Destructive potions administered during early gestation / new moon cycles. Continues on leaf p320.

[^865]: CS: "є҆́же до смр҃ти сѐ тво́рѧт . а҆́ще того̀ не ѡ҆ста́ноу́тсѧ , да̀ не ко́мкают́ сѧ .". Completes sentence from fol. 151r. The verb "ко́мкатисѧ" is the traditional Ruthenian liturgical term for receiving Holy Communion (*κοινωνεῖν* / *communicare*).

[^866]: CS: "За́повѣди же , и҆ разли́чнаа прѣще́нїа ѡ҆ моуже́хъ , и҆ ѡ҆ жена́хъ .". Section title introducing the canonical tariff of penances (*ἐπιτίμια* / *interdicts*).

[^867]: CS: "є҆ли́кѡ и҆́хъ сътвори́ша пре́жде л҃ , лѣ́тъ . мл҃тивно ско́ро проще́ни боу́доутъ грѣсѝ . Ѡ҆ є҆динкѣмъ г҃ , лѣ́та . а҆ ѡ҆ дроуѕѣ́мъ в҃ , лѣ́тѣ да̀ и҆́матъ запрѣще́нїе .". Lighter canonical discipline for transgressions committed before thirty years of age (the threshold of mature adulthood in Byzantine-Slavonic canon law; cf. Trullo, Canon 14).

[^868]: CS: "а҆́ще ли по л҃ , лѣ́тѣхъ , и҆деже оу҆бі́йство и҆ є҆́же съ бли́жнимъ блоу́дъ . и҆ съ пръ́ною сестро́ю . и҆ли съ снохо́ю . д҃ , и҆ли пѧ́ть лѣ́тъ .". Penances for murder and severe degrees of incestuous fornication (first cousin, daughter-in-law).

[^869]: CS: "а҆́ще ли с кꙋмо́ю , и҆ли съ кр҃ще́нною дще́рїю , и҆ли съ сестро́ю . є҆ , и҆ли ѕ҃ , лѣ́тъ .". Penances for spiritual incest (carnal relations with a godmother or baptismal daughter; cf. Trullo, Canon 53) or consanguineous sister.

[^870]: CS: "а҆́ще кто̀ по є҆́ствоу съгрѣ́шитъ , ре́кше". Catchphrase at the foot of fol. 151v, continuing on fol. 152r (leaf p321).

[^871]: CS: "не съ бли́жнимъ . є҆ди́но лѣ́то , и҆ли в҃ , за́повѣди .". Completes the canonical tariff for fornication according to nature (*по є҆́ствоу съгрѣши́ти*) from fol. 151v ([^870]). If the sin was committed with a person not related by blood or spiritual affinity, the penance (*за́повѣдь*) is one or two years of excommunication.

[^872]: CS: "и҆ є҆ли́кѡ оу҆мнѡ́жиша творѧ́ще . мнѡ́зи творѧ́тъ доста́рости . а҆́ще ли є҆диною, и҆ли два́щи , ꙗ҆ци́иже боу́доутъ . а҆́ лѣ́то , и҆ли по , даꙗ́ти заповѣ́ди .". The abbreviation "по" denotes *полъ лѣ́та* (half a year / six months). The canonical rule distinguishes habitual fornication persisting into old age from isolated lapses of once or twice.

[^873]: CS: "А҆́ще ли къ жена́хъ оу҆бі́йства нѣ́какова . и҆ли влъше́бства . и҆ли пре́ є҆стество . то̀ и҃ , и҆ли і҃ , лѣ́тъ .". Canonical penances for women guilty of infanticide or procured abortion (*оу҆бі́йство*), sorcery/witchcraft (*влъше́бство* / *pharmakeia*), or unnatural sexual sins (*пре́ є҆стество* / *παρὰ φύσιν*). Penance ranges from eight to ten years of excommunication.

[^874]: CS: "Въпросѝ и҆сповѣ́дающихсѧ . є҆да̀ боу́доутъ пре́жде и҆сповѣ́данїа причаща́лисѧ та́и не досто́йни сꙋ́ще . да а҆́ще боу́доутъ ма́лїи грѣсѝ , и҆ли вели́цїи . проти́вꙋ грѣхоу̀ ѿлоучи́ти ѿ ст҃го комка́нїа . въсѣ́хъ бо тѧжча́йшїи є҆́стъ грѣ́хъ , не досто́йны". Pastoral instruction requiring the confessor to interrogate whether the penitent sacrilegiously partook of the Holy Mysteries in an unconfessed state. The sentence concludes on fol. 152v.

[^875]: CS: "соу́щемъ комка́тисѧ . тѣ́мже ѿ Ѻглаше́нныхъ , си́рѣчь . є҆гда̀ рече́тъ дїа́конъ . є҆ли́ци Ѻглаше́ннїи и҆зыдѣ́те , и҆сходи́ти и҆з цр҃кве.". Completes sentence from fol. 152r. Unworthy communion is designated the most grievous of sins. Penitent sinners subject to this excommunication are relegated to the class of catechumens (*ѿ Ѻглаше́нныхъ*), obliged to depart the nave when the deacon chants the dismissal of catechumens (*Елицы оглашеннии, изыдите*).

[^876]: CS: "пръ́вое разли́чїе ѿ бра́шенъ . въ пне́, въ сре́ , въ пѧто́ , лѣ́то а҃ , за́повѣди .". The dietary discipline (*разли́чїе ѿ бра́шенъ*) for the first degree of penance: fasting on Mondays (*въ пне́* / *понедѣ́лникъ*), Wednesdays (*въ сре́* / *сре́ду*), and Fridays (*въ пѧто́* / *пѧто́къ*) throughout one year of penance.

[^877]: CS: "ꙗ҆́сти то́кмо сочиво и҆ ѕе́лїе . а҆ и҆ного всего̀ блюсти́сѧ . си́рѣчь сы́ра , ры́бы , ме́доу , и҆ всего сла́дка , и҆ вина̀ . є҆ди́ною же днемъ въ тыѧ рече́нныѧ г҃ , дни̑ ꙗ҆́сти . а҆́ще ли же слоучи́тсѧ Гпⷭ҇кїи пра́здникъ , и҆ли Бц҃и . и҆ли а҆рха́гг҃лоу . и҆ли прⷭ҇тчи . и҆ли ві҃ а҆пл҃ъ . тогда̀ ꙗ҆дѧ́тъ ри́бꙋ :~". Prescription of xerophagy (dry food): consuming only boiled wheat/grain (*сочиво*) and vegetables (*ѕе́лїе*), strictly abstaining from dairy, fish, mead, sweets, and wine, with meals restricted to once per day in the evening. Mitigations allowing fish are permitted on Great Feasts of the Lord, the Theotokos, the Archangels, the Forerunner, and the Twelve Apostles.

[^878]: CS: "Мл҃тва , разрѣши́ти и҆сповѣ́дника гл҃емаѧ ѿ дх҃овника . Гдⷵꙋ помолисѧ .". Rubric introducing the primary prayer of absolution uttered by the spiritual father over the kneeling penitent.

[^879]: CS: "Г҃ь прости́вый нада́но [= Наѳа́номъ] дв҃да своꙗ̀ и҆сповѣ́давша зла́ѧ". 2 Sam. (2 Kings LXX) 12:13: "And David said unto Nathan, I have sinned against the Lord. And Nathan said unto David, The Lord also hath put away thy sin." The printed form "нада́но" is an epigraphic/typesetting variant for "Наѳа́номъ" (through Nathan).

[^880]: Cf. Matt. 26:75 (Peter weeping bitterly after his denial); Luke 7:37–38 (the sinful woman washing Christ's feet with her tears); Luke 18:13–14 (the repentant publican); and Luke 15:11–24 (the return of the prodigal son).

[^881]: Scriptural quotations woven into the absolutory prayer: James 5:16: "Ἐξομολογεῖσθε ἀλλήλοις τὰ παραπτώματα" (Confess your transgressions one to another); and 1 John 1:9: "ἐὰν ὁμολογῶμεν τὰς ἁμαρτίας ἡμῶν, πιστός ἐστιν καὶ δίκαιος, ἵνα ἀφῇ ἡμῖν τὰς ἁμαρτίας καὶ καθαρίσῃ ἡμᾶς ἀπὸ πάσης ἀδικίας" (If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness).

[^882]: CS: "тъ́и са́мъ сп҃съ на́шъ Г҃ь і҃с х҃с , прости́тъ ти всѧ̑ , є҆ли́ка пре́днимъ мое́й и҆сповѣ́далъ є҆сѝ хоу́дости .". The classic Byzantine-Ruthenian deprecatory absolutory formula: Christ Himself forgives the penitent, while the priest acts as an unworthy minister (*хоу́дость*) witnessing and conveying divine remission.

[^883]: CS: "є҆ще́же , и҆ въ бꙋ́дꙋщемъ вѣ́цѣ не ѡ҆соужде́нна тѧ̀ на соуди́щи є҆го̀ прѣста́ти сподо́битъ". Absolution extending eschatologically to acquittal at the Dread Judgment Seat of Christ (cf. 2 Cor. 5:10). Concludes on fol. 153v.

[^884]: CS: "сы́и бл҃венъ въ вѣ́кы , а҆ми́нь :~". Doxology concluding the first prayer of absolution.

[^885]: CS: "Мл҃тва , дроуга́а подо́бнаа тои́же :". Rubric introducing the second alternative absolutory prayer.

[^886]: Cf. Col. 2:14: "ἐξαλείψας τὸ καθ’ ἡμῶν χειρόγραφον τοῖς δόγμασιν" (blotting out / tearing up the handwriting of ordinances against us); and Luke 4:18 (Isa. 61:1): "κηρύξαι αἰχμαλώτοις ἄφεσιν" (to preach release to the captives).

[^887]: CS: "ты̀ вл҃ко и҆ ра́ба твое́го [и҆́мѧ ре́къ] бл҃гтїю твое́ю свободѝ ѿ лежа́щаго съоу́за нане́мъ . и҆ дароу́и є҆моу̀ на всѧ́ко вре́мѧ , и҆ на всѧ́комъ мѣ́стѣ пристоупа́ти къ твое́моу вели́честву . и҆ съ дръзнове́нїе , и҆ чтою съвѣ́стїю". Rubrical insertion "[saying the name]" (*и҆́мѧ ре́къ*) where the confessor inserts the baptismal name of the penitent. Concludes on fol. 154r.

[^888]: CS: "проси́ти ѿ тебе бога́тыѧ мл҃ти .". Completes the final petition of the second absolutory prayer from fol. 153v.

[^889]: CS: "Ꙗ҆́ко мл҃тивъ и҆ чл҃колю́бецъ Б҃ъ є҆си , и҆ тебѣ̀ сла́воу възсыла́емъ ѿц҃оу и҆ сн҃оу и҆ ст҃омоу дх҃оу , нн҃ѣ и҆ при́сно и҆ въ вѣ́кы вѣкѡ́мъ :~". Hieratic sacerdotal doxology closing the prayer of absolution.

[^890]: CS: "та́же , ѿпоу́стъ :~". The formal liturgical dismissal (*ἀπόλυσις*) concluding the Order of Confession (Part XV).

[^891]: Tailpiece woodcut engraving depicting an ornamental Renaissance grotesque mask (mascaron) framed by strapwork and acanthus foliate scrollwork, serving as the typographic finis for Part XV (Confession).

[^892]: Fol. 154v is a blank folio (vacat) in the printed Striatyn edition. It features early manuscript pen trials (*probationes pennae*) in seventeenth- to eighteenth-century Ukrainian/Ruthenian cursive, recording hymnographic liturgical verses ("Благові́ствує земля́ / Ра́дость ве́лію / Хвали́те Небеса́ / Бо́жію сла́ву", evocative of the Annunciation Megalynarion) alongside a pen-and-ink cartoon sketch of a human face.

[^893]: CS: "ПОСЛѢ́ДОВА́НЇЕ СТ҃А́ГО ПРИЧАЩЕ́НЇА .". Foliated fol. 155r (leaf p327). Headed by an elaborate Renaissance floral woodcut headpiece across the full width of the text block containing the title in ligatured ornamental Cyrillic vyaz (*ПОСЛѢ́ДОВА́НЇЕ*) and large cinnabar display type (*СТ҃А́ГО ПРИЧАЩЕ́НЇА*). This marks the commencement of Part XVI in the codex structure: The Rule / Order of Preparation for Holy Communion (*Правило ко Святому Причащению*).

[^894]: CS: "А҆́ще сщ҃е́нникъ , гл҃етъ , Бл҃гослове́нъ Б҃ъ на́шъ .". Sacerdotal opening exclamation (*Εὐλογητὸς ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν πάντοτε...*). In accordance with Statutory Mandate 16, unwritten incipits are preserved verbatim as inked without silent interpolation.

[^895]: CS: "А҆́ще ли не сщ҃е́нникъ , сті́хъ За мл҃твъ ст҃ы́хъ ѿц҃ъ на́шихъ , Г҃и і҃с х҃е Б҃е на́шъ поми́лоуи на́съ , а҆ми́нь .". The monastic, deacon's, or lay opening verse (*Δι’ εὐχῶν τῶν ἁγίων πατέρων ἡμῶν...*) substituted when a priest is not presiding.

[^896]: CS: "и҆ по а҆ми́нѣ начина́емъ . Сла́ва тебѣ̀ Б҃е на́шъ , сла́ва тебѣ̀ .". Introductory doxological verses opening the Usual Beginning.

[^897]: CS: "Цр҃ю нб҃ный . тр҃тое . по Ѻ҆́ч҃е на́шъ . ꙗ҆́ко твоѐ є҆́стъ црⷭ҇тво . Г҃и поми́лоуй . в҃і .". Incipits denoting the invocation of the Holy Spirit (*O Heavenly King* / *Βασιλεῦ Οὐράνιε*), the Trisagion Prayers (*тр҃тое*), the Lord's Prayer (*Ѻ҆́ч҃е на́шъ*), priestly ecphonesis, and twelve repetitions of *Kyrie eleison*.

[^898]: CS: "прїидѣ́те поклони́мсѧ . г҃ .". Threefold recitation of the invitation to worship: "Come, let us worship and fall down before Christ our King and our God" (*Δεῦτε προσκυνήσωμεν...*).

[^899]: CS: "та́же , Ѱло́мъ , є҃і .". Rubric introducing Psalm 15 (LXX; Masoretic Ps. 16), the first of the three preparatory Psalms appointed for the Communion Rule.

[^900]: Ps. 15:1 (LXX; Masoretic Ps. 16:1): "Φύλαξόν με, Κύριε, ὅτι ἐπὶ σοὶ ἤλπισα." CS: "Съхрани́ мѧ Г҃и , ꙗ҆́ко на́ тѧ оу҆пова́хъ .".

[^901]: Ps. 15:2 (LXX; Masoretic Ps. 16:2): "εἶπα τῷ Κυρίῳ· Κύριός μου εἶ σύ, ὅτι τῶν ἀγαθῶν μου οὐ χρείαν ἔχεις." CS: "рѣ́хъ Г҃ви, Г҃ь мо́и є҆си ты, ꙗ҆́ко бл҃гы́х мои́хъ не тре́боу́еши .".

[^902]: Ps. 15:3 (LXX; Masoretic Ps. 16:3): "τοῖς ἁγίοις τοῖς ἐν τῇ γῇ αὐτοῦ ἐθαυμάστωσεν ὁ Κύριος πάντα τὰ θελήματα αὐτοῦ ἐν αὐτοῖς." CS: "Ст҃ы̑мъ и҆́же соу́тъ на землѝ є҆го, оу҆дивѝ Г҃ь всѧ̑ хотѣ́нїа своꙗ̀ въ ни́хъ .". Conforms to MTS-1 Anti-Slop: "marvelous" rather than "wondrous".

[^903]: Ps. 15:4 (LXX; Masoretic Ps. 16:4): "ἐπληθύνθησαν αἱ ἀσθένειαι αὐτῶν, μετὰ ταῦτα ἐτάχυναν· οὐ μὴ συναγάγω τὰς συναγωγὰς αὐτῶν ἐξ αἱμάτων, οὐδ’ οὐ μὴ μνησθῶ τῶν ὀνομάτων αὐτῶν διὰ χειλέων μου." CS: "оу҆мно́жишасѧ не́мощи и҆́хъ, по си́х оу҆скори́ша . не събероу́ събѡ́ры и҆́хъ ѿ крове́и , ни помѧноу́ же и҆ме́нъ и҆́хъ оу҆стна́ма мои́ма .".

[^904]: Ps. 15:5 (LXX; Masoretic Ps. 16:5): "Κύριος ἡ μερὶς τῆς κληρονομίας μου καὶ τοῦ ποτηρίου μου· σὺ εἶ ὁ ἀποκαθιστῶν τὴν κληρονομίαν μου ἐμοί." CS: "Г҃ь ча́сть досто́ѧнїа мое́го , и҆ ча́ша моꙗ́ . ты̀ є҆си оу҆строѧ́ѧ досто́ѧнїе моѐ мнѣ̀ .".

[^905]: Ps. 15:6 (LXX; Masoretic Ps. 16:6): "σχοινία ἐπέπεσόν μοι ἐν τοῖς κρατίστοις· καὶ γὰρ ἡ κληρονομία μου κρατίστη μοί ἐστιν." CS: "Ꙙ҆́жа допадо́ша ми въ дръжа́вныхъ мои́хъ . и҆́бо досто́ѧнїе моѐ дръжа́вно мнѣ̀ є҆́сть .".

[^906]: Ps. 15:7 (LXX; Masoretic Ps. 16:7): "εὐλογήσω τὸν Κύριον τὸν συνετίσαντά με· ἔτι δὲ καὶ ἕως νυκτὸς ἐπαίδευσάν με οἱ νεφροί μου." CS: "Бл҃гвлю Г҃а въразоуми́вшаго мѧ̀ . є҆ще́ же и҆ до но́щи наказа́ мѧ оу҆тро́ба моа̀ .". Fol. 155v ends here.

[^907]: Ps. 15:8 (LXX; Masoretic Ps. 16:8): "προωρώμην τὸν Κύριον ἐνώπιόν μου διὰ παντός, ὅτι ἐκ δεξιῶν μού ἐστιν, ἵνα μὴ σαλευθῶ." CS: "Пре́зрѣ́хъ Г҃а предомно́ю вы́нꙋ , ꙗ҆́ко ѻдесно́ю менѐ є҆́стъ да сѧ не подви́жꙋ .". Fol. 156r begins.

CS: "Ꙗ҆́ко не ѡ҆ста́виши дш҃ю мою въ а҆́дѣ , ни да́си же прпⷣбному своє́мꙋ ви́дѣти и҆стлѣ́нїа .". Messianic prophecy of the Resurrection quoted by St. Peter in Acts 2:27.

[^912]: Ps. 21:1 (LXX; Masoretic Ps. 22:1): "Ὁ Θεὸς ὁ Θεός μου, πρόσχες μοι· ἵνα τί ἐγκατέλιπές με;" CS: "Б҃е мо́и въньмѝ ми , въскоу́ю ѡ҆ста́ви мѧ .". The cry of Christ from the Cross (Matt. 27:46; Mark 15:34).

[^914]: Ps. 21:3 (LXX; Masoretic Ps. 22:2): "ὁ Θεός μου, κεκράξομαι ἡμέρας, καὶ οὐκ εἰσακούσῃ, καὶ νυκτός, καὶ οὐκ εἰς ἄνοιαν ἐμοί." CS: "Б҃е мо́и въззовоу̀ въ дне́хъ , и҆ не оу҆слы́шиши . и҆ но́щїю , и҆ не въ [p330: бєзоу́мїе мнѣ̀ .]". Concludes on fol. 156v.

[^915]: CS: "бєзоу́мїе мнѣ̀ .". Completes verse 3 of Psalm 21 (LXX; Masoretic Ps. 22:2) from fol. 156r: "and by night, and it shall not be reckoned as folly unto me" (*καὶ οὐκ εἰς ἄνοιαν ἐμοί*).

[^917]: Ps. 21:5 (LXX; Masoretic Ps. 22:4): "ἐπὶ σοὶ ἤλπισαν οἱ πατέρες ἡμῶν, ἤλπισαν, καὶ ἐρρύσω αὐτούς." CS: "На́ тѧ оу҆пова́ша ѿц҃и на́ши . Оу҆пова́ша , и҆ и҆зба́вилъ и҆́хъ є҆си .".

[^918]: Ps. 21:6 (LXX; Masoretic Ps. 22:5): "πρὸς σὲ ἐκέκραξαν καὶ ἐσώθησαν, ἐπὶ σοὶ ἤλπισαν καὶ οὐ κατῃσχύνθησαν." CS: "К тебѣ̀ възва́ша , и҆ сп҃со́шасѧ . На́ тѧ оу҆пова́ша , и҆ не постыдѣ́шасѧ .".

[^919]: Ps. 21:7 (LXX; Masoretic Ps. 22:6): "ἐγὼ δέ εἰμι σκώληξ καὶ οὐκ ἄνθρωπος, ὄνειδος ἀνθρώπων καὶ ἐξουθένημα λαοῦ." CS: "А҆́зъ же є҆́смь чръ́вь , а҆ не чл҃къ . Поноше́нїе чл҃кѡмъ , и҆ оу҆ничиже́нїе люде́й .". Prophecy of Christ's abasement.

[^920]: Ps. 21:8 (LXX; Masoretic Ps. 22:7): "πάντες οἱ θεωροῦντές με ἐξεμυκτήρισάν με, ἐλάλησαν ἐν χείλεσιν, ἐκίνησαν κεφαλήν." CS: "Вси ви́дѧщей мѧ̀ порꙋга́ша мисѧ . Гл҃аша оу҆стна́ми , покива́ша главоу̀ .". Fulfilled at Golgotha (Matt. 27:39).

[^921]: Ps. 21:9 (LXX; Masoretic Ps. 22:8): "ἤλπισεν ἐπὶ Κύριον, ῥυσάσθω αὐτόν, σωσάτω αὐτόν, ὅτι θέλει αὐτόν." CS: "Оу҆пова̀ на Г҃а да и҆зба́витъ и҆́ . Да сп҃сетъ є҆го̀ , ꙗ҆́ко хо́щетъ є҆го̀ .". Fulfilled in the mockery of the chief priests and scribes (Matt. 27:43).

[^922]: Ps. 21:10 (LXX; Masoretic Ps. 22:9): "ὅτι σὺ εἶ ὁ ἐκσπάσας με ἐκ γαστρός, ἡ ἐλπίς μου ἀπὸ μαστῶν τῆς μητρός μου." CS: "Ꙗ҆́ко ты̀ є҆си и҆стръгі́и мѧ и҆з чре́ва , оу҆пова́нїе моѐ ѿ съсоу мт҃ре мое́ѧ .".

[^923]: Ps. 21:11 (LXX; Masoretic Ps. 22:10): "ἐπὶ σὲ ἐπερρίφην ἐκ μήτρας, ἐκ κοιλίας μητρός μου Θεός μου εἶ σύ." CS: "К тебѣ̀ привръ́женъ є҆смь ѿ ложе́нъ . ѿ чре́ва мт҃ре мое́ѧ Б҃ъ мо́и є҆си ты̀ .". Leaf p330 concludes here; Psalm 21 continues on fol. 157r (leaf p331).

[^924]: Fol. 157r (leaf p331) continues Psalm 21 (LXX; Masoretic Ps. 22) from fol. 156v ([^923]). Ps. 21:12–14: "не ѿстꙋпѝ ѿ менѐ ꙗ҆́ко ско́рбь бли́зъ , ꙗ҆́ко нѣ́сть помага́ѧй ми : Ѡ҆быдо́ша мѧ̀ те́лци мнѡ́ѕи , ю҆́нци тоу́чнїи ѡ҆дръжа́ша мѧ̀ . Ѡ҆връ́зоша на́ мѧ оу҆ста̀ своꙗ̀ , ꙗ҆́ко ле́въ въсхища́ѧ и҆ рыка́ѧ ." (Depart not from Me, for affliction is near; for there is none to help Me. Many bullocks have compassed Me; fat bulls have beset Me round. They have opened their mouth against Me, as a ravening and a roaring lion).

[^925]: Ps. 21:15–16 (LXX; Masoretic Ps. 22:14–15): The somatic dissolution of the Crucified Messiah: "Ꙗ҆́ко вода̀ и҆злїѧ́хъсѧ , и҆ разсы́пашасѧ всѧ̑ ко́сти моꙗ̑ . Бы́сть срⷣце моѐ ꙗ҆́ко во́скъ , та́ѧ посредѣ̀ чре́ва мое́го . И҆́зше ꙗ҆́ко скоуде́ль крѣ́пость моꙗ̀ , и҆ ꙗ҆зы́къ мо́и прильпѐ горта́ни мое́моу . И҆ въ пръ́сть смръ́ти съве́лъ мѧ̀ є҆сѝ ." (I am poured out like water, and all My bones are scattered; My heart is become like wax, melting in the midst of My belly. My strength is dried up like a potsherd, and My tongue cleaves to My throat; and Thou hast brought Me down into the dust of death).

[^926]: Ps. 21:17–18a (LXX; Masoretic Ps. 22:16–17a): Prophecy of the Crucifixion: "Ꙗ҆́ко ѡ҆быдо́ша мѧ̀ ѱѝ мнѡ́ѕи , съ́немъ лоука́выхъ ѡ҆дръжа́ша мѧ̀ . И҆скопа́ша рꙋ́цѣ моѝ , и҆ но́ѕѣ моѝ , и҆счето́ша всѧ̑ кѡ́сти [моꙗ̀]" (For many dogs have compassed Me; the assembly of the wicked hath beset Me round. They have pierced My hands and My feet; they have numbered all My bones). Concludes on fol. 157v.

[^927]: Ps. 21:18b–19 (LXX; Masoretic Ps. 22:17b–18): Completes verse 18 from fol. 157r: "моꙗ̀ . Ті́иже смотрѣ́ша и҆ пре́зрѣша мѧ̀ . Раздѣли́ша ри́зы моꙗ̑ себѣ̀ , и҆ ѡ҆ мати́змѣ мое́й мета́ша жрѣ́бїа ." (My bones; they looked and stared upon Me. They parted My garments among them, and upon My vesture did they cast lots). Features the Greek calque/loanword *мати́зма* for ἱματισμός (vesture/garment; cf. Matt. 27:35; John 19:24).

[^928]: Ps. 21:20–22 (LXX; Masoretic Ps. 22:19–21): "Ты́же Г҃и не оу҆да́ли по́мощь твою̀ ѿ менѐ , на застоупле́нїе моѐ въньмѝ . И҆зба́ви ѿ ѻ҆рꙋ́жїа дш҃ю мою̀ , и҆ и҆з рꙋкѝ пе́сїа є҆диноро́дную мою̀ . Сп҃си́ мѧ ѿ оу҆́стъ льво́въ , и҆ ѿ рѡ́гъ є҆диноро́ждь смѣре́нїе моѐ ." (But Thou, O Lord, remove not Thy help far from Me; attend unto My defense. Deliver My soul from the sword, and Mine only-begotten from the hand of the dog. Save Me from the mouth of the lion, and My lowliness from the horns of the unicorns). CS "ѿ рѡ́гъ є҆диноро́ждь" translates Greek ἀπὸ κεράτων μονοκερώτων.

[^929]: Ps. 21:23–25a (LXX; Masoretic Ps. 22:22–24a): "Повѣ́мъ и҆́мѧ твоѐ бра́тїи мое́й , посредѣ̀ цр҃кве въспою́ тѧ . Боѧ́щїисѧ Г҃а въсхвали́те и҆̀ . Всѐ сѣ́мѧ і҆а́ковле просла́вите и҆̀ . Да оу҆бои́т же сѧ ѿ него всѐ сѣ́мѧ і҆и҃лево . Ꙗ҆́ко не оу҆ничижѝ , ни негодова̀ мл҃твы ни́щаго . Ни ѡ҆врати́лъ же є҆́стъ [лица̀ своє́го ѿ менѐ]" (I will declare Thy name unto My brethren; in the midst of the church will I sing praise unto Thee. Ye that fear the Lord, praise Him; all ye seed of Jacob, glorify Him; let all the seed of Israel fear Him. For He hath not despised nor abhorred the prayer of the poor; neither hath He turned away...). Verse 23 is cited in Heb. 2:12. Concludes on fol. 158r.

[^930]: Ps. 21:25b–26 (LXX; Masoretic Ps. 22:24b–25): Completes verse 25 from fol. 157v: "лица̀ своє́го ѿ менѐ . И҆ є҆гда̀ възъзва́[хъ] къ немоу , оу҆слы́ша мѧ̀ . Ѡ҆ тебѣ̀ похва́ла моꙗ̀ . Въ цр҃кви вели́цѣ и҆сповѣ́мсѧ тебѣ̀ . Мл҃твы моꙗ̑ възда́мъ предъ боꙗ́щимисѧ є҆го̀ ." (His face from Me; but when I cried unto Him, He gave ear unto Me. From Thee is My praise; in the great church will I confess unto Thee; My vows will I pay before them that fear Him).

[^931]: Ps. 21:27 (LXX; Masoretic Ps. 22:26): Eucharistic prophecy: "Ꙗ҆дѧ́тъ ни́щїи и҆ насы́тѧтсѧ, и҆ въсхва́лѧтъ Г҃а възыска́ющїи є҆го̀ . Жи́ва бꙋ́доутъ срⷣца и҆́хъ въ вѣ́кы вѣ́ка ." (The poor shall eat and be satisfied, and they that seek the Lord shall praise Him; their heart shall live unto ages of ages). Conforms strictly to the Father Paul Doxology Standard ("unto ages of ages").

[^932]: Ps. 21:28–30 (LXX; Masoretic Ps. 22:27–29): Universal eschatological homage: "Помѧноу́тсѧ и҆ ѡ҆братѧ́тсѧ къ Г҃оу вси́ кѡ́нци землѧ̀ . И҆ покло́нѧтсѧ пре́днимъ всѧ̑ ѿч҃ьствїа ꙗ҆зы́къ . Ꙗ҆́ко Гн҃е є҆́стъ црⷭ҇твїе , и҆ тъ́и ѡ҆блада́етъ ꙗ҆зы́кы . Ꙗ҆до́ша и҆ поклони́шасѧ вси тоу́чнїи землѧ̀ . Пре́днимъ припа́доутъ вси низходѧ́щеи въ зе́млю . И҆ дш҃а моꙗ̀ томоу̀ [живє́тъ...]" (All the ends of the earth shall remember and turn unto the Lord, and all the kindreds of the nations shall worship before Him. For the kingdom is the Lord's, and He is the ruler over the nations. All the fat ones of the earth have eaten and worshipped; all they that go down into the earth shall fall down before Him. And My soul unto Him...). Concludes on fol. 158v.

[^933]: Ps. 21:30b–32 (LXX; Masoretic Ps. 22:29b–31): Completes Psalm 21 from fol. 158r: "живє́тъ , и҆ сѣ́мѧ моѐ порабо́таєтъ є҆моу̀ . Възвѣсти́тъ Г҃ви ро́дъ грѧдоу́щїи , и҆ възвѣстѧ́тъ пра́вдоу є҆го лю́демъ ро́дѧщимсѧ , и҆́х же сътворѝ Г҃ь :~" (shall live, and My seed shall serve Him. The generation to come shall be declared unto the Lord; and they shall declare His righteousness unto a people that shall be born, whom the Lord hath made).

[^934]: CS: "Ѱало́мъ , кв҃ .". Rubric introducing Psalm 22 (LXX; Masoretic Ps. 23), the pre-eminent Eucharistic psalm of the Good Shepherd, appointed in the Byzantine rite before approaching the Holy Mysteries.

[^935]: Ps. 22:1–3 (LXX; Masoretic Ps. 23:1–3): "Г҃ь пасе́тъ мѧ̀ , и҆ ничто́же мѧ лишитъ . На мѣ́стѣ зла́чнѣ , та́мо мѧ̀ въселѝ . На водѣ̀ поко́йнѣ въспита̀ мѧ , дш҃ю мою̀ ѡ҆братѝ . Наста́ви мѧ на сте́ѕѧ пра̑вы и҆мени своє́го ра́ди ." (The Lord is my shepherd, and nothing shall be lacking unto me. In a place of green pasture, there hath He made me to dwell; by the water of rest hath He nourished me. He hath converted my soul; He hath guided me into the paths of righteousness for His name's sake).

[^936]: Ps. 22:4–5a (LXX; Masoretic Ps. 23:4–5a): "А҆́ще бо и҆ поидоу̀ посредѣ̀ сѣ́ни смр҃тныѧ , не оу҆ бою́сѧ зла̀ , ꙗ҆́ко ты̀ съ мно́ю є҆си . Же́злъ тво́и , и҆ па́лица твоꙗ̀ , та̀ мѧ оу҆тѣ́шиста . Оу҆гото́валъ є҆си предо мно́ю трапе́зоу , прѣⷣстоужа́ющими [мнѣ̀ .]" (For though I should walk through the midst of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for Thou art with me; Thy rod and Thy staff, they have comforted me. Thou hast prepared a table before me against them that afflict me). Concludes on fol. 159r.

[^937]: Ps. 22:5b–6 (LXX; Masoretic Ps. 23:5b–6): Completes Psalm 22 from fol. 158v. Patristic Eucharistic typology: "мнѣ̀ . Оу҆масти́лъ є҆си є҆ле́емъ главꙋ̀ мою̀ , и҆ ча́ша твоꙗ̀ оу҆поѧ́ющи мѧ̀ ко́ль дръжа́вна . И҆ мл҃ть твоꙗ̀ пожене́тъ мѧ̀ всѧ̑ дни̑ живота̀ мое́го . И҆ да въселю́сѧ въ до́мъ Гн҃ь въ дълготоу̀ днїи :~" (me. Thou hast anointed my head with oil, and Thy cup which inebriates me, how excellent it is! And Thy mercy shall pursue me all the days of my life, and that I may dwell in the house of the Lord unto length of days). CS "ча́ша твоꙗ̀ оу҆поѧ́ющи мѧ̀ ко́ль дръжа́вна" translates Greek καὶ τὸ ποτήριόν σου μεθύσκον ὡς κράτιστον.

[^938]: CS: "Ѱло́мъ к҃г .". Rubric introducing Psalm 23 (LXX; Masoretic Ps. 24), chanting the majestic entrance of the King of Glory and the moral purity required of those who ascend the holy hill to receive the Sacred Mysteries.

[^939]: Ps. 23:1–4 (LXX; Masoretic Ps. 24:1–4): "Гн҃ѧ є҆́стъ землѧ̀ , и҆ и҆сплъне́нїе є҆ѧ̀ . Въселе́ннаѧ , и҆ всѝ живоу́щїи на не́и . Тъ́и на мѡ́рихъ ѡ҆снова́лъ ю҆̀ є҆́стъ , и҆ на рѣка́хъ оу҆гото́валъ ю҆̀ є҆́стъ . Кто̀ възы́дет на гороу̀ Гн҃ю , и҆ли кто̀ ста́нетъ на мѣ́стѣ ст҃ѣ́мъ є҆го . Непови́ненъ рꙋка́ма , и҆ чт҃ъ срⷣцем , и҆́же не прїѧ́тъ насоу́е дш҃ю свою̀ . И҆ не клѧ́тсѧ ле́стїю и҆́скрънемꙋ своє́мꙋ . Се́и прїи́ме [бл҃гве́нїе ѿ Г҃а...]" (The earth is the Lord's, and the fullness thereof; the world, and all that dwell therein. He hath founded it upon the seas, and prepared it upon the rivers. Who shall ascend into the mountain of the Lord, or who shall stand in His holy place? He that is innocent in hands and pure in heart; who hath not received his soul in vain, nor sworn deceitfully unto his neighbor. He shall receive...). Concludes on fol. 159v.

[^940]: Ps. 23:5–6 (LXX; Masoretic Ps. 24:5–6): Completes the blessing upon the pure in heart from fol. 159r: "бл҃гве́нїе ѿ Г҃а , и҆ млⷭ҇тыню ѿ Б҃а сп҃са свое́го . Се́и ро́дъ и҆́щоущихъ Г҃а , и҆щꙋ́щїи лицѐ Б҃а і҆а́ковлѧ ." (a blessing from the Lord, and mercy from God his Savior. This is the generation of them that seek the Lord, that seek the face of the God of Jacob).

[^941]: Ps. 23:7–10 (LXX; Masoretic Ps. 24:7–10): The dialogue of the celestial powers at the gates of heaven: "Възми́те врата̀ кнѧ́зи ва́ша, и҆ възми́тесѧ вра́та вѣ́чнаѧ . И҆ въни́детъ цр҃ь сла́вы . Кто̀ є҆́стъ съ́и цр҃ь сла́вы ; Г҃ь крѣ́покъ и҆ си́ленъ , Г҃ь си́ленъ въ бра́ни . Възми́те вра́та кнѧ́зи ва́ша , и҆ възми́тесѧ вра́та вѣ́чнаѧ . И҆ въни́детъ цр҃ь сла́вы . Кто̀ є҆́стъ съ цр҃ь сла́вы ; Г҃ь си́ламъ тъ є҆́стъ цр҃ь сла́вы :~" (Lift up your gates, O ye princes, and be ye lifted up, ye everlasting gates; and the King of glory shall enter in. Who is this King of glory? The Lord strong and mighty, the Lord mighty in battle. Lift up your gates, O ye princes, and be ye lifted up, ye everlasting gates; and the King of glory shall enter in. Who is this King of glory? The Lord of hosts, He is the King of glory).

[^942]: CS: "Ѱло́мъ , рі҃є .". Rubric introducing Psalm 115 (LXX; Masoretic Ps. 116:10–19), the ancient Eucharistic thanksgiving psalm cited by St. Paul (2 Cor. 4:13) and recited by the celebrant before partaking of the Holy Chalice.

[^943]: Ps. 115:1–3a (LXX; Masoretic Ps. 116:10–12a): "Вѣ́ровахъ, тѣ́мже възгл҃ахъ . А҆́зъ же смѣри́хсѧ ѕѣло̀ . А҆́зъ же рѣ́хъ въ оу҆́жасѣ мое́мъ всѧ́къ чл҃къ ле́жъ . Что̀ възда́мъ Г҃ви ѡ҆ [всѣ́хъ...]" (I believed, therefore have I spoken; but I was humbled exceedingly. I said in mine ecstasy: Every man is a liar. What shall I render unto the Lord for...). The particle *тѣ́мже* is translated as "therefore" in strict compliance with MTS-1 Anti-Slop, prohibiting pseudo-archaic "wherefore". Concludes on fol. 160r.

[^944]: Ps. 115:3b–5 (LXX; Masoretic Ps. 116:12b–14): Completes verse 3 from fol. 159v: "всѣ́хъ ꙗ҆́же възда́стъ ми ; Ча́шю сп҃се́нїа прїимꙋ̀ , и҆ и҆́мѧ Гн҃е призовꙋ̀ . Мл҃твы моꙗ̑ Г҃ви възда́мъ прѣⷣ всѣ́ми людьмѝ є҆го ." (all that He hath rendered unto me? I will take the cup of salvation, and will call upon the name of the Lord. My vows will I pay unto the Lord in the presence of all His people).

[^945]: Ps. 115:6–10 (LXX; Masoretic Ps. 116:15–19): Concluding verses of the psalm: "Чⷭ҇тна пред̾ Г҃мъ смр҃ть прпⷣбныхъ є҆го . Ѡ҆ Г҃и а҆́зъ ра́бъ тво́и , а҆́зъ ра́бъ тво́и и҆ сн҃ъ рабы̀ твоє́ѧ . Растръ́за ꙗ҆́зы моꙗ̑ . Тебѣ̀ пожроу̀ жръ́твоу хвалѣ̀ , и҆ и҆́мѧ Гн҃е призовоу̀ . Мл҃твы моꙗ̑ Г҃ви въздамъ прѣⷣ всѣ́ми людьмѝ є҆го . Въ дво́рѣхъ до́моу Гн҃ѧ , посредѣ̀ тебе і҆ерл҃име :~" (Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of His saints. O Lord, I am Thy servant; I am Thy servant and the son of Thine handmaid; Thou hast broken my bonds asunder. To Thee will I offer the sacrifice of praise, and will call upon the name of the Lord. My vows will I pay unto the Lord in the presence of all His people, in the courts of the Lord's house, in the midst of thee, O Jerusalem). CS *ꙗ҆́зы* is an orthographic variant for *оу҆́зы* (bonds).

[^946]: CS: "Сла́ . И҆ нн҃ѣ . А҆ллилоу́їа . г҃ . И҆ тропарѧ̑ сїа . Гл҃ . и҃ .". Rubric prescribing the Little Doxology, threefold Alleluia, and the three Penitential Troparia of Tone 8 appointed before Communion.

[^947]: First Penitential Troparion (Tone 8): "Безако́нїа моꙗ̀ пре́зри Г҃и , и҆́же ѿ дв҃ы рожде́исѧ . И҆ срⷣце моѐ ѡ҆чи́сти цр҃ковь то тво́рѧ прчⷭ҇тому твоє́моу [тѣ́лоу и҆ кро́ви...]" (Overlook mine iniquities, O Lord Who wast born of the Virgin, and cleanse my heart, making it a temple for Thine all-pure Body and Blood...). Concludes on fol. 160v.

[^948]: Completes the first Tone 8 Penitential Troparion from fol. 160r: "тѣ́лоу и҆ кро́ви . Ниже ѿри́неши менѐ ѿ твое́го лица̀ , и҆́же без̾ числа̀ имѣ́ѧй ве́лїю мл҃ть :~" (Body and Blood; neither cast Thou me away from Thy presence, O Thou Who without measure hast great mercy).

[^949]: CS: "Сла́ва .". Rubric appointing the Doxological verse before the second troparion.

[^950]: Second Penitential Troparion (Tone 8): Allusion to the Gospel parable of the wedding garment (Matt. 22:11–13): "Въ прича́стїи ст҃ы́хъ твои́хъ , ка́ко дръзноу̀ ѻ҆каѧ́нныи . А҆́ще бо дръзноу̀ к тебѣ̀ съ досто́йными пристоупи́ти , ѻ҆де́жда мѧ ѡ҆блича́етъ ꙗ҆́ко нѣ́сть бра́чна . И҆ ѡ҆соужде́нїе и҆сходата́йствоую мнѡ́го грѣ́шной дш҃и мое́и . Ѡ҆чи́сти Г҃и сквръ́ноу дш҃ѧ мое́ѧ, и҆ сп҃си́ мѧ ꙗ҆́ко чл҃колю́бецъ :~" (Into the communion of Thy holy things how shall I, the wretched one, dare to enter? For if I dare to approach Thee with the worthy, my garment convicts me, for it is not a wedding garment, and condemnation do I procure for my most sinful soul. Cleanse, O Lord, the defilement of my soul, and save me, as Thou art the Lover of mankind).

[^951]: CS: "И҆ нн҃ѣ .". Rubric appointing the Theotokion.

[^952]: Penitential Theotokion (Tone 8): "Мнѡ́гаѧ премнѡ́жества мои́хъ Бц҃е съгрѣше́нїи . К тебѣ̀ прибѣго́хъ прчⷭ҇таѧ сп҃се́нїа тре́боуѧ . Посѣтѝ недоу́гоуꙋ́щую мою дш҃ю . И҆ молѝ сн҃а своє́го и҆ Б҃а на́шего , пода́ти ми [ѡ҆ставле́нїе...]" (Great is the multitude of my transgressions, O Theotokos; unto thee have I fled, O all-pure one, requiring salvation. Visit my ailing soul, and pray unto thy Son and our God, that He grant unto me remission...). Concludes on fol. 161r.

[^953]: Completes the Tone 8 Penitential Theotokion from fol. 160v: "ѡ҆ставле́нїе , и҆́хъже съдѣ́лахъ ѕлѣ̀ є҆ди́на бл҃гве́наѧ ." (remission of the evils which I have done, O only blessed one).

[^954]: CS: "Та́же ѱало́мъ н҃ .". Rubric appointing the recitation of Psalm 50 (LXX; Masoretic Ps. 51).

[^955]: CS: "Поми́лꙋй мѧ̀ Б҃е . Кано́нъ причаще́нїю . Гла́ в҃ . Пѣ́снь а҆ . І҆рмо́съ . Грѧдѣ́те лю́дїе .". Rubric introducing the Canon of Preparation for Holy Communion in Tone 2, with the incipit of the Heirmos of Ode 1 (*Come, ye peoples* / Δεῦτε λαοί, ᾄσωμεν ᾆσμα Χριστῷ τῷ Θεῷ).

[^956]: CS: "сті́хъ . Срⷣце чⷭ҇то съзи́жди въ мнѣ̀ Б҃е . И҆ дх҃ъ пра́въ ѡ҆бновѝ въ оу҆тро́бѣ мое́й .". Stichos from Ps. 50:12 (LXX) intercalated before the first troparion.

[^957]: Ode 1, Troparion 1: "Хлѣ́бъ живота̀ вѣчноу́ющаго , да бꙋ́детъ ми тѣ́ло твоѐ ст҃ое бл҃гооу҆тро́бне Г҃и , и҆ чⷭ҇тнаѧ кро́вь . И҆ болѣ́знемъ мнѡгоѡ҆́бразным и҆сцѣле́нїе :~" (May Thy holy Body and precious Blood, O compassionate Lord, be unto me the Bread of eternal life, and healing of manifold infirmities).

[^958]: CS: "сті́ : Не ѡ҆връ́зи менѐ ѿ лица̀ твое́го , и҆ дх҃а ст҃го твое́го не ѿимѝ ѿ менѐ :~". Stichos from Ps. 50:13 (LXX) intercalated before the second troparion.

[^959]: Ode 1, Troparion 2: "Кро́вь твою̀ вл҃ко прчⷭ҇тоую , и҆ тѣ́ло твоѐ прⷭ҇тое , менѐ сподо́би не досто́инаго . Прїѧ́ти ꙗ҆́сти съ жела́нїемъ . [и҆ вѣ́рою и҆спи́ти :~]" (Vouchsafe me, an unworthy one, O Master, to receive and eat with longing Thine all-pure Blood and Thy most holy Body, and with faith to drink...). Concludes on fol. 161v.

[^960]: Completes Ode 1, Troparion 2 from fol. 161r: "и҆ вѣ́рою и҆спи́ти :~" (and with faith to drink).

[^961]: CS: "Сла́ва .". Rubric appointing the Doxology before Troparion 3.

[^962]: Ode 1, Troparion 3: "Ѡ҆сквръ́ненъ дѣ́лы без̾мѣ́стными ѻ҆каѧ́нный . Твое́го прчⷭ҇таго тѣ́ла и҆ Бж҃тве́ныѧ кро́ве , недосто́инъ сы́и Х҃е причаще́нїа . Є҆го́же мѧ̀ сподо́би :~" (Defiled by improper deeds, wretched that I am, and unworthy of the communion of Thine all-pure Body and divine Blood, do Thou, O Christ, make me worthy thereof).

[^963]: CS: "И҆ нн҃ѣ .". Rubric appointing the Theotokion.

[^964]: Ode 1, Theotokion: Patristic Marian-Eucharistic typology: Christ as the unplowed Ear of wheat (*кла́съ не ѡ҆ра́нный* / ἄротон στάχυν) brought forth from the untilled soil of the Virgin: "Бл҃гаа бл҃гве́наа невѣ́сто, ꙗ҆́же кла́съ въздрасти́вшїа не ѡ҆ра́нный , и҆ сп҃си́телный мироу . Сподо́би мѧ̀ сеѝ ꙗ҆доу́ща сп҃тисѧ :~" (O good and blessed Bride of God, who hast brought forth the unplowed Ear of grain that is salvation to the world: vouchsafe that I, eating thereof, may be saved).

[^965]: CS: "Пѣ́снь г҃ . І҆рмо́ : На ка́мени мѧ̀ вѣ́ры оу҆твръдѝ .". Rubric introducing Ode 3 and its Heirmos incipit *Ἐν πέτρᾳ με τῆς πίστεως στερεώσας* (CS: "На ка́мени мѧ̀ вѣ́ры оу҆твръдѝ" / "Establish me upon the rock of faith").

[^966]: Ode 3, Troparion 1: Intercalated with the repeated stichos from Ps. 50:12 ("Create in me a clean heart, O God; and renew a right spirit within me"): "Сле́зныѧ ми пода́ждь Х҃е ка́плѧ , сквръ́ноу срⷣчноую ѡ҆чища́ющѧ . ꙗ҆́ко да бл҃го́ю съвѣ́стїю ѡ҆чище́нъ, вѣ́рою прихождоу̀ и҆ стра́хомъ вл҃ко къ [твои̑мъ стра́шнымъ и҆ бж҃твеннымъ да́рѡмъ...]" (Grant me drops of tears, O Christ, purifying the defilement of my heart, that being cleansed with a good conscience, I may come in faith and fear, O Master, unto [Thy dread and divine Gifts...]). Leaf p340 concludes here; the sentence concludes on fol. 162r (leaf p341).

[^967]: Completes Ode 3, Troparion 1 from fol. 161v: "причаще́нїи да́рѡвъ твои́хъ :~" (the communion of Thy Gifts).

[^968]: CS: "ст҃і : Не ѡ҆́връзи менѐ ѿ лица̀ твое́го , и҆ :". Stichos from Ps. 50:13a (LXX; Masoretic Ps. 51:11a) intercalated before Troparion 2: "Cast me not away from Thy presence, and [take not Thy Holy Spirit from me]".

[^969]: Ode 3, Troparion 2: "Въ ѡ҆ставле́нїе да бꙋ́детъ ми прегрѣше́нїи , прчⷭ҇тое твоѐ тѣ́ло , и҆ Бж҃тве́наа кро́вь . Дх҃а же ст҃а́го ѻ҆бще́нїе , и҆ къ жи́знь вѣ́чноую чл҃колю́бче . И҆ ст҃рте́и и҆ скръбе́и ѿчꙋжде́нїе :" (May Thy most pure Body and divine Blood be unto me for the remission of sins, O Lover of mankind, and for communion of the Holy Spirit, and unto life eternal, and for estrangement from passions and afflictions).

[^970]: CS: "Сла́ва .". Rubric appointing the Doxology before Troparion 3.

[^971]: Ode 3, Troparion 3: "Сподо́би на́съ Г҃и твое́го тѣ́ла причⷭ҇ти́тисѧ не ѡ҆сꙋжде́нно , и҆ кро́ве твое́ѧ чⷭ҇тныѧ . И҆ славословити твою̀ бл҃госты́ню :~" (Vouchsafe us, O Lord, to partake without condemnation of Thy Body and of Thy precious Blood, and to hymn Thy goodness).

[^972]: CS: "И҆ нн҃ѣ .". Rubric appointing the Theotokion.

[^973]: Ode 3, Theotokion (opening): Patristic Eucharistic-Marian typology representing the Virgin as the "table of the Bread of life" (*Хлѣ́ба живо́тнаго трапе́за* / ἡ τράπεζα τοῦ ἄρτου τῆς ζωῆς): "Хлѣ́ба живо́тнаго трапе́за прчⷭ҇таа , съвы́ше мл҃ти ра́ди съше́дшаго . И҆ ми́рови но́выи живо́тъ даю́щаго . И҆ менѐ сподо́би нн҃ѣ недосто́инаго , [съ стра́хомъ въкꙋси́ти сегѡ̀, и҆ жи́воу бы́ти :~]". Concludes on fol. 162v.

[^974]: Completes Ode 3, Theotokion from fol. 162r: "съ стра́хомъ въкꙋси́ти сегѡ̀, и҆ жи́воу бы́ти :~" (to taste thereof with fear, and to live).

[^975]: Sessional Hymn (Kathisma / *Сѣда́ленъ*), Tone 2: CS: "Сѣда́лна . гла́съ в҃ . Огнь и҆ свѣ́тъ боу́ди ми сп҃се, прїѧ́тїе прчⷭ҇тыхъ и҆ животворѧ́щихъ твои́хъ та́инъ . пожига́ѧ грѣхо́вныи пле́велъ . и҆ просвѣща́ѧ всего̀ къ и҆сти́нномꙋ Бг҃осло́вїю . не и҆зда́во сты́нѧ вра́жїи лю́ти преда́вшисѧ, ни тебѣ̀ да́мъ цѣлова́нїа ле́стна . но ꙗ҆́ко блꙋ́дница припада́ю ти . и҆ ꙗ҆́ко разбо́иникъ и҆сповѣ́доуѧсѧ въпїю́ ти . помани́ мѧ Г҃и є҆гда̀ прїи́деши въ црⷭ҇твїи сѝ :". Incorporates ancient liturgical echoes of the pre-communion troparion (*Of Thy Mystical Supper...*) and the penitential tears of the harlot (Luke 7:37-38) and the confession of the good thief (Luke 23:42).

[^976]: CS: "Пѣ́снь д҃ . І҆рмо́съ . Пришетвова́въ ѿ дв҃ы .". Rubric introducing Ode 4 and its Heirmos incipit. The physical printed witness exhibits the rare morphological spelling "Пришетвова́въ" (from *прише́ствовати*, parallel to Greek: Ἐλήλυθας ἐκ Παρθένου / "Having journeyed from the Virgin" or standard Church Slavonic *Прише́дъ ѿ Дѣ́вы* / *Прише́лъ є҆сѝ ѿ Дѣ́вы*).

[^977]: CS: "ст҃і : Срⷣце чⷭ҇то съзи́жи въ мнѣ̀ Б҃е .". Stichos from Ps. 50:12 (LXX) intercalated before Troparion 1.

[^978]: Ode 4, Troparion 1 (opening): Allusion to the Paschal Lamb slain for human redemption (cf. Isa. 53:7; John 1:29): "Въсхотѣ́лъ є҆сѝ на́съ ра́ди въпло́щсѧ [мнѡ́гомл҃тве, закла́нъ бы́ти ꙗ҆́ко ѻ҆вча̀ грѣ́хъ ра́ди чл҃ч҄скыхъ...]". Concludes on fol. 163r.

[^979]: Completes Ode 4, Troparion 1 from fol. 162v: "мнѡ́гомл҃тве, закла́нъ бы́ти ꙗ҆́ко ѻ҆вча̀ грѣ́хъ ра́ди чл҃ч҄скыхъ . тѣ́м же молю́ тѧ и҆ моѧ̀ ѻ҆мы́ти прегрѣше́нїа :~".

[^980]: CS: "ст҃ : Не ѡ҆́връзи менѐ ѡ҆ лиц҃ :". Stichos from Ps. 50:13 (LXX) intercalated before Troparion 2. The printed abbreviation reads "ѡ҆ лиц҃" with a titlo.

[^981]: Ode 4, Troparion 2: "И҆сцѣлѝ д҃ша мое́ѧ ра́ны Г҃и , и҆ всего̀ ѡ҆ст҃и . и҆ сподо́би вл҃ко , ꙗ҆́ко да прича́стникъ бꙋ́дꙋ та́иныѧ твое́ѧ и҆ бж҃тве́ныѧ ве́черѧ ѻ҆каѧ́нный .". Note the Early Modern Ruthenian orthographic vocalism "д҃ша мое́ѧ" for standard Church Slavonic *дꙋши́ моея́*.

[^982]: CS: "Сла́ :". Rubric appointing the Doxology before Troparion 3.

[^983]: Ode 4, Troparion 3: "Ста́нѣмъ всѝ съ стра́хомъ и҆ тре́петомъ , ѻ҆́чи срⷣчнѣ́и горѣ̀ и҆моу́ще . и҆ къ сп҃соу въпїю́ще . оу҆твръдѝ и҆ въразоумѝ на́съ Б҃е ще́дрыи въ стра́сѣ твое́мъ :~" (Let us all stand with fear and trembling, having the eyes of our heart directed on high, and crying unto the Savior: Establish and give understanding unto us in Thy fear, O merciful God).

[^986]: Completes Ode 4, Theotokion from fol. 163r: "поро́ка . ꙗ҆́ко да̀ вноу́трь прїе́мъ оу҆́мныи би́серъ ѡ҆сщ҃лю́сѧ :~". The theological metaphor "spiritual Pearl" (*оу҆́мныи би́серъ* / τὸν νοητὸν μαργαρίτην) is an ancient Patristic paten/Eucharist title for the Holy Lamb / Body of Christ (cf. Ephrem the Syrian, John Chrysostom).

[^1022]: CS: "ст҃ : Не ѡ҆́връзи менѐ .". Stichos from Ps. 50:13 (LXX).

[^1023]: Ode 8, Troparion 2: "Къ твое́моу прибѣ́гъ бл҃гооу҆тро́бїю бл҃же , съ стра́хомъ зовꙋ́ ти . въ мнѣ̀ пребꙋ́ди сп҃се . и҆ а҆́зъ ꙗ҆́коже ре́клъ є҆си въ тебѣ̀ . се́ бо надѣ́ѧвсѧ на мл҃ть твою̀ . ꙗ҆́мъ тѣ́ло твоѐ, и҆ пїю̀ кро́вь твою̀ :~". Allusion to John 6:56 and John 15:4.

Concludes on fol. 166v.

[^1030]: CS: "ст҃і : Срⷣце чⷭ҇то съзи́жи въ мнѣ̀ Б҃е . и҆ :". Stichos from Ps. 50:12 (LXX).

Г҃ь на́ ради , по на́съ бо дре́вле бы́въ . є҆ди́ною же себѐ принесъ, ꙗ҆́ко жръ́твꙋ ѻ҆ц҃оу̀ свое́моу . прⷭ҇но закала́етсѧ , ѡ҆сщ҃а́ѧ причаща́ющихсѧ :~".

[^1032]: CS: "сті́хъ . Не ѡ҆́връзи менѐ ѿ лица̀ твое́го, и҆ дх҃ :". Stichos from Ps. 50:13 (LXX) intercalated before Troparion 2.

[^1033]: Ode 9, Troparion 2 (opening): Trinitarian indwelling through Eucharistic Communion (cf. John 14:23): "Д҃ше́ю съ тѣ́лом да ѡ҆сщ҃оу́сѧ вл҃ко, да просвѣщꙋ́сѧ , да сп҃соу́сѧ . да боу́доу до́мъ тво́й , причаще́нїемъ сщ҃енныхъ та́инъ . живоу́щаго тѧ̀ и҆мѣ́ѧ въ себѣ̀ съ ѻ҆ц҃е́мъ и҆ дх҃омъ, [бл҃гтелю мнѡ́гомл҃тиве :~]". Concludes on fol. 167r (leaf p351).

[^1034]: Concluding line of the final regular troparion of Ode 9 of the Canon of Preparation for Holy Communion, continuing across the leaf partition from leaf p350 (*живоу́щаго тѧ̀ и҆мѣ́ѧ въ себѣ̀ съ ѻ҆ц҃е́мъ и҆ дх҃омъ, бл҃годе́телю многомл҃тиве*).

[^1035]: Troparion of Ode 9 under *Glory...*: Patristic Eucharistic motif of the divine Fire and Light consuming sinful matter (*ѻ҆палѧ́ѧ грѣхо́вноую ве́щъ*) and burning the thorns of passions (cf. Heb. 12:29).

[^1036]: Theotokion of Ode 9 under *Both now...*: Incarnation from the pure blood of the Mother of God, presenting Christ as the Sovereign of all made substantial in human nature (Church Slavonic *ѻ҆соу́ществовавшагосѧ чл҃чествомъ*, Greek *οὐσιωθέντα ἀνθρωπότητι*).

[^1037]: Concluding rubric of the canon ordering the recitation of the Axion Estin (*It is truly meet*), the Trisagion Prayers, the Lord's Prayer (*Our Father*), and the preparatory troparion in Tone 8.

[^1038]: The solemn Troparion in Tone 8 (*Е҆гда̀ сла́внїи оу҆ч҃н҃ци*), appointed at Matins of Great and Holy Thursday commemorating the Mystical Supper, prescribed here in the pre-communion cell rule.

[^1039]: Allusion to the betrayal and despairing suicide of Judas Iscariot by hanging (Matt. 27:5), contrasting his avarice with the divine condescension of the Savior.

[^1040]: Monastic and rubrical cell prescription for 40 repetitions of *Lord, have mercy* (*Kyrie eleison*) and 12 metanias/prostrations, adjusted according to the physical capacity of the communicant, prior to the prayers of St. Basil the Great.

[^1041]: First Prayer of St. Basil the Great (*Вл҃ко Г҃и І҆с҃у Х҃е Бж҃е на́шъ*). The opening titles echo 1 Timothy 6:15 and Revelation 19:16 ("King of kings, and Lord of lords").

[^1042]: Physical witness error: the printed text reads *знонра́вныѧ* for *злонра́вныѧ* ("ill-disposed / perverse", Greek *κακογνώμονας*), an uncorrected compositorial ligature slip in the 1606 Balaban imprint.

[^1043]: Scriptural supplication for divine attentive audience: "incline Thine ear unto me, and hear my words" (Psalm 16:6 LXX).

[^1044]: Evangelical confession of the Prodigal Son: "Father, I have sinned against heaven, and before thee" (Luke 15:18, 21).

[^1045]: Direct quotation of the divine oath from Ezekiel 33:11: "As I live, saith the Lord God, I have no pleasure in the death of the wicked; but that the wicked turn from his way and live" (cf. Ezek. 18:23, 32).

[^1046]: Direct citation of the Pauline pastoral declaration of the universal salvific will of God: "Who will have all men to be saved, and to come unto the knowledge of the truth" (1 Timothy 2:4).

[^1047]: The four classical evangelical archetypes of penitence: the sinful woman/harlot who anointed Christ's feet (Luke 7:37-50), the wise thief on the cross (Luke 23:42-43), the repentant publican (Luke 18:13), and the prodigal son (Luke 15:11-32).

[^1048]: The Johannine title of the Lamb of God: "Behold the Lamb of God, which takes away the sin of the world" (John 1:29).

[^1049]: Christ's twin evangelical invitations to repentant humanity: Matthew 11:28 ("Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest") and Matthew 9:13 ("I am not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance").

[^1050]: Scriptural citation of 2 Corinthians 7:1: "let us cleanse ourselves from all filthiness of the flesh and spirit, perfecting holiness in the fear of God."

[^1051]: Patristic and liturgical designation of Holy Communion as *ephodion* / *viaticum* (*въ напоу́тїе живота̀ вѣ́чнаго*, Greek *εἰς ἐφόδιον ζωῆς αἰωνίου*), provision for the soul's journey into eternal life.

[^1052]: Doxological conclusion complying with the Father Paul Doxology Standard ("unto ages of ages", rendering Church Slavonic *въ вѣ́кы а҆ми́нь*).

[^1053]: Rubric heading ascribing the second pre-communion prayer to St. Basil the Great (*ТОГО́ЖЕ ВЕЛИ́КАГО ВАСИ́ЛЇА*), preserving the classical 16th-17th century Ruthenian Euchologion sequence.

[^1054]: Theological opening of the Second Prayer of St. Basil, meditating on Christ's self-oblation to restore the divine likeness and conform humanity to His image (cf. Romans 8:29).

[^1055]: Direct quotation of Psalm 29:2, 4 LXX (Psalm 30:1, 3 MT): "I will extol thee, O Lord; for thou hast lifted me up, and hast not made my foes to rejoice over me... O Lord, thou hast brought up my soul from the grave: thou hast kept me alive, that I should not go down to the pit."

[^1056]: Traditional Byzantine Eucharistic petition derived from the Divine Liturgy anaphora and post-communion thanksgiving, requesting remission of sins and communion of the Holy Spirit.

[^1057]: Scriptural citation of King David's penitential confession in Psalm 50:6 LXX (Psalm 51:4 MT): "Against thee, thee only, have I sinned, and done this evil in thy sight."

[^1058]: Reiteration of the evangelical models of repentance, invoking Christ's divine authority on earth to forgive sins (cf. Matthew 9:6).

[^1059]: Patristic and Byzantine Eucharistic typology of the burning coal (*оу҆́гле*) that purified the lips of the Prophet Isaiah (Isaiah 6:6-7), here applied to the life-giving Body of Christ, continuing across the leaf transition onto leaf p361 (*серафі́ма*).

[^1060]: Eucharistic typology of the burning coal (*оу҆́гле*) and the seraph continuing from leaf p360 (*стра́шнаго ра́ди твое́го серафі́ма*), evoking the prophetic vision of Isaiah 6:6-7, in which a seraph purifies the prophet's lips with a live coal taken with tongs from the celestial altar, applied patristically to the vivifying Body of Christ.

[^1061]: Pauline petition for bodily mortification and spiritual renewal, alluding to Colossians 3:5 ("Mortify therefore your members which are upon the earth") and Galatians 5:16, effected through the divine descent (*наи́тїемъ*, Greek *ἐπιφοιτήσει*) of the Holy Spirit.

[^1062]: Evangelical meditation on the divine indwelling and mutual abiding of the Holy Trinity within the faithful believer, quoting Christ's promise in John 14:23: "If a man love me, he will keep my words: and my Father will love him, and we will come unto him, and make our abode with him."

[^1063]: Textual witness note on Church Slavonic *пи́ꙋменнѣ*: an apparent typographical ligature slip or vernacular Ruthenian compositorial form for *прїе́мнѣ* (*приємнѣ*, "acceptably / graciously / pleasingly") or *поиме́ннѣ* ("specifically / essentially"), paired with *неразлꙋ́чнѣ* ("inseparably", Greek *ἀχωρίστως*).

[^1064]: Patristic Eucharistic invocation addressing the consubstantial Word of God as the supreme protector and quencher of passionate desire (*наи́же въ мнѣ̀ всѧ́ко жела́нїе оу҆томи́тель*), reflecting Early Modern Ruthenian superlative syntax (*най-* + *-же*), and petitioning Christ to be all things unto His servant (cf. 1 Cor. 9:22, Col. 3:11).

[^1065]: High Priestly Prayer allusion: "unite Thyself unto me in one spirit" (1 Cor. 6:17) according to Christ's supplication unto the Father that the disciples may be one, even as the Father and the Son are one (John 17:21-23).

[^1066]: Pauline baptismal typology: "flesh of Thy flesh" (Ephesians 5:30; Genesis 2:23) and "bearing Thee from divine Baptism" (Galatians 3:27: "For as many of you as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ").

[^1067]: Penitential confession acknowledging the defilement of the white baptismal garment of incorruption through post-baptismal sin (cf. Revelation 3:4; 16:15).

[^1068]: Direct quotation of Christ's Eucharistic discourse in John 6:56: "He that eats my flesh, and drinks my blood, dwells in me, and I in him."

[^1069]: Liturgical rubric in red cinnabar ink introducing the third pre-communion prayer attributed to St. Basil the Great (*ТОГО́ЖЕ ВАСИ́ЛЇА ВЕЛИ́КАГО МЛ҃ТВА, къ ст҃о́му причаще́нїю*).

[^1070]: Christological confession of the unconfused Incarnation: Christ receiving human nature—the creation of His own holy hands—subjected to passions through the Fall, yet without sin (Hebrews 4:15), and cleansing it with His precious Blood.

[^1071]: Meditation on the gratuitous divine economy of redemption, accomplished not for the righteous or those well-pleasing to God, but on behalf of sinners who had provoked Him to anger (Romans 5:8, 10).

[^1072]: Patristic Eucharistic title of Christ as the singular hope of salvation for those driven to despair by the magnitude of their transgressions (cf. 1 Timothy 1:15).

[^1073]: Direct quotation of Christ's medical-salvific aphorism in Matthew 9:12 / Mark 2:17 / Luke 5:31: "They that are whole need not a physician, but they that are sick."

[^1074]: Direct quotation of Christ's evangelical mission in Luke 19:10 and Matthew 18:11: "For the Son of man is come to seek and to save that which was lost."

[^1075]: Liturgical expression of Eucharistic fear and trembling: the communicant daring to approach the awesome Mysteries solely by relying on divine compassions (*щедрота́мъ*), entreating Christ to endure (*оу҆тръпѝ*) his unworthiness.

[^1076]: Liturgical supplication begging Christ not to abhor the sinner, nor to set him forth as guilty at the dread tribunal, despite drawing near in unworthiness (cf. 1 Corinthians 11:27).

[^1077]: Lexical note: Church Slavonic *любодѣ́йне* (*любодѣтельный* / Greek *φιλάγαθε* or *εὐεργέτα*), signifying the Lord as the bountiful Lover and Doer of good, granting His Body and Blood for the remission of sins.

[^1078]: Multi-fold Eucharistic petition: communion for the lightening of the crushing weight of iniquities, release from judicial guilt (*вины̀*), and the sanctification and cleansing of both soul and body.

[^1079]: Theological meditation on the shedding of Christ's divine and life-flowing Blood on the Cross on behalf of condemned sinners who are left without defense (*ѻ҆без̾ѿвѣ́тныхъ*).

[^1080]: Scriptural echo of 1 Corinthians 11:29: warning against partaking unto condemnation (*въ ѻ҆сꙋжде́нїе*) or a heavier defense/reckoning (*въ тѧжча́йшїи ѿвѣ́тъ*) instead of receiving the remission of sins.

[^1081]: Pauline liturgical disposition: approaching the dread Mysteries "with fear and trembling" (Philippians 2:12; Psalm 2:11 LXX), conscious of God's all-seeing omniscience (*всѧ̂ вѣ́дый*).

[^1082]: Epigraphic witness: Church Slavonic *съ здрога́нїемъ срⷣца, и҆ кості́и и҆са́мыхъ мѡ́зговъ* reflects Early Modern Ruthenian *здрогання* (shivering, trembling, shuddering; Polish *zadrżenie*), coupled with the Biblical motif of marrow and bones trembling before the divine Majesty (cf. Job 4:14; Hebrews 4:12).

[^1083]: Liturgical humility before the mystical table of the Eucharist, deemed too awesome even to behold with bodily eyes (cf. the prayer of the Cherubic Hymn in the Divine Liturgy).

[^1084]: Patristic Eucharistic metaphor of casting oneself into the boundless sea or abyss (*поучи́ноу*, Greek *πέλαγος*) of divine mercy (cf. Psalm 35:7 LXX [Psalm 36:6 MT]).

[^1085]: The dual emotional polarity of Byzantine Eucharistic reception: holy fear (*стра́хомъ*) at personal unworthiness, balanced by spiritual joy (*ра́достїю*) at the evangelical promise of forgiveness.

[^1086]: Scriptural citation of Psalm 24:18 LXX (Psalm 25:18 MT): "Look upon mine affliction [humility/lowliness] and my pain; and forgive all my sins."

[^1087]: Concluding petition of the third prayer of St. Basil, beseeching the eternal inheritance prepared for them that love God (1 Cor. 2:9) through the intercessions of the all-pure Theotokos and all the saints.

[^1088]: Rubric in red cinnabar ink heading the classical pre-communion prayer of St. John Chrysostom (*И҆́ЖЕ ВЪ СТ҃Ы́ХЪ ѼЦ҃А НА́ШЕГО І҆ѠА́ННА ЗЛАТООУ́СТАГО МЛ҃ТВА, КЪ СТ҃О́МУ ПРИЧАЩЕ́НЇЮ*).

[^1089]: Direct quotation and liturgical adaptation of the Centurion's evangelical confession of unworthiness: "Lord, I am not worthy that thou shouldest come under my roof" (Matthew 8:8; Luke 7:6), comparing the sinner's soul to a derelict and collapsed dwelling.

[^1090]: Evangelical allusion to Christ's earthly homelessness in Matthew 8:20 and Luke 9:58: "the Son of man hath not where to lay his head."

[^1091]: Meditation on the Kenosis of the Son of God, Who descended from heavenly glory to humble Himself for the salvation of mankind (Philippians 2:6-8).

[^1092]: Nativity typology: Christ's condescension to be born in a cave and laid in a manger of irrational beasts (Luke 2:7), taken as the paradigm for His entrance into the communicant's soul.

[^1093]: The Chrysostomic Eucharistic parallel: entreating Christ to enter the manger of an unreasoning soul (*безслове́сныѧ дш҃а*) and a defiled body, just as He lay in the Bethlehem crib.

[^1094]: Evangelical narrative of Christ dining in Bethany in the house of Simon the leper (Matthew 26:6; Mark 14:3), showing His willingness to associate with the outcast and ritually unclean.

[^1095]: Spiritual transference of Simon's physical leprosy to the spiritual leprosy of sin that infects the soul of the communicant.

[^1096]: Evangelical account of the penitent woman with the alabaster box who washed Christ's feet with her tears and wiped them with the hairs of her head (Luke 7:37-38).

[^1097]: Evangelical motif of the harlot kissing Christ's feet (Luke 7:38, 45), continuing across the leaf transition onto leaf p371 (*не въз̾гноуша́исѧ скврънѣ́йшихъ ѡ҆ноѧ оу҆́стъ...*), beseeching the Lord not to abhor the unclean lips and tongue of the communicant.

[^1098]: Penitential Eucharistic confession continuing from leaf p370 (*не въз̾гноуша́исѧ скврънѣ́йшихъ ѡ҆ноѧ оу҆́стъ и҆ нечистѣ́йшиⷯ*), in which the communicant entreats Christ not to abhor lips even more defiled and polluted than those of the penitent harlot in Luke 7:38, 45, who kissed the Savior's feet.

[^1099]: Patristic Eucharistic typology of the live burning coal (*оу҆́гль*) of Christ's Body and Blood, recalling Isaiah 6:6-7, wherein the seraphic coal purifies the prophet's lips, here applied to the reception of the Mysteries for sanctification, spiritual illumination, and bodily and spiritual health.

[^1100]: Multifold liturgical petitions beseeching deliverance from diabolical operations (*дїавольскыхъ дѣ́йствъ*), the overcoming and restraint of wicked personal habits, the mortification of passions (*оу҆мръщвле́нїе страсте́й*), and the preservation of the divine commandments.

[^1101]: Classical Byzantine Eucharistic metaphor of the spiritual or noetic wolf (*мы́сльнаго влъ́ка*, Greek *νοητοῦ λύκου*), designating the devil who preys upon and devours the sheep of Christ that remain too long estranged or distanced from the vivifying nourishment of Holy Communion (cf. John 10:12).

[^1102]: Comprehensive supplication for the total renewal and hallowing of the human person: soul, body, mind, heart, reins, and inward parts (*дш҃ю и҆ тѣ́ло, оу҆́мъ и҆ срⷣце, чревеса̀ и҆ оу҆тро́бꙋ*), entreating that the fear of God be deeply rooted in every bodily member and that divine sanctification remain irremovable.

[^1103]: Pastoral petition for divine guidance and governance (*ѻ҆крꙋмлѧ́ѧ*, "steering / directing", Greek *κυβερνῶν*) in peace, and for standing at the right hand of Christ among the sheep at the Last Judgment (Matthew 25:33).

[^1104]: Doxological conclusion of the prayer of St. John Chrysostom, invoking the intercessions of the all-pure Theotokos, the bodiless angelic ministers and celestial powers, and all the saints well-pleasing unto God from all ages.

[^1105]: Rubric in red cinnabar ink introducing another pre-communion prayer attributed to St. John Chrysostom (*ТОГО́ЖЕ СТ҃ГО І҆ѠА́ННА ЗЛАТООУ́СТАГѠ МЛ҃ТВА КЪ СТ҃ОМОУ ПРИЧАЩЕ́НЇЮ*).

[^1106]: Direct evangelical allusion to the Parable of the Sheep and the Goats in Matthew 25:32-33, pleading that Christ not place the communicant on His left hand (*ѡ҆шоую́ю*) among the goats that have provoked Him to anger.

[^1107]: Direct evangelical quotation of the dreadful sentence of rejection in Matthew 25:12 and Luke 13:25, 27: pleading that Christ not say unto the communicant: "Amen, I say unto thee, I know thee not."

[^1108]: Ascetic supplication for the foundational preparatory virtues of Byzantine liturgical life: perpetual weeping (*пла́чь кѻегда̀*), heart compunction (*оу҆миле́нїе*), humility, and purification through the fear of God.

[^1109]: Patristic vision of the communicant's heart becoming a consecrated temple and dwelling of divine goodness through participation in the pure and life-creating Mysteries (cf. 1 Corinthians 3:16-17; 6:19).

[^1110]: Evangelical confession of persistent faith despite spiritual sloth and despondency, perpetually knocking at the doors of divine mercy (Matthew 7:7-8; Luke 11:9-10) and clinging to the path of Christ.

[^1111]: Scriptural praise echoing Psalm 144:9 LXX (Psalm 145:9 MT): "The Lord is good to all: and his tender mercies are over all his works," concluding with an ascription of eternal dominion unto God.

[^1112]: Rubric in red cinnabar ink heading the prayer of St. John Chrysostom for the remission of sins (*ТОГО́ СТ҃Ѣ́ЙШАГО І҆ѠА́ННА ЗЛАТООУ́СТАГО, МО: КЪ СТ҃О́Мꙋ ПРИЧАЩЕ́НЇЮ*).

[^1113]: Christological confession acknowledging Christ as the singular Lord possessing divine authority to remit human transgressions (Matthew 9:6; Mark 2:10; Luke 5:24).

[^1114]: Classical liturgical supplication for the remission of sins committed in knowledge and in ignorance (*ꙗ҆́же въ вѣ́дѣнїи и҆ невѣ́дѣнїи съгрѣше́ннаѧ*), entreating reception of the Holy Mysteries without condemnation (1 Cor. 11:29).

[^1115]: Patristic Eucharistic fruits: communion received not unto heaviness or punishment (*не въ та́жесть ни въ моу́кꙋ*), but for the pledge and betrothal of the life and Kingdom to come (*въ ѡ҆броуче́нїе бꙋ́доущаго живота̀ и҆ цр҃твїа*, Greek *εἰς ἀρраβῶνα*).

[^1116]: Spiritual imagery of the Holy Eucharist as a protective wall and fortress (*въ стѣ́ноу и҆ по́мощъ*, Greek *τεῖχος*) against demonic adversaries and for the obliteration of transgressions.

[^1117]: Trinitarian doxology concluding the fifth prayer of St. John Chrysostom, sending up glory to the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit.

[^1118]: Rubric in red cinnabar ink introducing the sixth pre-communion prayer of St. John Chrysostom (*ТОГО́ЖЕ СТ҃ГО І҆ѠА́ННА ЗЛАТООУ́СТАГО • МЛ҃ТВА КЪ СТ҃О́МОУ ПРИЧАЩЕ́НЇЮ*).

[^1119]: Direct Pauline citation and penitential confession from 1 Corinthians 11:27, 29: acknowledging personal guilt and eating and drinking judgment unto oneself by failing to discern the Body and Blood of Christ.

[^1120]: Direct quotation of Christ's Eucharistic discourse in John 6:56: "He that eats my flesh, and drinks my blood, dwells in me, and I in him."

[^1121]: Liturgical supplication begging divine mercy rather than judicial rebuke and exposure (*не ѡ҆бличѝ менѐ грѣ́шнаго*, cf. Psalm 6:2 LXX / Psalm 37:2 LXX).

[^1122]: Multi-fold Eucharistic petition: Holy Communion received for enlightenment, salvation, healing, preservation, cleansing, and sanctification of both soul and body.

[^1123]: Ascetic prayer for deliverance from demonic delusions, fantasies, and deceitful operations (*всѧ́каго мечта́нїа, и҆ лоука́ваго дѣѧ́нїа, и҆ дѣ́йства дїа́вольска*) acting mentally within the bodily senses.

[^1124]: Spiritual fruits of Holy Communion: holy boldness and love toward God, amendment and strength of life, growth in virtue, fulfillment of the commandments, fellowship of the Holy Spirit, the viaticum of eternal life (*въ напоу́тїе живота̀ вѣ́чнаго*, Greek *εἰς ἐφόδιον ζωῆς αἰωνίου*), and a good defense before the dread judgment-seat of Christ.

[^1125]: Rubric in red cinnabar ink heading the seventh pre-communion prayer of St. John Chrysostom (*ТОГО́ЖЕ СТ҃И́ТЕЛѦ І҆ѠА́ННА ЗЛАТООУ́СТАГО, МЛ҃ТВА КЪ СТ҃О́МОУ ПРИЧАЩЕ́НЇЮ*).

[^1126]: Classical penitential formula of remission (*Бж҃е ѻ҆сла́би ѡ҆ста́ви, оу҆щедрѝ*): entreating God to remit, pardon, have compassion, and forgive sins committed in word, deed, or thought, voluntarily or involuntarily, knowingly or in ignorance.

[^1127]: Intercessory supplication invoking the Theotokos, the noetic angelic ministers (*оу҆́мныхъ ти слꙋжи́телей*), and all the saints well-pleasing to God throughout the ages.

[^1128]: Petition for the uncondemned reception of the Holy Body and Precious Blood of Christ, unto the healing of soul and body and the cleansing of wicked thoughts.

[^1129]: Classical liturgical doxology attributing the Kingdom, power, and glory to the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit (cf. Matthew 6:13).

[^1130]: Rubric in red cinnabar ink introducing the pre-communion prayer and confession of faith of St. John Chrysostom (*ТОГО́ЖЕ СТ҃ГО І҆ѠА́ННА ЗЛАТООУ́СТАГО МЛ҃ТВА, КЪ СТ҃ОМОУ ПРИЧАЩЕ́НЇЮ*).

[^1131]: The classical Byzantine pre-communion confession: combining the evangelical confession of St. Peter in Matthew 16:16 ("Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God") with St. Paul's confession of personal unworthiness in 1 Timothy 1:15 ("Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners; of whom I am chief").

[^1132]: Dogmatic affirmation of the Real Presence: confessing with unwavering faith that the consecrated Gifts are in truth Christ's very own most pure Body and very own precious Blood.

[^1133]: Penitential supplication for mercy and remission of all voluntary and involuntary offenses, committed in word or deed, in knowledge or ignorance, in intellect or thought.

[^1134]: Continuation of the pre-communion confession onto leaf p380, beseeching partaking of the pure Mysteries unto the remission of sins and unto life everlasting.

[^1135]: Rubric in red cinnabar ink heading the concluding short pre-communion prayer of St. John Chrysostom (*ТОГО́ЖЕ СТ҃ГО І҆ѠА́ННА ЗЛАТООУ́СТАГО • МЛ҃ТВА • КЪ СТ҃МОУ ПРИЧАЩЕ́НЇЮ*).

[^1136]: Concise Eucharistic petition pleading that communion not be unto condemnation, but rather grant cleansing, sanctification, and attainment of the life to come and of the Kingdom.
