[^1473]: St. Theophanes the Branded, Funeral Canon, Tone 6, Ode 3, Troparion 1 (*Зако́нно пострада́вше...*). Greek: Νομίμως ἀθλήσαντες οἱ σοὶ Μάρτυρες, Ζωοδότα, καὶ τῷ στεφάνῳ τῆς νίκης κοσμησάμενοι, τῷ μεταστάντι πιστῷ, αἰωνίαν πρεσβεύουσι λύτρωσιν. Reference to 2 Timothy 2:5. Acrostic letter 5: προσᾴδω / припѣва́ю.

[^1474]: St. Theophanes the Branded, Funeral Canon, Tone 6, Ode 3, Troparion 2 (*Наказа́въ пре́жде мнѡ́гыми чудесы̀...*). Greek: Παιδεύσας πρότερον πολλοῖς θαύμασι, καὶ σημείοις, ἐμὲ τὸν πλανηθέντα, ἐπ' ἐσχάτων ἑαυτὸν κενώσας ὡς εὔσπλαγχνος, καὶ ζητήσας εὗρες καὶ διέσωσας. Kenotic theology of Philippians 2:7 (*ἑαυτὸν ἐκένωσε*) and the Good Shepherd seeking the lost sheep (Luke 15:4–7). Acrostic letter 6: προσᾴδω / припѣва́ю.

[^1475]: St. Theophanes the Branded, Funeral Canon, Tone 6, Ode 3, Troparion 3 (*Текоу́щихъ непостоꙗ́нную тлю̀...*). Greek: Ῥεόντων ἄстаτον φθοράν, ἐκφυγόντα πρὸς σὲ τὸν προσελθόντα, ἐν σκηνώσεσιν αἰωνίοις οἰκεῖν ἀγαλλόμενον, ἀξίωσον Ἀγαθέ, δικαιώσας πίστει καὶ χάριτι. Paulinist doctrine of justification by faith and grace (Romans 3:24, 5:1). Acrostic letter 7: προσᾴδω / припѣва́ю.

[^1476]: St. Theophanes the Branded, Funeral Canon, Tone 6, Ode 3, Theotokion (*Нѣ́сть непоро́чнаѧ ꙗ҆́коже ты...*). Greek: Οὐκ ἔστιν ἄмеμπτος ὡς σύ, πανάχραντε Θεομῆτορ· μόνη γὰρ ἐξ αἰῶνος, τὸν ἀληθινὸν Θεὸν ἔσχες ἐν γαστρί, τὸν θανάτου διαλύσαντα τὴν ἰσχύν. Acrostic letter 8: προσᾴδω / припѣва́ю.

[^1477]: The Little Litany for the Departed with its exclamation (*Ꙗ҆́ко ты̀ є҆сѝ въскр҃енїе...*), referred back to the earlier rubrical occurrence (*ꙗ҆́коже назáдѣ* / 'as before', on fol. 239r, p. 495).

[^1478]: Sessional Hymn (Kathisma), Tone 6 (*Въи́стинноу соуета̀ всѧ́ческаѧ...*). Greek: Ὄντως ματαιότης τὰ σύμπαντα, ὁ δὲ βίος σκιὰ καὶ ἐνύпνιον· καὶ γὰρ μάτην ταράττεται πᾶς γηγενής, ὡς εἶπεν ἡ Γραφή· ὅτε τὸν κόσμον κερδήσωμεν, τότε τῷ τάφῳ οἰκήσωμεν, ὅπου ὁμοῦ βασιλεῖς καὶ πτωχοί. Combining LXX Psalm 38:6–7 (MT 39:5–6), Matthew 16:26, and James 4:14.

[^1479]: Sessional Theotokion (*Мт҃рь свѣ́та прчⷭтꙋю Бцⷣꙋ...*). Greek: Τὴν ὑπέρτιμον τοῦ Θεοῦ ἡμῶν Μητέρα / Μητέρα φωτὸς τὴν παναγνόν.

[^1480]: Ode 4 Heirmos, Tone 6: *Х҃с моѧ̀ си́ла Бг҃ъ и҆ Г͠ь* (Greek: Χριστός μου δύναμις, Θεὸς καὶ Κύριος). Based on the Canticle of Habakkuk, Habakkuk 3:2–19.

[^1481]: St. Theophanes the Branded, Funeral Canon, Tone 6, Ode 4, Troparion 1 (*Премоу́дрости бо́лшаѧ ꙗ҆влѧ́ѧ зна́менїе...*). Greek: Σοφίας πλείονος, δεικνὺς τεκμήριον, καὶ τῆς περὶ τὰ δῶρα πολυτελοῦς, Δέσпота χρηστότητος, τοὺς τῶν Μαρτύρων χορούς, τοῖς Ἀγγέλοις συνέταξας. Acrostic letter 9: προσᾴδω / припѣва́ю.

[^1482]: St. Theophanes the Branded, Funeral Canon, Tone 6, Ode 4, Troparion 2 (*Пречⷭтыѧ сла́вы твоеѧ̀ оу҆лоучи́ти сподо́би...*). Greek: Ἀχράντου δόξης σου, τυχεῖν ἀξίωσον, τὸν μεταστάντα πρὸς σέ, ὅπου Χριστὲ τῶν εὐφραινομένων ἡ κατοικία, καὶ φωνὴ καθαρᾶς ἀγαλλιάσεως. Acrostic letter 10: προσᾴδω / припѣва́ю.

[^1483]: St. Theophanes the Branded, Funeral Canon, Tone 6, Ode 4, Troparion 3 (*Пою́щаго прїимѝ Бж҃твеноу́ю дрьжа́вꙋ твою̀...*). Greek: Ὑμνοῦντα πρόσδεξαι, τὸ θεῖον κράτος σου, ὃν προσελάβου ἐκ γῆς, τέκνον φωτὸς τοῦτον ἀπεργαζόμενος, τὴν ἁμαρτίας ἀχλὺν ἐκκαθαίρων, Πολυέλεε. Reference to Ephesians 5:8. Acrostic letter 11: προσᾴδω / припѣва́ю.

[^1484]: St. Theophanes the Branded, Funeral Canon, Tone 6, Ode 4, Theotokion (*Прїѧ́телище прчⷭтое, хра́мъ пренепоро́чный...*). Greek: Δοχεῖον ἄχραντον, ναὸν πανάμωμον, κιβωτὸν πανάγιον, παρθενικὸν τόπον ἁγιάσματος, σὲ τὴν ὡραιότητα Ἰακώβ, ὁ Δεσπότης ἐξελέξατο. Reference to LXX Psalm 46:5 (MT 47:4: 'The beauty of Jacob which He loved'). Acrostic letter 12: προσᾴδω / припѣва́ю.

[^1485]: Ode 5 Heirmos, Tone 6: *Бж҃твенымъ свѣ́томъ твои́мъ бл҃же* (Greek: Τῷ θείῳ φέγγει σου, Ἀγαθέ). Based on the Canticle of Isaiah, Isaiah 26:9.

[^1486]: St. Theophanes the Branded, Funeral Canon, Tone 6, Ode 5, Troparion 1 (*Ꙗ҆́ко всепло́дїе сщ҃е́нно...*). Greek: Ὁλοκαύτωμα ἱερόν, καὶ ὡς ἀπαρχὴ τῆς βροτείας φύσεως, οἱ Ἀθλοφόροι τῷ δεδοξασμένῳ, προσενεχθέντες Θεῷ, ἡμῖν τὴν σωτηρίαν ἀεὶ βραβεύουσι. Acrostic letter 13: τοῖς / ѡ҆ше́дшимъ.

[^1487]: St. Theophanes the Branded, Funeral Canon, Tone 6, Ode 5, Troparion 2 (*Нб҃наго житїа̀, и҆ раздаа́нїа да́рѡвъ...*). Greek: Οὐρανίου διαγωγῆς, καὶ διανομῆς τῶν χαρισμάτων, ἀξίωσον Κύριε, τὸν προκοιμηθέντα πιστὸν δοῦλόν σου, παρέχων ὀφλημάτων τὴν ἀπολύτρωσιν. Acrostic letter 14: τοῖς / ѡ҆ше́дшимъ.

[^1488]: St. Theophanes the Branded, Funeral Canon, Tone 6, Ode 5, Troparion 3 (*И҆́же є҆ди́ныи є҆ст̀вомъ животво́рецъ...*). Greek: Ὁ μόνος φύσει ζωοποιός, τῆς ἀγαθότητος ὄντως ἀνεξιχνίαστον πέлаγος, τὸν τελευτήσαντα, τῆς βασιλείας σου ἀξίωσον Οἰκτίρμον, μόνε Ἀθάνατε. Acrostic letter 15: τοῖς / ѡ҆ше́дшимъ.

[^1489]: St. Theophanes the Branded, Funeral Canon, Tone 6, Ode 5, Theotokion (*Крѣ́пость и҆ пѣ́нїе и҆з̾ те́бе вл҃чце...*). Greek: Ἰσχὺς καὶ ὕμνησις ἡμῶν, ἐκ σοῦ Δέσποινα τῷ κόσμῳ γεννηθείς, καὶ σωτηρία ἐγένετο τοῖς ἀπολλυμένοις, τῶν ᾅδου πυλῶν ῥυόμενος τοὺς πίστει μακαρίζοντάς σε. Reference to LXX Psalm 117:14 and Exodus 15:2.

[^1490]: Ode 6 Heirmos, Tone 6: *Жите́йскаго мо́рѧ воздвиза́емое зрѧ̀ напа́стей бу́рею* (Greek: Τοῦ βίου τὴν θάλασσαν, ὑψουμένην καθορῶν). Based on the Canticle of Jonah, Jonah 2:1–10.

[^1491]: St. Theophanes the Branded, Funeral Canon, Tone 6, Ode 6, Troparion 1 (*На крⷭтѣ̀ пригвожда́емь...*). Greek: Σταυρῷ προσηλούμενος, τοὺς τῶν Μαρτύρων δήμους πρὸς σὲ συνήγαγες, μιμουμένους τὸ πάθος σου, Ἀγαθέ· διὸ δυσωпоῦμέν σε, τὸν μεταστάντα πρὸς σὲ νῦν ἀνάπαυσον. Acrostic letter 16: θανοῦσι / ѡ҆ше́дшимъ.

[^1492]: St. Theophanes the Branded, Funeral Canon, Tone 6, Ode 6, Troparion 2 (*Неизрече́нною сла́вою свое́ю...*). Greek: Ἀρρήτῳ τῇ δόξῃ σου, ὅταν ἔλθῃς φοβερὸς κρῖναι τὸν κόσμον ἅπαντα, ἐν νεφέλαις εὐδόκησον, Λυτρωτά, φαιδρῶς ὑπαντῆσαί σοι, ὃν προσελάβου ἐκ γῆς πιστὸν δοῦλόν σου. Reference to 1 Thessalonians 4:17. Acrostic letter 17: θανοῦσι / ѡ҆ше́дшимъ.

[^1493]: St. Theophanes the Branded, Funeral Canon, Tone 6, Ode 6, Troparion 3 (*Исто́чникъ жи́зни сы́й...*). Greek: Πηγὴ ζωῆς ὑπάρχων / Νεκρῶν τε καὶ ζώντων... Acrostic letter 18: θανοῦσι / ѡ҆ше́дшимъ.

[^1494]: St. Theophanes the Branded, Funeral Canon, Tone 6, Ode 6, Theotokion (*Въ зе́млю възврати́хомсѧ...*). Greek: Οἱ εἰς γῆν ὑпоστρέψαντες, παραβάντες Θεοῦ τὴν θείαν ἐντολήν, διὰ σοῦ Παρθένε εἰς οὐρανόν, ἐκ γῆς ἀνυψώθημεν, φθορὰν τοῦ θανάτου ἀποσεισάμενοι. Typological contrast with the curse of Genesis 3:19. Acrostic letter 19: θανοῦσι / ѡ҆ше́дшимъ.

[^1495]: The Little Litany for the Departed with the exclamation (*Ꙗ҆́ко ты̀ є҆сѝ въскр҃енїе...*), introducing the Kontakion and Ikos.

[^1496]: The Kontakion of the Departed, Tone 8 (*Съ ст҃ыми оу҆поко́й Х҃е...*). Greek: Μετὰ τῶν Ἁγίων ἀνάπαυσον, Χριστέ, τὰς ψυχὰς τῶν δούλων σου, ἔνθα οὐκ ἔστι πόνος, οὐ λύπη, οὐ στεναγμός, ἀλλὰ ζωὴ ἀτελεύτητος.

[^1497]: The Ikos of the Departed, Tone 8 (*Ты са́мъ є҆сѝ безмр҃тне...*), attributed to St. Romanos the Melodist. Greek: Αὐτὸς μόνος εἶ ὁ ἀθάνατος, ὁ ποιήσας καὶ πλάσας τὸν ἄνθρωπον· οἱ βροτοὶ οὖν ἐκ γῆς διεπλάσθημεν, καὶ εἰς γῆν τὴν αὐτὴν πορευσόμεθα, καθὼς ἐκέλευσας ὁ πλάσας με, καὶ εἰπών μοι· Ὅτι γῆ εἶ καὶ εἰς γῆν ἀπελεύσῃ· ὅπου πάντες βροτοὶ πορευσόμεθα, ἐπιτάφιον θρῆνον ποιοῦντες ᾠδήν, τὸ Ἀλληλούϊα. Quoting Genesis 3:19.

[^1498]: Repetition of the Kontakion incipit following the Ikos (*Съ ст҃ыми оу҆поко́й Х҃е*).

[^1499]: Ode 7 Heirmos, Tone 6: *Росода́тельну у́бо пе́щь содѣ́ла а́нгелъ* (Greek: Δροσοβόλον μὲν τὴν κάμινον εἰργάσατο Ἄγγελος). Based on the Song of the Three Holy Youths, Daniel 3.

[^1500]: St. Theophanes the Branded, Funeral Canon, Tone 6, Ode 7, Troparion 1 (*И҆зба́вльшесѧ твое́ю кро́вїю мч҃ници...*). Greek: Λυτρωθέντες τῷ σῷ αἵματι Μάρτυρες, τοῦ πρῴην πταίσματος, ῥαντισθέντες δὲ τῷ ἰδίῳ αἵματι, τὴν σὴν σαφῶς προτυποῦσι σφαγήν· Εὐλογητὸς εἶ ὁ Θεός, ὁ τῶν Πατέρων ἡμῶν. Acrostic letter 20: θανοῦσι / ѡ҆ше́дшимъ.

[^1501]: St. Theophanes the Branded, Funeral Canon, Tone 6, Ode 7, Troparion 2 (*Сверѣпѣ́ющоую съме́рть оу҆мр҃тви́лъ є҆си...*). Greek: Σκληρὸν θάνατον νεκρώσας, Λόγε ζωαρχικώτατε, τὸν ἐν πίστει κοιμηθέντα πρόσδεξαι, ὑμνοῦντα καὶ λέγοντα, Χριστέ· Εὐλογητὸς εἶ ὁ Θεός, ὁ τῶν Πατέρων ἡμῶν. Acrostic letter 21: θανοῦσι / ѡ҆ше́дшимъ.

[^1502]: St. Theophanes the Branded, Funeral Canon, Tone 6, Ode 7, Troparion 3 (*Въздхи́въ мѧ̀ чл҃ка, въздхонове́нїемъ Бж҃твенымъ...*). Greek: Ἐμπνεύσας μοι τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ, θείᾳ ἐπιπνοίᾳ Θεαρχικώτατε, τὸν μεταστάντα τῆς βασιλείας σου, ἀξίωσον ψάλλειν σοι, Σωτήρ· Εὐλογητὸς εἶ ὁ Θεός, ὁ τῶν Πατέρων ἡμῶν. Direct reference to Genesis 2:7. Acrostic letter 22: θανοῦσι / ѡ҆ше́дшимъ.

[^1503]: St. Theophanes the Branded, Funeral Canon, Tone 6, Ode 7, Theotokion (*Превы́шши въсѣ́хъ тва́реи пренепоро́чнаѧ бы́сть...*). Greek: Ὑψηλοτέρα πάσης κτίσεως, Πανάμωμε γέγονας, συλλαβοῦσα Θεόν, τὸν συντρίψαντα θανάτου πύλας, καὶ μοχλοὺς συνθλάσαντα· διὸ σὲ Ἁγνή, ὑμνολογοῦμεν οἱ πιστοὶ ὡς Θεομήτορα. Acrostic letter 23: μελῳδίαν / пѣ́снь.

[^1504]: Ode 8 Heirmos, Tone 6: *Изъ пла́мене преподо́бнымъ ро́су источи́лъ есѝ* (Greek: Ἐκ φλογὸς τοῖς Ὁσίοις δρόσον ἐπήγασας). Based on Daniel 3.

[^1505]: St. Theophanes the Branded, Funeral Canon, Tone 6, Ode 8, Troparion 1 (*Крѣ́пко пѡ́двигы показа́вше...*). Greek: Στερρῶς ἀγωνισάμενοι, νίκης στεφάνῳ κατεκοσμήθητε, Μάρτυρες Χριστοῦ τροπαιοφόροι, βοῶντες· Σὲ ὑπερυψοῦμεν, Χριστὲ εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας. Acrostic letter 24: μελῳδίαν / пѣ́снь.

[^1506]: St. Theophanes the Branded, Funeral Canon, Tone 6, Ode 8, Troparion 2 (*Сщ҃е́нѣ житїѐ ѡ҆ста́вльшаго вѣ́рно...*). Greek: Ἱερῶς τὸν βίον καταλιπόντα, καὶ πρὸς σὲ τὸν Δεσπότην μεταστάντα, εὐμενῶς πρόσδεξαι ἀναπαύων ὡς εὔσπλαγχνος, σὲ ὑπερυψοῦντα εἰς πάντας τοὺς αἰῶνας. Acrostic letter 25: μελῳδίαν / пѣ́снь.

[^1507]: St. Theophanes the Branded, Funeral Canon, Tone 6, Ode 8, Troparion 3 (*Нн҃ѣ въ землѝ кро́ткыхъ съ всѣ́ми въдвара́тисѧ...*). Greek: Νῦν ἐν χώρᾳ πραέων κατασκηνοῦσθαι, μετὰ πάντων τῶν προκεκοιμημένων, τὸν σὸν δοῦλον, Σωτὴρ εὐδόκησον, πίστει τῇ εἰς σὲ δικαιώσας καὶ χάριτι, σὲ ὑπερυψοῦντα εἰς πάντας τοὺς αἰῶνας. Combining Matthew 5:5 and LXX Psalm 36:11 ('the meek shall inherit the earth'). Acrostic letter 26: μελῳδίαν / пѣ́снь.

[^1508]: St. Theophanes the Branded, Funeral Canon, Tone 6, Ode 8, Theotokion (*Блажи́мъ тѧ̀ всѝ пребл҃женнаѧ...*). Greek: Μακαρίζομέν σε πάντες Πανυπερευλογημένη, τὴν τὸν ὄντως μακάριον Λόγον, σάρκα δι' ἡμᾶς γενόμενον κυήσασαν, ὃν ὑπερυψοῦμεν εἰς πάντας τοὺς αἰῶνας. Acrostic letter 27: μελῳδίαν / пѣ́снь. Completed on fol. 252r (p. 521).

[^1509]: Concluding clause of the Theotokion of Ode 8 (*его́же превъзноси́мъ въ вся̑ вѣ́кы : ~*), completing the stanza begun on fol. 251v (p. 520). Greek: ὃν ὑπερυψοῦμεν εἰς πάντας τοὺς αἰῶνας. Completes the final letter of the acrostic: μελῳδίαν / пѣ́снь.

[^1510]: Ode 9 Heirmos, Tone 6: *Бг҃а чл҃кѡмъ не оу҆до́бь ви́дѣ[ти]* (Greek: Θεὸν ἀνθρώποις ἰδεῖν ἀδύνατον, ὃν οὐ τολμᾷ ἀγγέλων ἀτενίσαι τὰ τάγματα· διὰ σοῦ δὲ Πάναγνε ὡράθη βροτοῖς, Λόγος σεσαρκωμένος, ὃν μεγαλύνοντες, σὺν ταῖς οὐρανίαις Στρατιαῖς, σὲ μακαρίζομεν). In the Ruthenian recension, Greek ἀδύνατον ('impossible') is translated literally as *не удобь видѣти* ('not readily / impossibly seen'). In accordance with Statutory Mandate 16, the unprinted troparion of the Heirmos is left unexpanded.

[^1511]: St. Theophanes the Branded, Funeral Canon, Tone 6, Ode 9, Troparion 1 (*Наде́жда мч҃ническыѧ ли́кы оу҆крѣпѝ...*). Greek: Ἐλπὶς τοὺς τῶν Μαρτύρων δήμους ἐκρατύνατο, καὶ πρὸς τὴν σὴν ἀγάπην διαπυσίως ἐπτέρωσε, τὴν μέλλουσαν τούτοις προτυπώσασα, ἄσειστον ὄντως ἀνάπαυσιν· ἧς τὸν μεταστάντα, Ἀγαθέ, πιστὸν ἀξίωσον. Acrostic letter 28: Ἐ / μελῳδίαν.

[^1512]: St. Theophanes the Branded, Funeral Canon, Tone 6, Ode 9, Troparion 2 (*Свѣ́тлаго и҆ Бж҃твеннаго оу҆лоучи́ти ѡ҆сїѧ́нїа...*). Greek: Λαμπρᾶς καὶ θείας τυχεῖν ἐλλάμψεως, Χριστὲ εὐδόκησον, τὸν ἐν πίστει μεταστάντα, τὴν ἐν κόλποις Ἀβραὰμ ἀνάπαυσιν, ὡς μόνος ἐλεήμων τούτῳ δωρούμενος, καὶ τῆς αἰωνίου ἀξιῶν μακαριότητος. Reference to Luke 16:22. Acrostic letter 29: Λ / μελῳδίαν.

[^1513]: St. Theophanes the Branded, Funeral Canon, Tone 6, Ode 9, Troparion 3 (*И҆́же сы́и є҆сттво́мъ бл҃гъ и҆ мл҃дъ...*). Greek: Ὁ φύσει ὑπάρχων ἀγαθὸς καὶ εὔσπλαγχνος, καὶ θελητὴς ἐλέους, εὐσπλαγχνίας ἄβυσσος, ὃν ἐκ τοῦ τόπου τούτου τῆς κακώσεως, καὶ σκιᾶς τοῦ θανάτου μετέστησας, Σῶτερ, ἔνθα ἐπιλάμπει τὸ σὸν φῶς, ἐκεῖνον κατάταξον. Begun on fol. 252r (p. 521) and completed on fol. 252v (p. 522). Reference to LXX Psalm 22:4 (MT 23:4). Acrostic letter 30: Ω / μελῳδίαν.

[^1514]: St. Theophanes the Branded, Funeral Canon, Tone 6, Ode 9, Theotokion (*Скѣ́нїю ст҃оу́ю чⷭ҇таѧ съвѣ́мы...*). Greek: Σκηνὴν ἁγίαν, Ἁγνὴ γινώσκομέν σε, καὶ κιβωτὸν καὶ πλάκα τοῦ νόμου τῆς χάριτος· διὰ σοῦ γὰρ ἄφεσις ἐδωρήθη, τοῖς δικαιωθεῖσι δι' αἵματος τοῦ σαρκωθέντος ἐκ τῆς σῆς γαστρός, Πανυπεράμωμε. Acrostic letter 31: Δ / μελῳδίαν (completing the acrostic: Ἕκτην προσᾴδω τοῖς θανοῦσι μελῳδίαν).

[^1515]: The Little Litany for the Departed with the exclamation (*Ꙗ҆́ко ты̀ є҆сѝ въскр҃енїе...*), introducing the funeral Idiomela (Самогласны) of St. John of Damascus (Ἰωάννου μοναχοῦ τοῦ Δαμασκηνοῦ Ἰδιόμελα), Tone 1 through Tone 8.

[^1516]: St. John of Damascus, Funeral Idiomelon, Tone 1 (*Ка́ѧ жите́йскаѧ пи́ща пребыва́етъ печа́ли не прича́стна...*). Greek: Ποία τοῦ βίου τρυφὴ διαμένει λύπης ἀμέτοχος; ποία δόξα ἕστηκεν ἐπὶ γῆς ἀμετάθετος; πάντα σκιᾶς ἀσθενέστερα, πάντα ὀνείρων ἀπατηλότερα· μιᾷ ῥοπῇ, καὶ ταῦτα πάντα θάνατος διαδέχεται. Ἀλλ' ἐν τῷ φωτί, Χριστέ, τοῦ προσώπου σου, καὶ τῷ γλυκασμῷ τῆς σῆς ὡραιότητος, ὃν ἐξελέξω ἀνάπαυσον ὡς φιλάνθρωπος. Begun on fol. 252v (p. 522) and completed on fol. 253r (p. 523).

[^1517]: Editorial rubric directing the reader to the Monastic Funeral (*чини мнишескаго погребенїѧ*), printed on fol. 334r (physical leaf p. 685), where the complete eight-tone funeral stichera cycle is recorded with all intermediary psalm verses and repetitions.

[^1518]: Rubric documenting the Balaban printing house's direct recensional collation against the Greek Euchologion edited or approved by Patriarch Meletios Pegas of Alexandria (1590–1601): *Мы же положи́хомъ здѣ̀ ꙗ҆́коже є҆́стъ въ є҆ѵхоло́икꙋ ст҃ѣ́йшаго миле́тїа патрїа́рха неѡдмѣ́нно* ('But we have set down here as it is in the Euchologion of the Most Holy Patriarch Meletios, without alteration'). This confirms the Balaban brothers' deliberate alignment of the Ruthenian printed text with contemporary Constantinopolitan/Alexandrian Greek liturgical models.

[^1519]: St. John of Damascus, Funeral Idiomelon, Tone 2 (*Оу҆вы̀ мнѣ̀ коли́къ по́двигъ и҆́мат[ь] дш҃а...*). Greek: Οἴμοι οἷον ἀγῶνα ἔχει ἡ ψυχή, χωριζομένη ἐκ τοῦ σώματος! οἴμοι πόσα δακρύει τότε, καὶ οὐχ ὑπάρχει ὁ ἐλεῶν αὐτήν! πρὸς τοὺς Ἀγγέλους τὰ ὄμματα ῥέπουσα, ἄπρακτα καθικετεύει· πρὸς τοὺς ἀνθρώπους τὰς χεῖρας ἐκτείνουσα, οὐκ ἔχει τὸν βοηθοῦντα. Διό, ἀγαπητοί μου ἀδελφοί, ἐννοήσαντες τὸ βραχὺ τῆς ζωῆς ἡμῶν, τῷ μεταστάντι τὴν ἀνάπαυσιν, παρὰ Χριστοῦ αἰτησώμεθα, καὶ ταῖς ψυχαῖς ἡμῶν τὸ μέγα ἔλεος. Begun on fol. 253r (p. 523) and completed on fol. 253v (p. 524).

[^1520]: St. John of Damascus, Funeral Idiomelon, Tone 3 (*Вьсѐ соу́етїе чл҃чкое , є҆ли́ко непребоу́детъ по смр҃ти...*). Greek: Πάντα ματαιότης τὰ ἀνθρώπινα, ὅσα οὐχ ὑπάρχει μετὰ θάνατον· οὐ παραμένει ὁ πλοῦτος, οὐ συνοδεύει ἡ δόξα· ἐπελθὼν γὰρ ὁ θάνατος, ταῦτα πάντα ἠφάνισεν. Διὸ Χριστῷ τῷ ἀθανάτῳ βοήσωμεν· Τὸν μεταστάντα ἐξ ἡμῶν ἀνάπαυσον, ἔνθα πάντων ἐστὶν εὐφραινομένων ἡ κατοικία. Begun on fol. 253v (p. 524) and completed on fol. 254r (p. 525). Reference to LXX Psalm 48:18 (MT 49:17) and 86:7 (MT 87:7).

[^1521]: St. John of Damascus, Funeral Idiomelon, Tone 4 (*Гдѣ̀ є҆́стъ мі́рское пристра́стїе...*). Greek: Ποῦ ἐστιν ἡ τοῦ κόσμου προσπάθεια; ποῦ ἐστιν ἡ τῶν προσκαίρων φαντασία; ποῦ ἐστιν ὁ χρυσὸς καὶ ὁ ἄργυρος; ποῦ ἐστι τῶν οἰκετῶν ἡ πληθὺς καὶ ὁ θόρυβος; πάντα κόνις, πάντα τέφρα, πάντα σκιά. Ἀλλὰ δεῦτε βοήσωμεν τῷ ἀθανάτῳ Βασιλεῖ· Κύριε, τῶν αἰωνίων σου ἀγαθῶν ἀξίωσον τὸν μεταστάντα ἐξ ἡμῶν, ἀναπαύων αὐτὸν ἐν τῇ ἀγήρῳ μακαριότητι.

[^1522]: St. John of Damascus, Funeral Idiomelon, Tone 5 (*Помѧноу́хъ прⷪ҇рка въпїю́ща...*). Greek: Ἐμνήσθην τοῦ Προφήτου βοῶντος· Ἐγώ εἰμι γῆ καὶ σποδός· καὶ πάλιν κατενόησα ἐν τοῖς μνήμασι, καὶ εἶδον τὰ ὀστᾶ τὰ γεγυμνωμένα, καὶ εἶπον· Ἆρα τίς ἐστι, βασιλεὺς ἢ στρατιώτης, ἢ πλούσιος ἢ πένης, ἢ δίκαιος ἢ ἁμαρτωλός; Ἀλλὰ ἀνάπαυσον, Κύριε, μετὰ δικαίων τὸν δοῦλόν σου. Begun on fol. 254r (p. 525) and completed on fol. 254v (p. 526). Quoting Genesis 18:27 and Job 30:19.

[^1523]: St. John of Damascus, Funeral Idiomelon, Tone 6 (*Нача́токъ ми и҆ съста́въ , зижди́телное твоѐ бы́сть повелѣ́нїе...*). Greek: Ἀρχή μοι καὶ ὑπόστασις, τὸ πλαστουργόν σου γέγονε πρόσταγμα· βουληθεὶς γὰρ ἐξ ἀοράτου τε καὶ ὁρατῆς με συμπῆξαι φύσεως, ἔπλασάς μου τὸ σῶμα ἐκ γῆς, δέδωκας δέ μοι ψυχήν, τῇ θείᾳ σου καὶ ζωοποιῷ ἐμπνεύσει. Διό, Σωτήρ, τὸν δοῦλόν σου, ἐν χώρᾳ ζώντων, ἐν σκηναῖς Δικαίων ἀνάπαυσον. Anthropological doctrine of the composite human being derived from Genesis 2:7 and St. Gregory of Nazianzus (Oration 38.11).

[^1524]: St. John of Damascus, Funeral Idiomelon, Tone 7 (*По ѻ҆́бразоу твоемоу̀ и҆ по подо́бїю...*). Greek: Κατ' εἰκόνα σὴν καὶ ὁμοίωσιν, πλαστουργήσας κατ' ἀρχὰς τὸν ἄνθρωπον, ἐν Παραδείσῳ τέθεικας, ἄρχειν τῶν σῶν κτισμάτων· φθόνῳ δὲ διαβόλου ἀπατηθείς, τῆς βρώσεως μετέσχε, τῶν ἐντολῶν σου παραβάτης γενόμενος· διὸ πάλιν εἰς γῆν ἐξ ἧς ἐλήφθη, κατεδίκασας ἐπιστρέφειν, Κύριε, καὶ αἰτεῖσθαι τὴν ἀνάπαυσιν. Begun on fol. 254v (p. 526) and completed on fol. 255r (p. 527). Reference to Genesis 1:26–28; 3:1–6, 19.

[^1525]: St. John of Damascus, Funeral Idiomelon, Tone 8 (*Пла́чюсѧ и҆ рыда́ю є҆гда̀ помышлѧ́ю съме́рть...*). Greek: Θρηνῶ καὶ ὀδύρομαι, ὅταν ἐννοήσω τὸν θάνατον, καὶ ἴδω ἐν τοῖς τάφοις κειμένην, τὴν κατ' εἰκόνα Θεοῦ πλασθεῖσαν ἡμῖν ὡραιότητα, ἄμορφον, ἄδοξον, μὴ ἔχουσαν εἶδος. Ὢ τοῦ θαύματος! τί τὸ γενόμενον περὶ ἡμᾶς τοῦτο μυστήριον; πῶς παρεδόθημεν τῇ φθορᾷ; πῶς συνεζεύχθημεν τῷ θανάτῳ; Ὄντως Θεοῦ προστάξει, ὡς γέγραπται, τοῦ παρέχοντος τῷ μεταστάντι τὴν ἀνάπαυσιν. Begun on fol. 255r (p. 527) and completed on fol. 255v (p. 528).

[^1526]: The Beatitudes (Макаризмы / Блаженны), Tone 6 (*Та́же блаже́на, Гла́съ ѕ҃*). The Gospel Beatitudes (Matthew 5:3–12) are sung with funeral troparia intercalated after the final six verses.

[^1527]: Funeral Beatitudes, Tone 6, Troparion 1 (*Разбо́йника ра́еви Хе҃ гражда́нина...*). Greek: Λῃστὴν τοῦ Παραδείσου πολίτην, ἐπὶ Σταυροῦ σοι βοήσαντα, τὸ Μνήσθητί μου, προφθάσας ἀπέδειξας· αὐτοῦ τῆς μετανοίας, ἀξίωσον κἀμὲ τὸν ἀνάξιον. Reference to Luke 23:42–43.

[^1528]: Funeral Beatitudes, Tone 6, Troparion 2 (*И҆́же дша́ми влⷣче́ствоуѧ и҆ телесы̀...*). Greek: Ὁ ψυχῶν δεσπόζων καὶ σωμάτων, οὗ ἐν χειρὶ ἡ πνοὴ ἡμῶν, τῶν θλιβομένων ἡ παράκλησις, ἀνάπαυσον ἐν χώρᾳ, τῶν ζώντων ὃν μετέστησας δοῦλόν σου. Begun on fol. 255v (p. 528) and completed on fol. 256r (p. 529). Reference to Job 12:10 and LXX Psalm 114:9 (MT 116:9).

[^1529]: Funeral Beatitudes, Tone 6, Troparion 3 (*Хрⷭ҇то́съ тѧ̀ оу҆поко́и въ страна́хъ живы́хъ...*). Greek: Χριστός σε ἀναπαύσει ἐν χώρᾳ ζώντων, καὶ πύλας Παραδείσου ἀνοίξει σοι, καὶ τῆς αὐτοῦ βασιλείας πολίτην ἀποδείξει, καὶ ἄφεσίν σοι δώσει, ὧν ἥμαρτες ἐν βίῳ, φιλόχριστε.

[^1530]: Funeral Beatitudes, Tone 6, Troparion 4 (*Да̀ и҆зы́демъ и҆ ви́димъ грѡ́бѣхъ...*). Greek: Ἐξέλθωμεν καὶ ἴδωμεν ἐν τάφοις, ὅτι γυμνὰ ὀστέα ὁ ἄνθρωπος, σκωλήκων βρῶμα καὶ δυσωδία· καὶ γνῶμεν τίς ὁ πλοῦτος, τὸ κάλλος, ἡ ἰσχὺς καὶ ἡ εὐπρέπεια.

[^1531]: Funeral Beatitudes, Tone 6, Troparion 5 (*Е҆гда̀ прїи́деши на ѡ҆́блацѣхъ въ сла́вѣ свое́й Хе҃...*). Greek: Ὅταν ἔλθῃς ἐν νεφέλαις ἐν τῇ δόξῃ σου, Χριστέ, κρῖναι ζῶντας καὶ νεκρούς, τότε καὶ τοῦτον ἀξίωσον, ἐν χαρᾷ ὑπαντῆσαί σοι. Reference to Matthew 24:30; 25:31; 1 Thessalonians 4:17.

[^1532]: Funeral Beatitudes, Tone 6, Troparion 6 (*Съ въсѣ́ми ст҃ы́ми , и҆ пра́ведными оу҆чинѝ Сло́ве...*). Greek: Μετὰ πάντων Ἁγίων καὶ δικαίων κατάταξον, Λόγε, ὃν ἐκ τῶν προσκαίρων πίστει μετέστησας, ἵνα σε δοξάζῃ.

[^1533]: Funeral Beatitudes, Tone 6, Triadikon (*Безнача́лнаго ра́ди рожде́нїа , и҆ происхожде́нїа...*). Greek: Τῆς ἀνάρχου ἕνεκεν γεννήσεως καὶ ἐκπορεύσεως, Πατέρα προσκυνῶ τὸν γεννήσαντα, Υἱὸν δοξολογῶ τὸν γεννηθέντα, ὑμνῶ τὸν συμφανέντα, Πατρί τε καὶ Υἱῷ, Πνεῦμα Ἅγιον. Trinitarian theological confession emphasizing the Father as sole cause and monarchia (*безначално*), the eternal generation (*γέννησις*) of the Son, and the eternal procession (*ἐκπόρευσις*) of the Holy Spirit.

[^1534]: Funeral Beatitudes, Tone 6, Theotokion (*Ка́ко ѿ сосцо́у твое́ю мле́ко и҆стача́еши Дв҃о...*). Greek: Πῶς ἐκ μαστῶν σου γάλα ἀναβλύζεις, Παρθένε; πῶς τρέφεις τὸν τροφοδότην τῆς κτίσεως; ὡς οἶδεν αὐτός... Stanza begun on fol. 256v (p. 530) and concluded on fol. 257r (p. 531): *источи́выи во́доу и҆с ка́мене , жи́лы во́дныѧ жа́ждꙋщимъ лю́демъ , ꙗ҆́коже є҆́стъ пи́сано : ~* (referencing Exodus 17:6 and Numbers 20:11).

[^1535]: The concluding clause of the Theotokion from the Beatitudes (continued from fol. 254v / p. 530). The Scriptural reference is to Exod. 17:6 and Num. 20:11 (cf. Ps. 77:15–16 [LXX]).

[^1536]: Prokeimenon of the funeral office (cf. Ps. 114:9 / 115:6 [LXX]; liturgical funeral chant).

[^1537]: Ps. 27:1 [LXX].

[^1538]: Lection from the First Epistle of Paul to the Thessalonians (1 Thess. 4:13–17), the statutory Epistle lection for the burial of a layman.

[^1539]: 1 Thess. 4:15–17. Slavonic: *не и҆ма́мы превари́ти оу҆со́пшихъ* (Greek: οὐ μὴ φθάσωмен τοὺς κοιμηθέντας, "shall not precede them that are asleep").

[^1540]: Ps. 64:5 [LXX 64:4].

[^1541]: Gospel lection from John 5:24–30, the statutory Gospel lection for the burial of a layman.

[^1542]: John 5:29. The printed Slavonic witness exhibits *сътко́ршей* (a typographical error or vernacular consonant shift for *сътво́ршей*, "they that have done").

[^1543]: John 5:30.

[^1544]: The Litany of Fervent Supplication for the Departed (*Погреба́льная є҆ктенїа̀*). In accordance with ancient euchological printing practice, standard responses and litany petitions are recorded in incipit or condensed form.

[^1545]: Rubrical instruction governing the silent recitation of the secret sacerdotal prayer (*Б҃е дх҃ѡвъ и҆ всѧ́коѧ пло́ти*, "O God of spirits and of all flesh") by concelebrating presbyters during the deacon's litany, followed by the statutory Absolution Prayer read by the reposed person's spiritual father (*дꙋхо́вный ѡ҆те́цъ*).

[^1546]: The 318 Holy Fathers of the First Ecumenical Council of Nicaea (AD 325), invoked as the primary patristic authority for the transmission of apostolic canon and sacerdotal power.

[^1547]: Combining Matt. 18:21–22 ("seventy times seven") and Matt. 18:18 ("whatsoever ye shall bind on earth... whatsoever ye shall loose on earth").

[^1548]: Doxological conclusion of the Absolution Prayer over the departed (*Моли́тва проща́льнаѧ на оу҆ме́ршымъ*).

[^1549]: The Last Kiss (*Послѣ́днее цѣлова́нїе* / ἀσπασμός), the solemn liturgical farewell offered by clergy, relatives, and faithful to the deceased before the grave is closed.

[^1550]: Melodic model: Tone 2, *Podoben: "When from the Tree"* (*Е҆гда̀ ѿ дрѣ́ва тѧ̀* / Ὅте ἐκ τοῦ ξύλου).

[^1551]: Opening Sticheron of the Last Kiss (*Прїидѣ́те послѣ́днее цѣлова́нїе...*).

[^1552]: Sticheron 2 of the Last Kiss (*Коѐ разлꙋче́нїе ѡ҆ бра́тїе...*).

[^1553]: Sticheron 3 of the Last Kiss (*Нн҃ѣ соуе́тнаго житїѧ̀...*); cf. Eccles. 12:6–7.

[^1554]: Sticheron 4 of the Last Kiss (*Коѐ жи́тїе на́ше є҆́стъ...*); cf. James 4:14; Ps. 102:15–16 [LXX].

[^1555]: Sticheron 5 of the Last Kiss (*Вели́къ пла́чь и҆ рыда́нїе...*).

[^1556]: Sticheron 6 of the Last Kiss (*Зрѧ́ще прележа́ща мр҃тва...*); cf. Ps. 101:4, 102:15 [LXX].

[^1557]: Sticheron 7 of the Last Kiss (*Прїидѣ́те и҆́же ѿ рѡ́да а҆да́млѧ...*).

[^1558]: Sticheron 8 of the Last Kiss (*Е҆гда̀ дꙋша̀ ѿ тѣ́ла хо́щетъ съ нꙋ́жею...*), reflecting the ancient Byzantine euchological motif of the soul's violent separation from the body and dread of the divine tribunal.

[^1559]: Sticheron 9 of the Last Kiss (*Прїидѣ́те на гро́бъ бра́тїе, ви́димъ пе́пелъ и҆ пра́хъ...*), contrasting mortal corruption with the equality of all social conditions in death; cf. Gen. 3:19; Job 30:19; Ps. 102:14–16 [LXX].

[^1560]: Sticheron 10 of the Last Kiss (*Въи́стинноу соуета̀ и҆ тлѧ̀...*); cf. Eccles. 1:2.

[^1561]: Sticheron 11 of the Last Kiss (*Всѝ нн҃ѣ тѣле́снїи ѡ҆роу́дїа пра́дны...*), describing the cessation of the bodily faculties and the dissolution of the senses in death.

[^1562]: Theotokion concluding the Idiomela of the Last Kiss (*Сп҃сѝ оу҆пова́ющихъ на́ тѧ, Мт҃и незаходи́маго слн҃ца...*).

[^1563]: Melodic model: Tone 6, Idiomelon (Samoglásen). The celebrated funeral Doxastikon attributed to St. John of Damascus (*Зрѧ́ще мѧ̀ безгла́сна и҆ бездꙋ́шна прележа́ща...* / Ὁρῶντές με ἄφωνον καὶ ἄпνουν προκείμενον), sung at "Glory..." as the personal testament and farewell supplication of the reposed person.

[^1564]: Concluding strophe of the Tone 6 Doxastikon (*но̀ прїидѣ́те всѝ любѧ́щїи мѧ̀...*), articulating the equality of master and servant before the divine tribunal; cf. Col. 3:25; Eph. 6:9.

[^1565]: Incipit indication for "Both now..." (*И҆ нн҃ѣ. Б҃ѡ.*), appointing the concluding Theotokion of Tone 6.

[^1566]: Concluding Theotokion of the Last Kiss (*Мл҃твами ро́жьшаѧ тѧ̀ Хрїстѐ...*), invoking the intercession of the Theotokos, the Forerunner, Apostles, Hierarchs, and all Saints.

[^1567]: Rubric appointing the Trisagion Prayers, the Lord's Prayer, the Troparia for the Departed (*Съ дꙋ́хы пра́ведными...*), the Deacon's Litany of Fervent Supplication, the general sacerdotal prayer (*Бж҃е дꙋхо́въ...*), and the Dismissal.

[^1568]: The Solemn Funeral Dismissal (*Въскр҃сый и҆з̾ мр҃твыхъ Хс҃ и҆́стинный Бг҃ъ на́шь...*), commemorating the reposed servant by name.

[^1569]: Concluding petition of the Dismissal and the triple proclamation of "Eternal Memory" (*Вѣ́чнаѧ ти па́мѧть...*).

[^1570]: Rubrics governing the transfer of the body to the grave while chanting the Trisagion (*Ст҃ы́й Бж҃е*), the cruciform casting of earth upon the remains with the verse of Ps. 23:1 [LXX] (*Гдⷭ҇нѧ є҆́стъ землѧ̀...*), and the pouring of lamp oil or ashes from the censer over the relics.

[^1571]: Concluding rubric directing the filling of the grave while chanting the funeral Troparia (*Съ дꙋ́хы пра́ведными...*), ending with the final Dismissal and the printer's doxological praise: "Glory to God Who has thus been well pleased."

[^1572]: Colophon marking the definitive completion of the Order of Burial for Laymen (*Коне́цъ и҆схо́днаго въслѣ́дованїа мирѧ́номъ*).

[^1573]: Folio 264v is a blank unprinted leaf in the physical codex, serving as a structural transition before Part XXII.

[^1574]: Woodcut headpiece of Christ in the Tomb (*Imago Pietatis*) and opening title rubric of Part XXII: Prayers of Absolution for Every Curse and Excommunication over the Departed (*Мл҃твы прѧща́лныи на всѧ́коу клѧ́твоу и҆ ѿлꙋче́нїе, на оу҆ме́ршимъ*), authored by Patriarch Matthew of Constantinople and transmitted in Ruthenian and Slavic euchologia.

[^1575]: Rubrical directions governing the recitation of these prayers by concelebrating presbyters at the Proskomedia and by the hierarch during the Great Entrance.

[^1576]: Rubric directing the hierarch to kneel and proclaim the prayer aloud with compunction and tears before receiving the Holy Gifts.

[^1577]: Opening section of the First Prayer of Absolution (*Гд҃и Бж҃е на́шъ, и҆́же неизрече́нною ти моу́дростїю...*), confessing the divine creation of man from the dust and the fall into transgression; cf. Gen. 2:7, 3:19.

[^1578]: Fol. 267r. Theological anthropology of bodily dissolution at death: the severance of soul and body ordained by God so that evil might not become immortal (a classical Patristic theme rooted in St. Gregory of Nazianzus, *Oratio 38 in Theophania*, and St. John Damascene), reserving the reunion of soul and reconstituted flesh for the General Resurrection (*до ѡ҆́бщаго въскр҃ні́ѧ*).

[^1579]: Fol. 267r. Triadological supplication: the hierarch addresses the unoriginate Father (*безна́чалному ѿц҃ꙋ̀*), the Only-begotten Son (*є҆диноча́домꙋ твоемоу̀ сн҃оу*), and the consubstantial and life-creating Spirit (*є҆диносоу́щномꙋ и҆ животворя́щемꙋ ти дх҃ꙋ*), imploring that God's handiwork not be consumed by ultimate destruction.

[^1580]: Fol. 267v. The petition for the soul's ranking in the assembly of the righteous (*въ лицѣ̀ пра́ведныхъ*), appealing to God's immeasurable mercy (*безмѣ́рнаа твоѧ̀ ми́лость*) and ineffable love for mankind (*чл҃колю́бі́е неи҆зрече́нное*).

[^1581]: Fol. 267v. Detailed catalog of canonical impediments, curses, and excommunications: parental imprecations from father or mother (*поклѧ́твою ѿчею, и҆ли ма́терні́ю*), self-curses (*сво́емꙋ проклѧ́ті́ю попа́дъ*), clerical censure resulting from grievance caused to a priest (*кое́го ѿ ѡ҆сщ҃е́нныхъ ѡ҆горчи́въ*), and episcopal excommunication neglected through sloth (*ѿ а҆рхі́ереѧ въ тѧ́жкое ѿлоуче́ні́е въпа́дъ, ѡ҆ не́мже неради́въ, и҆ въ лѣ́ности пребыва́ѧ*).

[^1582]: Fol. 268r. Apostolic authority of the keys (Matt. 16:19; Matt. 18:18): Christ's grant of binding and loosing to the Apostle Peter (*врьхо́вномоу петроу̀ сі́ю вла́сть да́вый*) transmitted through sacramental ordination unto the episcopate and priesthood to remit sins of both soul and body.

[^1583]: Fol. 268r. Forgiveness in both ages: invoking absolution in the present age and in that to come (*въ ны́нѣшнемъ вѣ́цѣ, и҆ въ бꙋ́доущемъ*, echoing Matt. 12:32), through the intercession of the Theotokos and all saints.

[^1584]: Fol. 268r. Title and opening rubric for the Second Prayer of Absolution (*Мли́тва втора́ѧ, томоу́жде*), proclaimed over the deceased by the hierarch or priest.

[^1585]: Fol. 268v. Petrine confession and ecclesiological authority: the founding of the Church upon the chief of the disciples, Peter (Matt. 16:18), the conferral of the keys of the Kingdom of Heaven (*клю́ча є҆моу̀ да́въ црⷭ҇тві́а нбⷭ҇наго*), and the transmission of this authority unto the ministers of the Church.

[^1586]: Fol. 269r. Tripartite classification of sins: remitting all offenses committed in word, deed, or thought (*сло́вомъ, и҆лѝ дѣ́ломъ, и҆лѝ въ мы́сли*).

[^1587]: Fol. 269r. Liberation from self-inflicted bonds arising from arrogance (*ѡ҆ себѣ̀ ѿ възноше́ні́а*), external episcopal suspensions, and diabolical stumbling (*зави́сті́ю и҆ споспѣ́шествомъ лоука́ваго*).

[^1588]: Fol. 269v. Final resolution of the body into nature (*тѣ́лꙋ же ѿ тебе създа́нномоу є҆сткꙋ̀ да́тисѧ*) and reception of the soul among the saints who have pleased God throughout all ages (*съ ст҃ы́ми и҆́же ѿ вѣ́ка тебѣ̀ бл҃гоꙋго́ждъшими*).

[^1589]: Fol. 269v. Renaissance woodcut vignette (foliate tailpiece) marking the formal conclusion of the Prayers of Absolution over the departed.

[^1590]: Fol. 270r. Woodcut headpiece depicting Renaissance scrollwork with tritons wielding clubs and serpents, opening Part XXIII: The Order for Burial on Holy Pascha and throughout Bright Week (*Подобаетъ вѣдати, аще кто преставится на святое воскресенїе, или въ который любо день свѣтлыя недѣля*).

[^1591]: Fol. 270r. Suspension of ordinary funeral mourning during Bright Week: the Typikon explicitly forbids singing the customary funeral sequences (*ничто́же надъ ни́мъ пое́тъ сѧ ѻ҆бы́чно ꙋ҆со́пше*), substituting the radiant joy of the Paschal Canon of St. John of Damascus (*Воскресе́нїя день*).

[^1592]: Fol. 270v. Intercalation of Paschal and funeral hymnography: the Paschal Hypakoe (*Предвари́ша оу҆́тро*), followed after Ode 6 by the funeral Kontakion (*Со святы́ми упоко́й*) and Oikos (*Самъ еди́нъ есѝ безсме́ртный*), bridging the grief of physical bereavement with the certainty of Christ's resurrection.

[^1593]: Fol. 270v. Paschal liturgical substitutions: the baptismal canticle *As many as have been baptized into Christ* (Gal. 3:27) replaces the customary Trisagion (*Святы́й Бо́же*); the first Matins Resurrection Gospel (Matt. 28:16–20) is proclaimed; and the final kiss of peace is accompanied by the triumphant greeting *Christ is risen!* (*Хрїсто́съ воскре́се*).

[^1594]: Fol. 270v. Chanting of the Paschal Exapostilarion *Having fallen asleep in the flesh* (*Пло́тїю оу҆сну́въ*, twice), followed by the Funeral Evlogetaria.

[^1595]: Fol. 271r. Concluding Paschal hymnody: the Funeral Evlogetaria (*Благослове́нъ есѝ Го́споди, научи́ мя оправда́ниемъ Твои́мъ: А́нгельскїй собо́ръ*), followed by the Paschal Stichera with their verses (*Да воскре́снетъ Богъ* / *Па́сха свяще́нная*), and the Paschal troparion *Christ is risen* sung thrice.

[^1596]: Fol. 271r. Liturgical ethos of Christian burial in Paschaltide: interment is conducted not with lamentation, but *with thanksgiving and with joy* (*съ бл҃годаре́ні́емъ, и҆ ра́дості́ю*), reflecting the Orthodox conviction that for the believer who dies in the radiant light of Pascha, death is transformed into life and entrance into the eternal banquet.

[^1597]: Fol. 271v. Blank leaf concluding Part XXIII (the Paschal Funeral Order) before Part XXIV (The Order for the Burial of Infants) begins on Fol. 272r.

[^1598]: Fol. 272r. Woodcut headpiece depicting the Crucifixion in a Renaissance cartouche opening Part XXIV: The Order for the Burial of an Infant (*Чи́нъ провожде́нію младе́нческомꙋ*). This specialized office, distinct from the burial of adults or priests, reflects the Byzantine theological tradition concerning infants who pass away before reaching moral culpability.

[^1599]: Fol. 272r. Customary liturgical opening: the celebrant's initial blessing (*Благослове́нъ Богъ нашъ*), followed by the Trisagion prayers, the Lord's Prayer with Trinitarian doxology, the twelvefold *Kyrie eleison*, and the triple call to worship (*Прїиди́те поклони́мся*).

[^1600]: Fol. 272r. Psalm 19 (LXX 19:2–5): royal and supplicatory psalm chanted over the deceased child, petitioning God's help from the sanctuary and remembrance of sacrifice in the face of sorrow.

[^1601]: Fol. 272v. Conclusion of Psalm 19 (LXX 19:6–10): confession of divine deliverance through the holy right hand of the Lord, contrasting reliance on worldly chariots and horses with trust in the Name of the God of Jacob.

[^1602]: Fol. 272v. Rubric directing the chanting of Psalm 141 (LXX 141:1).

[^1603]: Fol. 273r. Psalm 141 (LXX 141:2–8): Davidic prayer of the distressed soul poured out before God as the sole portion in the land of the living when all human recourse has vanished.

[^1604]: Fol. 273v. Final verse of Psalm 141 (LXX 141:8): supplication for deliverance from prison and entry into the assembly of the righteous.

[^1605]: Fol. 273v. Psalm 27 (LXX 27:1–4): supplication imploring God not to remain silent lest the soul descend into the pit, and petitioning preservation from hypocritical workers of iniquity.

[^1606]: Fol. 274r. Psalm 27 (LXX 27:4–9): thanksgiving for answered prayer and the closing blessing over God's inheritance (*Спасѝ лю́ди Твоя̀, и благословѝ достоянїе Твоѐ*).

[^1607]: Fol. 274r. Concluding doxological rubric chanting *Glory... Both now...* (*Пое́мъ сла́ва, и ны́нѣ*).

[^1608]: Fol. 274v. Trisagion sequence followed by the funeral Troparion in Tone 2 (*Помянѝ Го́споди я́ко благъ раба̀ Твоего̀*), affirming that God alone is without sin and able to bestow eternal rest.

[^1609]: Fol. 274v. Theotokion to the Mother of the Uncreated Light (*Ма́ти свята́я пречи́стаго свѣ́та*), petitioning the Virgin's intercession with angelic hymnody.

[^1610]: Fol. 274v. Chanting of the funeral Kontakion (*Со святы́ми упоко́й*), followed by the exclamation, Trisagion, Prokeimenon in Tone 6 (*Блаже́нъ путь въ о́ньже по́йдеши ду́ше*), and announcement of the Epistle.

[^1611]: Fol. 275r. Epistle reading (1 Cor. 15:39–44): St. Paul's exposition of the bodily resurrection, contrasting earthly corruptible flesh with celestial incorruption and the natural earthly body with the spiritual resurrected body.

[^1612]: Fol. 275v. Conclusion of the Epistle (1 Cor. 15:44–45): typology of the first Adam as a living soul and the last Adam, Christ, as a life-giving spirit.

[^1613]: Fol. 275v. Funeral Alleluia with verses from Psalms 64:5 and 24:13 LXX (*Блаже́нъ его́же избра́лъ и прїя́лъ есѝ, Го́споди*), followed by the announcement of the Gospel according to St. John.

[^1614]: Fol. 276r. Gospel pericope (John 6:37b–39): Christ's pledge that He will in no wise cast out anyone coming to Him, and that of all given to Him by the Father none will be lost, but raised up on the last day.

[^1615]: Fol. 276r. Cross-reference to fol. 230 (physical leaf p477): the celebrant is instructed to read the funeral litany of fervent supplication (*Помилуй насъ, Боже*), the prayer *O God of spirits and of all flesh*, and the exclamation *For Thou art the Resurrection and the Life* as printed in full in the adult burial rite.

[^1616]: Fol. 276r. Incipit and rubric for the specific Infant Funeral Prayer (*Храня́й младе́нцы Го́споди въ ны́нѣшнемъ житїи*), preceded by the deacon's bidding.

[^1617]: Fol. 276v. Conclusion of the Infant Funeral Prayer: committing the child's soul into Abraham's bosom and the luminous angelic realms reserved for pure souls, quoting Matt. 19:14 (*Of such is the Kingdom of Heaven*), concluding with a full Trinitarian doxology.

[^1618]: Fol. 276v. Concluding Dismissal rubric and Renaissance woodcut vignette (winged cherub head adorned with acanthus scrollwork and fruit garlands) concluding the infant funeral order.

[^1619]: Fol. 277r. Renaissance woodcut headpiece (foliate arabesque with acanthus scrollwork, blooming floral vase, and corner rosettes) opening Part XXV: The Order of the Funeral Singing for All Departed Fathers and Our Brethren, and Other Deceased Christians (*Чи́нъ надгро́бнаго пѣ́нія всѣ́мъ оусо́пшимъ отце́мъ и бра́тїямъ на́шимъ, и про́чіимъ христїа́номъ уме́ршимъ*), commonly designated in the Kyivan and Ruthenian tradition as the Great Parastas (*Параста́съ*).

[^1620]: Fol. 277r. Vesting rubric specifying that the presiding celebrant (or the monastery's hegumen himself) and all concelebrating priests enter the altar and vest in phelonia, and the deacons in sticharia, before beginning the solemn memorial office with the censing of the sanctuary and temple.

[^1621]: Fol. 277v. Initial liturgical blessing (*Благослове́нъ Богъ нашъ*) followed by the Trisagion prayers, the Lord's Prayer with Trinitarian doxology, the twelvefold *Kyrie eleison*, and the triple invitation to worship (*Прїиди́те поклони́мся*).

[^1622]: Fol. 277v. Cross-reference directing the chanting of Psalm 90 (LXX 90:1–16: *Живы́й въ по́мощи Вы́шняго* / *He that dwells in the help of the Highest*), which is printed in full on fol. 231r (physical leaf p479) in the burial rite for deceased laymen.

[^1623]: Fol. 277v. Concluding psalm doxology (*Glory... Both now...*), the threefold Alleluia in Tone 8, and the chanting of the funeral Troparion in Tone 8 (*И́же глубина́ми му́дрости* / *O Thou Who by the depth of wisdom*), with its thematic refrain repeated at *Glory...*.

[^1624]: Fol. 278r. Funeral Theotokion in Tone 8 (*Тебѐ гра́да и приста́нище и́мамы* / *Thee we have as a city and a haven*), appealing to the Mother of God as the secure refuge and acceptable intercessor before Christ her Son.

[^1625]: Fol. 278r. Rubric directing the deacon to proclaim the customary funeral petitions of the litany of fervent supplication (*Помилуй насъ, Боже*), followed by the prayer *O God of spirits and of all flesh* recited jointly by all concelebrating priests.

[^1626]: Fol. 278r. Rubric governing the chanting of the 17th Kathisma (Psalm 118 LXX, the *Amomos* or "Blameless"), divided into stases. At the midpoint verse (*Unto the ages I will not forget Thy statutes, for in them Thou hast given me life* — LXX 118:93), the choir sings the verse thrice, followed by diaconal petitions, the prayer *O God of spirits*, and the completion of the Kathisma with the funeral troparia (*Evlogitaria*).

[^1627]: Fol. 278v. Cross-reference to fol. 232r (physical leaf p481), where the full text of the 17th Kathisma and the Funeral Troparia (*The choir of the saints have found the Fountain of life*) are printed in the order for the burial of laymen; followed by diaconal petitions, the prayer *O God of spirits*, and Psalm 50 (LXX 50:3–21: *Have mercy on me, O God*).

[^1628]: Fol. 278v. Opening of the Funeral Canon in Tone 8, Ode 1, attributed to St. Theophanes the Branded. It begins with the Heirmos *Во́ду проше́дъ* (*Having traversed the water as upon dry land*), followed by the Martyrikon (*Through the death of Christ*), the first troparion for the departed (*Overlooking the sins of youth*), and the troparion at *Glory...*.

[^1629]: Fol. 279r. Conclusion of the troparion at *Glory...* in Ode 1, followed by the Theotokion (*Зачала̀ есѝ Сло́во О́тчее* / *Thou didst conceive the Father's Word*), confessing the hypostatic union of the divine Word and the harrowing of Hades.

[^1630]: Fol. 279r. Ode 3 of the Funeral Canon in Tone 8, opening with the Heirmos *Небе́сному кру́гу* (*Of the heavenly vault*), followed by the Martyrikon celebrating the martyrs' baptism in blood, and the troparion petitioning rest for the departed in the courts of the saints through Christ's voluntary burial.

[^1631]: Fol. 279v. Troparion at *Glory...* in Ode 3, imploring divine mercy and remission of transgressions according to God's innate goodness, followed by the Theotokion (*Вопло́щся от чре́ва твоего̀* / *Incarnate from thy womb*), honoring the Virgin as the Mother of the Savior Who rescues mankind from the gates of death.

[^1632]: Fol. 279v. Katavasia of Ode 3, repeating the Heirmos *Celestial vault's supreme Creator* in full, followed by the diaconal petitions, the prayer *O God of spirits*, and the announcement of the funeral Sessional Hymn in Tone 5.

[^1633]: Fol. 280r. Funeral Sessional Hymn (Kathisma hymn) in Tone 5 (*Поко́й, Спа́се нашъ, съ пра́ведными раба̀ Твоего̀* / *Give rest, O our Savior, with the righteous unto Thy servant*), with its concluding refrain repeated at *Glory...*, followed by the Theotokion (*И́же от Дѣ́вы возсїя́вый ми́ру* / *Thou Who didst shine forth from the Virgin*).

[^1634]: Fol. 280r. Ode 4 of the Funeral Canon in Tone 8, opening with the Heirmos *Ты ми Христе Господь, ты же и сила ми* (*Thou art my Lord, O Christ, Thou art also my strength*), and the opening lines of the Martyrikon troparion commemorating the steadfastness of the martyrs under torments.

[^1635]: Fol. 280v. Conclusion of the Martyrikon in Ode 4, followed by the troparion meditating on John 14:2 (*In My Father's house are many mansions*), petitioning that the departed soul be granted a dwelling place according to the measure of Christian virtue.

[^1636]: Fol. 280v. Troparion at *Glory...* in Ode 4, extolling the Incarnation of the Immortal One Who tasted death to reveal the pathway to life, and imploring remission of sins and participation in the divine light for the departed.

[^1637]: Fol. 281r. Theotokion of Ode 4 (*Ты вѣ́рнымъ похвала̀ есѝ, Безневѣ́стная* / *Thou art the boast of the faithful, O unwedded Bride*), depicting the Mother of God as an unassailable wall, haven, and advocate delivering believers from all perils.

[^1638]: Fol. 281r. Ode 5 of the Funeral Canon in Tone 8, opening with the Heirmos *Вску́ю мя отри́нулъ есѝ* (*Why hast Thou cast me away from Thy face, O Light unwaning*), followed by the first troparion contemplating the ineffable heavenly banquet in the tabernacles of the righteous, and the opening lines of the second troparion.

[^1639]: Fol. 281v. Conclusion of the second troparion of Ode 5, invoking the parable of the rich man and Lazarus (Luke 16:22) to petition rest in Abraham's bosom and bold presentation before the dread throne of Christ; followed by the troparion at *Glory...* (*Ѡчище́нїе намъ яви́ся*), celebrating the healing of human fallenness through the Savior's wounds (cf. Isaiah 53:5).

[^1640]: Fol. 281v. Theotokion of Ode 5 (*Ми́лостивно, Ми́лостиве, человѣ́чества мѣ́ру восприя́лъ есѝ* / *Mercifully, O Merciful One, Thou didst assume the measure of humanity*), proclaiming the destruction of death through Christ's animate flesh taken from the Virgin's womb, followed by the incipit of the Heirmos for Ode 6 (*Ѡчи́сти мя, Спа́се* / *Cleanse me, O Savior*).

[^1641]: Fol. 285r. Martyrikon troparion of Ode 6 of the Funeral Canon in Tone 8, extolling the holy martyrs whose souls were wounded with divine love (*любо́вію твое́ю ду́ша оуязвї́вше ст҃їи* / *amor Dei*), seeking eternal communion with Christ.

[^1642]: Fol. 285r. Troparion of Ode 6 contemplating Christ's harrowing of Hades, where by shattering the "hostile womb of death" (*чре́во вра́жїе сме́рти... растерза́лъ есѝ*), the divine Benefactor (*благодѣ́телю*) released all captive souls and granted life.

[^1643]: Fol. 285r. Troparion at *Glory...* in Ode 6, invoking Isaiah 25:8 / Revelation 21:4 (*God shall wipe away every tear from their faces*), beseeching Christ to deliver the departed servant from the tears and lamentation of Hades.

[^1644]: Fol. 285v. Conclusion of the Theotokion of Ode 6, expressing the Kenosis of the Incarnation (Philippians 2:7: *ἑαυτὸν ἐκένωσε* / *и҆стощава́етсѧ*), wherein the transcendent, immortal God voluntarily assumes flesh within the Virgin's womb and undergoes human death to redeem mankind.

[^1645]: Fol. 285v. Katavasia of Ode 6, repeating the Heirmos *Cleanse me, O Savior* (*Ѡ҆чи́сти мѧ̀, Спа́се* — Jonah 2:2–3) in full, chanted by the choir before the Little Litany.

[^1646]: Fol. 285v. Rubric for the Little Litany (*Дїа́конства ма́ла*), followed by the priest's secret prayer and exclamation.

[^1647]: Fol. 285v. Solemn funeral Kontakion in Tone 8 (*Съ святы́ми поко́й, Христѐ* / *With the saints give rest*), the quintessential hymn of Eastern Christian burial, petitioning eternal rest where pain and sorrow are banished.

[^1648]: Fol. 285v. Opening of the funeral Ikos in Tone 8 (*Са́мъ еди́нъ есѝ безсме́ртный* / *Thou alone art immortal*), attributed to St. Romanos the Melodist, juxtaposing God's uncreated eternity with mortal man's return to the dust of the earth.

[^1649]: Fol. 286r. Conclusion of the funeral Ikos, citing Genesis 3:19 (*Dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return*), acknowledging universal mortal dissolution transformed by faith into the funeral threnody of *Alleluia*.

[^1650]: Fol. 286r. Ode 7 of the Funeral Canon in Tone 8, opening with the incipit of the Heirmos *Дѣ́ти евре́йскїя въ пещѝ* (*The Hebrew children in the furnace boldly trod the flame*), based on Daniel 3.

[^1651]: Fol. 286r. Martyrikon troparion of Ode 7, commemorating the martyrs who directed all their desire to Christ alone, enduring torments while chanting the ancestral refrain of the Three Youths.

[^1652]: Fol. 286r. Troparion of Ode 7 petitioning that the departed servant be filled with celestial joy and gladness, joining the choir of the saints in praising the God of the fathers.

[^1653]: Fol. 286v. Troparion of Ode 7 petitioning for the departed the brightness of the heavenly Kingdom and the garment of incorruptibility (*нетлѣ́нїя оде́жду дару́я*), echoing the baptismal robe of immortality (Galatians 3:27).

[^1654]: Fol. 286v. Theotokion of Ode 7, highlighting the reversal of the ancestral curse of Eve through the Incarnation of Christ from the spotless Virgin Mother.

[^1655]: Fol. 286v. Ode 8 of the Funeral Canon in Tone 8, opening with the Heirmos incipit *Мусикї́йскихъ орга́новъ согла́сїе* (*The harmony of musical instruments sounded...*), recalling the Three Youths in Babylon defying Nebuchadnezzar's idolatrous music.

[^1656]: Fol. 286v. Martyrikon troparion of Ode 8, praising the martyrs who exchanged earthly afflictions for incorruptible crowns, chanting the universal canticle of Daniel 3:57.

[^1657]: Fol. 287r. Conclusion of the second troparion of Ode 8, celebrating the resurrection of all who rested in the grave by Christ's life-giving hand, and petitioning repose for the departed believer.

[^1658]: Fol. 287r. Troparion at *Glory...* in Ode 8, utilizing the Psalmic imagery of the "torrent of delight" (Psalm 35:9 LXX: *пото́комъ пи́щи Твоея̀ напои́ши я̀* / *torrente voluptatis tuae potabis eos*) and the inexhaustible fountain of life.

[^1659]: Fol. 287r. Theotokion of Ode 8, magnifying the Theotokos whose fleshly bearing of God brought salvation to humanity.

[^1660]: Fol. 287r. Ode 9 of the Funeral Canon in Tone 8, opening with the incipit of the Heirmos *Устраши́ся всякъ слухъ* (*Every hearing was affrighted at the ineffable condescension of God*), based on the Canticle of the Theotokos / Magnificat and Habakkuk 3.

[^1661]: Fol. 287v. Conclusion of the Martyrikon of Ode 9, depicting the martyrs in heaven illuminated by the uncreated radiant beams of the Holy Trinity (*просвѣща́еми тро́ичными заря́ми*).

[^1662]: Fol. 287v. Troparion of Ode 9 meditating on the harrowing of Hades and petitioning Christ to lead the departed soul into His "never-setting light" (*невече́рнему свѣ́ту* / *φῶς ἀνέσπερον*).

[^1663]: Fol. 287v. Troparion at *Glory...* in Ode 9, adapting the language of the Song of Songs (5:16: *ὅλος ἐπιθυμία* / *ве́сь жела́нїе*) to Christ, confessing Him as absolute sweetness, desire, insatiable love, and ineffable beauty.

[^1664]: Fol. 288r. Conclusion of the Theotokion of Ode 9, formulating classical Chalcedonian Christology: Christ is dual in nature (*согу́ба естество́мъ* / *διπλοῦν τῇ φύσει*) but not in person/hypostasis (*а не соста́вомъ* / *ἀλλ' οὐ τῇ ὑποστάσει*), the only-begotten of the Father and firstborn of all creation (Colossians 1:15).

[^1665]: Fol. 288r. Katavasia of Ode 9, chanting the Heirmos *Every hearing was affrighted* in full as the solemn conclusion of the Funeral Canon.

[^1666]: Fol. 288r. Rubric directing the Trisagion Prayers and the Lord's Prayer, followed by the four funeral troparia in Tone 4 (*Съ ду́хи пра́ведныхъ сконча́вшихся* / *With the spirits of the righteous*), traditionally sung at every pannikhida, litiya, and burial office.

[^1667]: Fol. 288v. Second funeral troparion in Tone 4 (*Въ поко́ищи Твое́мъ, Го́споди* / *In Thy resting place, O Lord*), asking that the departed soul be gathered among the saints in eternal rest.

[^1668]: Fol. 288v. Third funeral troparion in Tone 4 at *Glory...* (*Ты есѝ Богъ соше́дый во адъ* / *Thou art God Who descended into Hades*), celebrating Christ's liberation of the captive souls bound in chains.

[^1669]: Fol. 288v. Concluding funeral Theotokion in Tone 4 at *Both now...* (*Еди́на чи́стая и непоро́чная Дѣ́во* / *O only pure and spotless Virgin*).

[^1670]: Fol. 288v. Rubric and opening petitions of the Litany of Fervent Supplication for the Departed (*Дїа́конства*), beginning with the initial petition based on Psalm 50:3 (*Поми́луй насъ, Бо́же* / *Have mercy on us, O God*), followed by the specific petition commemorating the deceased by name (*и́мя рекъ*).

[^1671]: Fol. 289r. Continuation of the diaconal litany for the departed, petitioning remission of all sins, placement of the spirit among the righteous, and concluding with the committal of all life unto Christ God.

[^1672]: Fol. 289r. Rubric directing the priest to recite the Prayer for the Departed secretly (*Свяще́нникъ моли́твы та́й*) while the litany is concluded.

[^1673]: Fol. 289r. The classical Byzantine Funeral Prayer *O God of spirits and of all flesh* (*Бо́же духо́въ и вся́кїя пло́ти*), attributed liturgically to Saint John Chrysostom and Saint Basil, praying for the repose of the departed in the mansions of light and life.

[^1674]: Fol. 289v. Conclusion of the prayer *O God of spirits*, citing Psalm 22:2 LXX (*In a place of verdure... by the water of repose*), Isaiah 35:10 (*Sorrow and sighing have fled away*), 1 Kings (3 Kingdoms) 8:46 / 2 Chronicles 6:36 (*There is no man that sins not*), and Psalm 118:142 LXX (*Thy righteousness is an everlasting righteousness, and Thy law is truth*).

[^1675]: Fol. 289v. Rubric indicating the priestly exclamation (*Возглаше́нїе*) concluding the silent prayer for the departed.

[^1676]: Fol. 289v. The Christological exclamation citing John 11:25 (*I am the resurrection and the life*), uniting the commemoration of the deceased with the Trinitarian doxology; completed on fol. 290r (p591).

[^1677]: Dismissal formula concluding the Funeral / Memorial Singing (Parastas / Panikhida).

[^1678]: Physical leaf p591 (fol. 287r). Pre-Nikonian / Ruthenian dismissal text for the departed, invoking the abodes of the righteous (*въ ѡбителехъ праведныхъ*) and the bosom of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

[^1679]: Physical leaf p592 (fol. 287v). The ritual chanting of "Memory Eternal" (*Вѣчная память / Mnēmosynon aionion*) concludes the memorial order for deceased brethren.

[^1680]: Physical leaf p593 (fol. 288r). *Чи́нъ быва́емый на ѡдѣꙗ́нїи ра́сы* (Gk. *Ἀκολουθία εἰς ῥασоφοροῦντα*). This order constitutes the novice's or candidate's tonsure and clothing into the inner rassa (cassock) and kamilavka, known as the ryasophore rank (*расофор*), prior to the Little Schema.

[^1681]: Physical leaf p594 (fol. 288v). LXX Psalm 26:1–4 (MT Ps 27). Monastic investiture psalm expressing reliance upon the Lord in spiritual warfare and the aspiration to dwell in His temple.

[^1682]: Physical leaf p596 (fol. 289v). LXX Psalm 26:9–14 (MT Ps 27).

[^1683]: Physical leaf p596 (fol. 289v). LXX Psalm 50 (MT Ps 51), the primary penitential psalm of the Byzantine rite.

[^1684]: Physical leaf p596 (fol. 289v). Troparion of the Holy Fathers, Tone 4 (*Боже отецъ нашихъ* / *Ὁ Θεὸς τῶν πατέρων ἡμῶν*).

[^1685]: Physical leaf p597 (fol. 290r). Slavonic: *по твоему смотрению* (Gk. *κατὰ τὴν σὴν ἐπιείκειαν* / *κατὰ τὴν σὴν οἰκονομίαν*, "according to Thy gentleness/forbearance").

[^1686]: Physical leaf p597 (fol. 290r). Slavonic witness: *въ смире́нїи оу́строи живо́тъ на́шъ* ("in humility direct/order our life"), where standard modern recensions read *въ ми́рѣ упра́ви*.

[^1687]: Physical leaf p597 (fol. 290r). Theotokion, Tone 4 (*Къ Богородицѣ прилѣжно нынѣ притецемъ* / *Τῇ Θεοτόκῳ ἐκтеνῶς νῦν προσδράμωμεν*).

[^1688]: Physical leaf p597 (fol. 290r). The rubric designates the monastery superior (*игоуменъ*) to read the prayer over the candidate.

[^1689]: Physical leaf p598 (fol. 290v). First prayer of investiture (Gk. *Εὐχαριστοῦμέν σοι, Κύριε ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν...*). Note the designation of the monastic path as the "angelic life" (*въ агг҃льско семъ житїи* / *ἐν τῇ ἀγγελικῇ ταύτῃ πολιτείᾳ*).

[^1690]: Physical leaf p599 (fol. 291r). Second prayer of investiture (Gk. *Εἰς τὸν ζυγόν σου τὸν σωτήριον πρόσδεξαι, Δέσποτα...*).

[^1691]: Physical leaf p599 (fol. 291r). Slavonic: *дх҃ѡвны твоихъ да́рѡ съвръша́я да́ръ* (perfecting the gift of Thy spiritual gifts).

[^1692]: Physical leaf p599 (fol. 291r). The candidate personally presents the shears (*но́жицѣ*) to the hegumen, signifying voluntary surrender and obedience. The tonsure is made cruciformly upon four sides of the head.

[^1693]: Physical leaf p600 (fol. 291v). While the candidate is tonsured by the monastic brethren, the community chants Psalm 50.

[^1694]: Physical leaf p600 (fol. 291v). The candidate is invested in the rassa (*ряса* / Gk. *ῥάσον*) and kamilavka (*камилавка* / Gk. *καμηλαύκιον*). The rubric specifies that during the reading of the Epistle (*прочита́емꙋ а́пл҃у*), the newly clothed monk exchanges the kiss of peace with the brotherhood before the final dismissal.

[^1695]: Physical leaf p600 (fol. 291v). Dismissal Prayer of the Rassa (*Мл҃тва ѡпусти́лнаѧ* / Gk. *Εὐχὴ ἀπολυτική*), continuing on leaf p601 (*...narrow path wherein the holy fathers entered...*).

[^1696]: Physical leaf p601 (fol. 292r). Conclusion of the Dismissal Prayer of the Rassa (*Мл҃тва ѡпусти́лнаѧ*). The prayer evokes the narrow way of the holy fathers and requests divine grace upon the spirit, soul, and body of the candidate who has received the beginning of the holy habit (*нача́токъ ст҃го ѡ́браза*).

[^1697]: Physical leaf p602 (fol. 292v). *ПОСЛѢДОВАНЇЕ МАЛАГО ѠБРАЗА* (Gk. *Ἀκολουθία τοῦ μικροῦ σχήματος*). The Order of the Little Schema (or Little Habit), historically also designated as the Order of the Mantiya (*мантия*), constituting the full formal profession of monastic vows in the Byzantine-Ruthenian tradition.

[^1698]: Physical leaf p602 (fol. 292v). The striking of the wood (*оударе́нїе дре́ва слу́жбы*) refers to the liturgical sounding of the wooden semantron (*клепало* / *било* / Gk. *σήμαντρον*) to summon the brotherhood to the Hours and the Divine Liturgy, during which the tonsure is celebrated.

[^1699]: Physical leaf p602 (fol. 292v). The candidate divests himself in the church narthex (*притворъ*) of his customary secular or novice garments, symbolizing the putting off of the old man (cf. Ephesians 4:22; Colossians 3:9) before entering the nave for tonsure.

[^1700]: Physical leaf p603 (fol. 293r). The rubric specifies that the candidate stands before the holy doors clothed only in a simple inner tunic (*срачица* / Gk. *χιτώνιον*), barefoot, unbelted, and bareheaded, expressing absolute voluntary poverty, penitence, and surrender before God.

[^1701]: Physical leaf p603 (fol. 293r). The tonsure is integrated into the Little Entrance of the Divine Liturgy. Following the entrance, after the kontakion of the day at "Glory...", this special penitential troparion is chanted at "Now and ever...".

[^1702]: Physical leaf p603 (fol. 293r). Monastic tonsure troparion, Tone 1: *Ѡбъꙗ́тїа ѿча ѿвръстѝ ми потщи́сѧ* (Gk. *Τὰς πατρικὰς ἀγκάλας διανοῖξαί μοι σπεῦσον*), directly adapted from the parable of the Prodigal Son (Luke 15:11–32).

[^1703]: Physical leaf p604 (fol. 293v). While the brethren chant the troparion *Ѡбъꙗ́тїа ѿча* thrice, the candidate prostrates himself cruciformly upon the floor before the Royal Doors where the hegumen stands.

[^1704]: Physical leaf p604 (fol. 293v). Lighted tapers/candles are distributed to the brotherhood standing near the central pillars (*стлъпѡ́къ*), symbolizing the light of good works and the illumination of the angelic life.

[^1705]: Physical leaf p604 (fol. 293v). The catechetical exhortation and preliminary examination of monastic vows begins with the words of Christ: Matthew 11:28–29.

[^1706]: Physical leaf p605 (fol. 294r). Matthew 11:29.

[^1707]: Physical leaf p605 (fol. 294r). The hegumen solemnly warns the candidate that Christ, the Mother of God, and the heavenly host are invisibly present, and that judgment will be rendered not merely on verbal promises, but on actual observance of ascetic struggle.

[^1708]: Physical leaf p606 (fol. 294v). The rubric provides that if the monastery hegumen is an ordained hieromonk (*іере́й*), he conducts the interrogation himself; if he is not ordained, an ordained priest conducts the examination.

[^1709]: Physical leaf p606 (fol. 294v). The candidate articulates his primary monastic motive: desire for the ascetic/fasting life (*житїа по́стническаго* / Gk. *ἀσκητικοῦ βίου*).

[^1710]: Physical leaf p607 (fol. 295r). Traditional monastic interrogation formula: *Въи́стинноу добро̀ дѣ́ло и бл҃же́нно избра́ єси* (Gk. *Ὄντως καλὸν ἔργον καὶ μακάριον ἐξελέξω, ἀλλ᾽ ἐὰν καὶ τελειώσῃς αὐτό...*).

[^1711]: Physical leaf p607 (fol. 295r). Interrogation confirming free will: the candidate must affirm that he is not entering monastic life under compulsion, debt, fear of civil punishment, or worldly distress.

[^1712]: Physical leaf p607 (fol. 295r). The vow of renunciation of the world (*Ѡрица́еши ли сѧ ми́ра*), grounded in 1 John 2:15–17.

[^1713]: Physical leaf p608 (fol. 295v). The three fundamental monastic vows: lifelong perseverance / stability of place (*stabilitas loci*), chastity/virginity (*дѣтство и цѣломудрїе*), and obedience (*послушанїе*).

[^1714]: Physical leaf p608 (fol. 295v). The solemn catechetical instruction (*Та́же ѻглаше́нїе* / Gk. *Κατήχησις*) delivered by the priest/hegumen immediately following the examination of vows.

[^1715]: Physical leaf p609 (fol. 296r). The vows are described as an irrevocable written record inscribed by the holy angels, to be examined before the judgment seat of Christ at His Second Coming.

[^1716]: Physical leaf p609 (fol. 296r). The monastic way is termed "the most perfect life" (*съвръше́нное житїѐ* / Gk. *τελειοτάτη πολιτεία*) because it strives for the direct imitation of Christ's earthly life.

[^1717]: Physical leaf p609 (fol. 296r). 2 Corinthians 7:1: "Having therefore these promises, dearly beloved, let us cleanse ourselves from all filthiness of the flesh and spirit, perfecting holiness in the fear of God."

[^1718]: Physical leaf p610 (fol. 296v). Practical ascetical instruction detailing vigilance against demonic thoughts (*помысли* / Gk. *λογισμοί*), steadfastness in fasting, patience in sickness, and perseverance in prayer and vigils, continuing on leaf p611.

[^1719]: Physical leaf p611 (fol. 297r). Allusion to Luke 9:62: "No man, having put his hand to the plough, and looking back, is fit for the kingdom of God." The instruction warns the monastic novice that regression into worldly preoccupations forfeits the heavenly calling.

[^1720]: Physical leaf p611 (fol. 297r). Allusion to Christ's evangelical demands in Matthew 10:37 ("He that loves father or mother more than Me is not worthy of Me") and Luke 14:26.

[^1721]: Physical leaf p612 (fol. 297v). 2 Timothy 2:3: "Thou therefore endure hardness, as a good soldier of Jesus Christ." The passage also draws directly upon 2 Corinthians 8:9: "For ye know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that, though He was rich, yet for your sakes He became poor, that ye through His poverty might be rich."

[^1722]: Physical leaf p612 (fol. 297v). Direct citation of the Dominical logion in Matthew 16:24 (cf. Mark 8:34; Luke 9:23): "If any man will come after Me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow Me."

[^1723]: Physical leaf p613 (fol. 298r). Allusion to the eighth and ninth Beatitudes (Matthew 5:11–12; Luke 6:22–23): "Blessed are ye, when men shall revile you... Rejoice, and be exceeding glad: for great is your reward in heaven."

[^1724]: Physical leaf p614 (fol. 298v). Direct scriptural citation of Isaiah 49:15: "Can a woman forget her sucking child, that she should not have compassion on the son of her womb? yea, they may forget, yet will I not forget thee."

[^1725]: Physical leaf p615 (fol. 299r). Commemoration of the historic archetypes of Byzantine coenobitic and eremitic monasticism: St. Anthony the Great (†356), St. Euthymius the Great (†473), and St. Sabbas the Sanctified (†532). The cinnabar rubric *А҆ жена́мъ* ("And for women") supplies the feminine monastic equivalents: St. Thecla the Protomartyr, St. Euphraxia of Tabennisi, and St. Olympias the Deaconess.

[^1726]: Physical leaf p616 (fol. 299v). The ritual laying of the Sluzhebnik (*ѻ҆бразосло́вїе*, Gk. *εὐχολόγιον*) upon the bowed head of the candidate during the priestly prayer, symbolizing the imposition of the liturgical yoke and ecclesiastical transmission of monastic discipline.

[^1727]: Physical leaf p618 (fol. 300v). Allusion to Romans 12:1 ("present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable unto God") and Matthew 11:29–30 ("Take My yoke upon you... For My yoke is easy, and My burden is light").

[^1728]: Physical leaf p619 (fol. 301r). The solemn warning before the Holy Gospel affirming that monastic tonsure is strictly voluntary and that no coercion or external constraint has compelled the candidate to take the vows of the angelic habit (*вели́каго а҆гг҃лскаго чи́на*).

[^1729]: Physical leaf p620 (fol. 301v). Allusion to 1 Timothy 2:4: "Who will have all men to be saved, and to come unto the knowledge of the truth." The ceremonial taking and handing of the shears from the Holy Gospel is performed thrice to signify unconditional submission to the divine will and Christ Himself.

[^1730]: Physical leaf p621 (fol. 302r). Allusion to Isaiah 61:10: "He hath clothed me with the garments of salvation, He hath covered me with the robe of righteousness, as a bridegroom decks himself with ornaments." The monastic habit (rason/chiton) is designated the "garment of gladness" (*риза веселия*), symbolizing the joyous putting off of worldly decay.

[^1731]: Physical leaf p621 (fol. 302r). Allusion to Ephesians 6:14 ("having your loins girt about with truth") and Colossians 3:5 ("Mortify therefore your members which are upon the earth"). The rubric designates this vesting as the paramand (*парамандътъ*), accompanied by the formula of girding the loins unto the mortification of the flesh and spiritual renewal.

[^1732]: Physical leaf p621 (fol. 302r). Allusion to 1 Thessalonians 5:8 ("and for an helmet, the hope of salvation") and Ephesians 6:17 ("take the helmet of salvation"). The monastic head covering (klobuk / koukoulion) signifies the protection of the mind against demonic assault.

[^1733]: Physical leaf p622 (fol. 302v). The formula designates the reception of the paramand (*парамантъ*) as the solemn betrothal of the great angelic schema (*обручение великаго агглскаго образа, въ одежду нетлѣния и чистоты*). In Byzantine-Slavic monastic theology, the Lesser Schema (*малый образ*) functions as an earnest or betrothal anticipating the full ascetical perfection of the Great Schema.

[^1734]: Physical leaf p622 (fol. 302v). Direct citation of Ephesians 6:15: "And your feet shod with the preparation of the gospel of peace." The monastic sandals signify readiness to walk in the paths of evangelical obedience without hindrance.

[^1735]: Physical leaf p622 (fol. 302v). The formula for investing the candidate in the monastic mantle (*mandyas* / *pallium*), reiterating the reception of the betrothal of the great angelic habit.

[^1736]: Physical leaf p623 (fol. 303r). Citing 1 Peter 2:25: "For ye were as sheep going astray; but are now returned unto the Shepherd and Bishop [Gk. ἐπίσκοπος; ChSl. посѣтитель] of your souls." The prayer also draws upon 1 Corinthians 2:9 ("the things which God hath prepared for them that love Him") and Galatians 6:14 ("crucified unto the world").

[^1737]: Physical leaf p624 (fol. 303v). Rubrical directive specifying the bifurcation of the monastic tonsure rite: when celebrated independently outside the Divine Liturgy, the litany, Epistle, and Gospel are inserted directly; when celebrated within the Divine Liturgy, the readings are integrated into the Liturgy of the Word.

[^1738]: Physical leaf p625 (fol. 304r). Citing Galatians 3:27: "For as many of you as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ." Sung here crosswise as the newly tonsured monk is led into the midst of the brethren, manifesting the tonsure as a reaffirmation and seal of baptismal illumination.

[^1739]: Physical leaf p625 (fol. 304r). Prokeimenon in Tone 3, citing Psalm 26:1 (LXX; MT 27:1): "The Lord is my illumination and my Savior; whom shall I fear? The Lord is the defender of my life; of whom shall I be afraid?"

[^1740]: Physical leaf p626 (fol. 304v). The Epistle pericope Ephesians 6:10–17, expounding the whole armor of God (*panoplia* / *всеоружие*), which forms the spiritual foundation for each monastic garment and weapon of spiritual warfare.

[^1741]: Physical leaf p627 (fol. 305r). Alleluia verse citing Psalm 33:7 (LXX; MT 34:6): "This poor man cried, and the Lord heard him, and saved him out of all his afflictions."

[^1742]: Physical leaf p627 (fol. 305r). The monastic Gospel pericope combining Matthew 10:37–38 and Matthew 11:28–30, articulating the cost and reward of discipleship: forsaking familial attachments, taking up the cross, and entering into Christ's restful yoke.

[^1743]: Physical leaf p629 (fol. 306r). Dominical logion from Matthew 16:24 (cf. Mark 8:34; Luke 9:23) spoken at the delivery of the hand cross unto the newly tonsured monk.

[^1744]: Physical leaf p629 (fol. 306r). Dominical logion from Matthew 5:16 spoken at the delivery of the lighted wax candle unto the newly tonsured monk, signifying the light of good works and evangelical witness.

[^1745]: Physical leaf p629 (fol. 306r). The classical tonsure idiomelon (*Да познаимъ братие тайны силу* / Gk. Ἐπιγνῶμεν, ἀδελфоί, τοῦ μυστηρίου τὴν δύναμιν), based upon Christ's parable of the Prodigal Son (Luke 15:11–32). The brethren bestow the fraternal kiss of peace upon the new monk while this hymn is chanted.

[^1746]: Physical leaf p630 (fol. 306v). Allusion to Luke 15:23–24 and 1 Corinthians 5:7: the slain fatted calf of the parable is mystically interpreted as Christ Himself, the sacrificed Victim whose death brings joy to the heavenly hosts and salvation unto penitents.

[^1747]: Physical leaf p630 (fol. 306v). The concluding rubric prescribing that the newly tonsured monk remain in the church for five full days in continuous ascetical contemplation, prayer, and reading of the Scriptures, sequestered from all worldly and manual labors.

[^1748]: In the 1606 Striatyn Trebnyk (fol. 306r), this begins the Order of the Great Angelic Habit (Μεγαлоσχημοσύνη / Великий ангельский образ), the highest degree of monastic asceticism and tonsure.

[^1749]: Church Slavonic: "въ ст҃ы́й же́ртвенникъ" (into the holy sanctuary / altar area; Greek: εἰς τὸ ἅγιον θυσιαστήριον), inside of which stands the Holy Table (трапе́за / ἁγία τράπεζα).

[^1750]: Church Slavonic: "на подно́жїе ст҃ыѧ трапе́зы" (at the foot / base of the Holy Table). In Byzantine practice, the habit of the Great Schema (the analavos, koukoulion, and paramandyas) is placed before the Holy Table on the preceding evening, sanctified by proximity to the Holy Gifts throughout the night and during the preparatory Matins service.

[^1751]: Acrostic (Church Slavonic: краегра́нїе; Greek: ἀκροστιχίς): "Εὐδόκιμον τέλος εὐδοκίμῳ μοι γενομένῳ Χριστὲ παράσχου" ("Grant a well-proven / well-pleasing end unto me that am well-proven, O Christ"). The canon is traditionally ascribed to St. Theodore the Studite.

[^1753]: Ode 1, Troparion 2: An allusion to Christ's words in Matthew 11:29–30: "Take My yoke upon you, and learn of Me... For My yoke is easy, and My burden is light."

[^1754]: Ode 3 Heirmos incipit of Tone 2: "Establish us in Thee, O Lord, Who by the Tree didst slay sin, and plant the fear of Thee in the hearts of us who sing praises unto Thee."

[^1755]: Physical print slightly rubbed in lines 8–10; text restored from standard Ruthenian and Byzantine witnesses: "Ѡ҆цѣлѝ Хрїсте́ к тебѣ̀ притѣка́ющаго [раба̀], и҆ сего̀ житїю̀ пр[пⷣ]бныхъ спо[до́би], бл҃го[чⷭ҇т]но и҆ пра́ведно пожи́ти" (Greek: Ἴασαι, Χριστέ, τὸν πρὸς σὲ καταφεύγοντα δοῦλον...).

[^1757]: Physical leaf slightly worn in lines 14–15; collated with early Cyrillic and Greek euchologia: "Е҆ди́не [не] хотѧ́й сме́рти чл҃кѡ[мъ], [млⷭ҇рдне], твое́го раба̀ тебѣ̀ припада́ющаго, ли́коу ст҃ы́хъ съпричтѝ" (Greek: Ὁ μόνος μὴ θέλων τὸν θάνατον τῶν ἀνθρώπων, οἰκτίρμων...). [^1760]: Ode 4 Heirmos incipit of Tone 2: "I have heard, O Lord, the report of Thy dispensation, and I glorified Thee, Who alone art the Lover of mankind" (Hab. 3:2).

[^1762]: Gal. 3:13; Eph. 1:7.

[^1763]: John 11:1–44; 1 Cor. 15:55–56.

[^1764]: Ode 5 Heirmos incipit of Tone 2: "O Giver of light and Creator of the ages, Lord, guide us in the light of Thy commandments; for we know none other God save Thee" (Isa. 26:9).
