[^1766]: Ode 6 Theotokion: A bold Patristic-ascetic trope where the tonsure into the monastic habit is likened to being received anew as an innocent newborn infant from the womb of the Mother of God, echoing the archetype of the Schema as spiritual regeneration.

[^1767]: Kontakion of the Great Schema, Tone 1. Incipit: "О҆бъѧ́тїа ѻ҆́ч҃а ѿврьсти́ ми потщи́сѧ" (Greek: Τὰς πατρικὰς ἀγκάλας διανοῖξαί μοι σπεῦσον). Luke 15:18, 21.

[^1768]: Ode 7 Heirmos incipit of Tone 2: "Unto the golden image the all-wise children would not serve, but went into the midst of the flame and mocked their gods, singing: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers" (Dan. 3:18).

[^1769]: Dan. 3:52; Titus 3:5.

[^1770]: Ps. 72:23–24 [LXX]; Ps. 138:10 [LXX].

[^1771]: Common Patristic nautical metaphor representing the Cross as the mast and sail, and the Holy Spirit as the wind guiding the ascetic ship of the soul into the calm haven of salvation.

[^1772]: Luke 1:42.

[^1773]: Ode 8 Heirmos incipit of Tone 2: "The furnace ablaze with fire of old in Babylon divided its operation: burning the Chaldeans at the divine command, but bedewing the faithful as they sang: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord" (Dan. 3:49–50, 57).

[^1774]: Dan. 3:57 (The Song of the Three Holy Children / Benedicite: "Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord; sing praise and exalt Him above all forever"). Continued on physical leaf p641.

[^1775]: The conclusion of the final troparion of Ode 8, quoting the refrain of the Canticle of the Three Holy Children (LXX Daniel 3:57). The physical text ink witness has the contracted form "превъзно́те" for "превъзносите" (sing and exalt).

[^1776]: In Byzantine and Ruthenian ascetic theology, the monastic habit (and preeminently the Great Schema) is understood as a second baptism (*secunda baptismus*), wherein baptismal grace and the pristine garment of righteousness are renewed through repentance.

[^1777]: Slavonic: "ѻ҆́браза ра́ди лоу́чшаго, ᲂу҆дале́нїемъ го́ршаго" (for the sake of the better habit, by departing from the worse). The "better habit" designates the angelic habit of the Great Schema, as opposed to worldly attachment and fleshly lusts.

[^1778]: Slavonic: "хꙋдо́житвомъ чл҃колю́бїа, и҆ премнѡ́гыѧ ти бла́гости" (by the craftsmanship/dispensation of loving-kindness and Thine exceeding goodness).

[^1779]: Alluding to Colossians 2:14 ("blotting out the handwriting of ordinances that was against us"). Slavonic: "роукописа́нїе" (chirograph / certificate of debt / handwriting of sins).

[^1780]: Incipit of Ode 9 Heirmos, Tone 2: "Безнача́лна роди́телѧ сн҃ъ" (Greek: Ὁ τοῦ ἀνάρχου Γεννήτορος Υἱός Θεὸς καὶ Κύριος). The incipit is preserved unexpanded per Mandate 16.

[^1781]: Cf. Ephesians 4:1 ("that ye walk worthy of the vocation wherewith ye are called").

[^1782]: The physical print bears supralinear correction characters: "чⷭ҇ты[мъ] срⷣце[мъ]" (with a pure heart) resolving the base line "чты̀ срⷣце". The phrase continues onto p643.

[^1783]: Cf. Matthew 11:28 ("Come unto Me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest").

[^1784]: Cf. Hebrews 4:16 ("Let us therefore come boldly unto the throne of grace, that we may obtain mercy, and find grace to help in time of need").

[^1785]: Slavonic: "съри́щющꙋю твое́моу хоте́нїю си́лоу" (Greek: συντρέχουσαν τῷ θελήματί σου δύναμιν), meaning having power equal to, running alongside, or fulfilling Thy sovereign will.

[^1786]: Slavonic: "доспѣ́ти всебл҃гоговѣ́йно, многомоле́бномꙋ концоу̀" (to attain in all piety unto the end prayed for / much-desired end).

[^1787]: Canonical 3-layer melodic model heading (Tone 2, Greek: Ὅτε ἐκ τοῦ ξύλου).

[^1788]: Rubrical witness indicating the alternative liturgical usage of singing these repentance and tonsure stichera at Vespers the evening prior, combined with the Menaion stichera of the commemorated saint.

[^1789]: Slavonic: "къ а҆́гг҃лскомꙋ гражда́нствоу семоу̀" (Greek: εἰς τὴν ἀγγελικὴν ταύτην πολιτείαν) — designating the monastic life as angelic citizenship or commonwealth.

[^1790]: Cf. Ezekiel 33:11 ("I have no pleasure in the death of the wicked; but that the wicked turn from his way and live").

[^1791]: Quoting Psalm 17:30 LXX ("For by Thee I shall be delivered from a troop; and by my God I shall leap over a wall"). Slavonic: "Стѣнꙋ̀ прелѣ́зꙋ ѡ҆ тебѣ̀, грѣха̀ мое́го сп҃се, и҆ и҆збавлюсѧ".

[^1792]: The classic Theotokion "Всѣмъ предстательствуеши, Благая" (Greek: Πάντων προστατεύεις, Ἀγαθή), widely sung at supplicatory services and tonsures.

[^1793]: That is, the Little Entrance of the Divine Liturgy.

[^1794]: Slavonic: "кали́гвы" (Latin: *caligae*; Greek: καλίγια) — monastic shoes or sandals. The removal of the head-covering and footwear symbolizes the humility, renunciation, and nakedness of the candidate standing before the holy altar, ready to put on Christ and the new man.

[^1795]: Slavonic: "Хотѣ́хъ слеза́ми ѻ҆чи́стити, мои́хъ грѣхопаде́нїи Гдⷭ҇и роукописа́нїе...". The refrain "Lord, before I perish utterly, save me" echoes the Great Canon of St. Andrew of Crete.

[^1796]: Ascetic trope presenting the monastic life as a storm-free harbor (*haven*) and spiritual infirmary (*remedy*).

[^1797]: Alluding to Psalm 118:176 LXX ("I have gone astray like a lost sheep; seek Thy servant").

[^1798]: Theotokion closing Antiphon 1.

[^1799]: Slavonic: "Въ и҆сто́чницѣ та́инѣмъ порожде́нїа, сп҃оположе́нїе прїи́мъ и҆ и҆збавле́нїе" — alluding to holy baptism as the "laver of regeneration" (Titus 3:5).

[^1800]: Alluding to Matthew 14:30-31 (the Apostle Peter sinking in the Sea of Galilee and crying: "Lord, save me! And immediately Jesus stretched forth His hand, and caught him").

[^1801]: Theotokion concluding Antiphon 2.

[^1802]: Ascetic troparion echoing the Funeral Idiomela of St. John of Damascus and quoting Matthew 16:24 / Mark 8:34.

[^1803]: Psalm 33:12 LXX. Printed incipit: "Прїидѣ́те ча́да послꙋ́шайте ме́[не]".

[^1804]: Direct quotation of the words of Christ from Matthew 11:28-29.

[^1805]: Psalm 118:176 LXX. Printed incipit: "Заблꙋди́хъ ꙗ҆́ко ѻ҆вча̀ погы́бшее".

[^1806]: Repeated troparion combining LXX Psalm 118:176 and John 10:11.

[^1807]: Psalm 94:6 LXX. Slavonic: "Прїидѣ́те поклони́мсѧ и҆ припадѣ́, и҆ въспла́чимся прѣⷣ Гм҃ъ сътво́ршимъ на́съ".

[^1808]: Rubric prescribing the candidate's solemn prostration (cruciform on the floor) before the Holy Doors of the iconostasis during the singing of the antiphons at the Liturgy, remaining prostrate until the celebrant bids him rise. Continued on leaf p651.

[^1809]: Ps. 79:15-16 LXX (Ps. 80:14-15 Masoretic). This solemn liturgical verse is sung as the concluding troparion of the third antiphon during the procession of the postulant unto the Holy Doors in the Order of the Great Schema (*Poslidovanie Velikaho Obraza*).

[^1810]: Standard Theotokion of the Great Schema antiphons, beseeching the intercession of the Virgin Mother of God.

[^1811]: Church Slavonic red rubric: *го́л[асъ] :* (Tone) or *го́л[осно] :* (aloud / chanted). In Ruthenian liturgical typography, the abbreviation *гол.* denotes either the musical Tone (*holos* / *glas*, here Tone 1 for the canonical penitential sessional hymn *Obiatiia otcha*) or an instruction to chant aloud.

[^1812]: Sessional Hymn (*Sedalen*) of the Prodigal Son, Tone 1 (*Obiatiia otcha otvrzsti mi potshchysia*), appointed in the Lenten Triodion (Sunday of the Prodigal Son) and in the monastic tonsure of the Great Schema; cf. Luke 15:18, 21.

[^1813]: Church Slavonic rubric: *Пото́мъ въста́вшоу|гомоу̀, въпраша́етъ и҆̀ іере́й гл҃ѧ :* (Then, when he has arisen, the priest questions him, saying). The participle spans the leaf division between p651 (*въста́вшоу-*) and p652 (*-гомоу̀*).

[^1814]: The initial interrogation (*voprosoposledovanie*) of the monastic candidate before the Holy Doors.

[^1815]: Church Slavonic: *по́стническаго житіа̀* (the ascetic life; lit. "fasting life").

[^1816]: Patristic exhortation by the presiding hieromonk/hegumen on the necessity of sustained ascetic labor and spiritual travail (*boliniiu ispraveliaiutsia*).

[^1817]: Canonical examination asserting that the candidate enters monasticism freely, without external coercion, debt, or secular compulsion; cf. Canon 43 of the Holy Apostles and Canon 40 of the Quinisext Council (in Trullo).

[^1818]: The solemn vow of renunciation of the world (*otritzanie mira*), grounded in 1 John 2:15-17.

[^1819]: The vow of monastic obedience (*poslushanie*) unto death toward the hegumen and the brotherhood.

[^1820]: The vow of endurance in afflictions and straits (*skorb i tisnotu*) for the sake of the Kingdom of Heaven; cf. Matthew 7:14; Acts 14:22.

[^1821]: Church Slavonic rubric: *И па́ки ѡ҆глаше́ніе .* (And again, the Catechesis / Admonition). The formal instructional address delivered by the hegumen or priest unto the postulant prior to the vows and tonsure.

[^1822]: The solemn reminder of the unseen presence of the Holy Angels recording the candidate's vows for the Day of Judgment.

[^1823]: The Great Schema defined as the mystical adoption of the Cross and daily mortification (*skazuiu ubo tebi vsesovorshennoie zhitie... razvi krsta i somrty obishchanie*); cf. Galatians 6:14.

[^1824]: Matthew 16:24; Mark 8:34; Luke 9:23.

[^1825]: Exhortation to voluntary poverty and ascetic struggle rather than bodily comfort.

[^1826]: Matthew 5:12; Luke 6:23.

[^1827]: The setting apart of the monastic from secular life before the face of God.

[^1828]: Philippians 3:20 (*our citizenship is in heaven*); Church Slavonic: *на́ше бо житіѐ по а҆п[осто]лоу на нб҃се́хъ е҆́стъ*.

[^1829]: Patristic theology of the monastic habit as a "second baptism" (*vtoroe krshchenie*) of repentance, renewing baptismal grace and accompanied by the joy of the Angels; cf. Luke 15:10, 23.

[^1830]: Ephesians 4:1 (*walk worthily of the vocation wherewith ye are called*).

[^1831]: Genesis 19:26; Luke 17:32 (*Remember Lot's wife*).

[^1832]: Proverbs 26:11; 2 Peter 2:22 (*The dog is turned to his own vomit again*).

[^1833]: Luke 9:62 (*No man, having put his hand to the plow, and looking back, is fit for the kingdom of God*).

[^1834]: Strict warning against apostasy, monastic instability (*xeniteia* violation), and breaking monastic vows.

[^1835]: Ecclesiastes 5:4-5 (5:3-4 LXX: *Better is it that thou shouldest not vow, than that thou shouldest vow and not pay*).

[^1836]: The admonition continues across the leaf boundary into p661 (*Page_0661.jpg*), warning of escalated demonic warfare following the assumption of the Great Habit.

[^1837]: An exhaustive monastic catalogue of cenobitic passions and sins of discord: disobedience (*neposlushanie*), contradiction/gainsaying (*prekoslovie*), pride (*grydynia*), strife (*rvenie*), jealousy (*revnost'*), envy (*zavist'*), wrath (*iarost'*), clamor (*klich'*), blasphemy/slander (*khula*), secret eating (*tainnoiadenie* / Greek *kryphophagia*), insolence/boldness (*drznovenie* / *parrhesia* in the pejorative sense), private friendships/cliques (*osobnoe druzhestvo*), insubordination/disorder (*bezchinie*), contentiousness (*liuboprenie*), murmuring (*roptanie*), whispering/backbiting (*sheptanie*), and private possession of petty things (*pritiazhanie osobnoe malyia i okaiannyia veshchi*), which violates the vow of complete poverty (*anektēmosynē*).

[^1838]: Colossians 3:6; Ephesians 5:6 (*for which things' sake the wrath of God comes on the children of disobedience*).

[^1839]: Church Slavonic: *дшамъ тлител[ь]* (*the corrupter / destroyer of souls*), designating the devil, who takes root within the cenobitic community through these hidden and divisive sins.

[^1840]: The corresponding cenobitic virtues: brotherly love (*philadelphia*), hesychastic stillness/silence (*bezmolvie* / *hēsychia*), meekness (*praotēs*), reverence (*eulabeia*), meditation upon Scripture (*meletē*), vigilance over the heart (*phylakē kardias* / *nēpsis*) against evil logismoi, ascetic labor according to strength (*ergon kata dynamin*), temperance (*enkrateia*), and enduring patience unto death (*hypomonē mechri thanatou*).

[^1841]: Confession of the secrets of the heart (*ispovedanie serdechnykh tain*) unto the spiritual father (*abba* / hegumen), rooted in Scriptural baptismal confession; cf. Matthew 3:6; Mark 1:5.

[^1842]: The final question of the catechetical examination before the tonsure of the Great and Angelic Schema, concluding the solemn vows.

[^1843]: Isaiah 49:15 (LXX: *Can a woman forget her sucking child... yet will I not forget thee, saith the Lord*).

[^1844]: The first solemn prayer of the Great Schema (*Vseshchedryi ubo Bog i mnogomilostivyi*), invoking the shelter and strengthening of the Lord over the newly tonsured schema-monk.

[^1845]: Psalm 60:4 LXX (61:3 Masoretic: *For Thou hast been a shelter for me, and a strong tower from the face of the enemy*).

[^1846]: Invocations of the great founding fathers of Eastern monasticism: Saint Antony the Great (c. 251–356, father of eremitic monasticism), Saint Euthymius the Great (377–473, organizer of Palestinian monasticism), and Saint Sabbas the Sanctified (439–532, author of the Jerusalem Typikon).

[^1847]: Rubric: the priest signs (*blesses*) the head of the candidate with the sign of the cross thrice, then bids the congregation to prayer.

[^1848]: The prayer *Syj Vladyko vsederzhiteliu* ("O Thou Who art, Master Almighty"): an exalted theological synthesis confessing the Holy Trinity—the living and hypostatic Word (*sostavnym slovom*) and the proceeding Holy Spirit—and the heavenly liturgy of the Cherubim and Seraphim; cf. Daniel 7:10; Isaiah 6:2-3.

[^1849]: John 1:9 (*That was the true Light, which lights every man that comes into the world*).

[^1850]: Hebrews 12:22-23 (*the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, and to an innumerable company of angels, to the general assembly and church of the firstborn*).

[^1851]: Ruthenian recension reads *ѿ пр[а́]родителей да́ру с[ы]ноположе́ніа* (*from [his] forebears/ancestors the gift of adoption*); Greek Euchologion witnesses *ἐκ παλιγγενεσίας χάριτι τῆς υἱοθεσίας* (*from regeneration the gift of adoption*), reflecting an archaic Slavonic variant translation or glossing of *παλιγγενεσία* in early liturgical antigraphs.

[^1852]: Ephesians 6:12 (*For we wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against principalities, against powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this world, against spiritual wickedness in high places*).

[^1853]: Ephesians 6:14-17: the complete spiritual armory of the Christian ascetic—the girdle of truth, the breastplate of righteousness, the shoes of the gospel of peace, the shield of faith quenching the fiery darts of the devil, the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the Spirit, which is the Word of God.

[^1854]: Romans 8:26 (*the Spirit Itself makes intercession for us with groanings which cannot be uttered*) and Acts 9:15 (*he is a chosen vessel unto Me*).

[^1855]: 1 Thessalonians 5:5 (*Ye are all the children of light, and the children of the day*) and 1 Corinthians 1:30 (*Christ Jesus, Who of God is made unto us wisdom, and righteousness, and sanctification, and redemption*).

[^1856]: Ephesians 4:22-24 (*That ye put off concerning the former conversation the old man, which is corrupt according to the deceitful lusts... and that ye put on the new man, which after God is created in righteousness and true holiness*).

[^1857]: Galatians 6:14, 17 (*I bear in my body the marks of the Lord Jesus; the world is crucified unto me, and I unto the world*); Galatians 1:10 (*for if I yet pleased men, I should not be the servant of Christ*).

[^1858]: 2 Peter 1:6-7 (the ladder of divine virtues) and Ephesians 5:19 (psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs).

[^1859]: Rubric: the shears/scissors (*nozhnitsi*) are deposited upon the Holy Gospel book upon the Holy Table or analogion, symbolizing that the candidate receives the monastic tonsure not from human hands, but from Christ Himself.

[^1860]: A contemporary 17th-century Ruthenian reader's marginal inscription in semi-uncial/cursive hand: *Помилуй мя Бже по велицей милости твоей* (Psalm 50:1 LXX).

[^1861]: Opening petition of the second tonsure prayer (*Sviatyi Gospodi sil, Otche Gospoda nashego Isusa Khrista*), asking for the grace of the governing Spirit (*pneuma hēgemonikon* / *dukh vladychii*; Psalm 50:14 LXX) and entrance into the spiritual bridechamber (*nymphōn* / *nevistnyk*); continuing across the leaf boundary into p671 (*Page_0671.jpg*).

[^1862]: Slav. въ съкрыше́нїствѣ (vъ sъkryšenistvě), an archaic recensional variant formed on the root съкруша́ти / сокруше́нїе (contrition, brokenness of heart; cf. Ps. 50:19 LXX: се́рдце сокруше́нно и смире́нно).

[^1863]: Slav. въ хꙋдо́житвѣ (vъ xudožitvě), an Early Modern Ruthenian variant of художество, designating spiritual craftsmanship, ascetical mastery, or disciplined monastic praxis (Gk. τέхνη τῶν τεχνῶν, "art of arts").

[^1864]: The printed witness abbreviates съ пр҃ты (sъ pr[ěsvę]ty[mъ]) with a titlo, denoting the All-Holy (Пресвяты́й) Spirit, co-equal with the Father and the Son.

[^1865]: The rubric prescribes that the priest extend his right hand directly over the Holy Gospel resting on the analogion/tetrapod, signifying Christ's invisible presence and ratification of the monastic vow.

[^1866]: The outer margin of leaf 672 preserves a faint 17th-century contemporary cursive pen trial or liturgical cue in Ruthenian Skoropis: [Господи...] ([O Lord...]).

[^1867]: In this Ruthenian monastic recension, the candidate hands the scissors to the hegumen (пода́вшоу же є҆моу̀ нѡ́жицѣ и҆гꙋ́менові), from whose hand the presiding priest then takes them (И҆ взе́мъ їерѣй нѡ́жицѣ ѿ рꙋкѝ и҆гꙋ́меновы), reflecting the collegial participation of the local archimandrite or hegumen alongside the officiating hieromonk.

[^1868]: 1 Tim. 2:4.

[^1869]: The Ruthenian recension employs the traditional Byzantine third-person indicative active formula for the tonsure: Бра́тъ на́шъ и҆́мѧ ре́къ пострига́ет вла́сы главы̀ своеѧ̀ ("Our brother N. shears the hair of his head"), accompanied by the congregational response: рцѣ́мъ въсѝ ѻ҆ не́мъ: Гдⷭ҇и поми́лꙋй.

[^1870]: The investiture in the inner monastic robe or tunic (хитон / риза правды), invoking Isa. 61:10.

[^1871]: The paramandyas (парама́нтъ) of the Great Schema is a square cloth emblazoned with the instruments of the Passion, worn across the back and bound to the chest by cords, symbolizing the yoke of Christ and continuous mortification.

[^1872]: The cowl or pointed hood of the Great Schema (коу́коль беззло́бїа, "koukoulion of innocence"), embroidered with crosses and seraphim, interpreted liturgically as the helmet of saving hope (cf. 1 Thess. 5:8; Eph. 6:17).

[^1873]: The printed witness exhibits a mechanical truncation: а҆нала́, (analá,), an evident typographical defect for а҆нала́въ (analávъ; Gk. ἀνάλαβος). The analavos is the distinctive cruciform scapular of the Great Schema adorned with crosses, representing taking up the Cross upon one's shoulders (въспрїемлаѧ крⷭ҇тъ своѝ нара́мо).

[^1874]: The leather belt (пояс), symbolizing chastity, readiness for spiritual battle, and the mortification of carnal passions (cf. Luke 12:35; Eph. 6:14).

[^1875]: The monastic sandals or shoes (санда́лїа), signifying preparation to walk in the way of the Gospel of peace (cf. Eph. 6:15).

[^1876]: The concluding proclamation of the investiture, confirming that the monk has now fully received the Great Angelic Habit (вели́кїй а҆́гг҃лскїй ѻ́бразъ).

[^1877]: A vesting troparion in Tone 4 synthesizing the Pauline armor of God (Eph. 6:11–17) with the dominical promise of rest unto souls (Matt. 11:29).

[^1878]: Isa. 61:10 (LXX: 61:10).

[^1879]: The opening of the first major post-investiture euchological prayer over the newly tonsured schemamonk, invoking divine steadfastness and perseverance in the ascetic citizenship.

[^1880]: This prayer mystagogically reiterates each item of the Schema vestments (robe of righteousness, belt of mortification, koukoulion of humility, analavos of faith, sandals of peace) as spiritual armor against demonic powers.

[^1881]: Elijah the Tishbite and St. John the Forerunner are cited in Byzantine euchological tradition as the biblical archetypes and prototypic exemplars of the celibate, wilderness-dwelling monastic life.

[^1882]: 2 Tim. 4:7.

[^1883]: The printed witness features a dittography: оу҆слы́шитъ бл҃же́ннаго гла́са . гла́са . ("and may hear the blessed voice, voice"), which is regularized in translation while preserved in the epigraphic record.

[^1884]: Matt. 25:34.

[^1885]: The prayer of the inclination of heads (молитва главоприклонения), invoking Christ as the Good Shepherd and Overseer (пастырь и посѣтитель; cf. 1 Pet. 2:25) to preserve the candidate who has crucified himself to the world (cf. Gal. 6:14).

[^1886]: An important rubrical directive stipulating that if the Great Schema is conferred outside the Divine Liturgy, a special diaconal litany (настоѧ́щїа дїа́конства), followed by the Epistle and Gospel, must be celebrated.

[^1887]: The litany petitions are printed in the historical source as abbreviated incipits (e.g. Ѡ҆ съвы́шнеⷨ ми́рѣ, и҆ ѡ҆ сп҃се́нїи дꙋ́шъ), preserved here without unwritten additions in strict conformity with Rule 16.

[^1888]: Leaf 680 concludes with the incomplete word на- (na-), which is completed on leaf 681 as намѣре́нїе (naměrenie; "intent" or "purpose") of the monastic habit.

[^1889]: Slav. пристрѣ́тїѧ (pristrětija), an epigraphic recensional variant or typographical defect for пристра́стїѧ (pristrastija; Gk. προσпаθείας), denoting worldly affection or passionate attachment to kinsfolk according to the flesh.

[^1890]: Slav. вы́шше мирскыхъ мꙋдрова́нїи (vyšše mirskyxъ mudrovanij; Gk. ἀνώτερον τῶν κοσμικῶν φρονημάτων), referring to transcending earthly, carnal calculations and mindsets.

[^1891]: Eph. 4:22–24; Col. 3:9–10.

[^1892]: Gal. 3:27; the traditional baptismal hymn sung here in place of the Trisagion to emphasize the Great Schema tonsure as a radical renewal and intensification of the baptismal covenant.

[^1893]: Ps. 26:1 (LXX).

[^1894]: Eph. 6:10.

[^1895]: Eph. 6:11–12; Slav. къ дꙋхо́внымъ зло́бѣ въ поднебе́сныхъ (Gk. πρὸς τὰ πνευματικὰ τῆς πονηρίας ἐν τοῖς ἐπουρανίοις).

[^1896]: Eph. 6:13; Slav. всеѡрꙋ́жество бж҃їе (Gk. τὴν πανοπλίαν τοῦ Θεοῦ, "the panoply of God").

[^1897]: Eph. 6:15.

[^1898]: Eph. 6:16–17.

[^1899]: The Alleluia psalmody following the Epistle reading, designated with the numerical tone indicator г҃ (Tone 3).

[^1900]: Ps. 33:7 (LXX).

[^1901]: Matt. 10:37–38.

[^1902]: Matt. 11:28–30; note the vernacularized Early Modern Ruthenian verbal form навчи́тисѧ (navčitysja) in place of standard Church Slavonic научи́тесѧ.

[^1903]: The Augmented Litany (сугубая ектения) following the Gospel reading.

[^1904]: The rubrical investiture of the hand-cross given into the hands of the newly professed schemamonk, symbolizing his voluntary cruciform life in imitation of Christ.

[^1905]: Matt. 16:24; Mark 8:34.

[^1906]: The ritual handing of a lighted candle to the monk, symbolizing the light of good works and monastic virtue before men (Matt. 5:16).

[^1907]: Matt. 5:16.

[^1908]: Slav. самогла́сенъ (samoglasenъ; Gk. ἰδιόμελον).

[^1909]: The classic Byzantine monastic sticheron/idiomelon based on the Parable of the Prodigal Son (Luke 15:11–32), chanted during the fraternal kiss of peace (поцелуй мира).

[^1910]: Slav. чл҃ко люби́бомоу (č[e]l[ově]koljubibomu), exhibiting an epigraphic scribal defect (б for в) for человеколюбивому. The sacrifice of the fatted calf in the Prodigal Son narrative is interpreted Christologically as the slaying of the Savior for the life of the world.

[^1911]: The mutual fraternal kiss (братское целование) and the daily monastic dismissal concluding the Rite of the Great Schema.

[^1912]: The Prayer at the Taking Off of the Koukoulion (Молитва на снятие кукуля), traditionally appointed for the eighth day following tonsure, after the neophyte has spent a week in the temple in prayer wearing the cowl.

[^1913]: Cf. 1 Thess. 5:8.

[^1914]: Slav. ра́зꙋма є҆го̀ влⷣчственое (Gk. τὸ ἡγεμονικὸν τοῦ νοός), the Patristic euchological concept of the *hegemonikon*—the ruling or sovereign faculty of the rational intellect.

[^1915]: Gen. 3:15 (LXX).

[^1916]: The Father Paul Doxology Standard (*"unto ages of ages"*), rendering Slav. въ вѣ́кы вѣкѡ́мъ.

[^1917]: Slav. ѻ҆́гненѣй главѣ̀ (ógneněj glavě), a vivid euchological metaphor designating God as the uncreated Fiery Head (cf. Dan. 7:9; Heb. 12:29).

[^1918]: The concluding doxological exclamation of the prayer of head-inclination.

[^1919]: The monastic burial order (Погреба́нїе / Про́водъ и҆́нокомъ; Gk. Ἀκολουθία εἰς κεκοιμημένους μοναχούς). The term прѡ́водъ (próvodъ) is the Ruthenian liturgical designation for a funeral conducting or procession (cf. Ukr. проводи).

[^1920]: Slav. мо́щи (móšči), the standard Byzantine and East Slavic monastic term applying the title "relics" to the physical mortal remains of every deceased monk, reflecting the sanctification of the body through the angelic habit and ascetical struggle.

[^1921]: The ablution of the monastic body is strictly symbolic and modest, restricted to tracing the sign of the cross on the forehead, breast, hands, feet, and knees, precluding general bathing or exposing the deceased naked.

[^1922]: Slav. скръ́бнꙋю ѻ҆де́ждꙋ (skrъbnuju odeždu; Gk. τὸ πενθικὸν ἔνδυма), the penitential, soiled clothing worn during daily ascetical labor, exchanged for clean vestments at burial.

[^1923]: For a deceased monk of the Great Schema (великий образ), the cowl is drawn down over the forehead to the beard, veiling the face so that the mortal remains are concealed from view.

[^1924]: Slav. а҆нала́въ... є҆́же соу́тъ пле́ти (analavъ... eže sutъ pleti), referring to the cruciform cords or plaited bands of the analavos worn by schemamonks.

[^1925]: Slav. рого́зина (rogozina), a coarse woven rush mat upon which the deceased monk was placed during the initial ritual sponging prior to being wrapped in his monastic cloak (mantiya).

[^1926]: The ritual wrapping of the monastic body in the mantiya (manteion): cutting strips (оукрои) from both lateral edges and tying them across the body to form three crosses—at the head, over the breast, and at the knees—symbolizing total consecration to the Crucified Christ.

[^1927]: The remaining ends of the cloth strips are used to bind the feet together in repose.

[^1928]: Summoning the hebdomadary priest (сщ҃енникъ є҆моу́же чреда̀; Gk. ὁ ἐφημέριος), who vests in the epitrachelion, takes the censer, and gives the initial blessing ("Glory to our God...") for the cell prayers preceding the funeral procession.

[^1929]: The Trisagion prayers (Holy God, Holy Mighty, Holy Immortal; All-Holy Trinity; Our Father) chanted at the cell over the deceased.

[^1930]: The traditional funeral troparia (Со ду́хи пра́ведныхъ сконча́вшихсѧ... / "With the spirits of the righteous made perfect...") specified previously in the office for laymen (fol. 317v et seq.).

[^1931]: The small funeral litany, the prayer of rest ("O God of spirits and of all flesh..."), and the initial dismissal at the cell prior to translating the relics.

[^1932]: The solemn translation of the monastic relics from the cell to the monastic church.

[^1933]: Liturgical spatial distinction in the placement of the deceased: a departed priest or hieromonk is placed in the center of the nave (посредѣ церкве), whereas a simple monk (простецъ, here printed with a typographical error as посте́цъ) is placed in the narthex (в притворѣ).

[^1934]: Slav. кандиловъжига́тель (kandilovъžigatélъ; Gk. κανδηλάπτης), the monastic lamp-lighter/ecclesiarches. Striking the "heavy irons" (тѧ́жкаа желѣ́за; the heavy iron semantron) with three pauses or stations (постоѧ́нїа трѝ) summons the entire monastic brotherhood to the funeral office.

[^1935]: Slav. съсудохрани́тель (sъsudoxranítelъ; Gk. σκευοφύλαξ), the sacristan, distributing beeswax tapers to the gathered brethren.

[^1936]: Psalm 90 (LXX; Masoretic 91), "He that dwells in the help of the Most High," the solemn opening psalm of the Byzantine monastic burial rite.

[^1937]: Psalm 64:5a (LXX; Masoretic 65:4a), the primary funeral Alleluia verse.

[^1938]: Psalm 101:13 / 134:13 (LXX; Masoretic 102:12 / 135:13), the second Alleluia verse.

[^1939]: The funeral troparion of Tone 8 (Ὁ βάθει σοφίας φιλανθρώπως πάντα οἰκονομῶν / "O Thou Who by the depth of wisdom...").

[^1940]: Slav. Сл҃ва того̀ (Slava togo), indicating that at "Glory..." the same troparion is repeated or followed by its companion martyr troparion.

[^1941]: Theotokion of Tone 8 concluding the opening troparia: Σὲ καὶ τεῖχος καὶ λιμένα ἔχομεν... ("Thee do we have as a rampart and a haven...").

[^1942]: Psalm 118:12 (LXX), serving as the foundational refrain of the first stasis of the 17th Kathisma (The Undefiled / Непорочны; Gk. Ἄμωμοι).

[^1943]: Psalm 118:1 (LXX).

[^1944]: The first stasis spans Psalm 118:1–93, concluding immediately before verse 94 ("I am Thine, save me").

[^1945]: Division of the 17th Kathisma into two stases (на двѣ статїи) in the Ruthenian monastic burial rite, rather than the three stases standard in the parochial order.

[^1946]: Psalm 118:93 (LXX): В вѣки не забуду оправданій твоих... ("Unto eternity I will not forget Thy statutes..."), repeated thrice at the conclusion of the first stasis.

[^1947]: The secret prayer ("O God of spirits and of all flesh...") and exclamation recited by the priest concluding the first stasis.

[^1948]: Psalm 118:94 (LXX): Твой есмь аз, спаси мя, яко оправданій твоих взысках ("I am Thine, save me: for I have sought Thy statutes"), opening the second stasis.

[^1949]: At Psalm 118:132 (LXX; "Look upon me and have mercy on me..."), the chant shifts to Tone 3 for the remainder of the second stasis.

[^1950]: The second stasis refrain, derived from the prayer of the Good Thief (Lk. 23:42): "In Thy Kingdom, O Lord, remember Thy servant."

[^1951]: Psalm 118:175 (LXX): Жива будет душа моя и восхвалит тя... ("My soul shall live and shall praise Thee..."), sung thrice to conclude the second stasis.

[^1952]: The Funeral Evlogitaria (тропари по непорочнах) in Tone 5: "The choir of the saints has found the Fountain of life and the Door of Paradise..."

[^1953]: Funeral sessional hymn (Sessional Hymn) in Tone 5.

[^1954]: Tone 5 funeral sessional hymn (Покой, Спасе наш, с праведными раба твоего... / "Give rest, our Savior, with the righteous unto Thy servant...").

[^1955]: Tone 5 Theotokion (Иже от Дѣвы возсіявый міру, Христе Боже... / "O Christ God, Who didst shine forth to the world from a Virgin...").

[^1956]: Psalm 50 (LXX; Masoretic 51).

[^1957]: The sequential chanting of the Antiphons (Hymns of Ascent / Anavathmoi) of the Eight Tones alternating with funeral stichera of St. Theophanes Graptos, a defining feature of the Byzantine monastic burial office.

[^1958]: The 1st Antiphon of Tone 1 (Внегда скорбѣти ми...), based on Psalm 119:1 (LXX).

[^1959]: Saint Theophanes the Branded / the Confessor (ca. 778–845; Slav. ст҃ый Дїѡфа́нъ), Metropolitan of Nicaea and Studite hymnographer, author of the eight-tone cycle of monastic funeral stichera.

[^1960]: First sticheron of Tone 1 (Gk. Σὲ δυσωποῦμεν Σωτήρ). The printed text reads въ нѣ́снаа се́ла, an obvious typographical error for въ нб҃снаа се́ла (in the heavenly abodes).

[^1961]: Second sticheron of Tone 1, invoking the theological premise that God alone is sinless (2 Chr. 6:36; 1 Jn. 1:8).

[^1962]: Third sticheron of Tone 1, citing 1 Corinthians 2:9 (Isa. 64:4) regarding the heavenly goods prepared for those who love God.

[^1963]: Doxasticon ("Glory...") sticheron of Tone 1, emphasizing salvation through the Cross and the Blood poured out for the life of the world (Jn. 6:51).

[^1964]: Theotokion of Tone 1. Slav. твои́мъ прижи́тїемъ (tvoímъ prižítijemъ; Gk. τῇ μητρικῇ σου παρρησίᾳ / συμβιώσει) denotes maternal boldness and intimate communion with her divine Son.

[^1965]: The 1st Antiphon of Tone 2 (На небо очи пущаю...), sung here as the second funeral antiphon.

[^1966]: Based on Psalm 122:1 (LXX).

[^1967]: Tone 2 funeral stichera of St. Theophanes, modeled on the automelon Ὅτε ἐκ τοῦ ξύλου σε νεκρόν (When from the Tree).

[^1968]: Conclusion of the first sticheron of Tone 2: Christ's life-giving death shattering corruption and granting resurrection unto mortal men.

[^1969]: Second sticheron of Tone 2, celebrating Christ's voluntary Crucifixion and death as opening the Divine Kingdom to mankind.

[^1970]: Third sticheron of Tone 2, spanning the leaf break at the foot of physical leaf p700 (съмотре́нїа въи́стинноу тре́петное...) and continuing onto leaf p701 (...таинство, радуѧсѧ съвръшилъ єси).

[^1971]: Leaf p701 (fol. 345 / тм҃е). Continuing the Tone 2 stichera (Podoben: *When from the Tree* / *Є҆гда̀ ѿ дрѣ́ва*) commenced on fol. 344v (p700). The text draws upon 1 Corinthians 6:20 ("For ye are bought with a price") and 1 Peter 1:18–19.

[^1972]: Leaf p701. Stichic hymn for *Glory...* depicting the dread eschatological assembly of the dead from all ages standing before Christ's judgment seat (cf. 2 Cor. 5:10).

[^1973]: Leaf p701. Theotokion for *Both now...*, carrying over to fol. 345v (p702). The text contrasts Eve's ancestral debt of death with the Virgin's conception of God, through Whom incorruption and resurrection are granted to mortals.

[^1974]: Leaf p702 (fol. 345v). Concluding the Tone 2 Theotokion from fol. 345 (p701), petitioning the Mother of God to intercede for the departed monk's placement in divine light.

[^1975]: Leaf p702. *Antiphon 3, Tone 3* (А҆нтифѡ́нъ тре́тїи · Гла́съ г҃). Corresponds to the first antiphon of the Songs of Ascents (*Anabathmoi*) of Tone 3, drawing upon LXX Psalm 125:1 ("When the Lord turned again the captivity of Zion") and Psalm 125:5–6 ("They that sow in tears shall reap in joy").

[^1976]: Leaf p702. Doxasticon to the Holy Spirit concluding the Anabathmoi strophes of Tone 3, citing Acts 17:28 ("For in Him we live, and move, and have our being").

[^1977]: Leaf p702. *Stichera, Tone 3, Podoben: "To the form of the Cross"* (Ст҃ры Гла́ г҃ · по́ · Ѻ҆́бразоу кр҃та). The Greek automelon model is Τῷ τύπῳ τοῦ σταυροῦ (or Σταυροфанῶς), invoking the triumphant sign of the Cross as the tree of life.

[^1978]: Leaf p703 (fol. 346 / тм҃ѕ). First Tone 3 sticheron on the Cross, featuring the recurring liturgical refrain for monastic burial: "where all who rejoice have their dwelling with Thee, to glorify Thy Divinity" (cf. LXX Ps. 86:7: "As of them that rejoice is the dwelling of all in Thee").

[^1979]: Leaf p703. Second Tone 3 sticheron, appealing to Christ's unfathomable deep of compassion (*поучи́нѫ бл҃гости*) and His knowledge of human frail clay as our Creator (cf. LXX Ps. 102:14).

[^1980]: Leaf p704 (fol. 346v). Third Tone 3 sticheron for *Glory...*, meditating on Christ's bodily rest in the tomb and His divine resurrection of the dead.

[^1981]: Leaf p704. Tone 3 Theotokion for *Both now...*, hailing the Virgin as the "intelligible candlestick" (λυχνία νοερά) carrying the divine fire united to human bodily density (*де́бельство чл҃ч҃каго существа̀*).

[^1982]: Leaf p705 (fol. 347 / тм҃з). *Antiphon 4, Tone 4* (А҆нтифѡ́нъ четве́ртый · Гла́съ д҃). First antiphon of the Songs of Ascents of Tone 4, based on LXX Psalm 128:1–2 ("Many a time have they afflicted me from my youth").

[^1983]: Leaf p705. Second strophe of Tone 4 Anabathmoi, based on LXX Psalm 128:5–6 ("Let them be confounded and turned back all they that hate Zion; let them be as the grass upon the housetops").

[^1984]: Leaf p705. Celebrated pneumatological Doxasticon of Tone 4 (*Ст҃ы́мъ дх҃омъ всѧ́ка дш҃а живи́тсѧ*), sung at every Sunday Polyeleos Matins, proclaiming the Holy Spirit's quickening and sanctifying life in the Trinity.

[^1985]: Leaf p705. First sticheron of Tone 4, Podoben: *Thou hast given a sign* (Да́лъ є҆сѝ зна́менїе; Greek: Ἔδωκας σημείωσιν). Attributed to Saint John of Damascus, meditating on the violent separation of soul and body at death; continues onto fol. 347v (p706).

[^1986]: Leaf p706 (fol. 347v). Concluding the sticheron on the dissolution of natural bodily bonds and imploring Christ to grant rest in the tabernacles of the righteous.

[^1987]: Leaf p706. Second Tone 4 sticheron, proclaiming death to be a sleep for the faithful since Christ was laid in the grave and overturned death's ancient tyranny.

[^1988]: Leaf p706. Third Tone 4 sticheron, alluding to 1 Corinthians 1:30 ("Christ Jesus, Who of God is made unto us wisdom, and righteousness, and sanctification, and redemption"); carries over to fol. 348 (p707).

[^1989]: Leaf p707 (fol. 348 / тм҃и). Concluding the sticheron on Christ taking upon Himself our owed penalty (*на́ше длъ́жное запрѣще́нїе*).

[^1990]: Leaf p707. Tone 4 sticheron for *Glory...*, celebrating Christ washing away ancestral sin through the Blood and water from His pierced side (cf. John 19:34).

[^1991]: Leaf p707. Tone 4 Theotokion for *Both now...*, affirming the fulfillment of Old Testament prophetic types in Mary's virginal childbearing; carries over to fol. 348v (p708).

[^1992]: Leaf p708 (fol. 348v). Concluding the Tone 4 Theotokion, praying that the departed monk may be illumined by Christ's heavenly radiance.

[^1993]: Leaf p708. *Antiphon 5, Tone 5* (А҆нтифѡ́нъ пѧ́тый · Гла́съ є҆). First antiphon of the Songs of Ascents of Tone 5, based on LXX Psalm 119:1–2 ("In my distress I cried unto the Lord... Deliver my soul, O Lord, from lying lips, and from a deceitful tongue").

[^1994]: Leaf p708. Second strophe of Tone 5 Anabathmoi, extolling the blessedness of the solitary desert life (*Пусты́ннымъ живо́тъ блаже́нъ є҆́стъ*), elevated by divine longing.

[^1995]: Leaf p708. Doxasticon to the Holy Spirit of Tone 5, professing His universal sovereignty and consubstantial union as One of the Holy Trinity.

[^1996]: Leaf p708. *Stichera, Tone 5, Podoben: "Rejoice, O container of ascetics"* (Ст҃ры · Гла́ є҆. подо́бенъ · ра́дуисѧ по́стникомъ; Greek: Χαίροις ἀσκητικῶν).

[^1997]: Leaf p709 (fol. 349 / тм҃ѳ). First Tone 5 sticheron, weaving together the pastoral peace of LXX Psalm 22:2 ("He makes me to lie down in green pastures; He leads me beside the still waters") with the patriarchal reward of the bosom of Abraham (Luke 16:22).

[^1998]: Leaf p709. Second Tone 5 sticheron, petitioning that the departed brother may hymn God with harmonious voices; carries over to fol. 349v (p710).

[^1999]: Leaf p710 (fol. 349v). Concluding the second Tone 5 sticheron, depicting the celestial liturgy where angelic choirs and assemblies of saints encircle the divine throne.

[^2000]: Leaf p710. Tone 5 sticheron for *Glory...*, invoking the heavenly ranks of prophets, apostles, and martyrs who were redeemed by Christ's Passion; sentence completes on fol. 350 (p711).

[^2001]: Physical leaf p711 (`Page_0711.jpg`, fol. 341r, signature єє д҃). Completes the Tone 5 sticheron for *Glory...* from leaf 710. The phrase "free among the dead" (Church Slavonic: `въ мр҃твы[х] свобо́д[ь]`) directly cites LXX Ps. 87:5 (ἐν νεκροῖς ἐλεύθερος).

[^2002]: Physical leaf p711 (`Page_0711.jpg`, fol. 341r). The printed text contains the typographic error `пора́кѡщенныхъ` (*porakoshchennykh*) for `пора́бо́щенныхъ` (*poraboshchennykh*, "enslaved"), reflecting a graphic confusion between Cyrillic `б` and `к` in the Striatyn workshop. The Theotokion contrasts bondage under the law of sin (cf. Rom. 7:23, 8:2) with justification through grace. The phrase "Book of Life" (`въ кни́ѕѣ живо́тнѣй`) alludes to LXX Ps. 68:29 and Rev. 20:12, 21:27.

[^2003]: Physical leaf p712 (`Page_0712.jpg`, fol. 341v). The first strophe of the 6th Gradual Antiphon (Tone 6 Anabathmoi, first antiphon) paraphrases LXX Ps. 122:1 ("Unto Thee have I lifted up mine eyes, unto Thee that dwellest in heaven").

[^2004]: Physical leaf p712 (`Page_0712.jpg`, fol. 341v). Paraphrases LXX Ps. 122:2–3 ("for we are utterly filled with contempt"). The Trinitarian pneumatological strophe attributes all divine inspiration and spiritual elevation to the Holy Spirit (`Ст҃ы́мъ дх҃омъ въсѧ́ка сп҃саѧ вина́` / Greek: Ἁγίῳ Πνεύματι, πᾶσα κοινὴ αἰτία).

[^2005]: Physical leaf p712 (`Page_0712.jpg`, fol. 341v). Headpiece for the Tone 6 Stichera of the Priest's Funeral. The melodic model heading `Всѐ възло́жше` corresponds to the Greek automelon Ὅλην ἀποθέμενοι ("Having laid aside all earthly hope"). The sticheron sentence continues across the leaf boundary onto leaf 713 (`Page_0713.jpg`).

[^2006]: Physical leaf p713 (`Page_0713.jpg`, fol. 342r, signature єє є҃). Conclusion of the first sticheron of Tone 6 from leaf 712. The phrase "land of the living" (`въ землѝ живы́хъ`) alludes to LXX Ps. 26:13 and Ps. 114:9; "beloved tabernacles" (`въ села̀ възлю́бленнаѧ`) cites LXX Ps. 83:2.

[^2007]: Physical leaf p713 (`Page_0713.jpg`, fol. 342r). The second sticheron of Tone 6 emphasizes Christ's voluntary Passion as the source of eternal nourishment (`пи́щꙋ вѣ́чнꙋю`) and forgiveness of sins for the departed priest.

[^2008]: Physical leaf p714 (`Page_0714.jpg`, fol. 342v). Tone 6 sticheron for *Glory...*, professing Christ's sovereign dominion over both the living and the dead (cf. Rom. 14:9).

[^2009]: Physical leaf p714 (`Page_0714.jpg`, fol. 342v). Theotokion of Tone 6 expressing Chalcedonian Christology: Christ born of the Virgin "in two essences and in one hypostasis" (`въ двою̀ соу́ществоу, въ є҆ди́нои же ѵ҆по́стаси` / Greek: ἐν δύο οὐσίαις, μιᾷ δὲ τῇ ὑποστάσει). Sentence continues onto leaf 715 (`Page_0715.jpg`).

[^2010]: Physical leaf p715 (`Page_0715.jpg`, fol. 343r). Conclusion of the Tone 6 Theotokion from leaf 714, affirming the perpetual virginity of the Mother of God (*post partum virgo*, `по рождествѣ̀ съхра́нша`).

[^2011]: Physical leaf p715 (`Page_0715.jpg`, fol. 343r). The 7th Gradual Antiphon (Tone 7 Anabathmoi, first antiphon) paraphrases LXX Ps. 125:1–6 ("When the Lord turned again the captivity of Zion... Turn again our captivity, O Lord, as streams in the south. They that sow in tears shall reap in joy"). The Trinitarian strophe enumerates the gifts of the Holy Spirit (cf. Isa. 11:2). The rubrical cue `С҃ . И҆ н҃ .` abbreviates `Сла́ва, И҆ ны́нѣ` (*Glory... Both now...*).

[^2012]: Physical leaf p716 (`Page_0716.jpg`, fol. 343v). Headpiece for Tone 7 Stichera of the Priest's Funeral. The model heading `Оу҆жѐ невозбра́нше` reflects the Ruthenian recension's witness of the Greek automelon Οὐκέτι κωλυόμεθα ("No longer are we forbidden").

[^2013]: Physical leaf p716 (`Page_0716.jpg`, fol. 343v). The second sticheron of Tone 7 invokes hesychastic imagery of uncreated divine light (`бж҃тве́наго свѣ́та твое́го лꙋча́ми`) and immaterial brightness (`въ невеще́ственѣй свѣ́тлости`). Line 16 ends with the rubrical cue `Сла́ва .` (*Glory...*), leading into leaf 717.

[^2014]: Physical leaf p717 (`Page_0717.jpg`, fol. 344r). Tone 7 sticheron for *Glory...* The rare term `неиздрї́мое` corresponds to `неиздря́емое` (inexhaustible / unemptiable, Greek: ἀδαπάνητον). The phrase `въ дѣ́тве́нѣмъ чръто́зѣ ꙗ҆́ко мл҃дъ` represents the soul entering the heavenly bridal chamber in pure childlike innocence (cf. Matt. 18:3).

[^2015]: Physical leaf p717 (`Page_0717.jpg`, fol. 344r). Theotokion of Tone 7 expounding the Pauline theology of justification by Christ over the ceremonial Law (cf. Rom. 3:20, 8:3–4, Gal. 2:16), invoking the Theotokos' maternal boldness (`мт҃рьнимъ дръзнове́нїемъ`) for the soul of the departed priest.

[^2016]: Physical leaf p718 (`Page_0718.jpg`, fol. 344v). The 8th Gradual Antiphon (Tone 8 Anabathmoi, first antiphon) paraphrases LXX Ps. 128:1–6 ("Many a time have they afflicted me from my youth... Let them be as grass upon the housetops, which withers before it is plucked up"). The Trinitarian strophe confesses the Holy Spirit as "Light of Light, God great" (`свѣ́тъ ѿ свѣ́та бг҃ъ вели́къ`).

[^2017]: Physical leaf p718 (`Page_0718.jpg`, fol. 344v). Headpiece for Tone 8 Stichera of the Priest's Funeral. Melodic model `Ѡ҆ пресла́вное чю́до` (Greek: Ὢ τοῦ παραδόξου θαύματος, "O most marvelous wonder"). The hymn uses imperial chancellery imagery: Christ signs the charter of emancipation of the Church (`свобожде́нїе`) by dipping His fingers into His own Blood upon the Cross as vermilion/cinnabar ink (`ша́ромъ чръвле́нымъ`, Greek: κινναβάρεως / πορφύρας). The sentence continues onto leaf 719 (`Page_0719.jpg`).

[^2018]: Physical leaf p719 (`Page_0719.jpg`, fol. 345r). Conclusion of the first sticheron of Tone 8 from leaf 718. The phrase "number with the firstborn" (`съ пръворо́дными причтѝ`) evokes Heb. 12:23 ("to the general assembly and church of the firstborn registered in heaven").

[^2019]: Physical leaf p719 (`Page_0719.jpg`, fol. 345r). The second sticheron of Tone 8 presents Christ as the High Priest Who is simultaneously the Offerer and the Offered Sacrifice (cf. Liturgy of St. John Chrysostom, Prayer of the Cherubic Hymn: "For Thou art the Offerer and the Offered, the Receiver and the Received"). The phrase "streams of delight" (`потѡ́ци пи́щїи`) echoes LXX Ps. 35:9 ("Thou shalt make them drink of the torrent of Thy delights").

[^2020]: Physical leaf p719 (`Page_0719.jpg`, fol. 345r). The third sticheron of Tone 8 meditates upon God's providence in determining human lifespan. The phrase "waters of rest" (`на вода́хъ поко́йныхъ`) quotes LXX Ps. 22:2 (ἐπὶ ὕδατος ἀναπαύσεως). Sentence continues onto leaf 720 (`Page_0720.jpg`).

[^2021]: Physical leaf p720 (`Page_0720.jpg`, fol. 345v). Conclusion of the third sticheron of Tone 8 from leaf 719. The phrase "voice of rejoicing and praise" (`гла́съ ра́дованїа и҆ хвале́нїа`) quotes LXX Ps. 41:5 (φωνὴ ἀγαλλιάσεως καὶ ἐξομολογήσεως).

[^2022]: Physical leaf p720 (`Page_0720.jpg`, fol. 345v). Tone 8 sticheron for *Glory...*, professing the full consubstantiality and co-enthronement of the incarnate Word with the Father and the Holy Spirit (`є҆диное́стве́но ѻ҆ц҃ꙋ, и҆ дх҃ови съпрⷭ҇то́лно`).

[^2023]: Physical leaf p720 (`Page_0720.jpg`, fol. 345v). Concluding Theotokion of the Tone 8 Stichera. The phrase "sweet voice of those who feast" (`сла́дкїй гла́съ пра́здноующихъ`) echoes LXX Ps. 41:5 (φωνὴ ἑορτάζοντος). This marks the completion of the 8-Tone cycle of Gradual Antiphons and Stichera in the Funeral Service for Priests, directly preceding the deacon's litany on leaf 721 (Cohort 73).

[^2024]: Physical leaf p721 (`Page_0721.jpg`, fol. 325r, signature ж ж). Following the 8-tone cycle of the funeral office for monastics, the deacon intones the Little Litany (`па́ки и҆ па́ки`), followed by the priest's ecphonesis and the Kontakion in Tone 8 (`С̾ ст҃ыми поко́и Хрⷭ҇ѐ` / Greek: Μετὰ τῶν ἁγίων ἀνάпаυσον, Χριστέ). The rubric `ко҃` abbreviates `кондакъ`.

[^2025]: Physical leaf p721 (`Page_0721.jpg`, fol. 325r). The funeral Ikos `Ты̀ є҆ди́нъ є҆си без̾сме́ртне` (Greek: Αὐτὸς μόνος εἶ ἀθάνατος) quotes Gen. 3:19 ("for dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return"). The phrase "graveside weeping" (`на́дгробное рыда́нїе`) reflects the Greek ἐπιτάφιον θρῆνον.

[^2026]: Physical leaf p722 (`Page_0722.jpg`, fol. 325v). At the Beatitudes, the first four verses (Matt. 5:3–6) are sung without strophes, after which troparia are intercalated with each verse starting with the fifth Beatitude (`Блаже́ни млⷭ҇тивїи`, Matt. 5:7). The opening troparion invokes Christ's remembrance of the Good Thief on the cross (Luke 23:42).

[^2028]: Physical leaf p722 (`Page_0722.jpg`, fol. 325v). Intercalated with the Beatitude verse `Блаже́ни миротво́рци` ("Blessed are the peacemakers", Matt. 5:9). The troparion commends the deceased monastic's life of ascetic fasting (`въ по́стничествѣ порабо́тавшаго`) and steadfast adherence to Orthodoxy (`въ правосла́вїи`).

Text continues across the leaf boundary onto leaf 727.

The pericope details the healing pool of Bethesda (*Виѳезда*) by the Sheep Gate in Jerusalem, where an angel of the Lord troubled the water at certain seasons, healing the first sufferer to step in.

[^2120]: Petition for this holy house and all who enter with faith (*О святѣмъ храмѣ семъ...*), spanning across the leaf boundary onto leaf p752.

[^2121]: Conclusion of the petition for this holy house and all who enter it (*...with faith, reverence, and the fear of God*), and the petitions for the bishop and the clergy. Note the red rubric *и҆́мⷬ҇къ рⷱ҇къ* ("*[Name]* is said").

[^2122]: Petitions for the civil authorities (*О благовѣрныхъ царехъ нашихъ...*) and the heavily abbreviated standard petitions: for this city and country (*О градѣ семъ...*), temperate seasons and abundance of fruits (*О благорастворенїи воздуховъ...*), and travelers, the sick, and captives (*О плавающи[хъ], пу[ть] шествующи[хъ]...*).
