[^2124]: Second special water-blessing petition: *That there may be sent down upon it the grace of redemption and the blessing of Jordan* (*О еже послатися на ню благодати избавленїа, и благословенїе іорданово...*).

[^2125]: Third and fourth special water-blessing petitions: *That there may be granted unto it healing power by the descent of the Holy Spirit* (*О дароватися ей силу цѣлебну...*) and *That it may be for the sanctification of our souls and bodies, and for the turning away of every adverse power* (*О быти ей на освященїе душамъ и тѣломъ нашимъ...*).

[^2126]: Fifth and sixth special water-blessing petitions: *That it may be shown forth as a fountain of incorruption and a gift of salvation* (*О явитися ей источнику нетлѣнїа...*) and *For them that draw and take thereof* (*О чръплющихъ и взимающихъ от нея...*).

[^2127]: Seventh and eighth special water-blessing petitions: *That it may be for the remission of sins and the healing of diseases* (*О быти ей оставленїе грѣхомъ...*) and *That we may be enlightened with the illumination of understanding for the sake of the consubstantial Trinity* (*О просвѣтитися намъ просвѣщенїемъ разума...*).

[^2128]: Ninth special water-blessing petition: *That the purifying operation of the supersubstantial Trinity may be sent down upon this water* (*О низпослатися на воду сїю чистителному пресущественыя Троица дѣйству*). The physical leaf ends with the abbreviated noun *дѣ́йств[у]*, with the printer omitting *Господу помолимся* due to lack of space at the lower margin.

[^2129]: Tenth and eleventh special water-blessing petitions: *That the Lord our God may send illumination and understanding into our hearts* (*О еже Господу Богу нашему послати просвѣщенїе и разумъ въ сердца наша...*) and *For all who need help and protection from our God* (*О всѣхъ требующихъ яже от Бога нашего помощи и заступленїа...*).

[^2130]: Twelfth special water-blessing petition: *That the Lord our God may show us forth as sons and heirs of His Kingdom through the communion and sprinkling of this water* (*О яко да Господь Богъ нашъ явитъ насъ сыны и наслѣдники царствїа своего, причащенїа и окропленїа ради воды сея...*).

[^2131]: Concluding general petitions of the litany: for deliverance from all affliction, wrath, and need (*О избавитися намъ от всякоя скорби...*); the suffrages *Help us, save us, have mercy on us, and keep us...* (*Заступи, спаси...*); and the commemoration of the Most-holy Theotokos and all saints (*Пресвятую, чистую, и преблагословенную...*), spanning across the leaf boundary onto leaf p755.

[^2132]: Conclusion of the litany entrustment: *...commending ourselves and one another, and our whole life unto Christ our God* (*...и весь животъ нашъ Христу Богу [предадимъ]*), followed by the priest's exclamation (*възгласъ:*): *For unto Thee is due all glory, honor, and worship...* (*Яко подобаетъ ти всяка слава...*).

[^2133]: Rubric introducing the great prayer of the Lesser Sanctification of Water: *Let us pray to the Lord. Then the priest [says] this prayer:* (*Господу помолимся. Таже іерей молитву сїю.*).

[^2134]: Opening Trinitarian invocation of the great prayer: *O God great and highest, Who art worshipped in the Holy Trinity...* (*Боже великый и вышнїй, иже въ троици святѣй покланяемый...*). The physical imprint reads *є҆стко*, an apparent typographical misprint for *естество* ("substance / nature").

[^2135]: Supplicatory address to the Master Who loves mankind (*Ты человѣколюбче Владыко...*), spanning across the leaf boundary onto leaf p756.

[^2136]: Petition for divine inspiration and spiritual understanding: *...and grant in our mind the spirit of wisdom and understanding...* (*...и даждь въ мысли нашей духъ премудрости и разума...*).

[^2137]: Scriptural allusion to Philippians 2:13: *For from Thee and from Thy life-giving gift it is both to will and to work according to Thy will and Thy good pleasure unto men* (*От тебе бо и твоего животворнаго дарованїа, и еже хотѣти, и еже дѣйствовати по воли твоей, и твоего благоволенїа человѣкомъ есть*).

[^2138]: Invocation of the blessing and healing grace upon the water, echoing Titus 3:5 (*Who hast given to our race the washing of regeneration...* / *иже банею пакы бытїа роду нашему даровавъ...*).

[^2139]: Allusion to Hebrews 10:22: *...and make us, who are sprinkled [in hearts] from an evil conscience...* (*...и сподоби насъ окропленыхъ сердци от [съвѣсти лукавны]*), spanning across the leaf boundary onto leaf p757.

[^2140]: Continuation of the baptismal and cleansing typology from Hebrews 10:22 (*...from an evil conscience, and having our body washed with pure water* / *...съвѣсти лукавны, и омывеныхъ тѣло водою чистою*), turning into a prayer for active good works and charity toward the brethren.

[^2141]: Petition that this spiritual service and water sanctification be not for carnal pleasure, but for the healing of soul and body (*не къ сласти плотстѣй, но къ исцѣленїю души и тѣлу творимая нами служба духовная*).

[^2142]: Invocation to the merciful Master (*Еи, Владыко многомилостиве, помилуй рабы Своя...*), spanning across the leaf boundary onto leaf p758.

[^2143]: Supplication for purification: *...bowing down unto our lowliness: Who hast given us to wear this pure garment from water and the Spirit, wash [us] with this water, and by the sprinkling of Thy blessing cleanse the defilements of our passions* (*...смиренїе наше прекланяяся... одежду от воды и духа, омый водою сею...*).

[^2144]: The extensive intercession of saints in the prayer of water blessing: invoking the Most-holy Theotokos, the heavenly bodiless powers, the Prophet and Forerunner John the Baptist, the holy Apostles, the holy Ancestors of God Joachim and Anna, Zacharias and Elizabeth, and the holy sovereign equals-to-the-apostles Constantine and Helen.

[^2145]: Commemoration of the great Hierarchs: Basil the Great, Gregory [the Theologian], spanning across the leaf boundary onto leaf p759.

[^2146]: Continuation of the Hierarchs (Gregory the Theologian, John Chrysostom, Nicholas the Wonderworker) and the holy Unmercenary Physicians (*безсребреници*): Cosmas and Damian, Cyrus and John, Panteleimon and Hermolaus, Florus and Laurus, Samson and Diomedes; Saint Simeon Stylite of the Mandra (*иже въ Оградѣ*); the holy Seven Maccabee Martyrs (commemorated on August 1); and Venerable Athanasius.

[^2147]: Intercession for the sovereign rulers (*рабы своя вѣрныя царя нашя...*), with rubric *[Name]* (*рⷱ҇къ* / *і҆́мⷬ҇къ*), asking for peace, victory over adversaries, and all petitions unto salvation; spanning across the leaf boundary onto leaf p760.

[^2148]: Continuation of the imperial petitions (*...and eternal life*), followed by intercessions for the hierarch (*our Archbishop [Name]* / *архїеппла нашего імя рекъ*) and the Orthodox episcopate rightly dividing the word of truth (2 Timothy 2:15).

[^2149]: Commemoration of the priestly and monastic orders, benefactors, those who remember the poor, the people present, and absent fathers and brethren.

[^2150]: Petitions for captives (*помяни, Господи, братїа наша плѣненыя, и избави ихъ всякаго злаго обстоянїа*) and the sick (*помяни, Господи, сущихъ въ болѣзни, и посѣти ихъ вся, и исцѣли по велицей милости твоей*).

[^2151]: Petition for travelers by land and sea (*помяни, Господи, въ [путь шествующихъ, и в мори...]*, spanning across the cohort boundary onto leaf p761.

[^2152]: Conclusion of the intercessory petitions in the great prayer of the Lesser Sanctification of Water (*Боже великый и вышнїй...*), continuing from leaf p760: for those journeying by land and sea, in prisons, and in deserts throughout the divine dominion (*на всякомъ мѣстѣ владычества твоего*), asking for petitions unto salvation and eternal life.

[^2153]: Priestly exclamation concluding the great prayer: *For Thou art good, and sanctifiest all things, O Christ our God...* (*Яко ты еси благый, и святяй всяческая, Христе Боже наш...*). The Ruthenian witness has the rare present active participle *святяй* (*ст҃ѧ́й*) governing the neuter plural accusative *всяческая* (Greek: ὁ ἁγιάζων τὰ πάντα).

[^2154]: Liturgical blessing of peace (*Миръ всѣмъ* / Greek: Εἰρήνη πᾶσι).

[^2155]: Deacon's bidding for the bowing of heads (*Главы ваша Господеви приклоните* / Greek: Τὰς κεφαλὰς ὑμῶν τῷ Κυρίῳ κλίνατε).

[^2156]: Rubric prescribing the prayer of head-bowing to be recited secretly by the priest (*іерей молитву тай*).

[^2157]: Incipit of the prayer of head-bowing at the Lesser Sanctification of Water (*Приклони, Господи, ухо твое, и услыши ны...* / Greek: Κλῖνον, Κύριε, τὸ οὖς σου καὶ ἐπάκουσον ἡμῶν...), invoking Christ Who willed to be baptized in the Jordan and sanctified the nature of waters, spanning across the leaf boundary onto leaf p762.

[^2158]: Conclusion of the prayer of head-bowing: blessing those who manifest the sign of servitude by bowing their heads (*назнаменующїи работы въображенїе* / Greek: εἰκονίζοντας τὸ τῆς δουλείας σχῆμα), and praying that partaking of the sanctified water may grant health of soul and body.

[^2159]: Priestly exclamation of the head-bowing prayer: *For Thou art our Sanctification, O Christ our God...* (*Ты бо еси Освященїе наше, Христе Боже наш...* / Greek: Σὺ γὰρ εἶ ὁ ἁγιασμὸς ἡμῶν...).

[^2160]: Rubric for the immersion and elevation of the Holy Cross: the priest takes the precious Cross and blesses the water thrice cruciformly (*крестообразно*), plunging and raising the Cross upright (*низводя и възводя крестъ правѣ*), while singing the Troparion of the Cross.

[^2161]: Incipit of the Troparion of the Cross, Tone 1 (*Спаси, Господи, люди твоя, и благослови достоянїе твое...* / Greek: Σῶσον, Κύριε, τὸν λαόν σου...), prescribed to be sung thrice.

[^2162]: Rubric directing the singing of the following Theotokion in Tone 2 (*поютъ же тропарь, сїи, Гласъ в*).

[^2163]: Theotokion of the Lesser Sanctification of Water, Tone 2 (*Твоихъ даровъ достойны насъ сътвори, Богородице Дѣво...* / Greek: Τῶν σῶν δωρημάτων ἀξίους ἡμᾶς ποίησον, Θεοτόκε Παρθένε...), imploring the Mother of God to overlook sins and grant healings unto those receiving her blessing with faith and love.

[^2164]: Rubric for the veneration of the Holy Cross (*цѣлуетъ іерей честный крестъ, такожде и вси людїе*) followed by the general sprinkling of the church, monastery, and all the faithful with the sanctified water (*кропитъ вся люди, и обитель съ водою священною*), while the choir sings the sticheron in Tone 4.

[^2165]: Troparion of the Holy Unmercenary Physicians (*Безсребреници*), Tone 4 (*Источникомъ исцѣленїемъ имуще, святїи безсребрьници...* / Greek: Πηγὴν ἰαμάτων ἔχοντες, ἅγιοι Ἀνάργυροι...), celebrating the healing grace bestowed upon them from the fountain of the Savior, spanning across the leaf boundary onto leaf p764.

[^2166]: Conclusion of the Unmercenaries' troparion, paraphrasing the Dominical commission to the disciples in Matthew 10:1, 8 (*Се дахъ вамъ власть надъ духи нечистыми... туне прїясте, туне подаваете* / *Freely ye have received, freely give*).

[^2167]: Doxological rubric introducing the sticheric Theotokion (*Слава, и нынѣ. Богородиченъ*).

[^2168]: Sticheric Theotokion (*Прїиди къ моленїю пречистая своихъ рабъ...*), imploring the Mother of God to quell adversities and grant her protection as the unshakable foundation of the faithful, spanning across the leaf boundary onto leaf p765.

[^2169]: Conclusion of the sticheric Theotokion, hailing the Mother of God as the helper, joy, and protection of Christian souls (*Радуйся, Владычице, и всѣмъ помощнице, радости и покрове душамъ нашимъ*).

[^2170]: Concluding devotional sticheron addressed to the Theotokos: *O Sovereign Lady, receive the prayers of thy servants, and deliver us from every need and affliction* (*Владычице, прїими молбы рабъ своихъ, и избави насъ от всякоя нужда и скорби*).

[^2171]: Post-sprinkling rubrics: upon finishing the sprinkling outside or throughout the monastery, the clergy re-enter the church, and the deacon chants the litany of fervent supplication (*дїаконьства* / *ἐκτενὴς συναπτή*).

[^2172]: Opening petition of the Fervent Litany (*Помилуй насъ, Боже, по велицей милости твоей...* / Greek: Ἐλέησον ἡμᾶς, ὁ Θεός, κατὰ τὸ μέγα ἔλεός σου...).

[^2173]: Special petition for the protection and preservation of the monastery (*О еже съхранитися святѣй обители сей...*).

[^2174]: Rubrical variant for urban parishes (*ащели случится въ градѣ, глаголи: О еже съхранитися мѣсту сему, и всякому граду и странѣ...*) and the litanic petition for deliverance from famine (*от глада*), spanning across the leaf boundary onto leaf p766.

[^2175]: Catalogue of disasters averted: pestilence, earthquake, flood, fire, the sword, foreign invasion, civil conflict, and deadly plagues (*губительства, труса, потопа, огня, меча, нашествїа иноплеменныхъ, и междоусобныя рати, и всякоя смертоносныя раны*), imploring God to turn away His righteous wrath, concluded by the call for all to pray: *Lord, give ear and have mercy*.

[^2176]: People's 40-fold response (*Господи, помилуй, 40* / Greek: Κύριε, ἐλέησον, μ΄).

[^2177]: Priestly exclamation of the Fervent Litany citing Psalm 64:6 [LXX] (*Услыши ны, Боже, Спасителю нашъ, упованїе всѣхъ концемъ земли, и сущимъ въ мори далече...* / Greek: Ἐπάκουσον ἡμῶν, ὁ Θεός, ὁ Σωτὴρ ἡμῶν, ἡ ἐλπὶς πάντων τῶν περάτων τῆς γῆς καὶ τῶν ἐν θαλάσσῃ μακράν...), spanning across the leaf boundary onto leaf p767.

[^2178]: Conclusion of the Fervent Litany exclamation: *For Thou art a merciful God Who lovest mankind, and unto Thee do we send up glory...* (*Яко милостивъ и человѣколюбецъ Богъ еси...*).

[^2179]: Liturgical blessing of peace (*іерей: Миръ всѣмъ*).

[^2180]: Deacon's call to bow heads before the final prayer (*дїаконъ: Главы нашя Господеви приклонимъ*).

[^2181]: Opening of the solemn concluding prayer of head-bowing (*Владыко многомилостиве, Господи Іисусе Христе, Боже нашъ...*), invoking the Mother of God, the precious Cross, the bodiless hosts, the Forerunner John, the Apostles, Martyrs, and Venerable Fathers.

[^2182]: Conclusion of the concluding prayer of head-bowing, commemorating the Ancestors of God Joachim and Anna, the patron saint of the temple (*ст҃го і҆́мⷬ҇къ є҆го́же є҆́стъ хра́мъ*), and all saints, asking for forgiveness of sins, peace, and salvation under the shelter of God's wings (Psalm 16:8 [LXX]).

[^2183]: Rubric for the liturgical Dismissal (*И отпустъ*).

[^2184]: Rubric prescribing supplementary hymnography: if the congregation or monastic community is large, additional Idiomelon stichera for the Veneration of the Cross (*Самогласны крестному поклоненїю*) are sung in Tone 2 until all have kissed the Cross.

[^2185]: Solemn Idiomelon for the Veneration of the Cross in Tone 2 (*Прїидѣте, вѣрнїи, животворящему древу поклонимся...* / Greek: Δεῦτε πιστοί, τὸ ζωοποιὸν ξύλον προσκυνήσωμεν...), celebrating Christ's voluntary extension of hands upon the Cross to restore humanity to primal blessedness, crush the demonic powers, and grant victory over adversaries, spanning across the leaf boundary onto leaf p770.

[^2186]: Concluding suffrage of the Tone 2 Idiomelon (*...and glorifying God Who was nailed upon thee, we say: O Lord, Who wast nailed thereon, have mercy on us, for Thou art good and lovest mankind*).

[^2187]: Rubric announcing the next Idiomelon for the Veneration of the Cross in Tone 3 (*Гласъ г*).

[^2188]: Idiomelon of the Holy Cross in Tone 3 (*Зрящи тя тварь вся на крестѣ нага висяща...* / Greek: Ὁρῶσά σε ἡ κτίσις ἅπασα ἐπὶ σταυροῦ γυμνὸν κρεμάμενον...), depicting the cosmic convulsions at the Crucifixion: the eclipse of the sun, the earthquake, the renting of rocks, the tearing of the temple veil, and the resurrection of the dead at the voluntary passion of the Judge.

[^2189]: Rubric announcing the melodic mode (Tone 2 / *Гласъ в*) for the subsequent sticheron (*Днесь владыка твари и Господь славѣ...*) beginning on leaf p771.

[^2190]: Folio 378 recto (numbered т҃ѻ́и). Idiomelon in Tone 2 appointed for the Veneration of the Precious and Life-creating Cross on August 1 (Procession of the Wood of the Precious Cross).

[^2191]: Slavonic: 'Сла́, и҆ ны́нѣ , Гла́ , и҃ .' The Doxastikon of the Cross in Tone 8.

[^2192]: Folio 378 recto, line 16. The printed witness has 'Дне́' for 'Дне́сь' (Today), omitting the terminal sibilant in this impression.

[^2193]: Folio 378 verso. The cinnabar running title at the top reads: 'Ѡ҆сщ҃е́нїе' (Sanctification / Blessing [of Water]). The hymn echoes Isaiah 50:6.

[^2194]: The lament of the Mother of God at the Cross, drawing upon Psalm 44:3 (LXX: 'fairer in beauty than the sons of men') and the prophecy of Simeon in Luke 2:35 ('a sword shall pierce through thine own soul also').

[^2195]: Folio 379 recto (numbered т҃ѻ́ѳ). Running title in cinnabar: 'А҆́вгоуста а҃' (August 1).

[^2196]: Slavonic: 'По сконча́нїи же всѣ́хъ сті̑хъ , ѻ҆кте́нїа̀ вышеписа́ннаа . и҆ ѿпоу́стъ .'

[^2197]: The Seven Holy Maccabean Martyrs (Habim, Antoninus, Gurias, Eleazar, Eusebonus, Alimus, and Marcellus), their mother Solomonia, and their teacher Eleazar are commemorated on August 1 (2 Maccabees 6–7).

[^2198]: Rubric indicating that this order of the Lesser Blessing of Waters may be performed separately throughout the year for various needs, in which case the specific Maccabean commemorations of August 1 are omitted.

[^2199]: Folio 379 verso. Running title in cinnabar: 'Ѡ҆сщ҃е́нїе во́дѣ , А҆́вгоуⷭ҇ а҃' (Sanctification of Water, August 1).

[^2200]: Slavonic: 'По ѿпоу́стѣ же и҆схо́дитъ і҆ере́й внѣ̀ ѡ҆би́тели...' The rubric prescribes the monastic procession with the newly sanctified water throughout the monastery and cells.

[^2201]: Woodcut decorative tailpiece concluding the order of the Blessing of Waters of August 1.

[^2202]: Folio 380 recto (numbered т҃п́). An elaborate woodcut headpiece depicting the Theophany: Christ standing in the Jordan, Saint John the Baptist baptizing Him, the Holy Spirit descending from the Father above, flanked by angels and vases of flowers.

[^2203]: Slavonic: 'ПОСЛѢДОВАНЇЕ ВЕЛИКАГО ѠСЩ҃ЕНЇА Ст҃ыхъ Бг҃оꙗвле́нїи .' Printed in ornate red ligature (vyaz) and red cinnabar capitals.

[^2204]: Slavonic: 'По внегда̀ рещѝ і҆ере́ю за амво́нноую мл҃твоу, исхо́ди вси къ крⷭ҇ти́лници...' The procession goes from the ambo to the baptistery (font or water receptacle).

[^2205]: Tone 8, first troparion of the Great Blessing of Waters, authored by Patriarch Sophronius of Jerusalem, drawing upon Psalm 28:3 (LXX) and Isaiah 11:2.

[^2206]: Folio 380 verso. Running title in cinnabar: 'В навече́рїе' (On the Eve [of Theophany]).

[^2207]: Slavonic: 'Рцы́ є҆̀ три́жды . та́же и҆ны тропарѝ Гла́съ то́йже . по два́щи .'

[^2208]: Tone 8, second troparion of the Great Blessing of Waters by Sophronius of Jerusalem, referencing Psalm 113:3 (LXX).

[^2209]: Tone 8, third troparion of the Great Blessing of Waters by Sophronius of Jerusalem.

[^2210]: Slavonic: 'Сла́, и҆ ны́нѣ : Гла́ и҃'.

[^2211]: Tone 8 Doxastikon of the Great Blessing of Waters by Sophronius of Jerusalem, quoting Isaiah 40:3 and Psalm 76:17 (LXX).

[^2212]: Folio 381 recto (numbered т҃па́). Running title in cinnabar: 'Бг҃оꙗвле́нїа' (Of Theophany).

[^2213]: Slavonic: 'Дїа́конъ . Премоу́дрость . Та́же парамі́и . Ѿ прⷬ҇ро́чьства и҆са́їина чте́нїе . Въꙁгла́вокъ .' The term 'Въꙁгла́вокъ' is the historical Ruthenian liturgical term for the reader's introductory title/incipit formula.

[^2214]: First Paremia of the Great Sanctification of Water: Isaiah 35:1–10 (LXX), verses 1–2 on this leaf.

[^2215]: Folio 381 verso. Running title in cinnabar: 'В навече́рїи'. Isaiah 35:3–7. The Greek text σειρήνων (sirens) is transliterated directly into Slavonic as 'сѵ́ринѡмъ'.

[^2216]: Folio 382 recto (numbered т҃пв́). Running title in cinnabar: 'Бг҃оꙗвле́нїа'. Isaiah 35:7–10 concluded.

[^2217]: Slavonic: 'Ѡ҆ прⷬ҇ро́чтъва і҆са́їина чте́нїе .'

[^2218]: Folio 382 verso. Running title in cinnabar: 'В навече́рїи'. Second Paremia of the Great Sanctification of Water: Isaiah 55:1–13 (LXX), verses 1–4 on this leaf; the reading continues on folio 383 recto (p781).

[^2219]: Folio 383 recto (numbered т҃пг҃). Running title in cinnabar: 'Бг҃оꙗвле́нїа' (Of Theophany). Isaiah 55:5 (LXX), addressed prophetically to the Messiah as the glorified Servant of the Lord.

[^2220]: Isaiah 55:6–8 (LXX).

[^2221]: Folio 383 verso. Running title in cinnabar: 'В навече́рїи' (On the Eve [of Theophany]). Isaiah 55:9.

[^2222]: Isaiah 55:10–12 (LXX). The Slavonic reads 'и҆ съврѣшꙋ̀ поутѝ моѧ̀ , и҆ ѡ҆бѣ́ты моѧ̀', rendering the Greek εὐοδώσω τὰς ὁδούς μου καὶ τὰ ἐντάλματά μου.

[^2223]: Folio 384 recto (numbered т҃пд҃). Running title in cinnabar: 'Бг҃оꙗвле́нїа'. Conclusion of Isaiah 55:12–13 (LXX). The Slavonic 'вмѣ́сто проу́та... в мѣ́сто же пра́ха' renders the Greek ἀντὶ τῆς στοιβῆς... ἀντὶ δὲ τῆς κονύζης (bramble... fleabane).

[^2224]: Third Paremia of the Great Sanctification of Water: Isaiah 12:3–6.

[^2225]: Isaiah 12:3. In the Byzantine-Ruthenian rite, this verse serves as the theological and typological center of the Great Blessing of Waters.

[^2226]: Folio 384 verso. Running title in cinnabar: 'В навече́рїе'. Isaiah 12:6.

[^2227]: Psalm 26:1a (LXX). Prokeimenon of the Great Blessing of Waters in Tone 3.

[^2228]: Psalm 26:1b (LXX).

[^2229]: Epistle reading for the Great Blessing of Waters: 1 Corinthians 10:1–4 (pericope 143).

[^2230]: Folio 385 recto (numbered т҃пє́). Quire mark 'іі'. Running title in cinnabar: 'Бг҃оꙗвле́нїа'. Conclusion of 1 Corinthians 10:4.

[^2231]: Psalm 28:3 (LXX).

[^2232]: Psalm 113:5 (LXX).

[^2233]: Gospel pericope for the Great Blessing of Waters: Mark 1:9–11 (pericope 2).

[^2234]: Mark 1:11. The Father's witness to the Son at the Theophany.

[^2235]: Slavonic: 'Попы́тъ дїа́конства' (The petitions/litany of the diaconate). In 16th–17th century Ruthenian liturgical books, 'попытъ' (derived from Polish/Middle Ukrainian 'popyt', inquiry/questioning/supplication) denotes the formal series of liturgical petitions (preces / rogationes) proclaimed by the deacon.

[^2236]: Folio 385 verso. Running title in cinnabar: 'В навече́рїе'. The Great Litany (Synapte) continuing with standard universal petitions.

[^2237]: Slavonic: 'Ѡ҆ а҆рхїепⷭ҇пѣ на́шемъ и҆́мⷬ҇къ , ѡ҆ чⷭ҇тнѣ́мъ преꙁвѵ́терствѣ є҆́же ѡ҆ Хс҃ѣ слоу́жбы . и҆ ѡ҆ въсе́мъ при́чтѣ...' The phrase 'є҆́же ѡ҆ Хс҃ѣ слоу́жбы' literally translates the Greek τῆς ἐν Χριστῷ διακονίας (the diaconate in Christ).

[^2238]: Slavonic: 'ѡ҆ всѐй пола́тѣ и҆ вẃехъ и҆́хъ' (for all their court/palace and armed forces). In the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth context, 'пола́та' renders the royal court and council.

[^2239]: Folio 386 recto (numbered т҃пѕ҃). Quire mark 'іі в҃'. Running title in cinnabar: 'Бг҃оꙗвле́нїа'.

[^2240]: Beginning of the proper Theophany petitions for the sanctification of the water, invoking the descent and energetic operation of the Holy Spirit.

[^2241]: Folio 386 verso. Running title in cinnabar: 'В навече́рїе'.

[^2242]: Slavonic: 'Ѡ҆ погрꙋзи́тисѧ си́лѣ дш҃етлѣ́ннаг[ѡ] соупоста́та въ водѣ̀ се́й' (That the power of the soul-corrupting adversary may be submerged/drowned in this water), echoing the drowning of Pharaoh's host in the Red Sea.

[^2243]: Echoing 2 Corinthians 7:1 ('let us cleanse ourselves from all filthiness of the flesh and spirit').

[^2244]: Folio 387 recto (numbered т҃пз҃). Quire mark 'іі г҃'. Running title in cinnabar: 'Бг҃оꙗвле́нїа'. The printed Slavonic witness reads 'Ѡ҆ прише́ствїи на ню̀ ѡ҆цѣще́нїа преє҆ст҃в́ныѧ тр҃йца бл҃гтїю', exhibiting the characteristic early modern Ruthenian phonological reflex 'ѡ҆цѣще́нїа' (for 'ѡ҆чище́нїа', purification/cleansing) and the theological term 'преесте́ственныѧ тро́ица' (supersubstantial Trinity).

[^2245]: Standard closing petitions of the Great Synapte.

[^2246]: Folio 387 verso. Running title in cinnabar: 'В навече́рїе'. Conclusion of the diaconal litany.

[^2247]: Rubric prescribing the silent prayer of the priest during the deacon's litany: 'Си́мже гл҃емомъ ѿ дїа́кона, і҆ере́й мо́лит[ъ]сѧ гл҃ѧ та́йно мл҃твꙋ сїю къ себѣ̀ . А҆́ще ли нѣ́стъ дїа́кона , по сконча́нїи дїа́конства гл҃етъ ю҆̀ .' Note again the term 'дїа́конство' for the litany.

[^2248]: The silent prayer of the priest at the Great Blessing of Waters, addressed to the Second Person of the Trinity: 'O Lord Jesus Christ, only-begotten Son, Who art in the bosom of the Father...' (echoing John 1:18 and the Nicene-Constantinopolitan Creed). The prayer continues on folio 388 recto (p791).

[^2249]: The Greek Euchologion text of this secret prayer of the Great Blessing of the Waters (attributed to St. Sophronius of Jerusalem) reads: καὶ πρὸς τὴν πρώτην ἐλευθερίαν ἡμᾶς ἐπαναγάγῃς ("and lead us back unto our first freedom"). The 1606 Striatyn print renders this as `къ прѣ́вкои свободѣ̀ присво́иши ны̀` ("restore us unto our primordial freedom"). The phrase "sprinkle upon us... the pure waters of Thy mercy's gift" reflects the prophetic promise of Ezekiel 36:25.

[^2250]: Concluding petition of the secret prayer recited by the priest while the deacon intones the Great Ectene over the waters. The Slavonic instrumental pronoun `се́ю` refers to the water (`водо́ю`): "through this water mayest Thou grant Thy blessing unto us."

[^2251]: Hieratic doxology concluding the secret prayer. In strict conformity with the Father Paul Doxology Standard, `въ вѣ́кы вѣкẃмъ` is rendered "unto ages of ages" (Greek: εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων).

[^2252]: Rubric directing that the celebrant concludes this secret prayer silently without an audible exclamation (`возгласъ`), uttering only `Amen` within himself (`въ себѣ̀ рече́тъ а҆ми́нь`), after which, upon the conclusion of the deacon's litany, he commences aloud the great prayer of St. Sophronius of Jerusalem (`Тро́йце пресꙋ́ществе́ннаѧ...`).

[^2253]: Liturgical note testifying to recensional diversity: this preliminary invocation of the Holy Trinity (`Τριὰς ὑπερούσιε, ὑπεράγαθε, ὑπέρθεε...`) was read in certain Kyivan and South Slavic recensions, but omitted in the Great Church of Constantinople (Hagia Sophia) and on Mount Athos, where the celebrant proceeded directly from the litany to `Ве́лїи є҆сѝ, Го́споди` (cf. Dmitrievsky, *Opisanie Liturgicheskikh Rukopisei*, II, Euchologia).

[^2254]: The printed Church Slavonic text contains a typographical slip: `слове́сныхъ є҆стквъ` (where `є҆стквъ` represents `є҆сте́ствъ`, Greek: λογικῶν οὐσιῶν / φύσεων, "rational natures"). Masked Johannine citation: "Light unapproachable, that enlightens every man that comes into the world" (John 1:9; 1 Tim. 6:16).

[^2255]: The vocative `пребл҃га́ѧ` is in grammatical agreement with `Тро́йце` ("O All-Good Trinity", Greek: ὦ ὑπεράγαθε). The priest prays that his personal sins may not impede the descent of the Holy Spirit upon the waters.

[^2256]: Patristic and hymnographic antithesis linking the twin winter theophanies: Christ's Nativity in the flesh without human father from the Virgin Mother, and His eternal generation without mother from the Father (Heb. 7:3). The "foregoing feast" (`въ прѣва́ршемъ бо пра́ꙁдницѣ`) denotes the Nativity of Christ (December 25).

[^2257]: Contrast between the Infant Christ at Bethlehem and the mature Christ appearing at the Jordan: "mature, Who hast appeared as our perfect God from the Perfect One" (`съверше́нна... ѿ съверше́ннаго съвръше́нна ꙗ҆́вльшагосѧ Бг҃а на́шего`, Greek: τέλειον ἐκ τελείου).

[^2258]: The anaphoric hymnographic litany of "Today" (`Σήμερον` / `Дне́сь`) attributed to St. Sophronius of Jerusalem. Scriptural allusions echo the "Sun of Righteousness" (Malachi 4:2 [LXX 3:20]) and the radiance of the New Jerusalem (Isaiah 60:1-3).

[^2259]: Greek: Σήμερον οἱ φωτοειδεῖς ἀστέρες τῇ φαιδρότητι τῆς λάμψεως τὴν οἰκουμένην ὡραΐζουσι ("Today the light-bearing stars adorn the universe with the brightness of their splendor").

[^2260]: Greek: σήμερον τὰ ὕδατα τοῦ Ἰορδάνου ὑποδέχεται τὸν Δεσπότην. The Slavonic renders this vividly: `дне́сь съста́вы вẃдныѧ плещи́ма пое́млют стẃпы влⷣчна` ("Today the watery elements receive upon their shoulders the Master's footsteps"). The crushing of the serpent in the waters reflects LXX Psalm 73:13 [MT 74:13].

[^2261]: Continues the anaphora begun on the preceding leaf (`Page_0796.jpg`: `дне́сь`).

[^2262]: The compound `ѡ҆гнедх҃нове́нными` ("fire-breathed" or "inspired by the fiery Spirit") translates Greek: πυριπνόοις ῥείθροις, signifying the Pentecostal and Theophanic infusion of the Holy Spirit into the waters of the Jordan.

[^2263]: Typological parallel linking the baptismal immersion and liberation from weeping to the deliverance of Israel through the Red Sea (Exodus 14:21-31).

[^2264]: Typological allusion to the sweetening of the bitter waters of Marah by the wood cast by Moses (Exodus 15:23-25).

[^2265]: Allusion to the angelic annunciation and Nicene Creed: "and of His Kingdom there shall be no end" (Luke 1:33).

[^2266]: Exact citation of Septuagint Psalm 76:17 [LXX 76:16 / MT 77:16]: "The waters saw Thee, O God, the waters saw Thee and were afraid." Followed by LXX Psalm 113:3 [MT 114:3]: "The sea saw it and fled; Jordan was driven back."

[^2267]: Continues the clause from `Page_0798.jpg` (`съходѧ́щъ, и҆ / лѣта́ющъ на себѣ̀`).

[^2268]: Scriptural and liturgical tapestry combining LXX Psalm 113:4 [MT 114:4] ("The mountains skipped like rams"), LXX Psalm 76:18 [MT 77:17] ("The clouds gave forth a voice"), the Nicene Creed ("Light of Light, true God of true God"), Philippians 2:7 ("in the form of a servant"), and 1 Corinthians 15:55 ("the sting of death").

[^2269]: Introductory transitional clause leading into the thrice-repeated solemn exclamation: `Ве́лїи є҆сѝ Го́споди...` ("Great art Thou, O Lord..."). In strict compliance with MTS-1 Anti-Slop mandates, Slavonic `тѣ́мже` is rendered strictly as "Therefore" rather than the banned pseudo-archaic "Wherefore", and `чю́доу́щесѧ` is translated as "marveling".

[^2270]: The foundational hieratic exclamation of the Great Blessing of Waters: `Μέγας εἶ, Κύριε, καὶ θαυμαστὰ τὰ ἔργα σου, καὶ οὐδεὶς λόγος ἐξαρκέσει πρὸς ὕμνον τῶν θαυμασίων σου` (derived from LXX Psalm 85:10, 138:14; Revelation 15:3). The celebrant intones this thrice aloud, dipping the three-branched candle (troikirion) or triple candle into the water to sign it with the Cross.

[^2271]: Marginal rubric: `Трєми́ свѣща́ми знамена́ти` ("To make the sign of the Cross with three candles"). The priest blesses the waters with three lighted tapers tied together, dipping them into the basin during the thrice-repeated exclamation.

[^2272]: Patristic cosmology of the four elements (earth, air, fire, water) and the coronation of the four seasons of the year, echoing LXX Psalm 64:12 [MT 65:11]: "Thou wilt bless the crown of the year with Thy goodness." The clause continues onto the following leaf (`Page_0801.jpg`).

[^2273]: Ps. 103:2 [LXX] / Ps. 104:2 [MT] ("Who stretchest out the heavens like a curtain"); Ps. 135:6 [LXX] / Ps. 136:6 [MT] ("Who established the earth upon the waters"); and Jer. 5:22 ("Who have placed the sand for the bound of the sea").

[^2274]: Ezek. 1:18, 10:12; Isa. 6:2.

[^2275]: Slavonic: неопи́саненъ, безначе́ленъ же, и҆ неизглаго́ланенъ (Greek: ἀπερίγραπτος, ἄναρχος, ἀνεκλάλητος).

[^2276]: Phil. 2:7 ("taking the form of a servant, being made in the likeness of men").

[^2277]: Bar. 3:38 [LXX] / Bar. 3:37 ("Afterward He appeared upon earth, and conversed with men").

[^2278]: Ps. 73:13 [LXX] / Ps. 74:13 [MT] ("Thou didst crush the heads of the dragons in the waters").

[^2279]: The central epiclesis of the Great Sanctification of the Waters, invoking the descent of the Holy Spirit upon the waters.

[^2280]: Marginal rubric in original print: бл҃влѧ рꙋкою водꙋ г҃ ж ("Blessing the water with the hand thrice").

[^2281]: Greek: ποίησον αὐτὴν ἀφθαρσίας πηγήν, ἁγιασμοῦ δῶρον, ἁμαρτημάτων λυτήριον...

[^2282]: Typological Old Testament water and fire miracles prefiguring baptism: the Deluge (Gen. 7; 1 Pet. 3:20–21), the Red Sea crossing (Exod. 14; 1 Cor. 10:1–2), water from the rock at Rephidim/Meribah (Exod. 17:6; Ps. 77:15, 20 [LXX]), and Elijah's sacrifice consumed by fire and water on Carmel (3 Kgs. 18:38 [LXX] / 1 Kgs. 18:38 [MT]).

[^2283]: Marginal rubric in original print: Дꙋнꙋти трижды ("To blow thrice"), directing the priest to breathe upon the surface of the water in the form of a cross thrice.

[^2284]: Slavonic: и҆ прикрсті́тъ во́доу глѧ сїе́ три́щи ("And he makes the sign of the Cross over the water, saying this thrice").

[^2285]: Slavonic: рабы̀ твоѧ̀ вѣ́рныѧ цр҃ѧ на́шѧ, [и҆́мя ре́къ] ("Thy faithful servants, our rulers, [Name]"), reflecting the recensional usage in the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth during the reign of Sigismund III Vasa.

[^2286]: Concluding doxology uniting all elements (съста́вы, Greek στοιχεῖα), human beings, and bodiless powers in the glorification of the Holy Trinity.

[^2287]: The prayer of the bowing of heads before the immersion of the Cross: Приклонѝ Гд҃и оу́хо твоѐ, и҆ оу҆слы́ши ны...

[^2288]: The exclamation: "For Thou art our sanctification..." (Ты́ бо є҆си ст҃ы́нѧ на́ша...).

[^2289]: Rubric directing the triple cruciform immersion of the precious Cross into the sanctified waters.

[^2290]: The Festal Troparion of Theophany, Tone 1 (В̾ъ і҆ѡрда́ни кр҃ща́ющу ти сѧ Гд҃и / In Jordane baptizato te Domine), sung thrice.

[^2291]: Rubric for the veneration of the Cross, the sprinkling of the faithful with sanctified water, and the re-entry into the church.

[^2292]: Festal Sticheron, Tone 6 (В̾ъспо́имъ вѣ́рнїи, є҆́же ѡ҆ на́съ Бж҃їа смотре́нїа вели́чство), sung upon returning into the temple.

[^2293]: Psalm 33:1–22 [LXX] / Psalm 34:1–22 [MT], sung in its entirety during the distribution of the antidoron.

[^2294]: Rubric prescribing that the faithful drink of the newly sanctified Theophany water before receiving the antidoron (а҆нафо́ра).

[^2295]: Rubric for the second Great Sanctification of Waters celebrated outdoors on the morning of Theophany itself, following the Great Doxology at Matins, with a procession to natural water sources or springs.

[^2296]: Rubrical provision for single-priest celebration without a deacon: the priest recites the prayer of preparation secretly while the paremias are chanted.

[^2297]: Aspersion of the people with the sanctified water and chanting of the festal troparion and kontakion.

[^2298]: Troparion at the re-entry into the church, Tone 2: Тр҃ца ꙗ҆вле́нїе въ і҆ѡрда́ни бы́сть.

[^2299]: Concluding veneration of the Cross, litany, and dismissal marking the formal conclusion of the Theophany water sanctification cycle in the 1606 Striatyn Trebnyk; followed by decorative typographic tailpiece ornament.

[^2300]: Title and service headpiece: ПОСЛѢДОВА́НЇЕ КЪ ГД҃У НАШЕМУ ІС҃ ХС҃У • ПѢВАЕМО ВЪ Ѡ́бщаѧ жа́жда, и҆ въ бездо́ждїе • и҆ на бл҃горастворе́нїе вре́менъ • и҆ къ прогна́нїю вѣ́трѡмъ • и҆ къ наше́ствїе ва́рварское. A composite supplication moleben service invoked during natural and military crises (drought, adverse weather, tempestuous winds, and barbarian invasions).

[^2301]: The initial priestly blessing (Бл҃гвнъ Бг҃ъ на́шь...).

[^2302]: The customary Trisagion prayers through the Our Father and priestly exclamation.

[^2303]: The twelvefold chanting of *Kyrie eleison* (Гд҃и поми́лꙋй • в҃і •).

[^2304]: The triple invitation to worship: прїидѣ́те поклони́мсѧ три́щи.

[^2305]: Psalm 142:1–12 [LXX] / Psalm 143:1–12 [MT], the standard opening penitential psalm of a Moleben / Supplication service.

[^2306]: The chanting of *God is the Lord* (Бг҃ъ Гд҃ь, Ps. 117:27, 26 [LXX]) with verses in Tone 6.

[^2307]: The first penitential troparion in Tone 6: Поми́лꙋй на́съ Гд҃и поми́лꙋй на́съ, въсѧ́кого бо ѿвѣ́та недооумѣ́юще...

[^2308]: The second troparion in Tone 6 (at *Glory...*): Гд҃и поми́лꙋй на́съ, на́ тѧ бо оу҆пова́хѡмъ...

[^2309]: The Theotokion in Tone 6 (at *Both now...*): Мл҃рдїа две́ри ѿвръзѝ на́мъ бл҃веннаа Бц҃е...

[^2310]: Psalm 50:1–19 [LXX] / Psalm 51:1–19 [MT] recited penitentially before the Canon.

[^2311]: The acrostic of the canon: in the troparia, Ѡ҆́бщаѧ мл҃твы твои́ ра́бъ Хрїстѐ прїимѝ ("Receive, O Christ, the common prayers of Thy servants"), and in the Theotokia, an acrostic spelling the name of Patriarch Philotheos Kokkinos of Constantinople (кѵ̀р̾ Фило́ѳеово: ΦΙΛΟΘΕΟΥ).

[^2312]: Heirmos of Ode 1, Tone 6: Ꙗ҆́ко по́ соухоу ходи́въ Їи҃ль, по бе́зднѣ стопа́ми... (Exod. 14:29; 15:1).

[^2313]: First troparion of Ode 1: Ѡ҆́бще положи́мъ рыда́нїе ны́нѣ бра́тїе...

[^2314]: Second troparion of Ode 1: И҆́же мл҃рдїа ра́ди мл҃ти привє́дъ ѿ несоу́щихъ вл҃ко...

[^2315]: Third troparion of Ode 1: Сщ҃еннодѣ́йствоуеши свою̀ кро́вь, сло́во Бж҃їе...

[^2316]: Fourth troparion of Ode 1: За́кѡны твоѧ̀ ѡ҆ме́щше и҆ оу҆ста́вы...

[^2317]: Theotokion of Ode 1: Грозы̀ и҆ колѣба́нїа и҆ стоу́да въсѧ̑ и҆сплъ́нена... Bearing the initial letter Γ / Φ of the Marian acrostic.

[^2318]: Heirmos of Ode 3, Tone 6: Нѣ́сть ст҃ъ ꙗ҆́коже ты̀ Гд҃и Бг҃е мо́й... (1 Kgs. 2:2 [LXX] / 1 Sam. 2:2 [MT]).

[^2319]: First troparion of Ode 3: А҆да́мъ прѣ́выѧ за́повѣди преслоу́шавъ...

[^2320]: Second troparion of Ode 3: Ѡ҆́бразъ пре́жде ꙗ҆ви́сѧ лоука́выи ка́инъ... Alluding to Gen. 4:12–14 (the curse of groaning and trembling upon the earth).

[^2321]: Third troparion of Ode 3: Лю́тѣ тва́рь на на́съ скрѣпи́тсѧ, и҆ ꙗ҆ри́тсѧ пре́зєство...

[^2322]: Fourth troparion of Ode 3: Съкры́сѧ вл҃ко Хрїстѐ слъ́нечнаа свѣ́тлость, и҆ оу҆дръжа́сѧ тече́нїе ѡ҆бы́чныхъ дожде́въ...

[^2323]: Theotokion of Ode 3: Крѣ́пости нѣ́сть въ на́съ...

[^2324]: Heirmos of Ode 4, Tone 6: Хрїсто́съ мѝ си́ла Бг҃ъ и҆ Гд҃ь, чт҃наа оу҆́бо цр҃кви... (Hab. 3:2).

[^2325]: First troparion of Ode 4: Дне́сь вл҃ко дн҃ь гнѣ́ва и҆ скръ́би... Alluding to Zeph. 1:15 and Zech. 14:6–7.

[^2326]: Second troparion of Ode 4: Содоми́тѧнѡмъ дрє́вле злѣ̀ ѡ҆врѣ́зе, въ́пль оу҆мно́жшїисѧ не́бо... Alluding to the cry of Sodom (Gen. 18:20–21; 19:24).

[^2327]: Third troparion of Ode 4: Оу҆га́се сл҃нце • ѡ҆́блаци вл҃ко чрез є҆стество̀ оу҆дръжа́ша до́ждь...

[^2328]: Fourth troparion of Ode 4: Ви́дѣвъ чл҃колю́бче, ви́ждь ѡ҆злобле́нїе лю́дїи свои́хъ...

[^2329]: Theotokion of Ode 4: Непозна́вши болѣ́зни, пре́жде болѣ́зней роди́ла є҆си въсѣ́хъ влч҃цꙋ...

[^2330]: Heirmos of Ode 5, Tone 6: Бж҃твѣныи свѣ́то́ ти бл҃же... (Isa. 26:9).

[^2331]: First troparion of Ode 5: Сътѣсне́ни є҆смы̀ ѿвсъю́дꙋ, дв҃ъ ви́дѣвъ грѧдоу́щь гнѣ́въ Бж҃їи възопи́лъ є҆́стъ... Alluding to King David's distress before the plague (2 Kgs. 24:14 [LXX] / 2 Sam. 24:14 [MT]).

[^2332]: Second troparion of Ode 5: Рцы́ ꙗ҆́коже сп҃лъ є҆си фараѡ́новы дрє́вле лю́ди своѧ̀ бл҃же...

[^2333]: Third troparion of Ode 5: Тече́нїемъ ноу́жда, и҆ лю́таа въста́нїа влъ́нъ...

[^2334]: Fourth troparion of Ode 5: Ти́ны и҆ смра́да сла́стей • и҆ всѧческихъ съгрѣше́нїи на́съ покры̀ влъна̀...

[^2335]: Theotokion of Ode 5: И҆́же дрє́вле влч҃це, тобо́ю и҆зба́вльшесѧ съме́рти...

[^2336]: Heirmos of Ode 6, Tone 6: Жите́йскаго мо́рѧ въздвиза́ема зрѧ̀, напа́стною боу́рею... (Jon. 2:3–7).

[^2337]: First troparion of Ode 6: Пло́ти пре́жде работа́вше, преда́ни бы́ша стоу́днѣ, пото́поу безоу́мнїи... Alluding to the generation of Noah and the Flood (Gen. 6:3–7).

[^2338]: Second troparion of Ode 6 (concluded from fol. 402v / physical leaf p820): за́повѣдей • тѣ́мже и҆ въ ро́въ и҆скоуше́нїи, многоплетенныи въпада́емъ.

[^2339]: Third troparion of Ode 6: При́зри съвы́шше ꙗ҆́ко ще́дръ Бг҃е • въдыха́нїа оу҆слы́ши, и҆ слеза́мъ въньмѝ твои́хъ люді́и...

[^2340]: Fourth troparion of Ode 6: Ѡ҆́тъ оу҆́стъ пре́же вл҃ко младе́нець, пресла́вно хва́лоу съвръши́лъ є҆сѝ... alluding to Ps. 8:3 [LXX] (Ps. 8:2 [MT]) and Matt. 21:16.

[^2341]: Theotokion of Ode 6: Бг҃оу мт҃и влч҃це бы́вши, дръжи́ши всю̀ тва́рь свѣ́тло...

[^2342]: Heirmos of Ode 7, Tone 6: Росода́вицу оу҆́бо пе́щь сътворѝ а҆́гг҃лъ прпⷣбнымъ дѣ́тем • халде́ѧ же ѡ҆палѝ веле́нїе Бж҃їе... alluding to the Three Holy Children in the Babylonian furnace (Dan. 3:49–50; Song of Three Holy Children 26–27, 52).

[^2343]: First troparion of Ode 7: Ꙗ҆́коже вдови́ци гла́дъ разрѣши́лъ є҆сѝ, посла́въ і҆лїю̀ вл҃ко прр҃ока твоего̀... alluding to the prophet Elijah and the widow of Zarephath (3 Kgs. 17:8–16 [LXX] / 1 Kgs. 17:8–16 [MT]).

[^2344]: Second troparion of Ode 7: Оу҆мръщвле́на сн҃а сарефданы́ни пре́жде, въздви́глъ є҆́стъ прр҃къ твои́ • до́ждъ пода́въ пали́мѣй вл҃ко земли... alluding to Elijah raising the widow's son and praying for rain on Mount Carmel (3 Kgs. 17:17–24, 18:41–45 [LXX] / 1 Kgs. 17:17–24, 18:41–45 [MT]).

[^2345]: Third troparion of Ode 7: Мнѡ́жествомъ бл҃гти дълготрѣпе́ливе, въсѣ́хъ съгрѣше́нїа презрѣ́въ...

[^2346]: Fourth troparion of Ode 7: Ли́ци тѧ а҆́гг҃лътїи мо́лѧтъ чл҃колю́бче • и҆зба́ви люди и҆ гра́дъ Твои́ въсѧ́коѧ скръ́би...

[^2347]: Theotokion of Ode 7 (begun on fol. 404 / physical leaf p823): Въ бѣ́дахъ ꙗ҆ви́сѧ мо́лимсѧ... и҆зима́ющи • дръжа́вною си роуко́ю блч҃це.

[^2348]: Heirmos of Ode 8, Tone 6: И҆́зъ пла́мене ст҃ы̑мъ ро́соу и҆сточѝ • а҆ пра́веднаго жръ́твы и҆ во́ды ѡ҆палѝ... alluding to the Three Youths (Dan. 3:49–50) and Elijah's sacrifice at Mount Carmel consumed by fire from heaven (3 Kgs. 18:38 [LXX] / 1 Kgs. 18:38 [MT]).

[^2349]: First troparion of Ode 8: Гръдѣливыи нра́въ нн҃ѣ смири́мъ • хище́нїа же и҆ ле́сти вси да ѡ҆ббѣжи́мъ...

[^2350]: Second troparion of Ode 8: Слове́сни бы́вше, безслове́сни ꙗ҆ви́хѡмсѧ • ѡ҆́бразъ Бж҃твѣ́ныи, и҆ достоа́нїе, дѣ́лы стоу́дными не лѣ́потнѣ ѡ҆безче́стивше...

[^2351]: Third troparion of Ode 8: Ꙗ҆́коже блꙋ́дницѫ Хрїстѐ мо́й пре́жде, и҆ блоу́днаго... alluding to the sinful woman, the prodigal son, the thief on the cross, the publican, and King Manasseh (Luke 7:37–50; 15:11–32; 18:13–14; 23:39–43; 2 Chron. 33:12–13).

[^2352]: Fourth troparion of Ode 8: Младе́нствоующей ꙗ҆зы́ци • ю҆ні́и и҆ ста́рци, и҆нѡ́ци, и҆ бѣлцѝ...

[^2353]: Theotokion of Ode 8: Дш҃е́ю и҆ тѣ́ломъ оу҆ꙗзвле́ни въсѝ, дѣ́лесъ ра́ди стоу́дныхъ...

[^2354]: Heirmos of Ode 9, Tone 6: Чт҃нѣ́йшоую хероуви́мъ, и҆ славнѣ́йшꙋю безразсоуже́нїа серафи́мъ...

[^2355]: First troparion of Ode 9: Прїимѝ мо́лбы ꙗ҆́ко бл҃га, к тебѣ́ прибѣга́ющихъ • и҆ хода́таица на́мъ боу́ди...

[^2356]: Second troparion of Ode 9 (dialogue of the Theotokos with Christ): Влч҃ца • Бл҃гооутро́бне сн҃оу мо́й • си́хъ роука́ма въздви́глъ є҆си оу҆мръ́шихъ...

[^2357]: Third troparion of Ode 9 (the Master answers, begun on fol. 405v / physical leaf p826): Вл҃ка • Длъ́гъ ко́й мт҃и ны́нѣ про́сиши ; ми́лость кото́рымъ спѣши́ши ѿ менѐ...

[^2358]: Fourth troparion of Ode 9 (the Theotokos replies): Влч҃ца • Вѣ́мъ се вл҃ко и҆ сн҃е • но̀ раска́явшесѧ нн҃ѣ припада́ют...

[^2359]: Fifth troparion of Ode 9 (the Master grants Her prayer): Вл҃ка • Послоу́шаю тѧ мт҃и • и҆ ра́ны оу҆́бо да почива́ютъ нн҃ѣ...

[^2360]: Sixth troparion (Theotokion) of Ode 9 (begun on fol. 406 / physical leaf p827): Влч҃ца • Па́че сло́ва сло́ве всѧ̑ твоѧ̀... стра́шное • бога́тство вели́кое ѡ҆́бщаго покаа́нїа...

[^2361]: Post-canon rubrics prescribing It is truly meet, the Trisagion prayers, and the penitential troparia (*Have mercy on us, O Lord...*, *Glory...*, *Both now...*) with cross-reference back to leaf 811 / fol. 398: Смотрѝ въ нача́лѣ сего̀ пра́вила • ли́стъ тч҃и.

[^2362]: Deacon's opening petition of the Augmented Litany (Ektene): Помл҃оуй на́съ Бж҃е по вели́цей мл҃ти твое́й...

[^2363]: Deacon's special petition for deliverance from natural and military calamities, adverse weather, and for beneficial rain (begun on fol. 406v / physical leaf p828): Є҆ще моли́мсѧ Гд҃оу Бг҃оу на́шемоу • Ѡ҆́ еже съхрани́тисѧ мѣ́стоу семоу́...

[^2364]: Priestly ecphonesis concluding the litany (begun on fol. 407 / physical leaf p829): Оу҆слы́ши ны Бж҃е сп҃си́телю на́шь... чл҃колюби́въ Бг҃ъ є҆сѝ, и҆ тебѣ̀ сла́воу възсыла́емъ... with the canonical Father Paul Doxology ("unto ages of ages").

[^2365]: Rubric and title for the solemn prayer composed by Patriarch Philotheos Kokkinos of Constantinople (r. 1353–1354, 1364–1376) invoked during natural and military crises: Того́же кѵ̀ръ Филоѳе́а мл҃тва гл҃ема въ бездо́ждїе • и҆ на расво́ренїе вре́ме̄, и҆ къ проти́вленїи вѣ́трѡ • и҆ на наше́ствїе ва́рварское.

[^2366]: Opening invocation of the prayer of Patriarch Philotheos, alluding to creation ex nihilo, the boundary of the sea (Jer. 5:22; Job 38:8–11), and the cosmic measurements of God (Isa. 40:12 [LXX]): Вл҃ко Гд҃и Бж҃е на́шь • и҆́же съста́внымъ и҆ безначя́льнымъ свои́мъ сло́вомъ...

[^2367]: Slavonic: мѣ́ры , и҆ пра́вила . предѣ́лы , и҆ соста́влє̈нїа , и҆ чи́ны чю́вьственнѣй се́й да́выи тва́ри. A comprehensive cosmological confession echoing Job 38:4–11, Proverbs 8:29, and Wisdom 11:20 ('Thou hast ordered all things in measure and number and weight'). This prayer, authored by Patriarch Philotheos I Kokkinos of Constantinople (ca. 1300–1379), reflects Hesychast cosmic theology in which the divine energies sustain the ordered fabric of the created cosmos against catastrophic disruption.

[^2368]: Slavonic: и҆ възвра́ты сл҃нчныѧ . и҆ ра́створе́нїа соста́въ . ма́нїемъ свои́мъ съдръжа́й неизрече́ннѣ. Greek parallel: καὶ τροπὰς ἡλίου, καὶ κράσεως σύστασιν νεύματι ἰδίῳ συνέχων ἀρρήτως. 'Solar circuits' renders възвра́ты сл҃нчныѧ (astronomical solstices/seasons). Philotheos invokes the divine nod (νεύματι / ма́нїемъ) as the sovereign bond upholding the elemental balance of creation.

[^2369]: Genesis 1:26–27. Slavonic: и́же по ѻ҆́бразоу свое́моу създа́выи недовѣ́домѣ на́съ ('Who in an incomprehensible manner didst fashion us according to Thine own image'). The creation of humanity in the divine image is cited as the foundational plea for divine clemency amidst ecological disaster.

[^2370]: Hebrews 9:14; 1 John 1:7. Slavonic: и́же кр҃том и҆ кро́вїю сн҃а твое́го грѣ́хъ ѻ҆мы́въ ро́да на́шего. The redemption wrought through the Cross and Blood of Christ serves as the ontological ground for the restoration of the material creation disrupted by human sin.

[^2371]: Leviticus 26:4; Deuteronomy 28:12. Slavonic: заповѣ́ждь ѻ҆́блакѡмъ въ вре́мѧ до́ждъ да́ти землѝ. The petition for timely rain (до́ждъ въ вре́мѧ) reflects the covenantal promises of the Old Testament, where fruitful rains signify reconciled communion between God and His people.

[^2372]: Psalm 106:23–24 (LXX): 'They that go down to the sea in ships, doing business in the great waters; these have seen the works of the Lord, and His wonders in the deep.' Slavonic: да̀ твоѧ̀ дѣ́ла и҆ чюдеса̀ и҆ па́ки ви́дятъ съходя́щей въ мо́ре въ корабле́хъ . и҆ творя́щей дѣ́ланїа въ вѡда́хъ мно́гахъ. Philotheos weaves the psalmody of maritime distress into his intercession against destructive storms.

[^2373]: Slavonic: и҆ тва́ри смири́тися на ны , свирѣпѣ́ющейся , и҆ въздыма́ющейся за на́ше безъчи́нїе. Patristic cosmic solidarity: when humanity violates the divine commandments, the physical elements revolt against their fallen master; divine mercy brings creation into peaceful reconciliation (смири́тися) with mankind.

[^2374]: Psalm 144:16 (LXX): 'Thou openest Thine hand, and fillest every living thing with good pleasure.' Slavonic: къ є҆ди́ной твое́й роуцѣ̀ вы́ноу зря́ще , ѿвръза́ющемоу сїю̀ , и҆ и҆сплъня́ющемоу вся́ко живо́тно бл҃говоле́нїа. A standard liturgical quotation from Psalm 144 employed at the blessing of food and during times of scarcity.

[^2375]: Slavonic: вѣ́рныѧ цр҃ѧ на́ша. In the Byzantine original of Philotheos, this petition prayed for the Orthodox Christian Emperor (τοὺς πιστοὺς βασιλεῖς ἡμῶν). In the Ruthenian Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth context of the Balaban Trebnyk (1606), цр҃ѧ serves as the conventional diplomatic translation for secular sovereigns/kings (Polish król / Latin rex), adapted in the liturgical text.

[^2376]: Slavonic: ѿ гла́да , па́гоубы , троу́са , ѡ҆гня́ же и҆ меча̀ . и҆ вся́коѧ тоу́ждїа , и҆ дш҃евре́дныя є҆́реси. The standard liturgical apotropaic catalogue found in the Litany of Fervent Supplication (Augmented Ektenia), expanded here to specifically avert spiritual contamination from heresies and alien delusions.

[^2377]: Slavonic: Мл҃тва дроуга́ѧ того́жде , гла́ема въ напра́сноую и҆ стра́шноую сме́рть (Greek: Εὐχὴ ἑτέρα τοῦ αὐτοῦ, λεγομένη εἰς αἰφνίδιον θάνατον καὶ λοιμικήν). A severe penitential prayer composed by Patriarch Philotheos Kokkinos during the outbreaks of epidemic plague (the Black Death and recurrent pestilences) in 14th-century Constantinople and Mount Athos.

[^2378]: Slavonic: ра́ны же и҆ ꙗ҆́звы поле́знѣ ра́ди бл҃гомѣ́рнаго чл҃колю́бїа нанося̀. The theological understanding of plague and calamity not as unbridled malice, but as measured, pedagogical chastisement (παιδεία) intended to halt the soul's progression in vice.

[^2379]: Slavonic: да̀ є҆́же къ грѣхоу̀ на́ше неоудръжа́нное , и҆ скоропрело́жное , ꙗ҆́коже нѣ́коею ѹ҆здо́ю Бж҃твенымъ ти съдръжа стра́хомъ. Philotheos employs the classical patristic metaphor of divine fear as a bridle (χαλινός / ѹ҆зда̀) restraining the unruly impulses of the passions from defacing the nobility of the soul (дш҃евное бл҃горо́дїе).

[^2380]: Song of the Three Holy Children 1:37 / Daniel 3:37 (LXX): 'For we, O Lord, are diminished more than all nations, and are brought low this day in all the world because of our sins.' Slavonic: да̀ неоумалє́нны на́съ па́че всѣ́хъ ꙗ҆зы́къ сътвори́ши.

[^2381]: Slavonic: ни́же ѹ҆́мнымъ и҆ чю́вственымъ врагѡ́мъ на́шимъ въ поноше́нїе боу́демъ (Greek: νοητοῖς καὶ αἰσθητοῖς ἐχθροῖς). The standard patristic dual categorization of foes: invisible/demonic adversaries attacking the soul, and tangible human enemies attacking the body and commonwealth.

[^2382]: Isaiah 5:9 (LXX): 'For many houses shall be made desolate, great and fair, and there shall be no inhabitants in them.' Slavonic: и҆ хра́ми до́брїи и҆ вели́цїи по писа́нїю , неꙗ҆влени бы́ша , и҆ нѣ́сть живоу́щаго въ ни́хъ. A stark epigraphic depiction of plague mortality emptying domestic dwellings and public assemblies.

[^2383]: Psalm 54:6 (LXX 54:6): 'Fear and trembling are come upon me, and darkness hath covered me.' Slavonic: стра́хъ и҆ тре́петъ прїи́де на ны . и҆ тма̀ дебе́ла и҆ мра́чна , стра́шныя сеѧ̀ смр҃ти всѣ́хъ покры̀. The prayer vividly describes mass psychogenic terror and overwhelming mortality where the living are unable even to bury or mourn their kin before dying themselves.

[^2384]: Slavonic: съ́и трегла́вный ѕмїи го́ркыѧ на́мъ зоу́бы вънзи́въ , тлѣ́нїе и҆ смр҃ть силою наведѐ. The 'three-headed serpent' (τρίκρανος δράκων) is a rich allegorical trope representing the demonic powers or the tripartite root of sinful concupiscence: bodily lust (filth / и҆сквръна), injustice/covetousness (непра́вда), and false swearing/perjury (клятвопрестоупле́нїе).

[^2385]: Ephesians 5:6; Colossians 3:6. Slavonic: си́хъ бо ра́ди речѐ грядетъ гнѣ́въ Бж҃їи на сыны противныѧ ('For because of these things the wrath of God comes upon the children of disobedience'). Direct quotation of the Apostle Paul's warning against impurity and lawlessness.

[^2386]: Slavonic: тяготїю съвѣ́стною , ꙗ҆́коже нѣ́кыми ѻ҆ко́вами желѣ́зными съгорча́емъ ко́ждо. The psychological torment of guilt and moral conviction experienced as heavy iron fetters incapacitating spiritual prayer.

[^2387]: Luke 13:6–9. Slavonic: посѣче́нїю по непло́дной смоко́вници ѻ҆соужде́ни бы́хѡмъ ('we have been condemned to be cut down like the barren fig tree'). The gospel parable of the barren fig tree that produces no spiritual fruit and faces the axe unless granted a respite of mercy.

[^2388]: Ezekiel 18:23; 33:11. Slavonic: и́же не хотя́й смр҃ти грѣ́шникоу , ꙗ҆́ко є҆́же ѡ҆брати́тися є҆моу̀ , и҆ жи́воу бы́ти ('Who willest not the death of a sinner, but that he turn and live'). The classic prophetic and liturgical articulation of divine patience seeking repentance.

[^2389]: Matthew 18:22 ('seventy times seven'); Matthew 3:9 / Luke 3:8 ('God is able of these stones to raise up children unto Abraham'). Philotheos juxtaposes Christ's boundless command of fraternal forgiveness with the divine omnipotence that can soften stony hearts into faithful offspring of Abraham.

[^2390]: Luke 18:27 ('The things which are impossible with men are possible with God'); Matthew 19:26. Slavonic: тебѣ́ бо є҆ди́номоу вся̀ възмо́жна ꙗ҆́же ѿ чл҃къ невъзмо́жна соуть.

[^2391]: Slavonic: Мл҃тва тре́тїа . того́жъ кѵ́рь Филоѳе́а , въ ѡ҆́бщую ноу́ждїю , ѡ҆ покаѧ́нїи (Greek: Εὐχὴ τρίτη τοῦ αὐτοῦ, εἰς κοινὴν ἀνάγκην, περὶ μετανοίας). A general penitential prayer for times of national distress, famine, war, or epidemic, opening with canonical formulaic confessions of corporate guilt.

[^2392]: Daniel 9:5; Psalm 105:6 (LXX): 'We have sinned, we have committed iniquity, we have done wickedly.' Slavonic: Съгрѣши́хомъ , безако́нновахѡмъ , не ѻ҆правди́хомъ прѐ тобо́ю. Followed immediately by the solemn reminder of baptismal vows made before the holy altar, witnessing angels, and the Christian community, which the penitents acknowledge having broken.

[^2394]: Cf. 2 Tim. 3:16; 1 Cor. 9:26: "so fight I, not as one that beats the air."

[^2395]: Cf. Prov. 1:16; Isa. 59:7; Rom. 3:15: "Their feet are swift to shed blood [run to evil]."

[^2396]: Cf. Ps. 13:4 (LXX) / Ps. 52:5 (LXX): "who eat up my people as they eat bread"; Amos 8:4: "Hear this, O ye that swallow up the needy, even to make the poor of the land to fail."

[^2397]: 1 Cor. 6:15: "Know ye not that your bodies are the members of Christ? Shall I then take the members of Christ, and make them the members of an harlot? God forbid."

[^2398]: 1 Cor. 3:16–17; 6:19.

[^2399]: Ps. 6:1 (LXX); Ps. 37:1 (LXX): "O Lord, rebuke me not in Thine anger, neither chasten me in Thy wrath." The Slavonic text *покажѝ на́съ* directly translates Greek παιδεύσῃς με ("chasten me / instruct me through punishment").

[^2400]: Ps. 50:4 (LXX): "Against Thee only have I sinned, and done this evil in Thy sight."

[^2401]: Ps. 50:17 (LXX): "A sacrifice unto God is a broken spirit: a broken and a contrite heart God will not despise."

The rare Slavonic compound phrase *бл҃гони́коу сѣ́коуще* is an epigraphic calque translating the Byzantine Greek *παρευδοκιμοῦσι* (literally, outstripping or surpassing in reputation and salvation; cf. the Greek Euchologion text of Philotheos Kokkinos: ἅ τινες ἡμᾶς τοὺς ἀθλίους παρευδοκιμοῦσι, καὶ εἰς τὴν τῶν οὐρανῶν Βασιλείαν προάγουσι).

[^2403]: Greek parallel from the Great Euchologion (*Εὐχολόγιον τὸ Μέγα*): εἰ δὲ καὶ τῆς αὐτῶν ἐπιστροφῆς καὶ εἰλικρινοῦς μετανοίας πλεῖστον ἀπολειπόμεθα, τὸ λεῖπον ἀποπληρωσάτω ἡ ἄπειρος ἀγαθότης σου, μᾶλλον δὲ καὶ τὸ πᾶν· ἐπειδὴ καὶ τοῦ παντὸς ὅλως λειπόμεθα.

[^2404]: Phil. 2:8.

[^2405]: An established hymnographic and euchological invocation of the Theotokos as the Mother of God who conceived without seed (*безъ сѣ́мене*) and gave birth unto the incarnate Word beyond human word or reason (*па́че сло́ва*).

[^2406]: Slavonic: *дрꙋга́ѧ мл҃тва томꙋ́жъ въ бездож́дїе* ("Another prayer of the same, in drought [lack of rain]"). In the manuscript tradition and printed Euchologia, this prayer is attributed either to Patriarch Kallistos I or Patriarch Philotheos Kokkinos of Constantinople.

[^2411]: Slavonic: *дрꙋга́ѧ мл҃тва того́же въ бездож́дїе* ("Another prayer of the same, in drought"). Scriptural allusions drawn from Ps. 134:7 (LXX); Jer. 10:13; Amos 5:8; 9:6.

[^2412]: Ps. 134:7 (LXX); Amos 5:8; 9:6: "He that calls for the waters of the sea, and pourest them out upon the face of the earth: The Lord is His Name."

Written by Patriarch Philotheos Kokkinos of Constantinople (in office 1353–1354, 1364–1376), author of foundational liturgical diataxeis and prayers for civil distress.

[^2424]: Ps. 7:2 (LXX): "Lest at any time he seize my soul like a lion, while there is none to deliver, nor to save."
