[^2441]: Col. 2:9: "For in Him dwells all the fulness of the Godhead bodily."

[^2442]: Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."

[^2443]: Slavonic: *ꙗ҆́же млъча́нїа незаблоу́дный поутѝ оу҆чи́телю* ("who art the unerring teacher of the way of stillness/silence"). An explicit euchological witness to the theology and practice of Byzantine Hesychasm (*ἡσυχία*). Patriarch Philotheos Kokkinos was the disciple, biographer, and liturgical defender of Saint Gregory Palamas.

[^2444]: Greek parallel from Philotheos's Euchologion text: καὶ παντοίων θεοειδῶν χαρισμάτων τε καὶ θαυμάτων ἀνεξάντλητον πέλαγος.

[^2445]: Ps. 60:3 (LXX): "For Thou hast been a shelter for me, and a strong tower from the face of the enemy."

[^2446]: Cf. Ps. 113:11 (LXX) / Ps. 115:3; Ps. 134:6 (LXX): "Whatsoever the Lord pleased, that did He in heaven, and in earth."

[^2447]: An allusion to the traditional Byzantine Litany petitions of the Divine Liturgy for travelers, the sick, and captives (*τοῖς πλέουσι, τοῖς ὁδοιποροῦσι, νοσοῦσι, κάμνουσι, αἰχμαλώτοις, καὶ τῆς σωτηρίας αὐτῶν*).

[^2448]: Slavonic: *вѣ́рныѧ же цр҃ѧ на́ша* (Greek: τοὺς πιστοὺς βασιλεῖς / ἄρχοντας ἡμῶν). In early modern Ruthenian imprints, civil rulers are commemorated within traditional Byzantine liturgical formulas.

[^2449]: Greek parallel in Philotheos: τὸ ἐπικείμενον τῆς ἀθυμίας νέφος ("the impending cloud of despondency/faintheartedness").

[^2450]: Standard Byzantine euchological litany clause: λιμοῦ, λοιμοῦ, σεισμοῦ, καταποντισμοῦ, πυρός, μαχαίρας, ἐπιδроμῆς ἀλлофύλων, καὶ ἐμφυλίου πολέμου ("from famine, pestilence, earthquake, flood, fire, sword, the incursion of foreign nations, and civil war").

[^2451]: Slavonic: *ПСЛѢДОВАНЇЕ БЫВА́ЕМО ВЪ ВРЕ́МЯ БЕЗЪДО́ЖДЇА* (Greek: Ἀκολουθία εἰς ἀνομβρίαν / Τάξις γινομένη ἐν καιρῷ ἀνομβρίας, "Order / Office performed in time of drought").

[^2452]: The initial blessing of the priest: *Blessed is our God always, now and ever, and unto ages of ages.*

[^2453]: The standard Byzantine Trisagion Prayers (Trisagion, All-Holy Trinity, Lord's Prayer with priestly doxology).

[^2454]: The customary twelve repetitions of *Lord, have mercy* (*Kyrie eleison*).

[^2455]: The threefold Invitation to Worship (Ps. 94:6 LXX): "O come, let us worship and fall down before Him..."

[^2456]: Psalm 142 (LXX) / Psalm 143: "Hear my prayer, O Lord, give ear to my supplication in Thy truth..."

[^2457]: Psalm 117:27, 26 (LXX): "God is the Lord, and hath appeared unto us: blessed is he that comes in the Name of the Lord."

[^2458]: The first penitential troparion in Tone 6: *Ἐλέησον ἡμᾶς, Κύριε, ἐλέησον ἡμᾶς...* ("Have mercy on us, O Lord, have mercy on us; for, at a loss for any defense, we sinners offer this supplication unto Thee as Master: have mercy on us, O Lord, have mercy on us").

[^2459]: The troparion following *Glory...*: *Κύριε, ἐλέησον ἡμᾶς, ἐπὶ σοὶ γὰρ πεποίθαμεν...* ("O Lord, have mercy on us, for in Thee have we trusted; be not exceedingly wroth with us, nor remember our iniquities; but look down even now as Thou art compassionate, and deliver us from our enemies...").

[^2460]: The Theotokion following *Both now...*: *Τῆς εὐσπλαγχνίας τὴν πύλην ἄνοιξον ἡμῖν, εὐλογημένη Θεοτόκε...* ("Open unto us the door of compassion, O blessed Theotokos: hoping in thee, let us not perish; through thee may we be delivered from adversities, for thou art the salvation of the Christian race"). The catchword *млⷭ҇р́дїа* at the bottom of physical leaf p860 continues as *две́ри ѿвръзѝ на́мъ* on physical leaf p861.

[^2461]: The continuation and conclusion of the Theotokion from the preceding page (p860): *Твоея бо милости двери отверзи нам, благословенная Богородице...* (Greek: Τῆς εὐσπλαγχνίας τὴν πύλην ἄνοιξον ἡμῖν, εὐλογημένη Θεοτόκε, "Open unto us the door of compassion, O blessed Theotokos: hoping in thee, let us not perish; through thee may we be delivered from adversities, for thou art the salvation of the Christian race").

[^2462]: Physical leaf p811. The rubric directs the reader back to the general supplicatory service (*Молебенъ*) at folio 398 (printed: *листъ тчи́*) for the full texts of the introductory prayers, Psalms, and initial troparia.

[^2463]: Psalm 50 (LXX) / Psalm 51: "Have mercy on me, O God, according to Thy great mercy: and according to the multitude of Thy compassions blot out my transgression..."

[^2464]: The Supplicatory Canon (*Канонъ молебный*) for drought in Tone 2 is a venerable Byzantine office preserved in the Great Euchologion (*Εὐχολόγιον τὸ Μέγα*) and ascribed to Joseph the Hymnographer (*Κανὼν παρακλητικὸς εἰς ἀνομβρίαν*).

[^2465]: Heirmos of Ode 1, Tone 2 (based on Ex. 15:1–19): "Come, ye peoples, let us sing a song unto Christ God, Who divided the sea and guided the people whom He brought forth from the bondage of Egypt, for He hath been glorified" (Greek: Δεῦτε λαοί, ᾄσωμεν ᾆσμα Χριστῷ τῷ Θεῷ, τῷ διελόντι θάλασσαν, καὶ ὁδηγήσαντι τὸν λαόν, ὃν ἀνῆκε δουλείας Αἰγυπτίων, ὅτι δεδόξασται).

[^2466]: Cf. Ps. 132:3 (LXX); Hos. 14:5: "I will be as the dew unto Israel: he shall grow as the lily, and cast forth his roots as Lebanon."

[^2467]: Ps. 94:6 (LXX): "O come, let us worship and fall down before Him: and let us weep before the Lord Who made us."

[^2468]: Greek: Διὰ σοῦ τὸ φῶς ἐπέγνωμεν, Θεοτόκε... Theotokion celebrating the Mother of God as the portal through whom the uncreated Light of the Word dawned upon humanity (cf. John 1:9; 8:12).

[^2469]: The second supplicatory canon is addressed to the Most Holy Theotokos in Tone 4, a classic Byzantine model sung to the famous Heirmos *Ἀνοίξω τὸ στόμα μου* (traditionally composed by Saint John of Damascus).

[^2470]: Heirmos of Ode 1, Tone 4: "I shall open my mouth, and it will be filled with the Spirit, and I shall utter a word unto the Queen Mother..." (Greek: Ἀνοίξω τὸ στόμα μου καὶ πληρωθήσεται πνεύματος...).

[^2471]: Slavonic: *хлѣ́би нб҃ныѧ* (a graphical and phonetic variant in early Ruthenian imprints for *хля́би небе́сныѧ*, the "cataracts" or "floodgates of heaven", citing Gen. 7:11 and Mal. 3:10: *отверзу вам хляби небесныя* / Greek: καταρράκτας τοῦ οὐρανοῦ). Here translated as "the floodgates of heaven" (pouring forth rain as sustenance/bread for earthly mortals).

[^2472]: The mystical typological title of the Theotokos as the "heavenly Cloud" (*νεφέλη οὐράνιος*) bearing the spiritual rain of Christ is drawn from Isaiah 19:1 ("Behold, the Lord rides upon a swift cloud").

[^2473]: An explicit Patristic articulation of Orthodox Triadology: the three unoriginate Hypostases (*лица*) distinguished by their unique personal hypostatic properties (*свойства*), yet co-equal in the one divine essence and undivided will (*въ единой воли*).

[^2474]: An allusion to the Prophet Elijah (3 Kings 17:1; 18:41–45 / James 5:17–18): "Elias was a man subject to like passions as we are, and he prayed earnestly that it might not rain: and it rained not on the earth by the space of three years and six months. And he prayed again, and the heaven gave rain, and the earth brought forth her fruit."

[^2475]: Again, Slavonic *хлѣ́би нб҃ныѧ* for *хля́би небе́сныѧ* (the floodgates/cataracts of heaven).

[^2476]: Heirmos of Ode 3, Tone 2: "Establish us in Thyself, O Lord, Who by the Tree didst put to death sin, and plant Thy fear in the hearts of us who sing praise unto Thee" (Greek: Στερέωσον ἡμᾶς ἐν σοὶ Κύριε, ὁ ξύλῳ νεκρώσας τὴν ἁμαρτίαν, καὶ τὸν φόβον σου ἐμφύτευσον, εἰς τὰς καρδίας ἡμῶν τῶν ὑμνούντων σε).

[^2477]: Isaiah 40:12: "Who hath measured the waters in the hollow of His hand, and meted out heaven with the span, and comprehended the dust of the earth in a measure..."

[^2478]: An allusion to the Parable of the Prodigal Son (Luke 15:13): "and there wasted his substance with riotous living."

[^2479]: Slavonic: *до́ждъ бл҃горастворе́нъ*, translating Greek εὔκρατον ὑετόν ("well-tempered / well-seasoned rain", beneficial for agricultural fertility without damaging downpours).

[^2480]: Heirmos of Ode 3, Tone 4: "Establish thy choir of singers, O Theotokos, living and plentiful fountain, who are banded together in spiritual fellowship; and in thy divine glory vouchsafe them crowns of glory" (Greek: Τοὺς σοὺς ὑμνολόγους, Θεοτόκε, ἡ ζῶσα καὶ ἄφθονος πηγή, θίασον συγκροτήσαντας πνευματικόν, στερέωσον...).

[^2481]: Ps. 78:4 (LXX): "We are become a reproach to our neighbors, a scorn and derision to them that are round about us."

[^2482]: Jer. 10:24; Ps. 6:1 (LXX): "O Lord, correct me, but with judgment; not in Thine anger, lest Thou bring me to nothing."

[^2483]: Mark 16:14; Eph. 4:18: "because of the blindness/hardness (*πώρωσις*) of their heart."

[^2484]: Ezekiel 44:2: "Then said the Lord unto me; This gate shall be shut, it shall not be opened, and no man shall enter in by it; because the Lord, the God of Israel, hath entered in by it, therefore it shall be shut."

[^2485]: Heirmos of Ode 4, Tone 2 (based on Hab. 3:2): "I praise Thee, O Lord, for I have heard the report of Thee and was afraid: for Thou didst come unto me, seeking me who had gone astray; therefore I glorify Thy great dispensation toward us, and our renewal" (Greek: Ὑμνῶ σε, ἀκοῇ γὰρ Κύριε εἰσακήκοα καὶ ἐξέστην· ἕως ἐμοῦ γὰρ ἥκεις, ἐμὲ ζητῶν τὸν πλανηθέντα· διὸ τὴν πολλήν σου οἰκονομίαν, τὴν εἰς ἐμὲ δοξάζω, πολυέλεε).

[^2486]: Luke 15:4–6; Luke 19:10: "For the Son of man is come to seek and to save that which was lost."

[^2487]: Ps. 101:19–20 (LXX): "Because He hath looked down from the height of His sanctuary; from the heaven did the Lord behold the earth; to hear the groaning of the prisoners; to loose those that are appointed to death."

[^2488]: Deut. 11:17; 3 Kings 8:35: "When heaven is shut up, and there is no rain, because they have sinned against Thee: if they pray toward this place, and confess Thy Name, and turn from their sin, when Thou afflictest them: then hear Thou in heaven, and forgive the sin of Thy servants..."

[^2489]: Slavonic: *во́лный до́жъ* [дождь], translating Greek ὑετὸν ἑκούσιον (Ps. 67:9 LXX: "Thou, O God, didst send a plentiful [voluntary/free] rain, whereby Thou didst confirm Thine inheritance, when it was weary").

[^2490]: Ps. 144:16 (LXX): "Thou openest Thine hand, and satisfiest the desire of every living thing."

[^2491]: Heirmos of Ode 4, Tone 4: "He Who sits in glory upon the throne of the Godhead, Jesus Most Divine, hath come on a light cloud, and with His incorrupt hand hath saved them that cry: Glory to Thy power, O Christ" (Greek: Ὁ καθήμενος ἐν δόξῃ ἐπὶ θρόνου θεότητος, ἐν νεφέλῃ κούφῃ, ἦλθεν Ἰησοῦς ὁ ὑπέρθεος, τῇ ἀκηράτῳ παλάμῃ καὶ διέσωσε, τοὺς κραυγαζόντας· Δόξα, Χριστέ, τῇ δυνάμει σου).

[^2492]: The Archangels Michael and Gabriel invoked as supreme commanders of the heavenly hosts (*ἀρχιστράτηγοι*) interceding before the throne of God (cf. Dan. 10:13; Luke 1:19; Rev. 8:2).

[^2493]: Slavonic: *лицѐ землѝ оу҆маща́ти* (cf. Ps. 103:15 LXX: τοῦ ἱλαρῦναι πρόσωπον ἐν ἐλαίῳ, "to make the face shine / to fatten the earth with rich produce").

[^2494]: Luke 15:20–24 (the Prodigal Son) and Luke 18:13–14 (the Publican).

[^2495]: Lev. 26:4; Deut. 11:14; 28:12: "The Lord shall open unto thee His good treasure, the heaven to give the rain unto thy land in his season, and to bless all the work of thine hand..."

[^2496]: Traditional Byzantine imperial petition for the subjugation of hostile enemies beneath the ruler's feet (cf. Ps. 17:39, 48 LXX; Ps. 46:4 LXX: "He hath subdued the people under us, and the nations under our feet").

[^2497]: Heirmos of Ode 5, Tone 2: "O Lord, Giver of light and Creator of the ages, guide us in the light of Thy commandments; for beside Thee we know no other God" (Greek: Ὁ τοῦ φωτὸς χορηγός, καὶ τῶν αἰώνων ποιητὴς Κύριος, ἐν τῷ φωτὶ τῶν σῶν προσταγμάτων ὁδήγησον ἡμᾶς· ἐκτὸς γάρ σου ἄλλον Θεὸν οὐ γινώσκομεν).

[^2498]: Isaiah 26:9, 13 (LXX): "With my spirit within me will I seek Thee early: for when Thy judgments are in the earth, the inhabitants of the world will learn righteousness... O Lord our God, other lords beside Thee have had dominion over us: but by Thee only will we make mention of Thy Name."

[^2499]: Ps. 62:2 (LXX); Ps. 142:6 (LXX): "My soul thirsts after Thee, as a thirsty land."

[^2500]: The text breaks off at the foot of physical leaf p870 (*въ врѣ́мѧ*, "in the time [of...]") and concludes on physical leaf p871 (*на́пастей на́шихъ...*, "...of our afflictions, and save us from the impending wrath; send down rain upon Thine earth, O Master, out of Thy good pleasure, O Lover of mankind").

[^2501]: Continuation of the supplication for rain from physical leaf p870: *Send rain unto Thy land, O Master...* Allusion to the prophetic prayers of Elijah for the cessation of drought (1 Kings / 3 Kingdoms 18:41–45) and the promise of seasonal rains (Joel 2:23).

[^2502]: *The Twelve Apostles* (Slavonic: `Ѡбоюна́десѧте [Ѡбона́десѧте] а҆пл҃ъ`): archaic dual-derived compound numeral denoting the sacred college of the Twelve Apostles interceding alongside the choirs of holy martyrs.

[^2503]: Slavonic: `Всѣ́хъ зе́мнїи ходата́ицоу къ Бг҃оу , и҆́мамы тѧ̀ дв҃о Бц҃е`. The nominative plural `зе́мнїи` ("we earthly ones / earthborn") functions as the subject of the clause, designating the collective mortal faithful invoking the Mother of God as universal mediatress before Christ.

[^2504]: Incipit of the second Heirmos of Ode 5: *All things were amazed at Thy divine [glory]...* (Slavonic: `Оу҆диви́шасѧ всѧ́ческаѧ ѡ Бж҃твѣнѣ́й [сла́вѣ твое́й]`), the classical Byzantine/Slavonic heirmos associated with Tone 4 and Tone 8 suppliant canons.

[^2505]: Allusion to Psalm 67:36 LXX: *Marvelous is God in His holy places / among His saints: the God of Israel, He will give power and strength unto His people.*

[^2506]: A classical Christological-theological antinomy articulating the dual generation of the Logos: eternally begotten of the Father without a mother in heaven, and temporally born in the flesh of the Virgin without an earthly father.

[^2507]: Triadological stanza invoking the *Thrice-unoriginate Trinity* (`Трибезначя́лноую тр҃цоу`), confessing the consubstantial and co-eternal Godhead, undivided in essence and single in divine will, yet existing in three distinct hypostases (*licy* / Persons).

[^2508]: Slavonic: `подъ нѡ́зѣ вѣ́рномоу цр҃ю на́шемоу` ("beneath the feet of our faithful sovereign"). Standard recensional prayer for the Christian sovereign / king, preserved faithfully in the 1606 Balaban imprint within the political realities of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth.

[^2509]: Incipit of Ode 6 Heirmos: *Held fast in the abyss of sins...* (Slavonic: `Въ бе́зднѣ грѣхо́внѣй ѻ҆дръжи́мъ...`). The Jonah heirmologic archetype drawing upon Jonah 2:2–7, where the belly of the sea monster typifies the depths of human sin and deliverance from Hades.

[^2510]: Slavonic: `ꙗ҆́ко и҆моу́ще дръзнове́нїе мнѡ́го къ Бг҃у` (Greek *parrhesia*): the spiritual boldness and intimacy of intercession granted to the martyrs through their shedding of blood for Christ.

[^2511]: Scriptural allusion to Psalm 84:4–5 LXX: *Turn us, O God of our salvation, and turn away Thine anger from us. Wilt Thou be angry with us unto ages?*

[^2512]: *temperate rain* (Slavonic: `до́ждъ бл҃горастворе́нъ` / Greek *eukraton hyeton*): a well-tempered, fruitful rain that brings vegetation to maturity without destroying crops through inundation, hail, or violent squalls.

[^2513]: Incipit of the second Heirmos of Ode 6: *Prefiguring, he cried out...* (Slavonic: `възопи́лъ проѻбразоу́ѧ`), referencing the prophetic typological cry of Jonah prefiguring the three-day burial and resurrection of Christ.

[^2514]: Scriptural allusion to Genesis 7:11 and Malachi 3:10 (Slavonic: `хлѧ́би нб҃сныѧ` / Greek *katarraktas tou ouranou*), the opening of the celestial sluice gates or cataracts to pour water upon the parched earth.

[^2515]: Slavonic: `Жестото́ю грѣхо́вною ѻ҆дръжи́ми` ("held fast by the hardness/callousness of sin"). A patristic lament denoting the dry, stony heart incapable of weeping, for which the intercession of the Virgin is sought to obtain compunction and the grace of tears (*penthos*).

[^2516]: Kontakion, Tone 6: *O Champion of Christians that cannot be put to shame...* (Slavonic: `Застоу́пнице хрїтїа́нѡмъ непосты́днаѧ`), the universally renowned Byzantine Marian kontakion appointed widely throughout molebens and daily liturgical cycles.

[^2517]: Ikos: *Stretch forth thy palms, wherewith thou didst embrace the Master of all as an Infant...* (Slavonic: `Прострѝ дла́ни своѝ, и҆́маже въсѣ́хъ вл҃коу ꙗ҆́ко младе́нца ѻ҆бѧ́тъ`). Poetic theological juxtaposition of the physical maternal holding of the incarnate Christ with her spiritual intercession for mankind.

[^2518]: *fountain of compassion* (Slavonic: `млр҃дїа сꙋ́щи исто́чникъ`): traditional Byzantine Marian title praising the Mother of God as the channel through whom divine mercy flows to believers.

[^2519]: Ode 7 Heirmos: *The most wise youths bowed not down to the golden image...* (Slavonic: `Образоу злато́моу непоклони́шасѧ дѣ́ти премꙋ́дрїи`), drawn from the Song of the Three Holy Youths in Babylon (Daniel 3), where the Angel of the Lord turned the fiery furnace into a dewy breeze.

[^2520]: Allusion to the Prayer of Manasses, King of Judah (2 Chronicles 33:11–13 / LXX Odes 12), the classical liturgical archetype of earnest repentance from grievous sin resulting in divine mercy and deliverance from bondage.

[^2521]: Scriptural penitential formula: *for we have sinned and committed iniquity exceedingly...* (cf. Daniel 9:5; Baruch 2:12; Psalm 105:6 LXX), acknowledging corporate transgression as the moral cause of natural calamities.

[^2522]: Slavonic: `прибѣ́жище стра́шно , и҆ ѻ҆роу́жїе непобѣди́мо` ("an awe-inspiring refuge and unconquerable weapon"), expressing the invincible military-protective role ascribed to the Mother of God in Byzantine-Slavonic hymnography.

[^2523]: Incipit of the second Heirmos of Ode 7: *He Who saved in the fire the Abrahamic children...* (Slavonic: `Сп҃сы́й въ ѡ҆́гни а҆враа́мскыѧ дѣ́ти`), referencing the Three Youths of the lineage of Abraham delivered from the furnace by the pre-incarnate Word.

[^2524]: Rubric *Glory...* (`Сла́ва ·`) at the foot of physical leaf p880 marks the transition to the Doxasticon troparion concluded on the subsequent leaf (p881: *May the fury of Thy threatening not come to an end, O Christ...*).

[^2525]: Troparion under *Glory...* concluding the first canon of Ode 7 (fol. 435r / physical page 881). The hymn petitions Christ to avert the extremity of divine chastisement (Да не сконча́етъсѧ ꙗ́рость преще́нїа твоего́ Хрїстѐ) and to water the fruits with dew, witnessing the Early Modern Ruthenian Church Slavonic vocalism весела̀ for modern Church Slavonic веселѧ̀.

[^2526]: Rubrical indication for the concluding Marian troparion (Theotokion) of Ode 7: *Both now and ever...* (И҆ ны́нѣ).

[^2527]: Theotokion of Ode 7 (fol. 435r / physical page 881). The text preserves the characteristic Early Modern Ruthenian Church Slavonic form грꙋ́бости на́шей ("our coarseness / callousness", from Ukrainian/Old Belarusian грубість), reflecting the spiritual hardness of heart that precipitated divine drought.

[^2528]: Fol. 435r. The printed witness reads сп҃са и҆ Бг҃а заны́съ молѧ́щи with the phonetic/typesetting composite заны́съ witnessing the prepositional syntagma за ны / за насъ ("for us").

[^2529]: Opening Heirmos of Ode 8 (Tone 8 / Tone 2 pattern): И҆́же въ пе́щь ѡ҆́гненоу къ дѣ́темъ є҆вре́йскымъ съше́дшаго... (Greek: Τὸν ἐν καμίνῳ τοῦ πυρὸς τῶν Ἑβραίων τοῖς παισὶ συγκαταβάντα...). Commemorates the Three Holy Children in the Babylonian furnace (Dan. 3:49–50 [LXX]), praising God Who transformed flame into moisture and coolness, invoking the Father Paul Doxology standard (*unto the ages*).

[^2530]: First troparion of Ode 8 (fol. 435v / physical page 882). Commemorates the Prophet Elijah (3 Kgdms. 17:1; 18:41–45 [LXX] / 1 Kings 17:1; 18:41–45 [MT]), whose prayer restrained and subsequently restored heavenly rain upon the earth.

[^2531]: Second troparion of Ode 8 (fol. 435v / physical page 882). Collective intercession of the celestial hierarchy: angelic choirs, assemblies of apostles, prophets, martyrs, hierarchs, and monastic saints entreating the Creator to deliver those who faithfully praise Him.

[^2532]: Third troparion of Ode 8 (fol. 435v / physical page 882). Scriptural typology of divine deliverance: Jonah preserved and delivered from the belly of the sea monster (Jonah 2:1–11) and Daniel delivered unharmed from the pit and lions (Dan. 6:16–23).

[^2533]: Concluding Theotokion of the first canon of Ode 8 (fol. 436r / physical page 883), imploring the Mother of God to plead before the Savior for the sinful city and people facing drought.

[^2534]: Rubric and truncated incipit for the second Heirmos of Ode 8: Ѻ́трокы бл҃гочти́выѧ въ пещи ро : ~ (Greek: Παῖδας εὐαγεῖς ἐν τῇ καμίνῳ...). Per Statutory Mandate 16, unwritten liturgical incipits are preserved without interpolative editorial expansion.

[^2535]: First troparion of the second canon, Ode 8 (fol. 436r / physical page 883). Pleads that divine visitation not mirror the full destructive severity of Elijah's zeal, but rather send gentle lightnings and rain, granting perfection of earthly fruits.

[^2536]: Second troparion of the second canon, Ode 8 (begun on fol. 436r / physical page 883 and concluding on fol. 436v / physical page 884). Recalls the penitential prayer and weeping of King Manasseh (2 Chron. 33:12–13; Prayer of Manasseh), pleading that divine wrath be transmuted into tender mercy through the prayers of the all-pure Mother of God.

[^2537]: Truncated doxological rubric: *Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit* (Сла́ва).

[^2538]: Third troparion of the second canon, Ode 8 (fol. 436v / physical page 884), addressed directly to the holy Forerunner and Baptist John, petitioning him to mobilize the company of all the prophets to intercede for the people that call upon the Name of the Lord.

[^2539]: Truncated Marian liturgical rubric: *Both now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen* (И҆ ны́нѣ).

[^2540]: Concluding Theotokion of the second canon of Ode 8 (begun on fol. 436v / physical page 884 and concluding on fol. 437r / physical page 885). The printed witness displays the dialectal/corrupt form Щедрота́ми си оу҆вѣ́ждиша мт҃и Бж҃їа... representing оу҆вѣ́жди сѧ / оу҆вѣ́ждьшисѧ ("relenting / being moved by thy compassions", Greek δυσωπουμένη), imploring Mary to loose the bonds of sins and heal infirmities.

[^2541]: Textual variant on fol. 437r (physical page 885). The Balaban print witnesses є҆диномрѣ́но (scribal/typesetting contraction for єдиномꙋ́дренно or єдиномѣ́рно, translating Greek ὁμοφρόνως — "with one mind / with one accord").

[^2542]: Opening Heirmos of Ode 9 (Tone 8 pattern): И҆́же ѿ Бг҃а Бг҃ъ сло́во... (Greek: Τὸν ἐκ Θεοῦ Θεὸν Λόγον...). Formulates the orthodox Christology of the Incarnation: the divine Word renewing fallen Adam through the Virginal birth.

[^2543]: First troparion of Ode 9 (begun on fol. 437r / physical page 885 and concluding on fol. 437v / physical page 886). Direct supplication to the Lord as All-Compassionate Creator to grant fruit-bearing rain unto the parched earth and save human souls.

[^2544]: Second troparion of Ode 9 (fol. 437v / physical page 886). Invocation of divine pity upon the works of God's hands, pleading that chastisement not be delivered in wrath, echoing Ps. 6:2 and Ps. 37:2 (LXX) [Ps. 6:1; 38:1 MT].

[^2545]: Third troparion of Ode 9 (fol. 437v / physical page 886). Petitions the Master for deliverance of cities and villages from famine and afflictions, granting abundant harvests and spiritual salvation.

[^2546]: Concluding Theotokion of the first canon of Ode 9 (fol. 438r / physical page 887). Typological meditation on the Babylonian furnace: as the dew-bearing presence of God refreshed the Three Youths in the flames, so may the rain won by the Mother of God refresh the faithful burning with drought.

[^2547]: Rubric and truncated incipit for the second Heirmos of Ode 9: Є҆́ва оу҆́бо не́дꙋгомъ преслоуша́нїа... (Greek: Ἡ μὲν τῷ τῆς παρακοῆς νοσήματι...). Contrasts the curse brought into the world through the disobedience of Eve with the universal blessing introduced through the Virgin Mary.

[^2548]: First troparion of the second canon, Ode 9 (begun on fol. 438r / physical page 887 and concluding on fol. 438v / physical page 888), addressed to the Holy Apostle Peter. Alludes to the Petrine keys of the Kingdom of Heaven (Matt. 16:19) and the apostolic power to bind and loose sins, begging Peter to unlock the rain-bearing floodgates of heaven.

[^2549]: Second troparion of the second canon, Ode 9 (fol. 438v / physical page 888), addressed to the Holy Apostle Paul. Commemorates Paul's mystical ascent unto the Third Heaven (2 Cor. 12:2–4), begging his bold intercession before God for both early and latter rain (Joel 2:23; James 5:7).

[^2550]: Truncated doxological rubric: *Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit* (Сла́ва).

[^2551]: Third troparion of the second canon, Ode 9 (fol. 438v / physical page 888), addressed to the Holy Protomartyr and Archdeacon Stephen. Recalls Stephen's vision of the heavens opened and the Son of Man standing at the right hand of God (Acts 7:55–56), asking his intercession alongside the holy martyrs.

[^2552]: Truncated Marian liturgical rubric: *Both now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen* (И҆ ны́нѣ).

[^2553]: Concluding Theotokion of the second canon of Ode 9 (begun on fol. 438v / physical page 888 and concluding on fol. 439r / physical page 889). Entreats the Virgin Mary to silence heretical blasphemies, defend against belligerent foes, and grant victory to the Christian monarch.

[^2554]: Post-canon rubrical sequence (fol. 439r / physical page 889): prescribes the Megalynarion (*It is truly meet*), the Trisagion Prayers through the *Our Father*, followed by the penitential troparia of Tone 6 (*Have mercy on us, O Lord, have mercy on us...*, *Glory...*, *Both now...*), directing the celebrant to the cross-referenced text on fol. 398 (physical leaf p811).

[^2555]: Liturgical rubric on fol. 439r (physical page 889) prescribing the chanting of the psalmody and the Prokeimenon in Tone 4 prior to the Epistle lection.

[^2556]: Prokeimenon response in Tone 4 (fol. 439r / physical page 889): Psalm 84:4 (LXX) [Psalm 85:4 MT]: *Turn us back, O God of our salvations, and turn away Thine anger from us* (Ѡ҆братѝ ны Бж҃е сп҃се́нїи на́шихъ, и҆ възвратѝ ꙗ҆́рость твою̀ ѿ на́съ).

[^2557]: Prokeimenon verse in Tone 4 (fol. 439v / physical page 890): Psalm 84:5 (LXX) [Psalm 85:5 MT]: *Wilt Thou be angry with us unto ages? Or wilt Thou stretch out Thy wrath from generation to generation?* (Є҆да̀ въ вѣ́кы прогнѣ́ваешисѧ на ны; и҆ли простреши гнѣ́въ своѝ ѿ ро́да въ ро́дъ).

[^2558]: Liturgical lection rubric announcing the Epistle reading: *The Catholic Epistle of James* (ѿ събо́рнаго посла́нїа і҆а́ковлѧ чте́нїе).

[^2559]: Opening of the Epistle lection for drought (fol. 439v / physical page 890): James 4:7–11a. The Apostle exhorts the faithful to humble repentance, purification of heart, and cessation of slander and fratricidal judgment as spiritual preconditions for divine relief.

[^2560]: Epistle lection for drought (fol. 438r / physical page 891): James 4:11b–12. St. James warns against evil speaking and judging one's brother, affirming that the sole Lawgiver and Judge is God Himself, Who possesses the divine power to save and destroy.

[^2561]: Epistle lection for drought (fol. 438r / physical page 891): James 4:13–15a. The Apostle condemns presumption and commercial arrogance in planning the future without reference to divine providence, comparing mortal human life to a transient vapor (па́ра / ἀτμίς) that quickly vanishes.

[^2562]: Conclusion of James 4 (fol. 438v / physical page 892): James 4:15b–17. The Apostle underscores submission to God's will (*If the Lord wills*), condemning empty boastings and defining sin as the conscious omission of known good (вѣ́доущему же оу҆́бо добро̀ твори́ти, и҆ не творѧ́щу, грѣ́хъ є҆моу є҆́сть).

[^2563]: Epistle lection for drought (fol. 438v / physical page 892): James 5:17–18. The liturgical lection omits James 5:1–16 and transitions directly to the typology of the Prophet Elijah, a man of like passions (чл҃къ подобостра́стенъ / ὁμοιοπαθὴς ἄνθρωπος) whose fervent prayer closed heaven for three years and six months and whose subsequent prayer reopened the skies to give rain and fruitful abundance.

[^2564]: Epistle lection for drought (begun on fol. 438v / physical page 892 and concluding on fol. 439r / physical page 893): James 5:19–20a. The Apostle encourages the fraternal restoration of those who have wandered from the path of truth.

[^2565]: Conclusion of the Epistle lection (fol. 439r / physical page 893): James 5:20b. The promise of spiritual reward for restoring an erring sinner: saving a soul from death and covering a multitude of sins (покры́етъ мно́жество грѣхѡ́въ).

[^2566]: Alleluiarion response in Tone 8 chanted following the Epistle (fol. 439r / physical page 893): *Look upon us and have mercy on us* (при́зри на ны и҆ поми́луй ны).

[^2567]: Alleluiarion verse (fol. 439r / physical page 893): Psalm 118:133 (LXX) [Psalm 119:133 MT]: *Direct our steps according to Thy word* (Стѡпы̀ на́шѧ напра́ви по словеси твое́му̀).

[^2568]: Rubric introducing the first Gospel lection for drought (fol. 439r / physical page 893): *The Gospel according to Luke* (Е҆ѵⷢлїе ѿ лоукы́).

[^2569]: Opening of the first Gospel lection (fol. 439r / physical page 893): Luke 4:22–24. Christ addresses the congregation in the synagogue of Nazareth, who marvel at His gracious words yet question His identity, stating that no prophet is accepted in his own country.

[^2570]: Continuation of the first Gospel lection (fol. 439v / physical page 894): Luke 4:25–29. Christ cites the historic famine of Elijah's day when rain was withheld for three years and six months and Elijah was sent only to the Gentile widow of Zarephath in Sidon, and the cleansing of Naaman the Syrian in Elisha's day, provoking the fury of the Nazarenes who drive Him toward the brow of the hill.

[^2571]: Conclusion of the first Gospel lection (fol. 440r / physical page 895): Luke 4:29b–30. The miraculous passage of Christ unharmed through the midst of the murderous crowd intending to cast Him down headlong from the precipice.

[^2572]: Rubric introducing the second alternative Gospel lection for drought (fol. 440r / physical page 895): *Another Gospel from Mark* (Дру́гое е҆ѵⷢлїе ѿ ма́рка).

[^2573]: Second Gospel lection for drought (begun on fol. 440r / physical page 895 and concluding on fol. 440v / physical page 896): Mark 11:22–25a. Christ instructs His disciples on the power of unshakable faith to move mountains, efficacy of prayer, and the absolute requirement to forgive others as a prerequisite for receiving divine forgiveness.

[^2574]: Conclusion of the second Gospel lection (fol. 440v / physical page 896): Mark 11:25b–26. Warning that failure to forgive others prevents the heavenly Father from forgiving our trespasses.

[^2575]: Liturgical rubric on fol. 440v (physical page 896): prescribes the deacon or priest to recite the special petitions of the augmented litany (*дїа́конства*) discreetly or with discernment (*разсу́дно*).

[^2576]: Opening petition of the special Augmented Litany for drought (fol. 440v / physical page 896), invoking Psalm 50:3 (LXX) [Psalm 51:1 MT]: *Have mercy on us, O God, according to Thy great mercy...*

[^2577]: Choral/congregational response rubric on fol. 440v (physical page 896): *People: "Lord, have mercy," thrice* (лю́дїе · Гдⷭи поми́луй · по г҃).

[^2578]: Second petition of the Augmented Litany for drought (fol. 440v / physical page 896), invoking the divine character revealed in Ezek. 18:23, 32; 33:11: God Who desires not the death of sinners, but awaits their return and repentance.

[^2579]: Third petition of the Augmented Litany for drought (fol. 440v / physical page 896), invoking Psalm 134:7 (LXX) [Psalm 135:7 MT] and Jer. 10:13: God Who brings up clouds from the ends of the earth and commands the rain to descend.

[^2580]: Fourth petition of the Augmented Litany for drought (fol. 441r / physical page 897), echoing Amos 5:8 and 9:6: God Who summons the waters of the sea and pours them upon the face of the earth, petitioning divine blessing and joy.

[^2581]: Fifth petition of the Augmented Litany for drought (fol. 441r / physical page 897), invoking Psalm 67:10 (LXX) [Psalm 68:9 MT] for bountiful or voluntary rain (*до́ждь во́ленъ* / βροχὴν ἑκούσιον) to water all creation and multiply grain in the fields.

[^2582]: Sixth petition of the Augmented Litany for drought (fol. 441r / physical page 897), combining Psalm 146:8 and Psalm 103:14 (LXX) [Psalm 147:8; 104:14 MT]: God Who clothes heaven with clouds, prepares rain for the earth, and makes grass spring up for beasts and herb for the service of men.

[^2583]: Seventh petition of the Augmented Litany for drought (begun on fol. 441r / physical page 897 and concluding on fol. 441v / physical page 898), citing Psalm 64:11 (LXX) [Psalm 65:10 MT]: *Water the furrows of the earth, and multiply her grain*.

[^2584]: Eighth petition of the Augmented Litany for drought (fol. 441v / physical page 898), quoting Psalm 122:2 (LXX) [Psalm 123:2 MT]: *As the eyes of servants look unto the hands of their masters, so do our eyes look unto Thee, O God...*

[^2585]: Ninth petition of the Augmented Litany for drought (fol. 441v / physical page 898), evoking Matt. 5:45: God Who makes His sun rise on the good and the evil, and sends rain on the just and the unjust.

[^2586]: Tenth petition of the Augmented Litany for drought (fol. 441v / physical page 898), invoking Psalm 103:2 (LXX) [Psalm 104:2 MT]: God Who covers Himself with light as with a garment, imploring Him to send down rain by His mercy.

[^2587]: Eleventh petition of the Augmented Litany for drought (begun on fol. 441v / physical page 898 and concluding on fol. 442r / physical page 899), petitioning the Holy One Who dwells on high to look with loving-kindness upon His people.

[^2588]: Twelfth petition of the Augmented Litany for drought (fol. 442r / physical page 899), invoking Psalm 78:8 and Psalm 129:3 (LXX) [Psalm 79:8; 130:3 MT]: *Remember not our iniquities, O Master; for if Thou shouldest mark iniquities, O Lord, O Lord, who shall stand?*

[^2589]: Thirteenth petition of the Augmented Litany for drought (fol. 442r / physical page 899), echoing Psalm 68:17 (LXX) [Psalm 69:16 MT]: *Give ear unto us, O Lord, for sweet is Thy mercy* (*ӕ҆́ко кро́тость твое́ѧ мл҃ти* / ὅτι χρηστὸν τὸ ἔλεός σου), petitioning Him to sustain the earth.

[^2590]: Fourteenth petition of the Augmented Litany for drought (fol. 442r / physical page 899), repeating the supplication of Psalm 68:17 (LXX) for divine goodness and the watering of the parched earth.

[^2591]: Fifteenth petition of the Augmented Litany for drought (fol. 442r / physical page 899), quoting Psalm 78:8 (LXX) [Psalm 79:8 MT]: *Let Thy tender mercies speedily prevent us, O Lord...*

[^2592]: Sixteenth petition of the Augmented Litany for drought (begun on fol. 442r / physical page 899 and concluding on fol. 442v / physical page 900): traditional prayer for the protection of the monastic habitation (*ѡ҆би́тель*), city, and region from famine, pestilence, earthquake, flood, fire, sword, foreign invasion, and civil strife.

[^2593]: Seventeenth petition of the Augmented Litany for drought (fol. 442v / physical page 900), praying for deliverance from all affliction and the dispensation of rich divine mercy upon all in need.

[^2594]: Eighteenth petition of the Augmented Litany for drought (begun on fol. 442v / physical page 900 and concluding on fol. 443r / physical page 901), pleading that divine love for mankind cover human sins and avert the impending wrath, witnessing the Ruthenian orthographic variation of preposition *ѡ* for *ѿ* (*ѡ въсѣ́хъ бѣ́дъ*).

[^2595]: Conclusion of the eighteenth petition of the Augmented Litany for drought (begun on fol. 442v / physical page 900 and concluding on fol. 442r [bis] / physical page 901), pleading that divine love for mankind deliver the faithful from the impending wrath, citing the interrogative of Ps. 75:8 (LXX) [Ps. 76:7 MT] and Nahum 1:6: *who shall stand against the face of Thy wrath?* (кто̀ постои́тъ проти́вꙋ лицꙋ̀ гнѣ́ва твоего́). Note the printer's repetition of folio number 442 (у̃м҃в) on physical page 901.

[^2596]: Nineteenth petition of the Augmented Litany for drought (fol. 442r [bis] / physical page 901), supplicating the Lord our God to bestow abundant rain upon the face of all the earth and gladden it.

[^2597]: Conclusion of the twentieth and final petition of the Augmented Litany for drought (begun on fol. 442r [bis] / physical page 901 and concluding on fol. 442v / physical page 902), praying for the turning away of divine wrath and the granting of beneficial rain out of God's innate goodness.

[^2598]: Liturgical rubric on fol. 442v (physical page 902): prescribes the congregation or choir to chant *Lord, have mercy* fifty times (*лю́дїе · Г͠и помл͠ꙋй · н҃*), an ancient monastic and Byzantine penitential practice for times of public calamity.

[^2599]: Liturgical rubric on fol. 442v (physical page 902): directs the priest to proclaim the prayer with a loud voice (*та́же попъ мл͠твоу въꙁгла́сноую гл͠етъ ве́лми*).

[^2600]: Priest's exclamatory prayer for drought (fol. 442v / physical page 902), opening with the classic Byzantine petition based on Psalm 64:6 (LXX) [Psalm 65:5 MT]: *Give ear unto us, O God our Savior, the hope of all the ends of the earth, and of them that be far off upon the sea* (Оу҆слы́ши ны Б͠же сп҃сителю на́шь, оу҆пова́нїе всѣ̑мъ кѡ́нцемъ землѝ, и҆ сꙋ́щимъ въ мо́ри дале́че). The Ruthenian text witnesses the phonetic spelling *сꙋ́ди* for *бꙋ́ди* (*милостиве мл͠тивъ сꙋ́ди на́мъ*).

[^2601]: Traditional sacerdotal concluding exclamation and doxology (fol. 442v / physical page 902), rendered strictly according to the Father Paul Doxology Standard (*unto ages of ages*).

[^2602]: Liturgical dialogue on fol. 442v (physical page 902): sacerdotal Pax (*Peace be unto all*) and the deacon's invitation to head-bowing (*Bow your heads unto the Lord* / Гла́вы ва́шѧ Г͠ви приклоните), introducing the kneeling prayers for rain.

[^2603]: Rubric on fol. 443r (physical page 903): directs all the faithful to bow their heads and kneel, while the priest recites the special prayers in order with great attention and compunction of heart (*На́мъже всѣ̑мъ гла́вы, и҆ колѣ́на преклѡ́ншимъ · С͠тль гл͠етъ мл͠итвы рѧдо́мъ съ всѧ́кы вниманїем, и҆ оу҆миле́нїем ср͠ца*).

[^2604]: Opening of the First Kneeling Prayer for Rain (fol. 443r / physical page 903), invoking the historic biblical typology of the Prophet Elijah (3 Kingdoms 17–18 / 1 Kings 17–18) whose prayers first withheld and then restored rain, imploring Christ to send bountiful rain upon His inheritance (Ps. 67:10 LXX [Ps. 68:9 MT]).

[^2605]: Continuation of the First Kneeling Prayer for Rain (begun on fol. 443r / physical page 903 and concluding on fol. 443v / physical page 904), pleading for the poor, the suckling infants, and the cattle, invoking Psalm 144:15 (LXX) [Psalm 145:15 MT]: *for they trust in Thee, Who givest them food in due season*.

[^2606]: Sacerdotal conclusion and Trinitarian doxology of the First Kneeling Prayer for Rain (fol. 443v / physical page 904).

[^2607]: Rubric introducing the Second Kneeling Prayer for Rain (fol. 443v / physical page 904): *Second Prayer for the Same* (мл͠тва .в҃. томꙋ).

[^2608]: Opening of the Second Kneeling Prayer for Rain (fol. 443v / physical page 904), drawing directly from Psalm 134:7 (LXX) [Psalm 135:7 MT] and Jeremiah 10:13: God Who brings up clouds from the ends of the earth, makes lightnings for the rain, and brings forth winds out of His treasuries.

[^2609]: Continuation of the Second Kneeling Prayer for Rain (begun on fol. 443v / physical page 904 and continuing on fol. 445r / physical page 905), invoking Amos 5:8 and 9:6 (summoning the waters of the sea), Genesis 7:11 and Malachi 3:10 (opening the cataracts of heaven: ѿве́рꙁи хлѧ́би нб͠ныѧ / καταρράκτας τοῦ οὐρανοῦ). Note that the printer omitted folio 444 in the Cyrillic numeration, jumping directly from fol. 443 (у̃м҃г) to fol. 445 (у̃м҃є).

[^2610]: Continuation of the Second Kneeling Prayer for Rain (fol. 445r / physical page 905), pleading on behalf of all segments of human society (elders, youths, nurslings, servants) and brute animals, citing Psalm 103:14 (LXX) [Psalm 104:14 MT]: *that the fields may bring forth grass for the cattle, and green herb for the service of men*.

[^2611]: Conclusion of the supplication of the Second Kneeling Prayer for Rain (begun on fol. 445r / physical page 905 and concluding on fol. 445v / physical page 906), evoking Psalm 6:2 (LXX) [Psalm 6:1 MT] (*rebuke us not in Thine indignation*) and reiterating Psalm 144:15 (LXX).

[^2612]: Sacerdotal conclusion and Trinitarian doxology of the Second Kneeling Prayer for Rain (fol. 445v / physical page 906).

[^2613]: Rubric introducing the Third Kneeling Prayer for Rain (fol. 445v / physical page 906): *Third Prayer* (мл͠тва тре́тїа).

[^2614]: Opening of the Third Kneeling Prayer for Rain (begun on fol. 445v / physical page 906 and continuing on fol. 446r / physical page 907), addressing the Lord as the high and glorious Lover of mankind Who rewards each according to his labors (Ps. 61:13 LXX [Ps. 62:12 MT]; Rom. 2:6).

[^2615]: Continuation of the Third Kneeling Prayer for Rain (fol. 446r / physical page 907), identifying the Christian flock with the sheep of God's pasture (Ps. 78:13 and 94:7 LXX [Ps. 79:13 and 95:7 MT]) gathered through the Incarnation from pagan idolatry, and invoking Christ as the Good Shepherd Who laid down His life for the sheep (John 10:11).

[^2616]: Scriptural quotation in the Third Kneeling Prayer for Rain (begun on fol. 446r / physical page 907 and continuing on fol. 446v / physical page 908): Luke 12:32 (*Fear not, little flock; for it is your Father's good pleasure to give you the kingdom* / не бо́йсѧ ма́лое моѐ ста́до, ꙗ҆́ко и҆ꙁво́ли ѿц͠ъ ва́шь нб͠ны[й] да́ти ва́мъ цр͠твїе).

[^2617]: Penitential supplication of the Third Kneeling Prayer for Rain (fol. 446v / physical page 908), invoking Colossians 2:14: imploring Christ to blot out the handwriting of our stumbling blocks and sins (*загла́ди рꙋкописа́нїе събла́ꙁнъ на́шихъ* / τὸ καθ' ἡμῶν χειρόγραφон).

[^2618]: Continuation of the Third Kneeling Prayer for Rain (begun on fol. 446v / physical page 908 and continuing on fol. 447r / physical page 909), confessing human frailty in the words of Abraham (Gen. 18:27) and Job (Job 42:6): *for we are dust and ashes before Thee, O Lord* (ꙗ҆́ко пръ́сть и҆ пра́хъ є҆смы̀ пр͠ед̾ тобо́ю Г͠и).

[^2619]: Supplication of the Third Kneeling Prayer for Rain (fol. 447r / physical page 909), quoting Psalm 142:2 (LXX) [Psalm 143:2 MT]: *Enter not into judgment with Thy servants* (не въни́ди въ сꙋ́дъ съ рабы̀ твои́ми).

[^2620]: Penitential confession in the Third Kneeling Prayer for Rain (begun on fol. 447r / physical page 909 and continuing on fol. 447v / physical page 910), acknowledging the prodigal flight from the divine Master, servitude to carnal passions, and begging for the salutary fear of God in hearts.

[^2621]: Supplication of the Third Kneeling Prayer for Rain (fol. 447v / physical page 910), pleading for mercy at the Dread Judgment and invoking Psalm 137:8 (LXX) [Psalm 138:8 MT]: *for we are Thy servants, and the work of Thy hands* (твои́ бо є҆смы рабѝ, и҆ дѣ́ло роу́коу твое́ю).

[^2622]: Concluding scriptural interrogation of the Third Kneeling Prayer for Rain (fol. 447v / physical page 910, concluding on fol. 448r / physical page 911), quoting Psalm 129:3 (LXX) [Psalm 130:3 MT]: *If Thou shouldest mark our iniquities, O Lord, O Lord, who shall stand?* (А҆́ще на беꙁакѡ́нїа на́ша при́зриши Г͠и; Г͠и кто постои́тъ;).

[^2623]: Ps. 129:4, 7 (LXX: ὅτι παρὰ σοὶ ὁ ἱλασμός ἐστιν... καὶ πολλὴ παρ' αὐτῷ λύτρωσις). The printed Slavonic witness reads ѡ҆цѣще́нїе (purification/propitiation), showing typical Ruthenian/Kyivan graphic interchange of ѣ for и/иі.

[^2624]: Hos. 6:4, 13:3 (LXX: ὡς δρόσος ὀρθρινὴ πρωϊπορευομένη).

[^2625]: Cf. Ps. 1:4 (LXX: ὡσεὶ χνοῦς, ὃν ἐκριπτεῖ ὁ ἄνεμος ἀπὸ προσώπου τῆς γῆς).

[^2626]: Ps. 13:3 / Rom. 3:12 (LXX: πάντες ἐξέκλιναν, ἅμα ἠχρειώθησαν).

[^2627]: Slavonic: ꙗ҆́ко ѻ҆всоу́дѣ прѣ́бныи на землѝ—"as though abiding everywhere/permanently upon the earth" (Early Modern Ruthenian adjectival form прѣбныи related to пребывати).

[^2628]: Ps. 102:10 (LXX: οὐ κατὰ τὰς ἁμαρτίας ἡμῶν ἐποίησεν ἡμῖν, οὐδὲ κατὰ τὰς ἀνομίας ἡμῶν ἀνταπέδωκεν ἡμῖν).

[^2629]: Cf. Ps. 142:10 (LXX: δίδαξόν με τοῦ ποιεῖν τὸ θέλημά σου, ὅτι σὺ εἶ ὁ Θεός μου).

[^2630]: Ps. 43:21 (LXX: εἰ ἐπελαθόμεθα τοῦ ὀνόματος τοῦ Θεοῦ ἡμῶν καὶ εἰ διεπετάσαμεν χεῖρας ἡμῶν πρὸς Θεὸν ἀλλότριον); Ps. 122:1 (LXX: Πρὸς σὲ ἦρα τοὺς ὀφθαλμούς μου τὸν κατοικοῦντα ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ).

[^2631]: Matt. 9:13; Lk. 5:32 (οὐ γὰρ ἦλθον καλέσαι δικαίους ἀλλὰ ἁμαρτωλοὺς εἰς μετάνοιαν).

[^2632]: Matt. 25:33–34.

[^2633]: Ps. 78:10, 113:10 (LXX: μήποτε εἴπωσι τὰ ἔθνη, Ποῦ ἐστιν ὁ Θεὸς αὐτῶν;); Joel 2:17.

[^2634]: Slavonic: да̀ не ѿпа́доутъ ѿ вѣ́ры, нетве́рди бо соу́тъ вѣ́рою—a pastoral recognition of human frailty under extreme calamity and prolonged famine.

[^2635]: Cf. Hos. 6:1 (LXX: ὅτι αὐτὸς ἥρπακεν καὶ ἰάσεται ἡμᾶς, паτάξει καὶ μοσχεύσει ἡμᾶς); Is. 5:24. The Ruthenian form стевлїе represents Church Slavonic сте́блїе (stubble/stalks).

[^2636]: Liturgical doxological formula concluding the Third Prayer in Time of Drought.

[^2637]: Rubric cross-reference citing printed leaves ч҃з (fol. 97) and ч҃и (fol. 98), corresponding to physical leaves p211 and p213 (the earlier Order in Time of Drought).

[^2638]: Rubric concluding the Third Prayer and directing the liturgical dismissal.

[^2639]: Fol. 451v is a blank unprinted leaf (vacat) concluding Part XXXIII (The Order in Time of Drought), preceding the major woodcut headpiece for Pentecost on Fol. 452r.

[^2640]: Slavonic Въ недѣ́лю святы́я Пентикостїи (On the Sunday of Holy Pentecost). In the Kyivan recension, the Kneeling Office of Pentecost (Слу́жба вече́рни съ колѣноприклоне́нїемъ) forms a major autonomous liturgical division of the Euchologion.

[^2641]: Rubric specifying the time of the service (слн҃цоу ꙋ҆стоупи́вшоу сполꙋ́дне—"when the sun has declined past midday") and the rhythmic striking of the wooden or metallic sounding board (кле́племъ вече́рни поко́е).

[^2642]: Initial sacerdotal blessing of Vespers (Бл҃гослове́нъ Бг҃ъ на́шь), recorded as an incipit without silent liturgical expansion.

[^2643]: Psalm 103 (LXX: Εὐλόγει, ἡ ψυχή μου, τὸν Κύριον), the customary introductory psalm of Byzantine Vespers.

[^2644]: The Great Litany (є҆ктені́а вели́каа) of Pentecost Vespers incorporates special kneeling petitions characteristic of the Byzantine-Slavonic Euchologion.

[^2645]: First special petition of the Pentecost Kneeling Litany, praying for sanctification of souls and bodies of the assembly.

[^2646]: Second special petition, praying for the heavenly inheritance through the grace of the Holy Spirit.

[^2647]: Third special petition, imploring steadfastness in faith and hope.

[^2648]: Fourth special petition, praying that the faithful become temples of the Holy and Life-creating Spirit (cf. 1 Cor. 6:19).

[^2649]: Fifth special petition, imploring manifest participation in the Holy Spirit.

[^2650]: Sixth special petition, asking for an angel of peace to enlighten the mind of the faithful.

[^2651]: Physical Leaf p921 (Folio ун҃ѓ [453]r). Slavonic: Ѡ҆ раздрѣше́нїи всѧ́коѧ ꙗ҆́зѧ неприа́зненыѧ прⷭ҇ты дх҃о, Гд҃у помоли́сѧ. The petition invokes the Holy Spirit for release from every demonic assault or wound (ꙗ҆́зва неприа́зненна, Greek: διαλύсеως πάσης πληγῆς τῆς ἐναντίας / τοῦ διαβόλου). The titlo abbreviation прⷭ҇ты дх҃о abbreviates прест҃ы́мъ дх҃омъ.

[^2652]: Physical Leaf p921 (Folio ун҃ѓ [453]r). Slavonic: Ѡ҆ сп҃се́нїи на́шемъ съвы́ше, колѣ́нѣ преклѡ́ньше вѣ́рою срⷣчнѣи и҆ теле́снѣи въ дн҃ь се́и пѧ́десѧ́тный, Гд҃у помли́. This petition explicitly links bodily prostration and inward spiritual faith on the Day of Pentecost, marking the solemn return to kneeling after the Paschal prohibition mandated by the First Ecumenical Council (Nicaea I, Canon 20).

[^2653]: Physical Leaf p921 (Folio ун҃ѓ [453]r). Slavonic: Ѡ҆ възда́нїи дш҃ь всѣ́хъ на напоклоне́нїе ст҃о́му дх҃оу. The printed text exhibits an uncorrected dittography across the line break: на напоклоне́нїе. Translated diplomatically according to intended syntax.

[^2654]: Physical Leaf p921 (Folio ун҃ѓ [453]r). Slavonic: Ѡ҆ въздръжа́нїи лю́дстѣм, и҆ ча́ѧнїи блгⷣти ст҃го дх҃а, Гд҃оу помѡли́мсѧ. The Ruthenian phrasing highlights both moral restraint (въздръжа́нїе) and the eager spiritual expectation (ча́ѧнїе) of the grace of the Holy Spirit.

[^2655]: Physical Leaf p922 (Folio 453v). Slavonic: Ѡ҆ оу҆слы́шанїи Гд҃оу Бг҃оу на́съ грѣ́шныхъ и҆ посла́ти на́ ны ст҃ы́й дх҃ъ · и҆ ѡ҆ст҃и́ти на́съ, Гд҃оу помоли́мсѧ. An epiclesis-like petition within the litany for the descent and sanctifying action of the Holy Spirit upon the gathered assembly.

[^2656]: Physical Leaf p922 (Folio 453v). Slavonic: Ѡ҆ бл҃говоли́ти Гд҃у на́ ны преклѡ́ншаѧ кѡлѣ́нѣ своѝ · и҆ и҆спꙋсти́ти на́мъ ст҃ы́й свой дх҃ъ, Гд҃у помли́сѧ. The printed text concludes with помли́сѧ for помоли́мсѧ.

[^2657]: Physical Leaf p922 (Folio 453v). Slavonic: Ѡ҆ приѧ́тїи мл҃твъ на́шихъ къ воню̀ бл҃гооуха́нїа дх҃овнаго. Reflecting the scriptural motif of prayers rising as a spiritual sweet-smelling savor (Greek: εἰς ὀσμὴν εὐωδίας πνευματικῆς; cf. Eph. 5:2; Phil. 4:18).

[^2658]: Physical Leaf p922 (Folio 453v). Slavonic: Ѡ҆ и҆зба́витисѧ на[мъ] ѿ всѧ́коѧ скръби гнѣ́ва и҆ нꙋ́жда, Гд҃у помли́лимсѧ. The 1606 imprint shows an accidental syllable duplication in the response verb: помли́лимсѧ for помоли́мсѧ.

[^2659]: Physical Leaf p923 (Folio ун҃д́ [454]r). Slavonic: Ꙗ҆́ко подоба́етъ ти всѧ́ка сла́ва чⷭ҇ть и҆ покланѧ́нїе... Concluding priestly doxological exclamation of the extended Pentecost Great Litany, sealed with the standard Father Paul Doxology: "unto ages of ages."

[^2660]: Physical Leaf p923 (Folio ун҃д́ [454]r). Slavonic rubric: кл҃, не гл҃емъ. Abbreviation for Каѳі́сма не глаго́лемъ (We do not recite the Kathisma). The Typikon prescribes that at Pentecost Sunday Vespers, the customary Sunday Kathisma ("Blessed is the man") is entirely omitted, proceeding directly to "Lord, I have cried."

[^2661]: Physical Leaf p923 (Folio ун҃д́ [454]r). Slavonic rubric: На Гд҃и възва́[хъ], поста́ви стихо́въ · ѕ҃ · и҆ пое́мъ, ст҃ры, самогла́сны, Гл҃а, д҃. Appointment of six verses on the Lucernarium with the three idiomela of Pentecost chanted twice each (or with Doxastikon) in Tone 4.

[^2662]: Physical Leaf p923 (Folio ун҃д́ [454]r). Slavonic: Пресла́внаа дне́сь, ви́дѣша всѝ ꙗ҆зы́ци въ гра́дѣ дв҃довѣ... First Sticheron of Pentecost (attributed to Leo VI the Wise / John of Damascus), paraphrasing the Pentecost account in Acts 2:1-4 and explicitly naming Saint Luke the Evangelist ("as Luke the God-proclaimer writes").

[^2663]: Physical Leaf p924 (Folio 454v). Slavonic: ...стра́нными гл҃ы, стра́нными веле́ньми · стра́нными оу҆че́ньми ст҃ыѧ тр҃ца. Greek: ξένοις ῥήμασι, ξένοις δόγμασι, ξένοις διδάγμασι τῆς Ἁγίας Τριάδος. The triple colometric repetition of "strange" (странный, miraculous/foreign/paradoxical) characterizes the novelty of the apostolic tongues and Trinitarian dogma.

[^2664]: Physical Leaf p924 (Folio 454v). Slavonic: Дх҃ъ ст҃ы́й бѧ́ше оу҆́бо прⷭ҇но, и҆ є҆́сть и҆ боу́детъ... Second Sticheron of Pentecost in Tone 4, drawn from the theological orations of Saint Gregory the Theologian (Oration 41 on Pentecost, PG 36:436). It affirms the eternal, unbegotten, co-equal hypostatic status of the Holy Spirit.

[^2665]: Physical Leaf p925 (Folio ун҃е́ [455]r). Slavonic: Дх҃ъ ст҃ы́й свѣ́тъ, и҆ живо́тъ живы́й, и҆сто́чникъ оу҆́менъ... Third Sticheron of Pentecost in Tone 4, synthesizing the biblical and patristic attributes of the Spirit (noetic Fountain, Spirit of wisdom and understanding, uncreated deifying Fire).

[^2666]: Physical Leaf p925 (Folio ун҃е́ [455]r). Slavonic rubric: Сла́ва, и҆ нн҃ѣ : Гла́съ шесты́й · Цр҃ю нб҃ный, оу҆тѣ́шителю дш҃е и҆́стинны́й... The universal invocation "O Heavenly King" (Царю Небесный) serves here in its native, ancient liturgical station as the Doxastikon of the Lucernarium at Pentecost Vespers, from whence it entered the Trisagion Prayers of the Byzantine Rite.

[^2667]: Physical Leaf p926 (Folio 455v). Slavonic rubric: Та́же въхо́дъ · Свѣ́те ти́хїи. The rubrics direct the liturgical Entrance (Introit) with the censer during the Doxastikon, followed by the singing of the 3rd-century hymn Phos Hilaron.

[^2668]: Physical Leaf p926 (Folio 455v). Slavonic rubric: прѡ́ · Гла́ · з҃ · Кто̀ Бг҃ъ ве́лїи ꙗ҆́ко Бг҃ъ на́шь... The Great Prokimenon of Pentecost, Tone 7, taken from Psalm 76:14-15 [LXX] with verses from Psalm 76:1, 11, and 12 [LXX].

[^2669]: Physical Leaf p926 (Folio 455v). Slavonic rubric: Па́ки и҆ па́ки прекло́ньше кѡлѣ́нѣ Гд҃оу помоли́мсѧ · на́мъ же преклѡ́ншимъ кѡлѣ́нѣ и҆ покрове́нными глава́ми · Сщ҃е́нникъ гла́воу прекло́нь мо́литсѧ, гл҃ѧ мл҃твоу сїю̀ въ оу҆слыша́нїе всѣ́мъ. The deacon invites all to kneel; the faithful bow their heads and knees while the priest kneels before the Holy Doors facing west toward the people to recite the First Kneeling Prayer aloud.

[^2670]: Physical Leaf p927 (Folio ун҃ѕ́ [456]r). Slavonic: Пречи́сте, несквръ́нне, и҆ небла́ꙁньне · беꙁнача́лне, неви́диме... The First Kneeling Prayer of Pentecost, attributed to Saint Basil the Great, opens with an apophatic theological exordium praising the transcendence and benevolence of God the Father.

[^2671]: Physical Leaf p927 (Folio ун҃ѕ́ [456]r). Slavonic: ...и҆ въсплѡщьшасѧ ѿ дх҃а ст҃го, и҆ зъ марї́а пресла́вныѧ. Note the Ruthenian syntax combining the preposition зъ with genitive марї́а пресла́вныѧ in parallel with ѿ дх҃а ст҃го.

[^2672]: Physical Leaf p928 (Folio 456v). Slavonic: ...и҆ чⷭ҇тною свое́ю стрⷭ҇тїю показа́въ на́мъ смѣрє́нымъ, и҆ недосто́йнымъ рабѡ́мъ твои́мъ, вы́ѧ и҆ кѡлѣ́на на́ша прекланѧ́ти... The prayer explicitly links the posture of kneeling to Christ's Passion, through which humility and repentance were revealed as the way to divine pardon.

[^2673]: Physical Leaf p928 (Folio 456v). Slavonic: ...и҆зрѧ́днѣе же въ дн҃ь се́и пѧтидесѧ́тный · въ́ньже по възнесе́нїи на нб҃са̀... посла́вый прест҃ый свой дх҃ъ на ст҃ыѧ своѧ оу҆́ченикы и҆ а҆́плы... Direct recollection of the historical descent of the Holy Spirit on Pentecost as the foundation of the current assembly's prayer.

[^2674]: Physical Leaf p929 (Folio ун҃з́ [457]r). Slavonic: ...възвратѝ плѣне́нїе дш҃ь на́шихъ... к тебѣ̀ привръжени є҆смы и҆з лѡ́жеснъ, ѿ чре́ва ма́тере на́шеѧ ты̀ є҆си Бг҃ъ на́шъ. Scriptural citations recalling Psalm 125:4 [LXX] ("Turn back our captivity, O Lord") and Psalm 21:10-11 [LXX] ("Upon Thee was I cast from the womb; from my mother's belly Thou art my God").

[^2675]: Physical Leaf p929 (Folio ун҃з́ [457]r). Slavonic: ...грѣ́хъ ю́ности на́шеѧ, и҆ невѣ́дѣнїа непомѧнѝ · ѿ та́йныхъ на́ших ѡ҆чи́сти на́съ... Quotations from Psalm 24:7 [LXX] ("The sins of my youth and mine ignorances remember not") and Psalm 18:13 [LXX] ("From my secret faults cleanse me").

[^2677]: Physical Leaf p930 (Folio 457v). Slavonic: ...възмѣ́ри безакѡ́нїемъ на́шимъ щедрѡ́ты твоѧ̑ · съпроти́въ поста́ви бе́здну щедро́тъ твои́хъ мно́жествоу съгрѣше́нїи на́шихъ... The prayer sets the infinite abyss of divine compassion over against the vast multitude of human sins, continuing on the following leaf with и҆змѝ... ("deliver...").

[^2719]: Deacon's liturgical invitation summoning the faithful to kneel for the third prayer station of Pentecost Vespers.

[^2720]: Rubric introducing the third kneeling prayer of Pentecost: *Сщ҃енникъ гл҃етъ мл҃твоу тре́тїю , ꙗ҆́коже прѣ́же сказа́хомъ . на́мъ гла́вы съ колѣ́ны прекло́ншимъ .*

[^2721]: Opening Christological invocation of the third kneeling prayer: *Присносꙋ́щїи , кипѧ́щїи , живы́и и҆ просвѣти́телныи и҆сто́чникъ* (Greek: Ὁ ἀέναος, ὁ ζωτικὸς καὶ φωτιστικὸς κρουνός, the ever-flowing, vital, and illuminating fountain).

[^2722]: Slavonic: *смр҃ти оу҆́зы нераздрѣши́мыѧ , и҆ затво́ры а҆́довы разроуши́въ* (Greek: θανάτου δεσμοὺς ἀλύτους, καὶ κλεῖθρα ᾅδου διαρρήξας).

[^2723]: Slavonic: *є҆́же всѧ́кого грѣха̀ неприкоснове́нно же , и҆ непрохо́дно* (Greek: τὴν πάσης ἁμαρτίας ἄψαυστόν τε καὶ ἀνεπίδεκτον, untouched and inaccessible to any sin).

[^2724]: Slavonic: *до́лѣ сѣдѧ́щимъ въхо́дъ показа́въ* (Greek: τοῖς κάτω καθημένοις ἄνοδον ὑποδείξας, having pointed out the ascent unto those who sat below).

[^2725]: Slavonic: *началозло́бнаго же и҆ глоуби́ннаго змїа , Бг҃омоу́дростнымъ лѧще́нїемъ оу҆ло́вль , и҆ плени́цами мра́ка свѧза́въ* (cf. Jude 1:6, 2 Pet. 2:4).

[^2726]: Slavonic: *напаствꙋ́емымъ вели́къ послꙋша́тель ꙗ҆ви́сѧ* (Greek: τοῖς ἐπηρεαζομένοις μέγας ἐπίκουρος ἐπιφανείς, having appeared as a great helper unto the assaulted).

[^2727]: Slavonic: *ты̀ сло́ве прⷭ҇носꙋ́щїи Гн҃и... въсто́къ сл҃нца пра́вдѣ* (Greek: Ἥλιε δικαιοσύνης, cf. Mal. 4:2).

[^2728]: The solemn commemoration of the departed in the third kneeling prayer of Pentecost: *и҆ оу҆поко́й дꙋ́ша ра́бъ твои́хъ , пре́жде оу҆со́пшихъ ѿц҃ъ и҆ бра́тїи на́шихъ...*. Pentecost Vespers is the liturgical locus par excellence for prayer on behalf of all the reposed, including those held in Hades.

[^2729]: Address to God the Father: *Вл҃ко вседрьжи́телю , Бг҃е ѿц҃ъ и҆ Гд҃и мл҃ти...* (Greek: Δέσποτα παντοκράτορ, Θεὲ πατέρων καὶ Κύριε τοῦ ἐλέους...).

[^2730]: Scriptural citation: *низводѧ̀ въ а҆́дъ и҆ възводѧ̀* (1 Sam. 2:6 LXX / 1 Kings 2:6: Κύριος θανατοῖ καὶ ζῳογονεῖ, κατάγει εἰς ᾅδου καὶ ἀνάγει).

[^2731]: Scriptural echo: *съмрътнымъ жа́ломъ оу҆ꙗзве́нныхъ* (Greek: τῷ τοῦ θανάτου κέντρῳ πληγέντας; cf. 1 Cor. 15:55-56).

[^2732]: Scriptural citation: *наде́жде всѣ́мъ ко́нцемъ землѝ , и҆ сꙋ́щимъ въ мо́ри дале́че* (Ps. 64:6 LXX: ἡ ἐλπὶς πάντων τῶν περάτων τῆς γῆς καὶ τῶν ἐν θαλάσσῃ μακράν).

[^2733]: Slavonic: *въ послѣ́днїи , и҆ вели́кыи и҆ сп҃си́телныи де́нь пра́здника* (cf. John 7:37: ἐν δὲ τῇ ἐσχάτῃ ἡμέρᾳ τῇ μεγάλῃ τῆς ἑορτῆς).

[^2734]: Slavonic: *правосла́внѣй вѣ́рѣ и҆сповѣ́дникы , и҆ проповѣ́дникы и҆́стиннаго Бг҃осло́вїа показа́въ*.

[^2735]: Theological core of the Pentecost Vespers kneeling prayers: propitiation and relief for the souls held in Hades (*ѡ҆цѣще́нїа моле́бнаа ѡ҆ є҆́же въ а҆́дѣ съдръжи́мыхъ сподо́билъ є҆сѝ прїима́ти*).

[^2736]: Memorial formula: *на мѣ́стѣ свѣ́тлѣ , на мѣ́стѣ зла́чнѣ , на мѣ́стѣ прохлажде́нїа , ѿню́доуже ѿбѣ́же всѧ́ка болѣ́знь , и҆ печа́ль и҆ въздыха́нїе* (cf. Isa. 35:10, 51:11; Rev. 21:4).

[^2737]: Scriptural citation: *ꙗ҆́ко не мр҃твїи въсхва́лѧтъ тѧ̀ Гд҃и , ниже сꙋ́щїи въ а҆́дѣ дрьзноу́тъ и҆сповѣ́данїе принести́ ти* (cf. Ps. 113:25 LXX: οὐχ οἱ νεκροὶ αἰνέσουσίν σε, Κύριε, οὐδὲ πάντες οἱ καταβαίνοντες εἰς ᾅδου).

[^2738]: Opening invocation of the second kneeling prayer of the third station: *Бж҃е вели́кыи и҆ вѣ́чныи , ст҃ыи и҆ чл҃колꙕби́выи...* (Greek: Ὁ Θεὸς ὁ μέγας καὶ αἰώνιος, ὁ ἅγιος καὶ φιλάνθρωπος...).

[^2739]: Slavonic: *подоба́ющее славосло́вїе , и҆ бл҃годаре́нїе вели́кыхъ ти да́рѡвъ*.

[^2740]: Scriptural echo: *въ дн҃е пра́вдѣ ше́ствоу́емъ* (cf. Rom. 13:12-13: "Let us walk honestly, as in the day...").

[^2741]: Scriptural echo: *ѡ҆дѣ́ѧвшесѧ въ ѻ҆роу́жїе свѣ́та : ненавѣ́тни пребꙋ́демъ ѿ всѧ́коѧ ко́зни лꙋка́ваго* (cf. Rom. 13:12, Eph. 6:11).

[^2742]: Slavonic: *временно рѣше́нїе твои́хъ тва́рей , и҆ є҆́же по си́хъ приѡ҆бще́нїе и҆ поко́и въ вѣ́кы* (Greek: ἥ τε πρόσκαιρος διάλυσις τῶν σῶν ποιημάτων, καὶ ἡ μετὰ ταῦτα συνάφεια, καὶ ἀνάπαυσις εἰς αἰῶνας).

[^2743]: Eschatological hope: *ѡ҆ вхо́дѣхъ на́шихъ є҆́же въ ми́ръ се́й . и҆ и҆схо́дѣхъ є҆́же ѡ҆ наде́ждахъ въскрⷭ҇енїа... предѡ҆броуча́ютсѧ*.

[^2744]: Slavonic: *ты́ бо є҆сѝ въскрⷭ҇енїю нача́токъ , и҆ житі́ю нелицемѣ́ренъ , и҆ чл҃колꙕ́бецъ сꙋдїа . и҆ мздовъздаа́нїю вл҃ка и҆ Гд҃ь* (Greek: Σὺ γὰρ εἶ καὶ τῆς ἀναστάσεως ἡμῶν ἀρχηγός, καὶ τῶν βεβιωμένων ἀδέκαστος καὶ φιλάνθρωπος κριτής, καὶ τῆς μισθαποδοσίας Δεσπότης καὶ Κύριος).

[^2745]: Incarnational theology: *приѡ҆бщи́въсѧ на́шей пло́ти и҆ кро́ви , за млⷭ҇рдїе кра́йнее на́шихъ ра́ди стра́стей неизлїѧ́нныхъ...* (cf. Heb. 2:14).

[^2746]: Slavonic: *и҆ въ не́мже пострада̀, и҆ и҆скꙋси́въсѧ са́мъ, и҆скꙋша́емымъ на́мъ бы́въ ѡ҆бѣща́ненъ помо́щникъ . тѣ́мъ же приведѐ на́съ къ свое́ безстрⷭ҇тїе* (Heb. 2:18: ἐν ᾧ γὰρ πέπονθεν αὐτὸς πειρασθείς, δύναται τοῖς πειραζομένοις βοηθῆσαι). The passage confesses Christ's voluntary suffering, temptation, and the imparting of His divine impassibility (*къ свое́ безстрⷭ҇тїе*).

[^2747]: The universal memorial intercession in the third kneeling prayer of Pentecost: *поко́й всѧ ѿца ко́ждо, и҆ ма́тере, и҆ ча́да . и҆ бра́тїю, и҆ сестры . и҆ коу́пнорѡ́дныхъ, и҆ є҆диноплеме́нныхъ . и҆ всѧ пре́жде почи́вшаѧ дꙋ́ша, Ѡ҆ оу҆пова́нїи въскрⷭ҇енїа , и҆ жи́зни вѣ́чныѧ*.

[^2748]: The bodily resurrection at the appointed time: *съвъздви́гъ тѣлеса̀ на́ша въ ча́съ и҆́же повелѣ́лъ є҆сѝ , по ст҃ы́хъ твои́хъ нелѡ́жныхъ ѡ҆бѣтова́нїихъ* (cf. John 5:28-29, 14:2).

[^2749]: Classical Patristic definition of Christian death: *нѣ́сть оу҆́бо Гд҃и рабѡ́мъ твои́мъ смр҃ть... но̀ преставле́нїе ѿ печальнѣ́йшихъ на бл҃женнѣ́йшаѧ, и҆ на поко́й и҆ ра́дость* (Greek: οὐκ ἔστι θάνατος... ἀλλὰ μετάστασις ἀπὸ τῶν λυπηροτέρων ἐπὶ τὰ χρηστότερα καὶ θυμηδέστερα).

[^2750]: Scriptural citation: *зане́же ни є҆ди́нъ чи́стъ прѣ̀ тобо́ю ѿ сквръ́ны , ни же а҆́ще и҆ є҆ди́нъ де́нь живо́тъ є҆го̀ є҆́стъ* (cf. Job 14:4-5 LXX: τίς γὰρ καθαρὸς ἔσται ἀπὸ ῥύπου; ἀλλ᾽ οὐθείς, ἐὰν καὶ μία ἡμέρα ὁ βίος αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς).

[^2751]: Christological mediation: *і҃с х҃с . є҆го́же ра́ди всѝ оу҆пова́емъ мл҃ть полꙋчи́ти, и҆ ѡ҆ставле́нїе грѣхѡ́въ* (cf. Eph. 1:7, Col. 1:14).

[^2752]: Comprehensive liturgical absolution formula: *Ѡ҆сла́би ѡ҆ста́ви , простѝ грѣхопаде́нїа на́ша . ꙗ҆́же въ ра́зꙋмѣ и҆ неразꙋмѣ́нїи . прѣꙗвле́ннаа, и҆ забыва́емаа . ꙗ҆́же въ дѣѧ́нїи, ꙗ҆́же въ дѣ́лѣ . ꙗ҆́же въ словесѝ . ꙗ҆́же въ всѣ́хъ на́шихъ хожде́нїихъ*.

[^2753]: Terminal petition concluding the third kneeling prayer of Pentecost Vespers.

[^2754]: Rubric introducing the appended prayer to the Holy Spirit: *Мл҃тва прилага́емаѧ по си́хъ мл҃тва[хъ], ѡ҆со́бнаѧ ст҃о́мꙋ дх҃ꙋ . творенїе ст҃ѣ́йшаго патрїа́рха константина гра́да кѵ́рь фило́ѳеа . гл҃и по тре́тїи мл҃твѣ и҆ при́стаѧ*. Patriarch Philotheos Kokkinos (c. 1300–1379) was a hesychast father, disciple and biographer of St. Gregory Palamas, and author of liturgical services and prayers.

[^2755]: Pneumatological titles: *Цр҃ю нб҃ныи , оу҆тѣши́телю вл҃ко събезнача́лныи , и҆ съпрⷭ҇носꙋ́щныи...* and the doctrine of deification: *сн҃оположе́нїа, и҆ ѡ҆боже́нїа оу҆́мнаго и҆ слове́снаго є҆стества̀ прїѧ́тель* (Greek: πρόξενος υἱοθεσίας καὶ θεώσεως).

[^2756]: Titles from the Psalter: *дх҃ъ пра́выи* (Ps. 50:12 LXX: πνεῦμα εὐθές) and *дх҃ъ влч҃ьнїи* (Ps. 50:14 LXX: πνεύματι ἡγεμονικῷ).

[^2757]: Orthodox Triadology: *дх҃ъ бж҃їи и҆ ѿ бг҃а . дх҃ъ ѻ҆́ч҃ь, и҆ ѿ ѻ҆ц҃а̀ . дх҃ъ сн҃овень, дх҃ъ хрⷭ҇то́въ* (cf. Rom. 8:9, Gal. 4:6). The Spirit proceeds eternally from the Father alone, yet is also the Spirit of the Son and of Christ.

[^2758]: Eternal procession (*и҆схожде́нїе*) versus temporal manifestation (*ꙗ҆вле́нїе*) in Palamite theology.

[^2759]: Pneumatological cosmology: the Holy Spirit creates and sustains all things together with the Father and the Son (*вку́пѣ тва́рь созда́въ , съ ѻ҆тце́мъ и҆ сн҃омъ... съѡ҆кръмлѧ́ѧ и҆ съвѧзꙋ́ѧ , и҆ оу҆твръжда́ѧ , и҆ съблюда́ѧ*).

[^2760]: Apophatic catalogue of divine attributes: *Безнача́лне, неви́диме, непости́жиме, неразꙋмѣ́нне, неисче́тенне, неизслѣ́дованне . неизрече́нне, безчисленоси́лне въсемогїи Гд҃и*.

[^2761]: Scriptural echo of Heb. 1:1: *и҆́же прѣ́вѣке ѿцы̀ , и҆ прⷪ҇рѡ́кы разли́чнѣ дѣ́йствовавъ, и҆ гл҃авъ*, through Whom the bodily dispensation and Ascension of the Son are revealed.

[^2762]: Descent of the Holy Spirit on Pentecost: *ꙗ҆́ко сꙋще́ственнѣ, и҆ ви́домъ ѡ҆́гненыхъ ꙗ҆зы́къ просвѣти́въ ми́ръ . и҆ на ст҃ы́хъ а҆пл҃ѣхъ и҆ оу҆чн҃цѣ́хъ сѣ́де* (cf. Acts 2:1-4).

[^2763]: Christ's promise fulfilled: *по не ло́жномꙋ ѡ҆бѣща́нїю хрⷭ҇о́вꙋ* (cf. Luke 24:49, Acts 1:4-8).

[^2764]: Trinitarian confession: *Бг҃ꙋ въ тре́хъ ли́цехъ покланѧ́тисѧ наоу҆чи́хомсѧ* (worship of God in three hypostases/persons).

[^2765]: Pneumatological titles: *Ѡ҆заре́нїе ѻ҆́ч҃ее , живы́й и҆ неизмѣ́нныи ѻ҆́бразъ ѻ҆́ч҃ь . въкоу́пѣ и҆ сн҃о́вень непрело́жный ѻ҆́бразъ, и҆ печа́ть сꙋщества̀ и҆ є҆́ства и҆́хъ*.

[^2766]: The Father as sole Cause (*вина̀*, αἰτία) and unbegotten Fountain (*и҆сто́чникъ є҆ди́ный нерожде́нный*) of the Godhead, conferring all gifts through the Son in the Spirit.

[^2767]: Sacerdotal confession of unworthiness: *прїимѝ мнѡ́гогрѣ́шнаго и҆ недосто́инаго моле́нїа и҆ въ се́й ча́съ . и҆́же мно́жество мои́хъ съгрѣше́нїи съвѣ́дыи є҆ди́нъ*.

[^2768]: Direct citation of the Penitential Psalm: *помл҃оуй мѧ̀ Бж҃е по вели́цей твое́й мл҃ти...* (Ps. 50:1-3 LXX).

[^2769]: Purification from passions: *ѡ҆мы́и наипа́че ти́ноу съгрѣше́нїи мои́хъ . и҆ належа́щоую стр҃тей дшѝ мое́й сквр́ьноу ѡ҆цѣстѝ*.

[^2770]: Scriptural citations: Ps. 18:13-14 LXX (*Ѡ҆чи́сти мѧ̀ ѿ та́йныхъ мои́хъ Гд҃и . и҆ ѿ чꙋ́ждихъ и҆зба́ви ра́ба твое́го*) and Ps. 24:7 LXX (*грѣ́хъ ю҆́ности моеѧ̀ и҆ невѣ́дѣнїа... не помѧнѝ*).

[^2771]: Spiritual illumination: *просвѣтѝ помраче́нныѧ мы́сли ѡ҆́чи, пога́сшїи свѣти́лникъ бл҃гти въже́гъ*.

[^2772]: Pastoral prayer for the flock: *си́лꙋ и҆ высотоу̀, и҆ крѣ́пость мл҃твы чи́стыѧ, и҆ просте́рты ѡ҆ лю́дехъ твои́хъ, и҆ ѡ҆ всеми́рной твое́й цр҃кви, и҆ ста́дѣ*.

[^2773]: The Church founded upon the rock of faith (Matt. 16:18) and redeemed by Christ's precious blood (Acts 20:28): *кро́вїю є҆диноро́днаго сн҃а и҆ бг҃а и҆скꙋ́пльшисѧ... оу҆твръдѝ є҆ѧ̀ на ка́мени и҆сповѣ́данїа бж҃тва, непрекло́ннꙋ*.

[^2774]: Allusion to Matthew 16:18: "and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it" (*πύλαι ᾅδου οὐ κατισχύσουσιν αὐτῆς* / *а҆́дьскыхъ две́рей крѣпча́йшꙋ*).

[^2775]: Church Slavonic *безмѣстныхъ* translates Greek *ἀτόπων* (inordinate, improper, out-of-place heresies); *бѣсо́вьскыхъ дѣ́йствъ* (*δαιμονικῶν ἐνεργειῶν*); *неоу҆ѧзве́нноу* (*ἄτρωτον*, invulnerable/unwounded).

[^2776]: *колѣ́нопреклоне́нїа* (*γονυκλισίας*) and *стена́нїа* (*στεναγμούς*); *прострѣ́тыѧ мл҃твы* refers to prayers offered with outstretched arms and hands (*ἐκτεταμένας εὐχάς*).

[^2777]: Church Slavonic *възира́ти* (*ἀτενίζειν* / *ἀποβλέπειν*) and *ча́ати* (*προσδοκᾶν*).

[^2778]: Conclusion of the prayer of Patriarch Philotheos Kokkinos to the Holy Spirit. Note the direct doxological address to the third Hypostasis: *и҆ тебѐ прⷭ҇та́го и҆ є҆диночⷭ҇тнаго дх҃а є҆ди́наго триѵ̈поста́снаго Бж҃тва* ("and of Thee, the All-Holy and equally honored Spirit, of the one tri-hypostatic Godhead").

[^2779]: The petition contains the imperative rubric *въста́ни* (*ἀνάστηθι* / *ἀνάστητε*, "stand up!"), directing the clergy and congregation to rise from their knees following the conclusion of the kneeling prayers.

[^2780]: The abbreviated commemorative petition of the Little Litany (*Пр҃стоу́ю чⷭ҇тоу́ю...*), concluding the kneeling intercession.

[^2781]: Conclusion of the priestly exclamation (*Ꙗ҆́ко бл҃гїи чл҃колꙕ́бецъ Бг҃ъ є҆сѝ...*). Note the strict Father Paul Doxology standard (*unto ages of ages*).

[^2782]: Opening petition of the Litany of Supplication (*И҆сплъ́нимъ вече́рнѧѧ мл҃твы на́ша Гдⷭ҇и* / *Πληρώσωμεν τὴν ἑσπερινὴν δέησιν ἡμῶν τῷ Κυρίῳ*).

[^2783]: Standard evening petition: *Ве́чера въсего̀ съвръше́нна ст҃а ми́рна и҆ безъ грѣ́шна* (*Τὴν ἑσπέραν πᾶσαν, τελείαν, ἁγίαν, εἰρηνικὴν καὶ ἀναμάρτητον*).

[^2784]: Church Slavonic *смире́нїе ми́рꙋ* translates Greek *εἰρήνην τῷ κόσμῳ* ("peace for the world").

[^2785]: Church Slavonic *въ смире́нїи и҆ покаа́нїи* ("in peace [lit. humility/peacefulness] and repentance"), translating Greek *ἐν εἰρήνῃ καὶ μετανοίᾳ*.

[^2786]: Church Slavonic *безъстра́стны* (*ἀνώδυνον*, painless / without suffering).

[^2787]: Abbreviated incipit of the Theotokion commemoration (*Пр҃стоу́ю чⷭ҇тоу́ю и҆ пребл҃ве́ноую вл҃чц[ꙋ]*).

[^2788]: The printed text prints the exclamation formula: *Ꙗ҆́ко ст҃исѧ и҆ прослависѧ и҆́мѧ твоѐ ѻ҆ц҃а̀ и҆ сн҃а и҆ ст҃го дх҃а* (*Ὅτι ἡγίασται καὶ δεδόξασται τὸ πάντιμον καὶ μεγαλοπρεπὲς ὄνομά σου...*).

[^2789]: Incipit of the Prayer of the Bowing of Heads (*Κύριε ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν, ὁ κλίνας οὐρανοὺς...*), left unexpanded in accordance with Statutory Mandate 16.

[^2790]: Priestly exclamation of the Bowing of Heads (*Εἴη τὸ κράτος τῆς βασιλείας σου εὐλογημένον καὶ δεδοξασμένον...*).

[^2791]: Rubric introducing the Aposticha of Pentecost Vespers: *и҆ пое́мъ начина́емъ стихи̑ры настихо́внѣ Гла́съ г҃ . самогла́сны* (*Εἰς τὸν Στίχον, Στιχηρὰ Ἰδιόμελα, Ἦχος γ'*).

[^2792]: Aposticha Idiomelon 1 of Pentecost Vespers (*Νῦν εἰς σημεῖον τοῖς πᾶσιν, ἐμφανῶς αἱ γλῶσσαι γεγόνασιν...*). Alludes to Romans 9:5: "of whom as concerning the flesh Christ came" (*ἐξ ὧν ὁ Χριστὸς τὸ κατὰ σάρκα* / *ѿ ни́хъже хс҃ по пло́ти*).

[^2793]: *съ ними́же срⷣца съ колѣ́ны прекло́ньше* (*μεθ' ὧν τὰς καρδίας σὺν γόνασι κλίναντες*).

[^2794]: Psalm 50:12 LXX (50:10 MT). The printed Ruthenian witness has the first-person plural: *съзи́жи въ на́съ Бж҃е . и҆ дх҃ъ пра́въ ѡ҆бновѝ въ оу҆трѡ́бахъ на́шихъ* ("Create in us, O God, and renew a right spirit within our inward parts"), adapting the singular Davidic verse into a communal liturgical prayer.

[^2795]: Aposticha Idiomelon 2 of Pentecost Vespers (*Νῦν τὸ Παράκλητον Πνεῦμα, εἰς πᾶσαν σάρκα ἐκκέχυται...*).

[^2796]: Church Slavonic *срⷣца оу҆́мнѣ ѡ҆сїа́еми* translates Greek *τὰς καρδίας νοερῶς ἐλλαμφθέντες* ("being illumined in hearts noetically").

[^2797]: Psalm 50:13 LXX (50:11 MT): *Не ѡ҆́връзѝ на́съ ѿ лица̀ твое́го . и҆ дх҃а ст҃го твое́го не ѿимѝ ѿ на́съ* (*Μὴ ἀποῤῥίψῃς ἡμᾶς ἀπὸ τοῦ προσώπου σου...*). Note plural *на́съ* in the liturgical witness.

[^2798]: Aposticha Idiomelon 3 of Pentecost Vespers (*Νῦν περιβάλλονται κράτος, οἱ Χριστοῦ Ἀπόστολοι...*). Alludes to Luke 24:49: "until ye be endued with power from on high" (*ἕως οὗ ἐνδύσησθε δύναμιν ἐξ ὕψους* / *ѡ҆дѣва́ютсѧ дръжа́вою хв҃и съвы́ше*).

[^2799]: Aposticha Idiomelon 3 conclusion: *присносоу́щное є҆ство́ же и҆ просто́е, трисъста́вно вѣ́ровати* translates Greek *τὴν συναΐδιον φύσιν καὶ ἁπλῆν, τρισυπόστατον σέβειν* ("to revere/believe the co-eternal and simple nature in three hypostases").

[^2800]: Concluding clause of the third Aposticha sticheron: *възвѣсти́вшоусѧ сп҃соу дꙋ́шамъ на́шимъ* (*τῷ καταγγελθέντι σωτῆρι τῶν ψυχῶν ἡμῶν*).

[^2801]: The celebrated Pentecost Vespers Doxasticon of the Aposticha (*Δεῦτε λαοί, τὴν τρισυπόστατον Θεότητα προσκυνήσωμεν...*), traditionally attributed to the Emperor Leo the Wise.

[^2802]: Theological formulation of the Trinitarian dogma: *ѻ҆ц҃ъ бо безлѣ́тнѣ родѝ сн҃а съпрⷭ҇носоу́щна , и҆ съпрⷭ҇толна . и҆ дх҃ъ сты́и бѧ́ше въ ѻ҆ц҃и , съ сн҃омъ прославла́емъ* (*Πατὴρ γὰρ ἀχρόνως ἐγέννησεν Υἱόν, συναΐδιον καὶ σύνθρονον, καὶ Πνεῦμα ἅγιον ἦν ἐν Πατρί, σὺν Υἱῷ δοξαζόμενον*).

[^2803]: Triadological triad: *є҆ди́на си́ла , є҆ди́но сꙋ́щество , и҆ є҆ди́но Бж҃тво* (*μία δύναμις, μία οὐσία, μία Θεότης*).

[^2804]: Doxasticon continuation, parsing the Trisagion clauses hypostatically: *Ст҃ы́и Бг҃ъ , и҆́же всѧ̑ съдѣва́ѧй сн҃омъ . и҆ дѣ́йствомъ ст҃го дх҃а* applies "Holy God" to the Father (*Ἅγιος ὁ Θεός, ὁ δι' Υἱοῦ τὰ πάντα δημιουργήσας, συνεργείᾳ τοῦ Ἁγίου Πνεύματος*).

[^2805]: "Holy Mighty" applied to the Son: *Ст҃ы́и крѣ́пкыи . и҆́мже ѻ҆ц҃а позна́хомъ . и҆ дх҃ъ сты́и прїиде въ ми́ръ* (*Ἅγιος Ἰσχυρός, δι' οὗ τὸν Πατέρα ἐγνώκαμεν, καὶ τὸ Πνεῦμα τὸ Ἅγιον ἐπεδήμησε τῷ κόσμῳ*).

[^2806]: "Holy Immortal" applied to the Holy Spirit: *Ст҃ыи бесмр҃тный оу҆тѣши́телный дш҃е . и҆́же ѿ ѻ҆ц҃а и҆сходѧ́й . и҆ на сн҃ѣ почива́ѧй* (*Ἅγιος Ἀθάνατος, τὸ Παράκλητον Πνεῦμα, τὸ ἐκ Πατρὸς ἐκπορευόμενον, καὶ ἐν Υἱῷ ἀναπαυόμενον*).

[^2807]: The concluding Trinitarian acclamation: *трⷪ҇це ст҃аа сла́ва тебѣ̀* (*Τριὰς Ἁγία, δόξα σοι*).

[^2808]: Rubrics for the concluding dismissal prayers: Song of Simeon (Luke 2:29–32), Trisagion Prayers, the Lord's Prayer with priestly ecphonesis, followed by the Festal Troparion of Pentecost (*Ἦχος πλ. δ'*).

[^2809]: Festal Troparion of Pentecost, Tone 8 (*Εὐλογητὸς εἶ Χριστὲ ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν, ὁ πανσόφους τοὺς ἁλιεῖς ἀναδείξας...*). Alludes to Matthew 4:19.

[^2810]: Conclusion of the Troparion of Pentecost (*чл҃колꙕ́бче сла́ва тебѣ̀* / *φιλάνθρωπε, δόξα σοι*).

[^2811]: Rubric prescribing the elaborate festal dismissal prayer (*посе́мъ по́пъ мл҃твоу ѿпоу́стноую сїю , и҆́же глаго́летсѧ въ тыи де́нь ст҃го дх҃а*), characteristic of the Great Church and ancient Kyivan euchologia.

[^2812]: Opening clause of the Great Dismissal of Pentecost Vespers, summarizing Christ's kenosis (*ἐκκενώσας ἑαυτόν* / *и҆злїѧ́въ себѐ*, Philippians 2:7), Incarnation, theosis of human nature (*ѡ҆божи́въ то̀*), Ascension, and the descent of the consubstantial Spirit upon the Apostles.

[^2813]: Conclusion of the Great Dismissal of Pentecost Vespers: *Хс҃ и҆́стинныи Бг҃ъ на́шъ . мл҃твами прⷭ҇тыѧ своеѧ мт҃ре . ст҃ы́хъ сла́вныхъ и҆ всехвалныхъ дх҃оно́сныхъ є҆го̀ оу҆чени́къ и҆ а҆пл҃ъ, и҆ всѣ́хъ ст҃ы́хъ . поми́лꙋетъ и҆ сп҃сетъ на́съ ꙗ҆́ко бл҃гъ, и҆ чл҃кѡлюбе́цъ*.

[^2814]: Rubric providing an alternative, shorter dismissal (*и҆́нъ ѿпоу́стъ въкра́тцѣ*), customary for standard parish use.

[^2815]: The short Festal Dismissal of Pentecost: *И҆́же въ видѣ́нїи ѡ҆́гненыхъ ꙗ҆зы́къ, низпосла́въ прⷭ҇ты́и дх҃ъ на ст҃ыѧ своѧ̑ оу҆чн҃кы и҆ а҆пл҃ы...* Note the invocation of the chief apostles (*връхѡ́вныхъ а҆пл҃ъ* / *κορυφαίων ἀποστόλων*).

[^2816]: Folio 478r (physical page 971) headpiece and title: *УТѢШИ́ТЕЛНЫЙ ПѢ́ТЫЙ ИЛЍ БЫВА́ЕМЫЙ ЗА ВСѦ́КО прошѐніе* (A Consolatory [Canon or Service], sung or performed for every petition). In Ruthenian and Byzantine liturgical practice, this marks the opening of the celebrated Supplicatory Canon (*Paraklesis* or *Moleben*) to the Most Holy Theotokos, chanted in times of illness, tribulation, public crisis, or personal necessity.

[^2817]: Rubric on fol. 478r (physical page 971): The initial blessing by the priest (*Благословенъ Богъ нашъ*), followed by the customary Trisagion Prayers, the Lord's Prayer with priestly doxology, twelve repetitions of *Lord, have mercy*, and the triple Invitation to Worship (*Come, let us worship*).

[^2818]: Psalm 142 (Septuagint LXX versification; Masoretic 143): *Господи услыши молитву мою* (O Lord, hear my prayer). This psalm constitutes the traditional opening penitential psalm of the Paraklesis / Moleben.

[^2819]: Folio 478r (physical page 971): Announcement of the Troparion in Tone 4, following the verses of *God is the Lord* (*Богъ Господь*, Ps. 117:27 [LXX]).

[^2825]: Heirmos of Ode 1, Tone 8, on fol. 479r (physical page 973): *Во́дꙋ прошѐдъ ꙗ҆́ко по сꙋ́хꙋ, и҆з̾ є҆гѵ́пе[тскаго зла бѣжав]* (*Ὑγρὰν διοδεύσας ὡсеὶ ξηράν*). Printed by incipit only, in strict conformity with Ruthenian liturgical typography.

[^2826]: Troparion 1 of Ode 1, Tone 8 (*Многими содержимь напастьми* / *Πολλοῖς συνεχόμενος πειρασμοῖς*), on fol. 479r (physical page 973).

[^2828]: Troparion 3 of Ode 1, Tone 8 (*Спаса рождшую тя и Бога молю* / *Σωτῆρα τεκοῦσάν σε καὶ Θεόν*), on fol. 479r (physical page 973), preceded by the cue for *Glory*.

[^2937]: Troparion incipits: `Къ бц҃и приле́жно нн҃ѣ` (Greek: *Τῇ Θεοτόκῳ ἐκτενῶς νῦν προσδράμωμεν*) and `Не оу҆молчи́мъ николи́же` (Greek: *Οὐ σιωπήσομέν ποτε*).

[^2940]: Physical folio 484v (Leaf p998) is an unprinted blank verso leaf (*vacat*), marking the codicological division between Gathering `ѡ̃ ѡ̃` (Gathering 52) and the newly beginning office.

[^2941]: Physical folio 485r (Leaf p999) opens with a monumental woodcut headpiece (100 × 50 mm) depicting the Crucifixion at Golgotha inside an oval wreath, flanked by angels and Renaissance foliage ornament, characteristic of the Striatyn printing house of Teodor and Hedeon Balaban.

[^2942]: Major section title: `ЧИ́НЪ НА ВЪЗДВИЖЕ́НЇЄ Че́стнаго Крⷭ҇та •` (The Order for the Elevation of the Precious Cross), celebrated on September 14 (Universal Exaltation of the Precious and Life-Creating Cross).

[^2943]: Rubric: During the chanting of the Great Doxology at Matins, the officiating priest vests in full sacerdotal vestments (*sticharion, epitrachelion, zone, epimanikia, phelonion*), reflecting the high solemnity of the Elevation ritual.

[^2944]: Rubric: The Priest censes the Holy Table where the Cross has rested in place of the Gospel book, places the diskos bearing the Precious Cross upon his head, and processes solemnly to the Royal Doors, preceded by two candle-bearers. Spanning across onto leaf p1000 (`славосло́вїа...`).

[^2945]: Rubric: At the singing of the final "Holy God" (*Trisagion*) of the Great Doxology, the priest carries the Cross into the center of the church to the prepared four-legged analogion (*четвероножному налою*) covered with an honorable silk cloth (*паволокою*).

[^2946]: Elevation exclamation: `Премоу́дрость про́сти •` (Greek: *Σοφία, ὀρθοί*), proclaimed by the Priest as he raises the diskos with the Cross before the congregation.

[^2947]: Troparion of the Cross: `Сп҃сѝ Гдⷭ҇и лю́ди своѧ̑` (Greek: *Σῶσον, Κύριε, τὸν λαόν σου*), Tone 1.

[^2948]: Rubric: The priest places the diskos upon the analogion, censes it cruciformly on all four sides (`крⷭ҇та ѡ҆́бра́зно`), and makes three bows/prostrations, noted specifically as obligatory even on Saturday or Sunday when full prostrations are normally prohibited by ancient canons.

[^2949]: Rubric: The priest takes the Precious Cross decorated with fragrant basil leaves (`съ благоуха́нными васи́льками` / Greek: *μετὰ βασιλικοῦ*) into his hands, stands before the analogion facing eastward, and begins the first of the five ceremonial elevations.

[^2950]: Opening petition of the Elevation: `Поми́лꙋй на́съ Бж҃е повели́цѣй мл҃ти...` (Greek: *Ἐλέησον ἡμᾶς, ὁ Θεός, κατὰ τὸ μέγα ἔλεός σου*), the first petition facing east, during which the people chant "Lord, have mercy" one hundred times as the Cross is slowly lowered and elevated.

[^2951]: Elevation of the Precious Cross, First Elevation (facing East): concluding clause of the first petition (`твое́й , мо́лимтисѧ оу҆слы́ши и҆ поми́лꙋй`), followed by the first hundred of *Lord, have mercy* (*Господи помилуй*). The priest signs with the Cross thrice and slowly bows until his head is one span (*пядь*, approximately 18–20 cm) from the ground, then gradually straightens as the hundred petitions are chanted.

[^2952]: Rubric: at count 97 of the first centenary, the Ekklesiarches cues the choir and priest, who stands fully upright while the remaining three repetitions of *Lord, have mercy* are chanted with an elevated voice (*высоча́йшимъ гла́сомъ*) to complete the hundred.

[^2953]: Station to the South: the priest turns southward and signs with the Cross thrice before intoning the second petition for the sovereign and state (`Є҆щѐ мо́лимсѧ ѡ҆ бл҃гочти́вѣмъ , и҆ бг҃охрани́мѣмъ цр҃и на́шемъ...`).

[^2954]: Second Elevation (facing South) and Station to the West: following the second centenary, the priest turns westward to intone the third petition for the local archbishop, spiritual fathers, and monastic brotherhood.
