[^4262]: If a priest who has dismissed an adulterous wife subsequently falls into fornication with another woman, he is permanently suspended from the Liturgy, but admitted to communion as a layman.

[^4263]: If a priest refuses to put away an unrepentant adulterous wife, he remains under permanent liturgical suspension, though given priestly viaticum at death.

[^4264]: If the adulterous wife dies and the priest has remained entirely celibate, he is restored to full active ministry.

[^4265]: Text breaks off mid-sentence at the bottom of fol. 677v (*а҆́щели жива̀ бꙋ́детъ и҆ не мо́жетъ ꙗ҆́тисѧ съ мꙋ́жемъ ѻ҆́нѣмъ ꙗ҆́вѣ...*), followed by a syntactical lacuna/jump in the 1606 imprint before fol. 678r (*Page_1371.jpg*), which abruptly begins mid-clause with an infanticide/adultery penalty.

[^4266]: Folio 678r header: *ст҃ы́хъ ѡ҆ц҃ъ* (*Of the Holy Fathers:*). Folio 677v (Cohort 137, leaf p1370) ended mid-sentence with *а҆́щели жива̀ бꙋ́детъ и҆ не мо́жетъ ꙗ҆́тисѧ съ мꙋ́жемъ ѻ҆́нѣмъ ꙗ҆́вѣ...* (*"but if she be alive, and cannot be caught openly with that man..."*), and fol. 678r opens mid-clause with *моу́жа оу҆мори́тъ є҆́же поѧ́ти и҆но́го* (*"...[or if she] slays her husband in order to marry another"*), representing an epigraphic ellipsis or textual jump in the 1606 Striatyn print.

[^4267]: Canonical penalty for maternal adultery combined with infanticide: lifetime excommunication from entrance into the consecrated temple.

[^4268]: Church Slavonic: *на мѣ́стѣ ѡ҆глаше́нныхъ люді́й* (in the place of the catechumens). In traditional Byzantine penitential discipline, this corresponds to the station of the prostrators or hearers in the narthex.

[^4269]: Church Slavonic: *ѿлоуче́на соу́щи ѿ всь́каго хрⷭ҇тїа́нскаго чи́на* (cast out from every Christian rank). The penitent is separated from liturgical communion and must make public confession and supplication before the entering congregation. Text continues syntactically across the physical folio turn onto leaf p1372 (fol. 678v).

[^4270]: Folio 678v header: *з҃аповѣди* (*Injunctions:*). The intercessory prayers of the faithful congregation entering the temple on behalf of the public penitent (*є҆да̀ ка́ко мл҃твами и҆́хъ прїи́метъ проще́нїе ѿ бг҃а*).

[^4271]: Church Slavonic: *соухоѣды́и* (xerophagy / dry fasting), the strictest canonical fast consisting solely of bread, salt, and water.

[^4272]: Lifting of the dry fast on Saturdays and Sundays, in strict conformity with Apostolic Canon 64, which forbids fasting on the Sabbath and Lord's Day except on Holy Saturday.

[^4273]: Scriptural precept of marital abstinence based on 1 Corinthians 7:5 (*"Defraud ye not one the other, except it be with consent for a time, that ye may give yourselves to fasting and prayer; and come together again, that Satan tempt you not for your incontinency"*).

[^4274]: Leaf p1372 breaks off at the foot of fol. 678v with the uncompleted opening *Лѣ́по же є҆́сть всьѧ́комоу хрⷭ҇тїаниноу...* (*"It is also fitting for every Christian..."*). The text does not continue on fol. 679r (leaf p1373), which immediately opens with the independent thematic title *Ѡ въсхища́ющихъ на бра́къ жены̀*, evidencing a brief catchword omission in the 1606 print.

[^4275]: Folio 679r header and title: *хо҃ѳ • Ѡ҆ въсхища́ющихъ на бра́къ жены̀* (*Concerning Those Who Abduct Women for Marriage*). Greek: *Περὶ τῶν ἁρπαζόντων πρὸς γάμον γυναῖκας*.

[^4276]: Canon 11 of the Local Council of Ancyra (314 AD): abducted betrothed maidens are to be restored to their original betrothed spouses if the latter are willing.

[^4277]: Canon 27 of the Fourth Ecumenical Council (Chalcedon, 451 AD) and Canon 92 of the Sixth Ecumenical Council (Trullo / In Trullo / Quinisext, 692 AD): deposition for clergy and anathema for laity who abduct women under pretext of marriage or who assist abductors. Text continues syntactically across the physical folio turn onto leaf p1374 (fol. 679v).

[^4278]: Folio 679v header: *ѡ҆ въсхища́ющихъ* (*Concerning Abductors:*). Canonical censure and anathema extended to accomplices and instigators who aid bride abduction.

[^4279]: Juridical and moral distinction between the abductor driven by passion (*по́хо въсхище́нїю... премо́гши*) and the calculating accomplice who acts from pure malice (*зло́боу*), disrupting public order (*гражда́нства не оу҆стро́єно полага́етъ бл҃гочи́нїе*).

[^4280]: Nomocanonical definitions: *сꙋдѣ́йствоуѧй* (active co-perpetrator who executes the kidnapping) and *съслага́ѧй* (accessory/conspirator who devises the plots and supplies counsel).

[^4281]: Folio 680r header: *х҃п • ѡ҆ и҆́ма[щихъ] на бра́къ* (*Concerning Those Taking for Marriage:*). Section title: *Закѡ́ни цр҃тїи* (*Imperial / Civil Laws:*), drawing from Byzantine civil law (Justinian's *Codex* IX.13, *Novels* 143 and 150; *Ecloga* XVII.23; *Prochiron* XXXIX.27).

[^4282]: Universal scope of the law against abduction: covering betrothed, unbetrothed, widows, nobles, slaves, freedwomen, and nuns (*ѡ҆сщ҃е́нна*).

[^4283]: Armed abduction (using swords or clubs) punished by decapitation (*мече́мъ да томи́мъ бꙋ́детъ*).

[^4284]: Mutilation (rhinotomy / cutting off noses) and flogging for accessories, informants, and accomplices. Text continues syntactically across the physical folio turn onto leaf p1376 (fol. 680v).

[^4285]: Folio 680v header: *ѡ҆ въсхища́ющихъ* (*Concerning Abductors:*). Amputation of the hand (*роука̀ да оусѣче́тсѧ*) for unarmed abduction, and flogging, tonsure, and exile for accomplices.

[^4286]: Imprisonment for parents who collude in or accept the forced marriage of their abducted daughter; burning at the stake (*да и҆жже́жетсѧ*) for slaves assisting in the abduction.

[^4287]: Absolute civil nullity of marriage between an abductor and his victim, even if the father grants retrospective consent.

[^4288]: Legal prohibition against the victim marrying her kidnapper; parents who subsequently acquiesce are committed to prison. Text continues syntactically across the physical folio turn onto leaf p1377 (fol. 681r).

[^4289]: Folio 681r header: *х҃па • на бра́къ ж[ены̀]* (*...for Marriage of a Woman*).

[^4290]: Juridical distinction between violent abduction (*похище́нїе*, which is unpardonable) and forceful defloration (*понꙋ́ди растли́въ дв҃цꙋ*, which permits subsequent marriage if the violated maiden chooses to grant forgiveness).

[^4291]: Civil forfeiture: an abducted maiden who refuses to marry her kidnapper receives his property; refusal to enforce this results in total confiscation of both parties' assets to the fiscus.

[^4292]: Statutory grading of the crime: abduction is classified as an offense more heinous than adultery (*вѧ́щше є҆́стъ прелюбодѣ́йства*). Text continues syntactically across the physical folio turn onto leaf p1378 (fol. 681v).

[^4293]: Folio 681v header: *ѡ҆ въсхища́ющи на бра́[къ жены̀]* (*Concerning Those Abducting for Marriage*). Capital punishment for abducting a married woman or virgin, regardless of private forgiveness; anyone may act as public prosecutor.

[^4294]: Manumission granted to any slave who reveals a bride abduction or exposes a concealed crime.

[^4295]: Special rule concerning a slave who abducts or harbours a female slave who is a harlot: exempted from capital penalties for kidnapping or corruption, but fined by the ruler and subject to disciplinary chastisement.

[^4296]: Reference to Novel 17 of Emperor Justinian (*Седмьна́десѧтлаа же і҆ꙋстинїа́нова но́вла*): denial of the right of church asylum / sanctuary to abductors of maidens, permitting their arrest and binding even during Holy Pascha.

[^4297]: Folio 682r: Opening of the formal colophon of the 1606 Striatyn Trebnyk. Theological opening doxology to the Holy Trinity.

[^4298]: Pan Teodor Yuriiovych Balaban (d. 1603/1606), starost of Terebovlia, brother of Bishop Hedeon Balaban of Lviv, who founded the Striatyn and Univ printing presses and funded the production of the 1606 *Trebnik*.

[^4299]: *Ѳеѡ́дѡра К*: Teodor/Feodor K., the learned editor and proofreader who revised and corrected the liturgical texts of the Striatyn press.

[^4300]: Traditional Ukrainian scribal/typographic apology and humility formula (*topos*), begging readers to correct typographical or editorial errors with meekness rather than curses.

[^4301]: Date of commencement of printing: Anno Mundi 7113 / Anno Domini 1605 (*҂з҃ р҃ г҃і / ҂а҃ х҃ є҃*). Text continues across the physical folio turn onto leaf p1380 (fol. 682v).

[^4302]: Folio 682v: Continuation and conclusion of the imprint colophon: printing began on July 22, 1605, and was completed on September 14, 1606 (AM 7114 / AD 1606, Feast of the Exaltation of the Holy Cross).

[^4303]: Location of publication: Striatyn (*В СТРѦ́ТИНѢ*), the estate of the Balaban family in the Rohatyn region (Western Ukraine), where the famous Striatyn press operated under Bishop Hedeon and Teodor Balaban before its equipment was acquired in 1618 by Archimandrite Yelysei Pletenetsky for the Kyiv Pechersk Lavra.

[^4304]: Concluding typographic woodcut printer's device: an elaborate diamond-shaped floral knotwork ornament marking the final impression of the 1606 edition.

[^4305]: Title: *О҆главле́нїе въслѣ́дованїй соу́щихъ въ настоѧ́щей се́й Кни́ѕѣ ско́рагора́ди ѡ҆брѣ́тенїа потре́бнѣ́йшихъ веще́й* (*Table of Contents of the Services Present in This Present Book, for the Speedy Finding of the Most Necessary Matters*). This unfoliated index follows immediately after the concluding imprint colophon on leaf p1380 (fol. 682v). It is preceded by a woodcut headpiece depicting Christ as the Man of Sorrows (*King of Glory* / *Akra Tapeinosis*) rising from the tomb amidst renaissance-baroque floral scrollwork.

[^4306]: The canonical preamble and instruction on Holy Baptism extracted from the Apostolic Canons (Canons 46, 47, 49, 50) and Patristic canons (fol. 1r; physical leaf p13).

[^4307]: The liturgical order of making a catechumen, comprising the prayers of exorcism, renunciation of Satan, and confession of faith (fol. 15r; physical leaf p41).

[^4308]: The office and ritual of Holy Baptism and holy Chrismation (fol. 23r; physical leaf p57).

[^4309]: The ablution and washing of the newly baptized on the eighth day (fol. 38r; physical leaf p87).

[^4310]: The canonical rite for receiving converts from various heresies unto the Catholic Church (fol. 43r; physical leaf p97).

[^4311]: The rite for receiving Armenian Christians through renunciation of Monophysitism and Chrismation (fol. 46r; physical leaf p103). Quire mark at foot of leaf: *ини кв*.

[^4312]: Order for receiving Latins (*Ка́ко подоба́етъ прїима́ти приходѧ́щихъ ѿ лати́нъ къ на́шей правосла́внѣй вѣ́рѣ*, fol. 49v–50r; physical leaf p116).

[^4313]: Order of Betrothal (*Въслѣ́дованїе ѡ҆броуче́нїю*, fol. 53r; physical leaf p123).

[^4314]: Order of Crowning / Matrimony (*Въслѣ́дованїе вѣнча́нїю*, fol. 58r; physical leaf p133).

[^4315]: Order of Holy Unction / Anointing of the Sick (*Въслѣ́дованїе ст҃а́гѡ є҆ле́а / маслосщ҃е́нїю*, fol. 78r; physical leaf p173).

[^4316]: The monastic tonsure of the Little Habit / Lesser Angelic Schema (*Въслѣ́дованїе ма́лаго ѻ҆́браза*, fol. 293r; physical leaf p603).

[^4317]: The Supplicatory Canon (Paraklesis) to the Most Holy Theotokos for Every Petition (*Паракли́съ къ Прест҃ѣ́й Бц҃ѣ*, fol. 478r; physical leaf p971).

[^4318]: The canon law treatise on Patriarchal Stavropegial status (*Ѡ ставропигїа́хъ*, fol. 495r; physical leaf p1005). Quire mark at foot of leaf: *ини г*.

[^4319]: The historical liturgical drama and office of the Holy Three Children in the Babylon Furnace (*Дѣ́йство пе́щное*, fol. 615r; physical leaf p1245).

[^4320]: Major section heading in red cinnabar: *А҆ сѐ мл҃твы потре́бныѧ* (*And here are the occasional/necessary prayers*), introducing the extensive collection of pastoral blessings and occasional prayers.

[^4321]: The solemn Prayer of Absolution read by the spiritual father over the grave of a departed monk (*Моли́тва разрѣше́нїю, ю҆́же прочита́етъ дх҃о́вный ѡ҆́тцъ надъ гро́бомъ оу҆ме́ршаго и҆́нока*, fol. 360r; physical leaf p736). Quire mark at foot of leaf: *ини д*.

[^4322]: Solemn prayers composed by Patriarch Philotheos I Kokkinos of Constantinople (1353–1354, 1364–1376) during drought and times of calamity (fol. 407r; physical leaf p830).

[^4323]: The ancient Byzantine Genuflection Prayers chanted at Great Vespers on the afternoon of Pentecost Sunday / Day of the Holy Spirit (fol. 456r; physical leaf p927).

[^4324]: The blessing of the memorial boiled wheat (*kolyvo* / *kutia*) on Pentecost and festal commemorations (fol. 510r; physical leaf p1035).

[^4325]: The formal Prayer of Absolution attributed to Patriarch Michael of Constantinople (fol. 516r; physical leaf p1047). Quire mark at foot of leaf: *ини є*.

[^4326]: The blessing of willow branches on Flowery / Palm Sunday (*Въ недѣ́лю ва́їй* / *цвѣ́тную*, fol. 522r; physical leaf p1059).

[^4327]: The blessing of the Paschal loaf (*Artos*) on Holy Pascha and its ceremonial breaking on Bright Saturday (fol. 526r; physical leaf p1067). In the printed witness, the numeral 526 is set with an initial *х* sort for *ф* (*х҃кѕ*).

[^4328]: The ancient agricultural exorcism prayer attributed to the Holy Martyr Tryphon against locusts, caterpillars, caterpillars, mice, and crop parasites (fol. 543r; physical leaf p1101).

[^4329]: The pastoral prayer of cleansing and consolation for a woman who has suffered an involuntary miscarriage or stillbirth (fol. 544r; physical leaf p1103).

[^4330]: Supplicatory prayer composed by Metropolitan Makarios of Philadelphia for protection during the invasion of foreign hostile nations (fol. 575r; physical leaf p1165).

[^4331]: Solemn supplicatory prayers composed by Patriarch Kallistos I of Constantinople (1350–1353, 1355–1363) in times of public misfortune and epidemic (fol. 582r; physical leaf p1179).

[^4332]: Supplicatory prayer against the pestilential scourge and lethal plague (*На ра́ну губи́тельную и҆ мо́ръ*, fol. 594r; physical leaf p1203). The Table of Contents continues onto leaf p1391 in Cohort 140.

[^4333]: Prayer for one wishing to embark upon a journey (*Моли́тва хотѧ́щему ѿити́ въ пꙋ́ть*, fol. 631r; physical leaf p1277).

[^4334]: Prayer for those embarking upon a voyage by ship or boat (*Моли́тва на хотѧ́щихъ плы́ти*, fol. 631v; physical leaf p1278).

[^4335]: Prayers over children departing to learn sacred letters / literacy (*Моли́твы надъ ѻ҆́троки ѿходѧ́щими оу҆чи́тисѧ гра́мотѣ*, fol. 617v–618r; physical leaves p1250–p1251). The printed table gives the numeral *х҃ні* (658 or misprint for *хі҃и* / 618).

[^4336]: Prayers at the partaking of the sanctified water of the Holy Theophanies (*Моли́твы къ причаще́нїю ст҃ы́ѧ воды̀ ст҃ы́хъ Бг҃оѧвле́нїй*, fol. 621r; physical leaf p1257).

[^4337]: Canonical instruction on the relaxation and dispensation of foods and meats during the fasts and continuous non-fasting weeks (*Ѡ҆ раздрѣше́нїи бра́шенъ въ пре́данныхъ седми́цахъ*, fol. 628r; physical leaf p1271).

[^4338]: Diverse canonical rules and injunctions compiled from the Holy Apostles and God-bearing Holy Fathers (*За́повѣди разли́чны ст҃ы́хъ а҆́пѡстолъ и҆ Бг҃оно́сныхъ ст҃ы́хъ ѻ҆тє́цъ*, fol. 633r; physical leaf p1281).

[^4339]: Canonical rulings concerning the celebration and rest from manual labor on the principal feasts of the Lord and the Theotokos (*Ѡ҆ пра́здницѣхъ Гдⷭ҇кихъ и҆ Бг҃оро́дичныхъ*, fol. 634r; physical leaf p1283).

[^4340]: Pastoral instruction concerning Holy Communion and the frequency and reverent disposition required of the faithful (*Ѡ҆ ст҃ѣ́мъ причаще́нїи*, fol. 637r; physical leaf p1289).

[^4341]: Canonical instruction concerning offerings, first-fruits, and tithes brought to the church (*Ѡ҆ приноше́нїи цр҃ко́внѣмъ*, fol. 637v; physical leaf p1290).

[^4342]: Canonical injunctions and prohibitions concerning consanguineous marriage and kinship (*За́повѣди ѡ҆ съродѣ́нїихъ*, fol. 634r / 639r; physical leaf p1293).

[^4343]: Canonical treatise on forbidden and incestuous unions (*Ѡ҆ бра́цѣхъ възбране́ныхъ*, fol. 640r; physical leaf p1295).

[^4344]: Canonical treatise setting forth the computation of degrees of natural kinship and affinity (*Ѡ҆ сте́пенехъ сродства̀*, fol. 641r; physical leaf p1297).

[^4345]: Canonical rules regarding in-laws and relatives through marital union (*Ѡ҆ бра́чныхъ рожакѡ́хъ* / *сватовствѣ*, fol. 643r; physical leaf p1301).

[^4346]: Canonical instruction concerning the duties, qualifications, and spiritual authority of the confessor or spiritual father (*Ѡ҆ дх҃о́вномъ ѻ҆тцѝ*, fol. 648r; physical leaf p1311).

[^4347]: Legal and canonical distinctions between lawful marriages and unlawful incestuous unions (*Ѡ҆ бра́цѣхъ зако́нныхъ и҆ безако́нныхъ, и҆ ѡ҆ разли́чїи сродства̀*, fol. 644r; physical leaf p1303).

[^4348]: Canonical prohibitions concerning unclean meat, carrion, and the flesh of strangled or torn beasts which Christians are forbidden to eat (*Ѡ҆ мр̃ацина* [= *мръщи́нахъ*] *и҆́хже не достои́тъ ꙗ҆́сти*, fol. 652r; physical leaf p1319–p1320).

[^4349]: Injunctions concerning memorial services, commemorations, and alms for the reposed (*Ѡ҆ па́мѧти оу҆ме́ршимъ*, fol. 656r; physical leaf p1327).

[^4350]: Canonical injunctions and epitemias for diverse mortal and venial sins (*За́повѣди на разли́чнаѧ съгрѣше́нїѧ*, fol. 657r; physical leaf p1329).

[^4351]: Canonical injunctions and moral rules specifically addressed unto women (*За́повѣди ѡ҆ жена́хъ*, fol. 664r; physical leaf p1343).

[^4352]: Canonical injunctions, disciplinary rules, and penalties regarding sacred ministers and priests (*За́повѣди ѡ҆ і҆ере́єхъ*, fol. 675r; physical leaf p1365).

[^4353]: Juridical and canonical decrees concerning the abduction of women for marriage (*Ѡ҆ въсхища́ющихъ на бра́къ жены̀*, fol. 679r; physical leaf p1373), concluding on fol. 681v (physical leaf p1378). In the printed index, the folio number is written out in full words: *шестьсѡ́тно седмьдесѧ́тъ девѧ́тый* (679).

[^4354]: Explicit: *Коне́цъ О҆главле́нію* (*The End of the Table of Contents*). This marks the conclusion of the printed contents of the 1606 Striatyn Trebnyk.

[^4364]: Rear exterior wooden board covered in contemporary blind-tooled calfskin (physical leaf p1401), marking the final physical leaf and rear cover of the 1606 Striatyn Euchologion (*Trebnyk*). The tooling features an outer foliate roll, an inner panel divided by a saltire cross with four circular medallions depicting the Tetramorph (Evangelist symbols), upper and lower medallion compartments, and two riveted leather clasp straps on the fore-edge.
